'''Thomas Aherne''' (26 January 1919 – 30 December 1999), also referred to as '''Bud Aherne''', was an Irish [[association football|footballer]] and [[hurling|hurler]]. He played football for [[Belfast Celtic F.C.|Belfast Celtic]] and [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] and was a [[List of dual Irish international footballers|dual internationalist]], playing for both Ireland teams – the [[Ireland national football team (IFA)|IFA XI]] and the [[Ireland national football team (FAI)|FAI XI]]. In 1949 he was a member of the FAI XI that defeated [[England national football team|England]] [[England v Ireland (1949)|2–0]] at [[Goodison Park]], becoming the first non-UK team to beat England at home. As a hurler he also played one game for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]].

After retiring as a player Aherne settled in [[Luton]] where he coached the [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] youth team, worked in the local car industry and ran a very successful licensed premises. He also continued to visit [[Limerick]] regularly and remained healthy and active until he was diagnosed with [[Alzheimer's disease]] in the mid-1990s. He died in December 1999 at the age of 80 and was survived by his wife, Eileen, two sons, Pat and Brian, and three daughters, Maura, Trisha and Catherine.

==Club career==

===Early years===
Aherne was born in [[Limerick]], Ireland. As a youth, he initially emerged as a prominent [[hurling|hurler]] with Treaty Sarsfields and also played one game for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]]. However he subsequently decided to concentrate on football and began his senior career with [[Limerick United F.C.|Limerick United]] where his teammates included [[Davy Walsh]]. During the Second World War, Aherne served in the [[Irish Army]] and was stationed at [[Crosshaven]]. His impressive performances in the [[League of Ireland]] attracted attention and in 1946 he was signed by [[Belfast Celtic F.C.|Belfast Celtic]].

===Belfast Celtic===
While at [[Belfast Celtic F.C.|Belfast Celtic]], Aherne played alongside [[Jackie Vernon (footballer)|Jackie Vernon]], [[Billy McMillan]], [[Robin Lawler]] and [[Johnny Campbell (footballer, born 1923)|Johnny Campbell]] and helped them win the [[Irish Cup]] in 1947 and an [[Irish Football League|Irish League]] title in 1948. Aherne was also at Celtic during the infamous [[Boxing Day]] riot which broke out during a game against local rivals [[Linfield F.C.|Linfield]]. Within a few months, Aherne had left Celtic and signed for [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]]. However, in May 1949, Aherne temporarily rejoined Celtic for their final tour before the club disbanded. Together with McMillan, Campbell, Lawlor, guest player [[Mick O'Flanagan]] and manager [[Elisha Scott]], he went on the Celtic tour of the North America. The highlight of the 10 game tour came on 29 May when Celtic beat the reigning [[1949 British Home Championship|British champions]], [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]], 2–0.

===Luton Town===
Aherne signed for [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] in March 1949 for a fee of £6,000 and made his [[Football League|English League]] debut on 19 March in a 2–1 away defeat to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. Despite the fact he was over 30 when he joined Luton, he quickly established himself as a regular. Aherne played competitive football into his late thirties and was an ever-present during the [[1954–55 in English football#Second Division|1954–55]] season when Luton won promotion to [[Football League Division One|Division One]]. After playing 288 games for Luton, including 267 in the league, he only retired after a hairline fracture of the ankle ended his career. Even then he continued to play for a local league team, Luton Celtic, into his forties.

==Irish international==
When Aherne began his international career in 1946 there were in effect, two Ireland teams, chosen by two rival associations. Both associations, the [[Belfast]]-based [[Irish Football Association]] and the [[Dublin]]-based [[Football Association of Ireland]], claimed jurisdiction over the whole of Ireland and selected players from the whole island. As a result, several notable Irish players from this era, including Aherne played for both teams.

===FAI XI===
Between 1946 and 1953 Aherne made 16 appearances for the [[Ireland national football team (FAI)|FAI XI]]. He made his FAI debut in June 1946 during an [[Iberian Peninsula|Iberian]] tour, playing in both the 3–1 defeat to [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] on 16 June and then helping the FAI XI gain a surprise 1–0 victory against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 23 June. He remained a regular in the FAI XI throughout the late 1940s and early 1950s and featured prominently in the qualifying rounds for the [[1950 FIFA World Cup qualification|1950 World Cup]]. He was also a member of the FAI XI that defeated [[England national football team|England]] [[England v Ireland (1949)|2–0]] at [[Goodison Park]], becoming the first non-UK team to beat England at home.

On 16 November 1953, during a 1–1 draw with [[France national football team|France]], Aherne briefly became involved in controversy. Although only a friendly, the game quickly became heated and at one point, Aherne chased [[Raymond Kopa]] down the tunnel after play had been stopped for a foul. Kopa allegedly ran for his life after upsetting Aherne once too often. The FAI selectors were not impressed and Aherne was told a repeat would end his international career. As it turned out he made only one more appearance for the FAI XI. That came on 4 October 1953 in 5–3 defeat against [[France national football team|France]] during a qualifier for the [[1954 FIFA World Cup qualification|1954 FIFA World Cup]].

===IFA XI===
Between 1946 and 1950, Aherne also made 6 appearances for the [[Ireland national football team (IFA)|IFA XI]]. These include two Victory internationals played in early 1946. On 2 February at [[Windsor Park]] he made his debut for the IFA XI in a 3–2 defeat to [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] at [[Windsor Park]]. Then on 4 May he helped the IFA XI defeat [[Wales national football team|Wales]] 1–0 at [[Ninian Park]]. On 28 September 1946 Aherne also played for the IFA XI in a heavy defeat to [[England national football team|England]]. The highlight of career with the IFA XI came on 4 October 1947 when he helped them gain a 2–0 win against Scotland.

He made his last appearance for the IFA XI in a 0–0 draw with Wales on 8 March 1950. As well as being part of the [[1950 British Home Championship]], the game also doubled up as a qualifier for the [[1950 FIFA World Cup qualification|1950 World Cup]]. Aherne, together with [[Con Martin]], [[Reg Ryan]] and [[Davy Walsh]], was one of four players from the Republic, included in the IFA XI that day and as a result he played for two different associations in the same [[FIFA World Cup]] tournament. This situation eventually led to intervention by [[FIFA]] and as a result Aherne became one of the last four [[Republic of Ireland|Republic]]-born players to play for the IFA XI.

Aherne died in [[Luton]], England, aged 80.

'''Ciarán Carey''' (born 16 January 1970) is an Irish [[List of hurling managers|hurling manager]], selector and former player.

Primarily playing at the centre-back position, Carey's club career was with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and at inter-county level with Limerick. He was a key member of the latter team during the 1990s and collected two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] titles, two [[National Hurling League]] titles and three [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] awards.

In retirement from playing Carey has become involved in team management and coaching. At club level he has taken charge of the [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]] and [[Granagh-Ballingarry GAA|Granagh-Ballingarry]] sides in hurling and [[camogie]] respectively. Carey began his inter-county coaching career when he was appointed manager of the Limerick senior camogie team in 2007. He subsequently took charge of the Limerick under-21 hurling team as well as being a selector with the Limerick senior hurling team under [[Dónal O'Grady]]. In November 2013, Carey was appointed for a second spell as manager of the Limerick under-21 team.

==Early life==

Ciarán Carey was born in [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]] in 1970.  He was educated locally and from an early age he showed an interest in the game of [[hurling]]. Carey's brothers, [[Pa Carey|Pa]] and [[Paul Carey (hurler)|Paul]], as well as his nephew [[Cian Lynch]] have also played for Limerick.

==Playing career==

===Club===

Carey played his club hurling with the [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] team in a club career that spanned three decades.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patrickswellgaa.com/roll_of_honour.htm|title=Roll of honour|publisher=[[Patrickswell GAA]]|access-date=22 September 2010}}</ref> He first came to prominence as a member of the club's minor team, capturing a county championship winners' medal in 1984.

Carey had just turned seventeen years-old when he lined out in his first senior county championship final as goalkeeper.  Parish rivals [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] provided the opposition, however, 'the Well' narrowly took the title by 1–17 to 3–10 and Carey collected his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] winners' medal.

In 1988 Patrickswell contested the county championship decider for the second consecutive year.  [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] provided the opposition, however, Patrickswell triumphed by ten points and Carey added a second county title to his collection.  Patrickswell later represented the county in the provincial series of games and even reached the final.  The famous [[Mount Sion GAA|Mount Sion]] club provided the opposition, however, Patrickswell won by 3–13 to 2–13 and Carey added a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster]] club winners' medal to his collection.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Munster Senior Club Hurling Champions|publisher=[[Munster GAA]]|access-date=22 September 2010}}</ref> Patrickswell's run of success came to an end in the All-Ireland semi-final when the [[O'Donovan Rossa GAC Belfast]] club defeated the Munster champions by a single point.

Patrickswell failed to make it three-in-a-row in 1989, however, the team bounced back the following year to defeat [[Adare GAA|Adare]] and give Carey a third county championship title.  He later missed the club's Munster final triumph over [[Éire Óg GAA (Clare)|Éire Óg]], however, he was back on the team for the All-Ireland final against [[Glenmore GAA|Glenmore]].  The game was an exciting one, however, Patrickswell only held the lead on one occasion when [[Leonard Enright]] opened the scoring. A 1–13 to 0–12 score line gave Glenmore the title.

The next decade saw Patrickswell become the dominant force in club hurling in Limerick.{{fact|date=June 2018}}  Carey won his fourth county championship title in 1993.  He added to his haul of medals as Patrickswell won three county championships in-a-row in 1995, 1996 and 1997.  This latter win was subsequently followed by another Munster final appearance.  [[Clarecastle GAA|Clarecastle]] provided the opposition and eventually won the game by two points.

Four-in-a-row proved beyond Patrickswell, however, in 2000 a one-point defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]] gave Carey an eighth county championship winners' medal.

Defeat in 2001 was followed by a ninth success for Carey in 2003 when Adare were accounted for by two points.  Patrickswell subsequently qualified for the Munster final, however, cork champions [[Newtownshandrum GAA|Newtwonshandrum]] recorded a 2–18 to 2–9 victory.

In 2006 Carey had the chance to capture a remarkable tenth county championship title.  [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]], a team who last won the championship in 1893, were the opponents.  While Patrickswell were expected to win by many a 1–16 to 1–15 score line resulted in defeat for Carey.

===Inter-county===

Carey made his senior championship debut for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in 1989 at a time when the county team was in the doldrums.  His first few seasons on the team ended with an early exit from the provincial championship, however, in 1992 Limerick's fortunes began to change.  That year Carey's side qualified for the final of the [[National Hurling League]] and a stern test awaited.  Reigning [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] champions [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] provided the opposition and took an eight-point lead at half-time.  Limerick battled back to claim a narrow 0–0–14 to 0–13 victory and gave Carey his first National League winners' medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|title=Limerick GAA profile|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=22 September 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archive-date=25 May 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref> The new league champions built on this momentum and subsequently qualified for a Munster final showdown with [[Cork GAA|Cork]].  A high-scoring game developed, however, at the long whistle Cork were the champions by 1–22 to 3–11.  In spite of this disappointment Carey was subsequently presented with his first [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/about-the-gaa/gaa-history/all-stars/0/0/4/ |title=GAA All-Star winners |publisher=[[Gaelic Athletic Association]] |access-date=22 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101211104117/http://gaa.ie/about-the-gaa/gaa-history/all-stars/0/0/4/ |archive-date=11 December 2010 |df=dmy }}</ref>

Limerick failed to reach the provincial decider the following year, however, in 1994 Carey's team bounced back and qualified for the Munster final again.  Provincial whipping boys [[Clare GAA|Clare]] were the opponents and a rout took place.  A 0–25 to 2–10 score line gave Limerick the win and gave Carey his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Munster Senior Hurling Champions|publisher=[[Munster GAA]]|access-date=22 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721124423/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=21 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> Limerick subsequently qualified to meet [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the All-Ireland final.  It looked as if Carey's side were going to make history and claim the title as Limerick had a five-point lead with as many minutes left.  Offaly suddenly sprang to life following a [[Johnny Dooley (hurler)|Johnny Dooley]] goal from a close-in free.  Following the puck-out Offaly worked the ball upfield and [[Pat O'Connor (hurler)|Pat O'Connor]] struck for a second goal. The Offaly forwards scored another five unanswered points in the time remaining to secure a 3–16 to 2–13 victory.  It was a bitter blow for Limerick who looked as if they had one hand on the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]].  In spite of the defeat Carey was later presented with a second All-Star award.

Carey surrendered their Munster title to Clare in 1995, however, both sides met in the opening round of the championship the following year.  Clare went into the game as reigning All-Ireland champions, however, neither side took a decisive lead.  With time running out both side were still deadlocked, however, Carey played a captain's role in securing the win.  In injury time Carey caught a puck-out, ran 50 yards with the ball balanced on the bas of his hurley and scored the winning point for Limerick. Limerick later faced Tipperary in the provincial final and looked to be heading out of the championship as Tipp took a ten-point lead.  Carey's side battled back to secure a 0–19 to 1–16 draw and a second chance to defeat their near rivals.  The replay also saw Tipperary take a decisive lead, however, Limerick's goal-scoring ability was the deciding factor.  A 4–7 to 0–16 score line gave Limerick the title and gave Carey a second Munster winners' medal.  The subsequent All-Ireland final pitted Limerick against [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] for the first time in over forty years.  The game was far from a classic; however, it did provide excitement. [[Tom Dempsey (hurler)|Tom Dempsey]] was the hero of the day as he scored a goal after nineteen minutes to give Wexford a major advantage. His side led by 1–8 to 0–10 at half-time in spite of having [[Éamonn Scallan]] sent off. Wexford took a four-point lead in the second-half; however, this was whittled back to two points as Wexford hung on for the last twenty minutes. The final score of 1–13 to 0–14 showed how vital Dempsey's goal was. It was Limerick's second All-Ireland defeat in two years.  Once again Carey's individual skill was recognised when he collected his third All-Star award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/about-the-gaa/gaa-history/all-stars/0/0/3/ |title=GAA All-Star winners |publisher=[[Gaelic Athletic Association]] |access-date=22 September 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101211104203/http://gaa.ie/about-the-gaa/gaa-history/all-stars/0/0/3/ |archive-date=11 December 2010 }}</ref>

Limerick bounced back immediately in 1997 by defeating [[Galway GAA|Galway]] by 1–12 to 1–9 to take the National League title.  It was Carey's second winners' medal in that competition.  The recent All-Ireland defeats, however, seemed to have damaged the team as Carey's side crashed out of the provincial championship at an early stage.

This process repeated itself over the next few years and it was 2001 before Carey lined out in another Munster final.  Tipperary were the opponents on that occasion, however, Limerick fell by 2–16 to 1–17.

Carey was now in the twilight of his career and success seemed as far away for Limerick as it did when he joined the panel in 1989.  He was named team captain for 2004, however, his last game at senior level was a National League tie between Limerick and Tipperary and he called time on his career before the start of the championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17966|title=Limerick axe Carey|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=19 April 2004|access-date=22 September 2010}}</ref>

Four years after his retirement at senior level Carey was back in a Limerick jersey on the county's intermediate team.  He was full-back on the Limerick team that faced Tipperary in the provincial final.  A 2–16 to 2–12 score line gave Limerick the win and gave Carey a [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medal at intermediate level.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/ih_teams/|title=Munster Intermediate Hurling Champions|publisher=[[Munster GAA]]|access-date=22 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100817034410/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/ih_teams/|archive-date=17 August 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> Limerick later faced [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final, however, Carey was left on the losing side once again as 'the Cats' recorded a 1–16 to 0–13 win.

===Inter-provincial===
Carey was selected for the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] team in the inter-provincial series of games. He first lined out for his province in 1991 as Munster faced [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] in the decider. That game ended in defeat for Carey's side as the westerners won by 1–13 to 0–12.

After being omitted in 1992 Carey was back on the team again the following year; however, Munster were defeated in the opening game. He was not selected again the following year; however, in 1995, Carey was at midfield as Munster reached the final.  [[Ulster GAA|Ulster]] provided the opposition; however, Munster scraped a win by 0–13 to 1–9 and Carey collected a [[Railway Cup]] winners' medal.

Munster retained the title in 1996 and made it three-in-a-row in 1997. Carey featured in both of these victories.

After failing to make the team for three years, Carey was back with Munster for the final time in 2001. On that occasion Munster faced Connacht in the decider; however, the southerners had a comfortable 1–21 to 1–15 victory and Carey collected his fourth Railway Cup title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup|publisher=[[Munster GAA]]|access-date=24 September 2010}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
===Early experience===
In 2007 Carey turned his hand to management when he was appointed to take over the Limerick senior [[camogie]] team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=72294|title=Ciaran Carey appointed Limerick camogie manager|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=5 February 2007|access-date=22 September 2010}}</ref> Success was immediate as he guided Limerick to the All-Ireland 'B' final.  Cork were the opponents, however, the game ended in a 1–10 to 2–7 draw.  The subsequent replay was much more conclusive as Carey's side trounced 'the Rebelettes' by 2–9 to 0–6 to take the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Camogie Championship|All-Ireland 'B']] title.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickindependent.com/sport/sport/well-deserved-joy-for-the-limerick-camogie-heroines-on-the-leeside/|title=Well deserved joy for the Limerick camogie heroines on the Leeside|publisher=Limerick Independent|date=10 October 2007|access-date=22 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713210637/http://www.limerickindependent.com/sport/sport/well-deserved-joy-for-the-limerick-camogie-heroines-on-the-leeside/|archive-date=13 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> Carey was later nominated for the Philips camogie manager of the year awards and, while he was expected to stay on as manager, he stepped down shortly afterwards.

In 2007 Carey simultaneously took charge of the [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]] senior club hurling team, however, he left after an unsuccessful season in charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/3420/13000----cost.2034583.jp|title=€13,000 . . . cost of club coaching|publisher=[[Limerick Leader]]|date=8 February 2007|access-date=22 September 2010}}</ref>

In spite of leaving the posts of Limerick camogie and Tournafulla club manager, Carey returned to inter-county coaching when he was appointed manager of the Limerick under-21 hurling team in early 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=89066|title=Carey gets the call|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=7 February 2008|access-date=22 September 2010}}</ref> His tenure in charge was not a successful one as Limerick crashed out of the provincial championship at a very early stage.  Carey resigned as manager early in 2009 due to work commitments.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=105937|title=Carey steps down|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=21 January 2009|access-date=22 September 2010}}</ref>

===Limerick===
In September 2010, Carey was named as a selector – along with former teammates [[Pat Heffernan]] and [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J. Ryan]] – of [[Dónal O'Grady]]'s Limerick senior hurling team for 2011.

===Patrickwell (first spell)===
Carey guided Patrickswell to the [[2015 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2015 Limerick SHC]] final.<ref name=2024-high-profile-return/> He then left to take over as Kerry senior manager.<ref name=2024-high-profile-return/>

===Kerry===
In October 2015, Carey was named as the new manager of the [[Kerry county hurling team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/sauce-for-kerry-goose-but-not-galway-gander-34127254.html|title=Sauce for Kerry goose but not Galway gander|date=21 October 2015|work=Irish Independent|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2015/1019/735902-ciaran-carey-kerry-hurling/|title=Ciaran Carey is new Kerry hurling boss|date=19 October 2015|publisher=RTÉ|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref>

Carey stepped down as Kerry senior hurling manager on 4 December 2016, citing increased work commitments for his decision.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/carey-quits-as-kerry-hurling-boss-35267767.html|title=Carey quits as Kerry hurling boss|date=5 December 2016|work=Irish Independent|access-date=6 December 2016}}</ref>

===Patrickswell (second spell)===
In his second spell in charge of Patrickswell, Carey led the club to the [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2019 Limerick SHC]] title, defeating Na Piarsaigh, seeking a third consecutive title, in the final.<ref name=2024-high-profile-return/>

===Patrickswell (third spell)===
Carey was ratified as Patrickswell senior hurling manager for a third time on 6 February 2024.<ref name=2024-high-profile-return>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-legend-ciaran-carey-makes-high-profile-return-as-patrickswell-senior-hurling-manager/a588676035.html|title=Limerick legend Ciarán Carey makes high-profile return as Patrickswell senior hurling manager|work=Irish Independent|first=Michael|last=Verney|date=7 February 2024}}</ref>

'''Richard "Richie" Bennis''' (born 1945) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a centre-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scoreboardmemories.com/sports-index/hall-of-fame/item/143-richie-bennis-limerick.html|title=Richie Bennis: Patrickswell & Limerick Hurling Legend|publisher=Scoreboard Memories website|access-date=27 June 2015|first=Derry J. F.|last=Doody|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630042146/http://www.scoreboardmemories.com/sports-index/hall-of-fame/item/143-richie-bennis-limerick.html|archive-date=30 June 2015}}</ref>

Born in [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]], Bennis first played competitive hurling during his schooling at [[CBS Sexton Street]]. He arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of seventeen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team before later joining the under-21 side. He made his senior debut during the [[National Hurling League 1965-66|1965–66 league]]. Bennis subsequently became a regular member of the starting fifteen and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and one [[National Hurling League]] medal.  He was an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion.

As a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team on several occasions Bennis won one [[Railway Cup]] medal as a non-playing substitute. At club level he is a ten-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medallist with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]].

Bennis's career tally of 9 goals and 106 points ranks him as one of Limerick's top championship scorers of all time.

His brothers, [[Phil Bennis|Phil]] and [[Peter Bennis]], and his nephew, [[Gary Kirby]], also played for Limerick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/what-s-on/arts-entertainment/it-s-a-family-thing-says-richie-bennis-1-2180839|title=It's a family thing says Richie Bennis|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 August 2007|access-date=27 June 2015}}</ref> Kirby is now the manager of the Patrickswell Senior Hurling Team.

Throughout his career Bennis made 19 championship appearances. His retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1975 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1975 championship]].

In retirement from playing Bennis became involved in team management and coaching. At club level he has been involved in the management of [[Camogue Rovers GAA|Camogue Rovers]] and Patrickswell before taking charge of the Limerick senior team.

==Playing career==

===School===

During his secondary schooling in Limerick Bennis was chosen as captain of the Limerick City vocational schools' team. In 1961 he won an [[All-Ireland Vocational Schools Championship|All-Ireland]] medal following a 10–6 to 7–9 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]].

===Club===

In 1965 Patrickswell, with six Bennis brothers on the team, qualified for the final of county championship for the first time ever. A 2–16 to 0-4 trouncing of [[St. Kieran's GAA|St. Kieran's]] gave Bennis his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal.

Patrickswell retained the title in 1966, with Bennis securing a second championship medal following a 5–11 to 3–7 defeat of [[St. Patrick's GAA (limerick)|St. Patrick's]].

After failing in their bid for a third successive championship, Patrickswell reached the decider once again in 1969 where the team faced [[Pallasgreen GAA|Pallasgreen]]. A 0–17 to 2–2 victory gave Bennis a third championship medal.

Patrickswell retained the title in 1970 with Bennis collecting a fourth championship medal following a 2–14 to 0-2 trouncing of [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaelic-games/limerick-shc-final-kilmallock-s-three-in-a-row-success-is-fondly-remembered-1-4339850|title=Kilmallock's three-in-a-row success is fondly remembered|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 October 2012|access-date=27 June 2015|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

After a period of decline, which involved the losing of three championship decider, Patrickswell returned to the final once again in 1977. Goals were key as a 3–7 to 0–7 defeat of [[Killeedy GAA|Killeedy]] gave Bennis a fifth championship medal.

After failing to retain the title Patrickswell bounced back in 1979. Once again goals were vital in a 2–16 to 0–16 victory over [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]], which gave Bennis a sixth championship medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sideline-view-with-martin-kiely-1-2184996|title=Sideline View...|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=13 August 2008|access-date=27 June 2015|first=Martin|last=Kiely}}</ref>

In 1982 Patrickswell faced [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]] for the very first time in a county final. The overall craft and experience of Patrickswell, plus some shrewd tactical switches by their mentors, brought a late flurry of scores which finally sounded the death knell for Bruree, as Bennis collected a seventh championship medal following a 0–17 to 0–15 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/patrickswell-tops-in-close-tie-in-1982-1-2177347|title=Patrickswell tops in close tie in 1982|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=13 October 2006|access-date=27 June 2015|first=Seán|last=Murphy}}</ref>

Patrickswell retained the title in 1983 with Bennis winning an eighth championship medal as [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] were downed by 1–13 to 1–7.

In 1984 Patrickswell secured their own piece of history by capturing a third successive championship title. The 4–13 to 3–5 victory over [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] gave Bennis a ninth championship medal.

Four-in-a-row proved beyond Patrickswell, however, Bennis, who was now in his forties, was still a member of the team when the club contest their next final in 1987. A narrow 1–17 to 3–10 defeat of local rivals Ballybrown gave Bennis a tenth and final championship medal.

===Inter-county===

Bennis first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the Limerick minor hurling team in 1963. He was an unused substitute that year when Limerick defeated [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] by 4–12 to 5–4 to take the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster]] crown. The subsequent All-Ireland decider saw Limerick face a 6–12 to 5–9 defeat by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/wexford/sport/gaa/minor-breakthrough-was-50-years-ago/29199055.html|title=Minor breakthrough was 50 years ago|publisher=Wexford People|date=16 April 2013|access-date=27 June 2015}}</ref>

His tenure with the Limerick under-21 hurling team yielded little in terms of success.

Bennis made his senior debut during the 1965-66 league at a time when Limerick hurling was in the doldrums.

Limerick contested five successive league deciders between 1970 and 1974, with success coming in 1971. A narrow 3–12 to 3–11 defeat of old rivals Tipperary, when Bennis scoring a last-second free to win the game, gave him a [[National Hurling League]] medal.

In 1973 Limerick faced Tipperary in the provincial decider and a close game developed. The game ended in welter of excitement as, with time almost up and the sides level, a controversial '70 was awarded to Limerick. Bennis, as free-taker, was told by the match referee that it was the last puck of the game and that he must score directly. Some debate followed as to the validity of the score, with Tipperary players and supporters claiming the sliotar had drifted wide, however, the score was give and Bennis collected his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal following a 6–7 to 2–18 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/0524/322251-history-of-limerick-v-tipperary/|title=History of Limerick v Tipperary|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=24 May 2012|access-date=27 June 2015|first=James|last=McMahon}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/why-this-could-be-the-bestever-munster-hurling-championship-30300382.html|title=Why this could be the best-ever Munster hurling championship|work=Irish Independent|date=24 May 2014|access-date=27 June 2015|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}</ref> On 2 September 1973 Limerick faced [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the subsequent All-Ireland decider, however, the reigning champions had a depleted team due to a combination of injuries and emigration. In spite of this, the game hung in the balance for the first-half, however, eight minutes after the restart [[Mossie Dowling]] got a vital goal for Limerick. Shortly after this Bennis spearheaded a rampant Limerick attack which resulted in a 1–21 to 1–14 victory for Limerick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.joe.ie/gaa/gaa-features/puc-fado-a-look-back-limericks-last-all-ireland-success-in-1973/|title=Puc Fado: a look back Limerick’s last All-Ireland success in 1973|publisher=Joe.ie website|date=14 June 2007|access-date=4 July 2013|first=Declan|last=Whooley}}</ref> The victory gave Bennis an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal while he was later presented with his an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]].

Limerick maintained their provincial dominance in 1974, with Bennis winning a second Munster medal following a 6–14 to 3-9 trouncing of [[Clare GAA|Clare]]. The subsequent All-Ireland decider on 1 September 1974 was a repeat of the previous year as Kilkenny provided the opposition once again. Limerick stormed to a five-point lead in the first eleven minutes, however, a converted penalty by [[Eddie Keher]], supplemented by further goals from [[Mick Brennan (hurler)|Mick Brennan]] and [[Pat Delaney (Kilkenny hurler)|Pat Delaney]] gave Kilkenny a 3–19 to 1–13 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/irish-news/1974-the-year-when-26002174.html|title=1974 – the year when|work=Irish Independent|date=3 January 2005|access-date=16 July 2013}}</ref>

In 1975 Limerick failed in their bid to win a third successive Munster title following a 3–14 to 0–12 defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]]. This defeat brought the curtain down on Bennis's inter-county career.

===Inter-provincial===

Bennis was also chosen on the Munster inter-provincial team. He was first picked for duty in 1970, however, he remained as a non-playing substitute during Munster's 2–15 to 0–9 defeat of [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]].

==Managerial career==
===Early experience===

Shortly after retiring from club hurling Bennis remained active as a coach at all levels with Patrickswell. He later took charge of junior club [[Camogue Rovers GAA|Camogue Rovers]] but enjoyed little success.

===Managing Limerick===

In June 2006 Bennis was included as part of a four-man interim management team that was appointed in Limerick following [[Joe McKenna]]'s resignation after a seventeen-point defeat to Clare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/limerick-gets-new-four-man-team-1.1188306|title=Limerick gets new four-man team|work=The Irish Times|date=21 June 2006|access-date=16 July 2013}}</ref> He took charge as manager of the team midway through a disastrous championship campaign. Limerick went on to win their subsequent qualifier games before narrowly losing to Cork by 0–19 to 0–19 in the All-Ireland quarter-final. At the end of the season Bennis was appointed Limerick manager on a full-time basis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/loughnane-tipped-for-galway-post-as-limerick-back-bennis-12817.html|title=Loughnane tipped for Galway post as Limerick back Bennis|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=8 September 2006|access-date=29 June 2015|first=Brendan & O'Sullivan, Jim|last=O'Brien}}</ref>

In his first full season in charge, Bennis's Limerick enjoyed a remarkable championship campaign and qualified for the All-Ireland decider against Kilkenny on 2 September 2007. The Cats got off to a flying start with [[Eddie Brennan]] and [[Henry Shefflin]] scoring two goals within the first ten minutes to set the tone. Limerick launched a second-half comeback, however, Kilkenny were too powerful and cruised to a 2–19 to 1–15 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/match-reports/cats-cruise-to-30th-title-41563.html|title=Cats cruise to 30th title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 September 2007|access-date=24 November 2014|first=Jim|last=O'Sullivan}}</ref>

Limerick's 2008 championship campaign ended without a single victory, as defeats by Clare and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] resulted in Bennis's side being dumped out of the championship. In a subsequent interview with the ''[[Limerick Leader]]'', Bennis criticized the social habits of a group of players whom he says "broke their hearts in training and then went drinking". He revealed how commitment to training was good but "some players let me down".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/ireland/bennis-launches-scathing-attack-on-players-who-let-me-down-67683.html|title=Bennis launches scathing attack on players who 'let me down'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=18 July 2008|access-date=24 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/bennis-blasts-limerick-drinking-26463793.html|title=Bennis blasts Limerick drinking|work=Irish Independent|date=18 July 2008|access-date=24 November 2014|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> Less than a month after this Bennis failed to have his contract renewed as Limerick manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/other/limerick-hurling-manager-bennis-sacked-373424.html|title=Limerick hurling manager Bennis sacked|publisher=Breaking News|date=13 August 2008|access-date=29 June 2015}}</ref>

Phil Bennis.text:
{{short description|Irish hurler and manager}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=January 2022}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Phil Bennis | irish = Pilib Ó Binéid | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 8 | nickname = | occupation = Agricultural equipment salesman | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] | cl_position = | cl_years = 1960-1979 | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 6 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Centre-back | ic_years = 1966-1973 | ic_apps_points = 13 (0-01) | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 1 | nhl = 1 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_date = 1942 | birth_place=[[Patrickswell]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Philip Bennis''' (born 1942) is an Irish [[hurling]] manager and former player. At club level, he played with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. Bennis later served as a manager at club and inter-county levels. ==Playing career== Bennis first played hurling and [[Gaelic football]] at juvenile and underage level with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickwell]].{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/home/320805/limerick-hurling-legend-phil-bennisis-honoured-by-outgoing-metro-mayor.html|title=Limerick hurling legend Phil Bennis is honoured by outgoing metro-mayor|date=28 June 2018|publisher=Limerick Live|accessdate=26 December 2018|first=Nick|last=Rabbitts}} His first county success was a Limerick JAFC in 1964, before claiming a second title in 1970. By that stage, Bennis had his first hurling success after [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ing Patrickswell to consecutive [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] titles in 1965 and 1966.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20036696.html|title=‘We didn’t win enough’|date=7 July 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=26 December 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2017/02/11/patrickswell-gaa-club-victory-dinner/|title=Patrickswell GAA Club Victory Dinner|date=11 February 2017|publisher=Limerick Post|accessdate=11 February 2017|first=|last=}} He won six SHC titles in total, with further victories in 1969, 1970, 1977, 1979. At inter-county level, Bennis first played for the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] in 1964. He later served as [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|team captain]] on three separate occasions.{{cite web|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/granagh-ballingarry-gaa-club-notes-25/|title=List of captains|publisher=Limerick GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Bennis was part of the Limerick team that beat [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] by a point to win the [[National Hurling League]] title in 1971. He later won consecutive [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals and was at right wing-back for Limerick's 1-21 to 1-14 win over [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1973 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/bennis-recalls-the-heroes-of-73-231789.html|title=Bennis recalls the heroes of ’73|date=20 May 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=26 December 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} ==Managerial career== Bennis has been involved in the majority of Patrickswell's Limerick SHC title victories, either as a player or manager or both. He guided the club to nine such triumphs between 1982 and 1997. Bennis's other club honours as manager include two [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] title, while he also managed the team when losing to [[Glenmore GAA|Glenmore]] in the [[1991 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1991 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA He plays [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]] with his local club [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret/St Paul's]] and was a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team in both codes from 2001 until 2007.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=41035|title=Begley, Brian}}{{cite web|url=http://www.waterford-today.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=966&Itemid=10167&ed=76|title=All over for another year |accessdate=2009-03-04}} ==Playing career== ===Club=== Begley plays his club [[hurling]] with his local [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret/St Paul's]] club. ===Inter-county=== Begley first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the Limerick under-21 team. He won a Munster title at this level in 2000 before later collecting an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]] medal following a victory over [[Galway GAA|Galway]]. It was Limerick's first step towards three such titles in-a-row; however, Begley was over-age for the latter two victories. By this stage, he had joined the county senior team. Following the county's victory over [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] in 2001, Limerick failed to win a game in the province until their 2007 Munster SHC semi-final victory over [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]]. This was achieved following a three-game saga;{{what?|reason=What saga? Is the reader just supposed to know?|date=October 2022}} however, Begley's side later lost the Munster SHC final to [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]]. Limerick beat Waterford in the subsequent All-Ireland SHC semi-final, setting up an All-Ireland SHC final meeting with [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] on 2 September 2007. While Begley scored a goal and won a penalty, his side lost by seven points to Kilkenny, on a scoreline of 2–19 to 1–15. ==Football== Begley won a [[Munster Under-21 Football Championship]] with Limerick in 2000, and played in the [[All-Ireland Under 21 Football Championship|All-Ireland U21FC]] final. but the team lost to [[Tyrone GAA|Tyrone]]. With the Limerick senior team he played in two [[Munster Senior Football Championship]] in 2003 and 2004 but lost both times to [[Kerry county football team|Kerry]] in 2004 only after a replay. ==Personal life== His cousin [[Cian Begley|Cian]] won the [[2005–06 All-Ireland Senior Club Football Championship]] title with [[Salthill-Knocknacarra GAA|Salthill-Knocknacarra]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10044674.html|title=Sheridan aiming to put Salthill on the map|work=Irish Examiner|first=Jim|last=O'Sullivan|date=18 February 2006}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Limerick panels |bg=green |fg=white |list1= {{Limerick Under 21 Football Team 2000}} {{Limerick Under 21 Team 2000}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 2006}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 2007}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Begley, Brian}} [[Category:1979 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[category:Dual players]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:Mungret hurlers]] [[Category:Mungret Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]] {{Limerick-hurling-bio-stub}}

'''Patrick Clohessy''' (16 April 1908 – 6 August 1971) was an Irish sportsperson and politician. He played [[hurling]] for his local club [[Fedamore GAA|Fedamore]] and at senior level for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]] from 1928 until 1940. He later became a [[Fianna Fáil]] politician.

==Playing career==
===Club===
Clohessy played club [[hurling]] with his local club in Fedamore. His brothers, [[Dave Clohessy|Dave]], Andy and Jack, also played for Fedamore.<ref name="LL">{{cite web |date=11 November 1986 |title=Crowds at funeral of Dave Clohessy |url=http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/sports%20people%20009.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722045844/http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/sports%20people%20009.pdf |archive-date=2011-07-22 |access-date=8 March 2016 |work=Limerick Leader}}</ref> He won his sole senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county title]] with the club in 1927.

===Inter-county===
Clohessy first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior hurling team in 1928. At that stage Limerick were down the pecking order in terms of the top teams in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].

All this changed in 1933 when Limerick defeated the reigning provincial champions of [[Clare GAA|Clare]], giving Clohessy his first Munster title. The subsequent All-Ireland final pitted Limerick against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] – the winners of the championship in 1932. The game was a low-scoring affair with Kilkenny claiming the title on a score line of 1–7 to 0–6.

In 1934 Limerick began their fight back with Clohessy added a second Munster medal to his collection as the team beat [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]. In their second consecutive All-Ireland final appearance Limerick faced [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]. Dublin proved to be no pushover as the game ended in a draw on a score line of 2–7 to 3–4. The replay saw Limerick capture the title by five points giving Clohessy his first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal.

1935 saw Limerick capture Clohessy win his first [[National Hurling League]] title, however, he later missed out on a third Munster title due to injury. Clohessy was back for the All-Ireland final as Limerick took on Kilkenny once again. Limerick had a run of 31 unbeaten games; however, Kilkenny put an end to this by defeating Clohessy's team by just a single point.

In 1936 Clohessy added a second National League medal to his collection before collecting a third Munster medal. For the third time in four years Kilkenny provided the opposition in the subsequent All-Ireland final.  Limerick, however, had the measure of them on the day and claimed victory on a score line of 5–6 to 1–5. It was Clohessy's second All-Ireland medal.

In 1937 Clohessy captured a fourth consecutive National League medal; however, Limerick later lost their provincial title for the first time since 1932. Three years later in 1940 Limerick regained their Munster title after an epic battle with [[Cork GAA|Cork]] giving Clohessy his fourth provincial title. In the subsequent All-Ireland final the two outstanding teams of the decade, Kilkenny and Limerick, did battle once again. Kilkenny were not the force of old as a third All-Ireland medal went to Clohessy following a 3–7 to 1–7 victory. It was Clohessy's last major title with the Limerick inter-county hurlers as he retired from inter-county hurling following the victory.

===Provincial===
Clohessy also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial hurling competition. He first played for his province in 1932, however, on that occasion his side was defeated by [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]].  Clohessy remained on the team and helped Munster to capture the [[GAA Interprovincial Championship|Railway Cup]] title in 1934. He won a further four title sin-a-row in 1937, 1938, 1939 and 1940.

==Political career==
A farmer by profession, he contested the [[1954 Irish general election|1954 general election]] in the [[Limerick East (Dáil constituency)|Limerick East]] constituency but was not elected.<ref name=elecs_irl>{{cite web|url=http://electionsireland.org/candidate.cfm?ID=2514|title=Patrick Clohessy|work=ElectionsIreland.org|access-date=13 December 2008}}</ref> He was elected to [[Dáil Éireann]] as a [[Fianna Fáil]] [[Teachta Dála]] (TD) at the subsequent [[1957 Irish general election|1957 general election]] and held his seat until retiring at the [[1969 Irish general election|1969 general election]].<ref name=oireachtas_db>{{cite web|url=https://www.oireachtas.ie/en/members/member/Patrick-Clohessy.D.1957-03-20/|title=Patrick Clohessy|work=Oireachtas Members Database|access-date=13 December 2008}}</ref>

His nephew [[Peadar Clohessy]] was a Fianna Fáil and [[Progressive Democrats]] TD for Limerick East in the 1980s and 1990s.

'''George Clancy''' is an [[Irish Rugby Football Union|Irish]] [[rugby union referee]]. Clancy refereed at the [[2011 Rugby World Cup|2011]] and [[2015 Rugby World Cup]]s. He has also refereed in the [[Pro14]], the [[European Rugby Champions Cup]], the [[Six Nations Championship]] and the [[The Rugby Championship|Rugby Championship]]. Clancy refereed the [[2007 Churchill Cup]] final and the [[2008–09 European Challenge Cup|2009]] and [[2010–11 European Challenge Cup|2011 European Challenge Cup]] finals. Between [[2013 Heineken Cup Final|2013]] and [[2017 European Rugby Champions Cup Final|2017]] Clancy also served as a touch judge/assistant referee at five consecutive [[List of European Rugby Champions Cup finals|European Rugby Champions Cup finals]].

==Early life==
George Clancy is the son of Seoirse and Helen Clancy.<ref name="examiner100911">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/ireland/limerick-mum-celebrates-son-refereeing-opening-match-167038.html|title=Limerick mum celebrates son refereeing opening match|publisher=www.irishexaminer.com|access-date=23 January 2018|date=10 September 2011}}</ref> He was raised in [[Bruff]] and he is the great grandnephew of [[George Clancy (politician)|George Clancy]], a former [[Mayor of Limerick]] killed during the [[Irish War of Independence]].<ref name="limerickleader161015">{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/news/118095/Limerick-s-George-chats-rugby-with.html|title=Limerick's George chats rugby with the Queen|publisher=www.limerickleader.ie|access-date=25 January 2018|date=16 October 2015}}</ref><ref name="independent180616">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/i-wouldnt-serve-that-guy-again-bruff-locals-react-to-footballers-comments-about-weird-limerick-village-34812088.html|title='I wouldn't serve that guy again' - Bruff locals react to footballer's comments about 'weird' Limerick village|publisher=www.independent.ie|access-date=25 January 2018|date=18 June 2016}}</ref> Clancy was educated at [[St Munchin's College]], where his fellow pupils included [[Marcus Horan]] and [[Jerry Flannery]]. He played [[rugby union]] for both St Munchin's and [[Bruff R.F.C.]]<ref name="stmunchins">{{cite web|url=http://www.stmunchinscollege.com/about-smc/past-pupils/|title=St Munchin's College Past Pupils|publisher=www.stmunchinscollege.com|access-date=20 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="irishrugby090911">{{cite web|url=http://www.irishrugby.ie/mobile/news/6851.php|title=Clancy: Refereeing First Game Is A Huge Honour|publisher=www.irishrugby.ie|access-date=27 January 2018|date=9 September 2011}}</ref><ref name="pro14rugby141217">{{cite web|url=https://www.pro14rugby.org/2017/12/14/getting-know-george-clancy/|title=Getting to know: George Clancy|publisher=www.pro14rugby.org|access-date=23 January 2018|date=14 December 2017}}</ref><ref name="pro14rugby191217">{{cite web|url=https://www.pro14rugby.org/2017/12/19/george-clancy-qa/|title=George Clancy Q&A|publisher=www.pro14rugby.org|access-date=25 January 2018|date=19 December 2017}}</ref><ref name="examiner230509">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/rugby/clancys-big-challenge-92389.html|title=Clancy's Big Challenge|publisher=www.irishexaminer.com|access-date=30 January 2018|date=23 May 2009}}</ref> He also played both [[gaelic football]] and [[hurling]] for [[Bruff GAA]]. Clancy also represented [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] at hurling. Clancy only gave up playing hurling when he was offered an IRFU refereeing contract which prohibited him playing sports that might result in an injury. He remains a hurling fan and he was attending a match between Bruff GAA and [[Ballybrown GAA]] when he received a phone call from [[Paddy O'Brien (rugby union)|Paddy O'Brien]] inviting him to referee the opening match of the [[2011 Rugby World Cup]].<ref name="examiner100911"/><ref name="pro14rugby141217"/><ref name="pro14rugby191217"/><ref name="examiner230509"/><ref name="hoganstand">{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/154657|title=Rugby World Cup ref told of appointment at hurling game|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|access-date=27 January 2018|date=7 September 2011}}</ref> Clancy has a master's degree in international relations and worked as a tax official with the [[Revenue Commissioners]] before becoming a full-time referee.<ref name="pro14rugby141217"/> As of 2015, Clancy had been living with [[Diabetes mellitus type 1|type 1 diabetes]] for over twenty years.<ref name="diabetes">{{cite web|url=https://www.diabetes.ie/event/an-evening-with-george-clancy/|title=Limerick: An evening with George Clancy|publisher=www.diabetes.ie|access-date=30 January 2018|date=9 November 2015}}</ref>

==Refereeing career==
===Early years===
Clancy was encouraged to become a [[rugby union referee]] by his father. Seoirse Clancy was involved with [[Bruff R.F.C.]] and had refereed at a local level. He encouraged his son to take up refereeing after injuries, including a broken leg, prevented him from playing [[rugby union]] at a top level.<ref name="examiner100911"/><ref name="pro14rugby141217"/><ref name="pro14rugby191217"/> In October 2000 Clancy refereed his first match, an U15s league match between Richmond and [[Garryowen Football Club|Garryowen]] which ended in a 0–0 draw.<ref name="irishrugby090911"/><ref name="pro14rugby3">{{cite web|url=https://www.pro14rugby.org/referee/george-clancy/|title=Referee: George Clancy|publisher=www.pro14rugby.org|access-date=27 January 2018|date=14 December 2017}}</ref> He subsequently began refereeing games in the [[All-Ireland League (rugby union)|All-Ireland League]]<ref name="examiner230509"/> before making his [[2004–05 Celtic League|Celtic League]] debut on 15 October 2004 when he took charge of a match between [[Border Reivers (rugby union)|Borders]] and [[Dragons (rugby union)|Gwent Dragons]].<ref name="pro14rugby141217"/><ref name="pro14rugby191217"/><ref name="pro14rugby3"/><ref name="examiner240514">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/rugby/clancys-rise-through-ranks-leads-him-to-biggest-stage-of-all-269781.html|title=Clancy's rise through ranks leads him to biggest stage of all|publisher=www.irishexaminer.com|access-date=27 January 2018|date=24 May 2014}}</ref><ref name="rugbyreferee231017">{{cite web|url=http://rugbyreferee.net/2017/10/23/seven-irish-referees-rewarded-with-professional-contracts/|title=Seven Irish referees awarded with professional contracts|publisher=rugbyreferee.net|access-date=21 December 2017|date=23 October 2017}}</ref>

===European competitions===
On 15 January 2005 Clancy made his [[Heineken Cup]] debut when he took charge of a [[2004–05 Heineken Cup pool stage|2004–05 pool stage]] match between [[CS Bourgoin-Jallieu|Bourgoin]] and [[Bath Rugby|Bath]]. He was originally supposed to be the touch judge for this match but after the original referee went sick, Clancy was called upon to replace him.<ref name="examiner240514"/><ref name="rugbyreferee231017"/>  
On 22 May 2009 Clancy refereed the [[2008–09 European Challenge Cup]] final between [[Northampton Saints]] and Bourgoin.<ref name="examiner230509"/><ref name="breakingnews">{{cite web|url=https://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/rugby/george-clancy-to-referee-challenge-cup-final-410451.html|title=George Clancy to referee Challenge Cup final|publisher=www.breakingnews.ie|access-date=30 January 2018|date=12 May 2009}}</ref> He also refereed the [[2010–11 European Challenge Cup]] final between [[Harlequin F.C.|Harlequins]] and [[Stade Français]].<ref name="irishrugby090511">{{cite web|url=http://www.irishrugby.ie/mobile/news/14439.php|title=Clancy And Poite To Referee European Finals|publisher=www.irishrugby.ie|access-date=31 January 2018|date=9 May 2011}}</ref><ref name="guardian210511">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2011/may/20/euorpean-challlenge-cup-harlequins-stade-francais|title=Late converted try edges Harlequins to victory over Stade Français|publisher=www.theguardian.com|access-date=31 January 2018|date=21 May 2011}}</ref>
Between [[2013 Heineken Cup Final|2013]] and [[2017 European Rugby Champions Cup Final|2017]] Clancy also served as a touch judge/assistant referee at five consecutive [[List of European Rugby Champions Cup finals|European Rugby Champions Cup finals]].<ref name="independent120517">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/rugby/munster-rugby/referees-are-honoured-to-officiate-at-euro-finals-35705448.html|title=Referees are honoured to officiate at Euro finals|publisher=www.independent.ie|access-date=30 January 2018|date=12 May 2017}}</ref>

===Early internationals===
Clancy refereed at the [[2004 FIRA Women's European Championship]] and at the [[2005 Under 21 Rugby World Championship|2005]] and [[2006 Under 21 Rugby World Championship]]s. He made his senior international debut on 30 September 2006 when he took charge of a [[2007 Rugby World Cup – Americas qualification|2007 Rugby World Cup qualifier]] between [[Uruguay national rugby union team|Uruguay]] and the [[United States national rugby union team|United States]]. He also refereed the [[2007 Churchill Cup]] final.<ref name="examiner230509"/><ref name="rugbyreferee231017"/><ref name="espn011006">{{cite web|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/scrum/rugby/story/65857.html|title=USA down Los Teros in RWC qualifier|publisher=en.espn.co.uk|access-date=27 January 2018|date=1 October 2006}}</ref> In [[2008 mid-year rugby union internationals|2008]] Clancy refereed his first top level internationals. On 1 June he took charge of a match between [[England national rugby union team|England]] and the [[Barbarian F.C.|Barbarians]] and on 21 June he refereed a match between [[South Africa national rugby union team|South Africa]] and [[Italy national rugby union team|Italy]].<ref name="irishrugby090911"/><ref name="pro14rugby3"/><ref name="espn2">{{cite web|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/ireland/rugby/player/15374.html|title=George Clancy Ireland Profile|publisher=en.espn.co.uk|access-date=28 January 2018}}</ref> Clancy made his [[Six Nations Championship]] debut on 14 February [[2009 Six Nations Championship|2009]] when he took charge of a match between [[France national rugby union team|France]] and the [[Scotland national rugby union team|Scotland]].<ref name="espn2"/><ref name="espn140209">{{cite web|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/sixnations/rugby/story/91768.html|title=Scotland undone by officiating error|publisher=en.espn.co.uk|access-date=28 January 2018|date=14 February 2009}}</ref> Clancy made his [[The Rugby Championship|Rugby Championship]] debut on 24 July [[2010 Tri Nations Series|2010]] when he took charge of a match between [[Australia national rugby union team|Australia]] and South Africa.<ref name="munsterrugby090710">{{cite web|url=https://munsterrugby.ie/domestic_news/clancy-to-referee-in-tri-nations/|title=Clancy to Referee in Tri Nations|publisher=munsterrugby.ie|access-date=28 January 2018|date=9 July 2010}}</ref>

===Rugby World Cup===
Clancy refereed the opening game of the [[2011 Rugby World Cup]], a [[2011 Rugby World Cup Pool A|pool stage game]] between [[New Zealand national rugby union team|New Zealand]] and [[Tonga national rugby union team|Tonga]].<ref name="examiner100911"/><ref name="irishrugby090911"/><ref name="hoganstand"/> Clancy subsequently refereed three more pool stage matches during the tournament.<ref name="eurosport">{{cite web|url=https://au.eurosport.com/rugby/world-cup/2011/referee-george-clancy_sto2939716/story.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180201075350/https://au.eurosport.com/rugby/world-cup/2011/referee-george-clancy_sto2939716/story.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 February 2018|title=Referee: George Clancy|publisher=au.eurosport.com|access-date=30 January 2018|date=7 September 2011}}</ref>
Clancy was also selected to referee at the [[2015 Rugby World Cup]].<ref name="irishtimes080415">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/rugby/pro12/rugby-world-cup-george-clancy-and-john-lacey-on-referee-panel-1.2167921|title=Rugby World Cup: George Clancy and John Lacey on referee panel|publisher=www.irishtimes.com|access-date=30 January 2018|date=8 April 2015}}</ref> Clancy refereed three pool stage matches at the 2015 tournament.

===Controversies and incidents===
During his refereeing career Clancy has been involved in several controversies and incidents. On his [[Six Nations Championship]] debut on 14 February [[2009 Six Nations Championship|2009]], Clancy awarded a try to [[France national rugby union team|France]]'s [[Fulgence Ouedraogo]] against [[Scotland national rugby union team|Scotland]]. Replays showed the final pass from  [[Maxime Médard]] was forward. However, Clancy had been knocked to the ground in the move building up to the score. He consulted with his assistant before confirming the try.<ref name="espn140209"/><ref name="eurosport"/>

On 5 December 2009, after refereeing an [[All-Ireland League (rugby union)|All-Ireland League]] match between [[Shannon RFC|Shannon]] and [[Cork Constitution]], Clancy was verbally abused by Shannon supporters and club officials. Among the alleged abusers was [[Gerry McLoughlin]]. After the match had finished Martin Clancy, the Shannon president, entered the referees dressing room and continued to verbally abuse the referee. He was eventually removed by the two touch judges. Shannon were subsequently fined €25,000.<ref name="irishtimes011410">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/shannon-fined-25-000-for-abuse-of-referee-1.1268364|title=Shannon fined €25,000 for abuse of referee|publisher=www.irishtimes.com|access-date=25 January 2018|date=14 January 2010}}</ref>

On 13 February [[2010 Six Nations Championship|2010]] during a match between [[Wales national rugby union team|Wales]] and Scotland, Clancy sin-binned Scotland's [[Phil Godman]] for an alleged off-the-ball trip on [[Lee Byrne]]. Byrne was later accused of deliberately diving to help Wales win.<ref name="eurosport"/><ref name="guardian150210">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2010/feb/15/lee-byrne-wales-six-nations|title=Wales' Lee Byrne claims he was tripped by Phil Godman of Scotland|publisher=www.theguardian.com|access-date=30 January 2018|date=15 February 2010}}</ref><ref name="telegraph150210">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/rugbyunion/international/scotland/7241518/Six-Nations-2010-Lee-Byrne-dived-to-help-Wales-win-says-Scotlands-Phil-Godman.html|title=Six Nations 2010: Lee Byrne dived to help Wales win, says Scotland's Phil Godman|publisher=www.telegraph.co.uk|access-date=30 January 2018|date=15 February 2010}}</ref>

On 10 April 2010, during a [[2009–10 Heineken Cup]] quarter-final, between [[Biarritz Olympique|Biarritz]] and [[Ospreys (rugby union)|Ospreys]], Clancy refused to award Ospreys a penalty towards the end of the match after an alleged knock-on by Biarritz's scrum-half, [[Dimitri Yachvili]]. The decision denied Ospreys a potential victory.<ref name="espn2"/><ref name="eurosport"/><ref name="independent100410">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/rugby/rugby-union/club-rugby/ospreys-fume-as-clancy-lets-biarritz-off-hook-1941327.html|title=Ospreys fume as Clancy lets Biarritz off hook|publisher=www.independent.co.uk|access-date=30 January 2018|date=10 April 2010}}</ref>

On 6 September [[2014 Rugby Championship|2014]] Clancy refereed a match between [[Australia national rugby union team|Australia]] and [[South Africa national rugby union team|South Africa]]. Clancy yellow carded South Africa's [[Bryan Habana]] for a high tackle on [[Adam Ashley-Cooper]] in the 65th minute. According to Paul Cully of ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]''
the decision was incorrect and was "the defining moment" of the match, costing South Africa a potential victory.<ref name="independent080914">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/rugby/international-rugby/irish-referee-george-clancy-slammed-for-decisions-in-australia-v-south-africa-game-30570038.html|title=Irish referee George Clancy slammed for decisions in Australia v South Africa game|publisher=www.independent.ie|access-date=28 January 2018|date=8 September 2014}}</ref><ref name="smh070914">{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/rugby-union/too-many-tests-decided-by-referees-blunders-20140907-10died.html|title=Too many Tests decided by referees' blunders|publisher=www.smh.com.au|access-date=30 January 2018|date=7 September 2014}}</ref>

On 16 September 2017 Clancy was serving as a touch judge during a [[2017–18 Pro14]] match between [[Cardiff Blues]] and [[Glasgow Warriors]]. A disgruntled Cardiff Blues fan threw his pint of beer at Clancy because he allegedly was unhappy with a decision made by the officials.  The act was caught on camera and the fan was quickly escorted from the ground.<ref name="sportinglimerick">{{cite web|url=http://sportinglimerick.com/watch-limerick-ref-george-clancy/|title=Limerick ref George Clancy has pint thrown at him by idiot fan ...|publisher=sportinglimerick.com|access-date=30 January 2018|date=18 September 2017}}</ref><ref name="walesonline">{{cite web|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/rugby/cardiff-blues-launch-search-mystery-13638239|title=The identity of the Cardiff Blues beer-thrower is a mystery as search is launched following shock incident|publisher=www.walesonline.co.uk|access-date=30 January 2018|date=18 September 2017}}</ref>

'''Paul Browne''' (born 21 September 1989) is an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Premier Intermediate Championship]] club [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]]. He played for the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] for 11 seasons, during which time he usually lined out at midfield.

Browne lined out for Limerick in three different grades of hurling over a 12-year period. After making his first appearance for the minor team in June 2007, he later had an unsuccessful three-year stint with the under-21 team. Browne made his competitive debut for the senior team aged 19 in [[2009 National Hurling League|2009]]. From his debut, he was ever-present as a midfielder and made a combined total of 91 [[National Hurling League|National League]] and Championship appearances in a career that ended with his last game in [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2018]]. During that time, Browne was vice-captain of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]]-winning team in [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2018]]. He also secured two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medals and a [[National Hurling League#Division 2|National League Division 2]] medal. Browne announced his retirement from inter-county hurling on 21 November 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/496017/limerick-hurler-paul-browne-confirms-his-inter-county-retirement-after-11-years.html|title=Limerick hurler Paul Browne confirms his inter-county retirement after 11 years|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 November 2019|accessdate=23 November 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Limerick Institute of Technology===

During his studies at the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]], Browne was selected for the college's senior hurling team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].

===Bruff===

Browne joined the [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's top adult team. On 25 October 2014, he won a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Premier Intermediate Championship]] medal following a 2–14 to 0–16 defeat of [[Croom GAA|Croom]] in the final.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Browne first played for the Limerick minor hurling team at the age of seventeen. He made his only appearance in that grade on 23 June 2007 in a 3–21 to 0-12 [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/match-reports/maher-fires-tipperary-to-final-as-limerick-routed-35784.html|title=Maher fires Tipperary to final as Limerick routed|date=25 June 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 5 June 2008, Browne made his first appearance for the Limerick under-21 hurling team, lining out at left corner-back in Limerick's 2–17 to 1–07 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/limerick-add-to-waterford-s-woes-1.1217210|title=Limerick add to Waterford's woes|date=6 June 2008|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> His three seasons in the under-21 grade ended with early championship defeats.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/ryan-s-3-9-gives-clare-timely-lift-1.700796|title=Ryan's 3-9 gives Clare timely lift|date=16 July 2009|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/oconnor-inspires-banner-in-thriller-125175.html|title=O'Connor inspires Banner in thriller|date=15 July 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

====Senior====

On 8 February 2009, Browne made his senior debut at midfield in a 3–13 to 1–18 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[National Hurling League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/mccarthys-limerick-scrape-past-clare-398187.html|title=McCarthy's Limerick scrape past Clare|date=8 February 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> Later that season he made his first championship appearance in a 1–08 to 0–11 draw with Waterford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/semple-snore-draw-simply-awful-94125.html|title=Semple snore draw simply awful|date=15 June 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

On 30 April 2011, Browne won a National League Division 2 medal after a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of Clare in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}}</ref>

On 14 July 2013, Browne scored a point from midfield in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Browne was named vice-captain of the Limerick senior team for the 2018 season. In June 2018, he sustained a cruciate knee injury which ruled him out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/paul-browne-cruciate-4101715-Jun2018/|title=Cruciate injury rules Limerick midfielder out for the rest of the season|date=30 June 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Paul|last=Dollery}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, Browne was a member of the extended panel when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> Prior to the game he was invited to line-up alongside the team for the pre-match photograph.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.sportsjoe.ie/gaa/paul-browne-limerick-team-photo-173627|title =Limerick's gesture to injured Paul Browne did not go unnoticed|date=21 August 2018|publisher=Sportsjoe|accessdate=21 August 2018}}</ref>

In December 2018, Browne was included on the Limerick panel for the upcoming season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/352321/42-man-limerick-hurling-panel-for-2019-includes-seven-newcomers.html|title=42-man Limerick hurling panel for 2019 includes seven newcomers|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 December 2018|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> His ongoing cruciate injury ruled him out of the [[2019 National Hurling League|National League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/370994/limerick-with-pretty-full-compliment-to-select-from-as-casey-and-o-donoghue-return.html|title=Limerick with 'pretty full {{sic|compli|ment|nolink=y}} to select from' as Casey and O'Donoghue return|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 March 2019|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, he won a second Munster Championship medal as a member of the extended panel after Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> Browne announced his retirement from inter-county hurling on 21 November 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/306111|title=Browne retires from Limerick duty|date=21 November 2019|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=23 November 2019|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/paul-browne-retires-limerick-4901744-Nov2019/|title ='The time is right for me to step away' - Limerick All-Ireland winner retires after 11 years|date=25 November 2019|work=The 42|accessdate=26 November 2019}}</ref>

===Munster===

On 9 February 2014, Browne was a substitute on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team that was defeated by [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] in the semi-final of the [[Railway Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/munster-reign-ended-by-tribesmen-in-disguise-258246.html|title =Munster reign ended by Tribesmen in disguise|date=10 February 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>
