[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Dave Clarke''' (born 1972) is an Irish [[hurling]] coach and former player. At club level, he played with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Playing career== Clarke attended [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]] and played hurling at all grades during his time there, including in the [[Dr Harty Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick CBS advance in style in 'Harty'|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=6 October 1990|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At club level, Clarke first played for [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] at juvenile and underage levels, and was part of the club's minor team that won the Limerick MAHC title in 1987.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Kilmallock abú!|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=19 September 1987|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to adult level and won [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medals in 1992 and 1994.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/128541/1992--When-Kilmallock-conquered-Limerick.html|title=1992: When Kilmallock conquered Limerick and Munster|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=20 November 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Both of these titles were subsequently followed by [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] titles.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Clarke also lined out in Kilmallock's 1-17 to 2-07 defeat by [[Sarsfields GAA (Galway)|Sarsfields]] in the [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1993 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-ireland-club-hurling/26713575.html|title=All-Ireland Club Hurling|publisher=Irish Independent|date=15 March 2011|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Clarke first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 1989 and 1990.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Clare clear in the end|publisher=Irish Press|date=5 July 1990|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He immediately progressed to the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick tops in under 21 thriller|publisher=Irish Independent|date=1 August 1991|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Clarke joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] on a permanent basis in 1993, however, he had already lined out with the team in a tournament game in 1990. He won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals in 1994 and 1996, however, Limerick faced subsequent All-Ireland final defeats by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] respectively.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40370429.html|title=A player-by-player guide to Wexford's All-Ireland 25 years on: 'We laughed as much as we hurled'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=1 September 2021|access-date=2 January 2025|first=|last=}} Clarke also collected an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] in 1994.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/the-whelahan-snub-the-red-card-rule-and-a-power-grab-gone-wrong-the-five-biggest-all-stars-controversies/40025112.html|title=The Whelahan snub, the red card rule and a power grab gone wrong - the five biggest All-Stars controversies|publisher=Irish Independent|date=29 January 2021|access-date=2 January 2025|first=|last=}} He added a [[National Hurling League]] medal to his collection in 1997.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/945696/limerick-county-final-day-to-honour-25th-anniversary-of-1997-hurling-league-title-victory.html|title=Limerick county final day to honour 25th anniversary of 1997 hurling league title victory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 October 2022|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Clarke being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won [[Railway Cup]] medals in 1995 and 1997.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Management career== Even during his playing days, Clarke became involved in team management and coaching. He had title successes in various grades with [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]], [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]], Kilmallock and [[Pallasgreen GAA|Pallasgreen]], while also serving as coach of the [[University of Limerick]] team in the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Coach Clarke making his amrk|publisher=Evening Echo|date=18 December 2002|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Clarke also served as trainer with Limerick's under-21 team in 2003.{{cite '''David Breen''' (born 20 September 1985) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] physiotherapist and [[hurling|hurler]] who played centre-forward and was the captain of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=160533|title=Breen to captain Limerick hurlers|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=18 January 2011|accessdate=19 January 2011}}</ref>

Breen made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2009|2009 championship]] and has become a regular member of the starting fifteen over the last few{{when|date=June 2021}} seasons. Since then he has won one [[National Hurling League|National Hurling League (Division 2)]] winners' medal.

At club level, Breen has won both [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster]] and [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] winners' medals with [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].

==Playing career==
===Club===

Breen plays his club hurling with the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club in Limerick. After developing his hurling at juvenile levels he later came to prominence as a member of the club's minor hurling team.  He enjoyed little success in this grade, however, he later joined the Na Piarsaigh under-21 team. He won a county under-21 championship title in this grade in 2004 following a defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]].

By this stage Breen had joined the club's senior hurling team. He won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]] winners' medal in 2011 following a 2–18 to 0–13 defeat of [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]]. It was Na Piarsaigh's first ever championship title. Breen later won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster]] club winners' medal following a 1–13 to 0–9 victory over [[Crusheen GAA|Crusheen]] in a replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Clare/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=158799|title=Munster club SHC final replay: Historic first for Na Piarsaigh|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=4 December 2010|accessdate=4 December 2011}}</ref>

He retired from hurling in 2015.<ref name="post">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishpost.com/sport/former-limerick-hurler-breen-joins-liverpool-as-physio-281010|title=Former Limerick hurler Breen joins Liverpool as physio|last1=O'Donoghue|first1=Conor|date=16 November 2024|access-date=3 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241129103606/https://www.irishpost.com/sport/former-limerick-hurler-breen-joins-liverpool-as-physio-281010|archive-date=29 November 2024|website=[[Irish Post]]}}</ref><ref name="examiner">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-41515502.html|title=Ex-Limerick hurler appointed by Liverpool to lead physio role|last1=Fogarty|first1=John|date=12 November 2024|access-date=3 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241125050243/https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-41515502.html|archive-date=25 November 2024|website=[[Irish Examiner]]}}</ref>

==Physiotherapy career==
In November 2024, Breen joined [[Liverpool Football Club]] in the position of first-team rehabilitation physiotherapist.<ref name ="Durkan">{{cite web|website=This is Anfield|date=13 November 2024|last1=Durkan|first1=Joanna|title=Liverpool appoint new physio with Man City experience to Arne Slot's backroom|url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2024/11/liverpool-appoint-new-physio-with-man-city-experience-to-arne-slots-backroom/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241113205331/https://www.thisisanfield.com/2024/11/liverpool-appoint-new-physio-with-man-city-experience-to-arne-slots-backroom/|archive-date=13 November 2024|access-date=3 December 2024}}</ref>

He had previously been physiotherapist with [[Munster Rugby]] between 2021 and 2023, also working with rugby clubs [[Wasps RFC|Wasps]], [[Leinster Rugby|Leinster]] and [[Harlequin F.C.|Harlequins]], and as physio with football teams including the [[Republic of Ireland national football team]] and the academy sides of [[Celtic F.C. B Team and Academy|Celtic F.C.]] and [[Manchester City F.C. EDS and Academy|Manchester City]].<ref name="post" /><ref name="examiner" /><ref name="Durkan" />

==Honours==

'''Thomas Francis Cooke''' (16 August 1914 – 13 February 2014<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/tributes-paid-to-legendary-limerick-hurler-1-5876157|title=Tributes paid to legendary Limerick hurler|date=14 January 2014|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=15 February 2014|first=Áine|last=Fitzgerald}}</ref>) was an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]] and [[Gaelic football]]er who played as a left wing-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Born in [[Knockainey]], [[County Limerick]], Cooke first played competitive hurling whilst at school in [[Warrenstown College]]. He made his first impression on the inter-county scene at the age of twenty-four when he joined the Limerick junior teams as a [[dual player]]. He made his senior debut during the [[Oireachtas Tournament|1939 Oireachtas Cup]]. Cooke went on to play a key role for Limerick for a short period, and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal and one [[Oireachtas Tournament|Oireachtas Cup]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=Hurling and football roll of honour|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=26 April 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archive-date=25 May 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=26 April 2012}}</ref>

At club level Cooke played both hurling and football with a number of local clubs including [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]], [[Knockane GAA|Knockane]] and [[Bulgaden GAA|Bulgaden]].

==Playing career==

===Club===

Cooke was instrumental in the foundation of the [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]] club. He was appointed as the club's first treasurer in 1936.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.knockaineygaa.ie/history.htm|title=Club history|publisher=Knockainey GAA website|access-date=24 February 2013}}</ref>

Five years later in 1941 Cooke was captain of the team when Knockainey won the south junior hurling championship. It was the first silverware for the new club.

===Inter-county===

Cooke first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a [[dual player]] in the junior grades in 1939. With the Limerick junior hurling team Cooke's side were defeated by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] on a score line of 4–2 to 2–4. An objection that was later upheld resulted in Limerick eventually being awarded the title and Cooke collecting a [[Munster Junior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/jh_teams/|title=Junior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=24 February 2013}}</ref> That same year he won a [[Munster Junior Football Championship|Munster]] medal in football as Limerick defeated [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] by 1–7 to 1–2.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/jf_teams/|title=Junior Football|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=24 February 2013}}</ref> Both Limerick teams were subsequently beaten in the All-Ireland semi-final stages.

By 1940 Cooke had joined the Limerick senior hurling team and lined out in his first provincial decider in the top grade. [[Cork GAA|Cokr]], the reigning champions, provided the opposition, however, the match ended in a draw. The replay was also a close affair, however, a 3–3 to 2–4 score line gave Limerick the win and gave Cooke a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal. A subsequent defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] set up an All-Ireland showdown with [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. 50,0000 spectators travelled to [[Croke Park]] to witness the last great game between the two most outstanding teams of the decade. Early in the second-half Kilkenny took a four-point lead, however, once [[Mick Mackey]] was deployed at midfield he proceeded to dominate the game. Limerick hung on to win the game on a score line of 3–7 to 1–7 and Cooke collected an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal.

Cooke continued with Limerick for another few seasons, however, Cork went on to dominate the championship for the rest of the forties.

==Personal life==

Born in Bottomstown, Knockainey, [[County Limerick]], Cooke was born into a farming family. He was educated at Bulgaden national school before later boarding for a year at [[Rockwell College]]. After an unhappy time here, Cooke subsequently attended [[Warrenstown College|Warrenstown Agricultural College]]. On returning to Knockainey he became active in farming circles, and was a founder-member of the Golden Vale Marts Group. Cooke was married to Nan, the local national school teacher at Bottomstown, and the couple had three children.

Cooke died aged 99 at St. Michael's nursing home in [[Caherconlish]] on 13 February 2014. At the time of his death he was the oldest living senior All-Ireland medal winner, a mantle he had held since the death of [[Martin White (hurler)|Martin White]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/oldest-all-ireland-medal-holder-launches-community-magazine-1-3396278|title=Oldest All-Ireland medal holder launches community magazine|date=6 January 2012|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=24 February 2013|first=Áine|last=Fitzgerald}}</ref>

'''David Stanislaus Clohessy''' (13 November 1905 – 16 November 1986) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played for his local club [[Fedamore GAA|Fedamore]] and at senior level for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]] in the 1920s and 1930s. In the 1934 All-Ireland final replay, he scored four goals against Dublin, a record that lasted beyond his death.<ref name=LL>{{cite web|url= http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/sports%20people%20009.pdf|title=Crowds at funeral of Dave Clohessy|work=Limerick Leader|date=11 November 1986|accessdate=8 March 2016}}</ref>

His brothers, Paddy, Andy and Jack, who predeceased him, also played for Fedamore.<ref name=LL/> [[Paddy Clohessy]] later entered politics and was elected to [[Dáil Éireann]] as a [[Fianna Fáil]] [[Teachta Dála]] (TD) at the [[1957 Irish general election|1957 general election]] and held his seat until standing down at the [[1969 Irish general election|1969 general election]].<ref name=oireachtas_db>{{cite web|url=http://oireachtas.ie/members-hist/default.asp?housetype=0&HouseNum=18&MemberID=181&ConstID=131|title=Mr. Patrick Clohessy|work=Oireachtas Members Database|accessdate=13 December 2008}}</ref>

'''Tom Condon''' (born 9 November 1987) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick Intermediate Championship]] club [[Knockaderry GAA|Knockaderry]]. He is a former player with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]], with whom he usually lines out as a right corner-back.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/dermot-crowe-ball-and-destiny-seized-by-condon-37652176.html|title=Ball and destiny seized by Condon|publisher=Irish Independent|date=23 December 2018|access-date=14 February 2019|first=Dermot|last=Crowe}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Knockaderry===

Condon joined the [[Knockaderry GAA|Knockaderry]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's top adult team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/positive-thinking-tom-putting-knockaderry-on-the-hurling-map-239868.html|title=Positive-thinking Tom putting Knockaderry on the hurling map|date=15 August 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=5 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Condon first lined out for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the minor team during the [[2005 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2005 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance on 4 May when he lined out at left corner-back in a 2–14 to 1–06 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/limerick-stun-tipp-to-book-final-place-25983462.html|title=Limerick stun Tipp to book final place|publisher=Irish Independent|date=5 May 2005|access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref> Condon was again at left corner-back on 26 June when Limerick suffered a 2–18 to 1–12 defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the Munster Championship final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/cronins-accuracy-guides-cork-to-30th-minor-title-25982253.html|title=Cronin's accuracy guides Cork to 30th minor title|publisher=Irish Independent|date=27 June 2005|access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref> Limerick subsequently qualified for the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] on 11 September. Condon was again at left corner-back for the 3–12 to 0–17 defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]], in what was his last game in the minor grade.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/galway-glee-as-goals-put-paid-to-gutsy-limerick-25965776.html|title=Galway glee as goals put paid to gutsy Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=12 September 2005|access-date=24 March 2019|first=Paddy|last=Hickey}}</ref>

After progressing onto the Limerick under-21 team, Condon was included on the panel for the [[2007 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2007 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance on 11 July when he lined out at full-back in Limerick's 2–14 to 2–10 defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

Condon was eligible for the under-21 grade again the following year. On 17 July 2008, he made his last appearance for the team when he lined out at full-back in Limerick's 1–13 to 0–15 defeat by Tipperary in the [[2008 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship semi-final]].

====Intermediate====

Condon was added to the Limerick intermediate team for the [[2007 All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship#Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|2007 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance on 10 June when he lined out at right corner-back in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–15 defeat of Tipperary. On 7 July, Condon started the Munster Championship final on the bench, however, he was introduced as a substitute in the 5–11 to 1–12 defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/match-reports/casey-fires-deise-to-historic-win-37687.html|title=Casey fires Déise to historic win|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 July 2007|access-date=24 March 2019|first=Brendan|last=Larkin}}</ref>

Condon was retained on the Limerick intermediate team for the [[2009 All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship#Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|2008 Munster Championship]]. On 31 July, he won a [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal when he lined out at right corner-back in Limerick's 2–16 to 2–12 defeat of Tipperary in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/98644|title=Munster IHC: Limerick lift crown|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=24 July 2008|access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref> Limerick subsequently qualified for the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] on 30 August. Condon was again at right corner-back for the 1–16 to 0–13 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]].

====Senior====

On 8 February 2009, Condon made his first appearance for the Limerick senior team when he lined out at left corner-back in a 3–13 to 1–18 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2009 National Hurling League|National League]]. He made his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] appearance on 20 June when he came on as a 60th-minute substitute for [[Mark O'Riordan]] in a 0–25 to 0–17 defeat by Waterford in a semi-final replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/gaa/deise-power-past-limerick-in-replay-415663.html|title=Deise power past Limerick in replay|publisher=Breaking News|date=6 June 2009|access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref> At the end of a disappointing season, Limerick manager [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]] dropped several high-profile players from the panel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/mccarthy-wields-the-axe-at-limerick-104495.html|title=McCarthy wields the axe at Limerick|date=30 October 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Martin|last=Kiely}}</ref> Over the course of the winter, many more players, including Condon, withdrew from the panel and refused to play while McCarthy and his management team remained in place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/2.823/four-more-players-quit-the-limerick-squad-1.1238677|title=Four more players quit the Limerick squad|date=2 January 2010|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=2 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/mccarthy-dispute-gets-silent-treatment-1.1244613|title=McCarthy dispute gets silent treatment|date=19 January 2010|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=2 August 2018}}</ref> The Limerick County Board refused to remove McCarthy and contested the 2010 season with a new group of players.

Condon returned to the panel the following year and made his first appearance under new manager [[Dónal O'Grady]] on 6 March 2011 in a 1–25 to 2-11 [[2011 National Hurling League|National League]] defeat of [[Down GAA|Down]]. On 30 April, he was at right corner-back when Limerick defeated Clare by 4–12 to 2–13 to win the Division 2 title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}}</ref> Condon ended the season by being one of three Limerick nominees for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/kilkenny-lead-list-of-hurling-all-star-nominees-522515.html|title=Kilkenny lead list of hurling All-Star nominees|date=29 September 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018}}</ref>

On 14 July 2013, Condon lined out in his first [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster Championship final]]. He was at left corner-back for Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and a first title in 17 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> Condon ended the season by being nominated for an All-Star.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaelicplayers.com/TabId/86/ArtMID/421/ArticleID/206/2013-Hurling-All-Star-Nominations.aspx|title=2013 Hurling All Star Nominations|date=4 October 2013|publisher=GPA website|access-date=2 August 2018}}</ref>

In July 2018, Condon received a two-match suspension after receiving a red card for jabbing the butt of his hurley into [[David Reidy (Clare hurler)|David Reidy]]'s midriff in a 0–26 to 0-15 Munster Championship defeat by Clare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/second-half-surge-crucial-as-clare-leapfrog-limerick-to-seal-munster-final-place-37019612.html|title=Second half surge crucial as Clare leapfrog Limerick to seal Munster final place|date=17 June 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/condon-hit-with-two-match-suspension-852897.html|title=Condon hit with two-match suspension|date=4 July 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> On 19 August, Condon was introduced as a 72nd-minute substitute for [[Richie English]] when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Condon was selected at right corner-back for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Condon won his first Munster Championship medal in six years when he was a non-playing substitute in Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

In January 2021, Condon announced his retirement form inter-county hurling.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/tom-condon-limerick-profile-retirement-knockaderry-5339339-Jan2021/|title= Hand of Tom: The Condon catch that ended Limerick's 45 years of hurt|date=30 January 2021|work=The 42|accessdate= 31 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tom-condon-retire-hurling-5338443-Jan2021/|title= Limerick All-Ireland winning defender retires after 12 senior inter-county seasons|date=30 January 2021|work=The 42|accessdate= 31 January 2021}}</ref>

===Munster===

Condon was first selected for the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team for the [[2012 Interprovincial Hurling Championship|2012 Inter-provincial Championship]]. He made his first appearance on 19 February when he lined out at left corner-back in a 3–14 to 1–16 defeat by [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] in the semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/early-leinster-damage-decisive-184406.html|title=Early Leinster damage decisive|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 February 2012|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>
 
Condon was selected for the Munster team again the following year. On 3 March 2013, he won a [[Railway Cup]] medal when he lined out at full-back in Munster's 1–22 to 0–15 defeat of [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] in the [[2013 Inter-Provincial Hurling Championship|final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/munster-beat-connacht-to-claim-interpro-crown-29105852.html|title=Munster beat Connacht to claim Interpro crown|date=5 March 2013|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=6 May 2013}}</ref>

For the third year in succession, Condon was selected for the Munster team. On 9 February 2014, he was at right corner-back when Munster suffered a 1–18 to 0–16 defeat by an all-Galway Connacht side in the semi-final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/munster-reign-ended-by-tribesmen-in-disguise-258246.html|title=Munster reign ended by Tribesmen in disguise|date=10 February 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=24 March 2019|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

After a one-year hiatus to the competition, Condon was back on the Munster panel for the [[2016 GAA Interprovincial Championships|2016 Championship]]. On 15 December he was an unused substitute when Munster defeated Leinster by 2–20 to 2–16 to win the Railway Cup.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/shanagher-strikes-late-as-munster-take-railway-35298457.html|title=Shanagher strikes late as Munster take Railway|date=16 December 2016|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=24 March 2019|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Condon is married to Limerick [[camogie]] player Sarah Carey.<ref>{{cite tweet |number=1301550177304694789 |user=granballcamogie |url-status=live |archive-date=September 3, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200903155850/https://twitter.com/granballcamogie/status/1301550177304694789 |title=We couldn’t be today to celebrate… |lang=en |url= https://twitter.com/granballcamogie/status/1301550177304694789}}</ref>

'''Dave Bulfin''' (born 1980) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a goalkeeper for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Bulfin joined the team during the [[National Hurling League 2003|2003 National League]] and was second choice goalkeeper until he left the panel after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2009|2009 championship]]. He enjoyed little success in the senior grade and was an unused substitute in Limerick's All-Ireland final defeat in 2007. Bulfin started two games during the 2008 National Hirling League and impressed during defeats away to Tipperary and home to Galway. He received praise for both performances from both local and national media. He made spectacular saves on both games and Limerick would have been defeated by a lot more only for him

At club level Bulfin plays with [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret/St. Paul's]].

==Playing career==

===Club===

Bulfin plays his club hurling with Mungret and has had a steady career helping his team in 16 championships and winning the Limerick County Junior title in 2006 when defeating Askeaton in the final. He retired from club hurling in 2013 citing a lack of motivation as his reason for packing it in.

===Inter-county===

Bulfin made his senior debut for Limerick in a [[National Hurling League]] game against [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17981|title=Limerick make 10 changes|publisher=Hogan Stand website|accessdate=4 November 2012|date=24 April 2003}}</ref> It was the only game he played during that campaign, however, he was subsequently included on Limerick's championship panel.

Bulfin was the sub goalkeeper for Limerick during their 2-19 to 1-15 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the 2007 All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2007/0902/1188603379646.html|title=Kilkenny overpowers Limerick to retain title|date=2 September 2007|quote=He did start two league games during the 2008 season. He is remembered for making some good saves in both matches, keeping the score down, in two heavy losses to Tipperary and Galway.|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref>

His [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] career with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] and [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] senior teams lasted from 1917 until 1923.{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1918.htm|title=1918 All-Ireland hurling champions|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|date=|accessdate=21 April 2014|first=|last=}} Raised in the townland of Baggotstown West, in the parish of [[Knockainey]], County Limerick, Barry first played competitive hurling and football with St. Colman's College, Fermoy. His prowess earned him the captaincy of the Munster team that won the 1914 All-Ireland College Hurling Final. That same year he was a member of the Munster team that reached in the All-Ireland College Football Final. Barry played [[Gaelic games]] with a number of clubs, beginning as a [[Gaelic football]]er with [[Fermoy GAA|Fermoy]], with whom he featured in two [[Cork Senior Football Championship|county senior championship]] finals. His return to Limerick saw Barry switch codes to hurling and joined the [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Boher]] team, while he also lined out with the [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]] and [[Fedamore GAA|Fedamore]] clubs. In 1916 Barry was selected for the Limerick junior football team, however, injury prevented him from lining out. He made his senior hurling debut during the [[1917 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1917 championship]]. Barry won his sole [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal in 1918. He also won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal that year before winning a second provincial title in 1921. Illness prevented him from participating in the 1921 All-Ireland final. [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a right wing-back for club side [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]].{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/201061/18-new-faces-on-Limerick-hurling.html|title=18 new faces on Limerick hurling panel|date=9 January 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=19 against Tipperary|date=16 June 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=19 June 2016|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} Outside of hurling, he works at DHL. ==Playing career== ===School=== Diarmuid Byrnes attended secondary school at Sexton Street CBS in Limerick city where he has subsequently returned to give motivational talks to students.{{Cite web |last=Lynch |first=Richard |date=28 November 2022 |title=CBS Sexton Street Students honoured at 2022 JP McManus scholarship awards |url=https://www.ilovelimerick.ie/2022-jp-mcmanus-scholarship-2/}} ===University=== During his studies at [[Limerick Institute of Technology]], Byrnes was selected for the college's senior hurling team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/fitzgibbon-cup-byrnes-points-way-as-lit-edge-out-ucd-34425558.html|title=Fitzgibbon Cup: Byrnes points way as LIT edge out UCD|date=5 February 2016|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}} Byrnes went on to study Supply Chain Management at the University of Limerick in 2022.{{Cite web |date=8 May 2026 |title=Linkedin Profile |url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/diarmaid-byrnes-356b521b7/}} ===GAA === Byrnes joined [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] GAA club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels. On 23 October 2016, Byrnes won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Hurling Championship]] medal after scoring six points from centre-back in Patrickswell's 1–26 to 1–07 defeat of [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/magnificent-patrickswell-still-pride-of-the-parish-427216.html|title=Magnificent Patrickswell still pride of the parish|date=14 October 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=6 August 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} Byrnes lined out in a second Limerick Championship final on 6 October 2019. Playing at centre-back, he scored two points, including a long-range free, and collected a second winners' medal following the 1–17 to 0–15 defeat of [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cian-lynch-comes-to-the-fore-as-patrickswell-hold-off-na-piarsaigh-in-limerick-county-final-38567636.html|title=Cian Lynch comes to the fore as Patrickswell hold off Na Piarsaigh in Limerick county final|publisher=Irish Independent|date=6 October 2019|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=Colm|last=Keys}} ===Inter-county=== ====Minor and under-21==== Byrnes first played for Limerick at minor level in 2012, in a season which ended with a defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] semi-final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/osullivan-sinks-cork-26849425.html|title=O'Sullivan sinks Cork|date=3 May 2012|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/banner-dig-deep-to-see-off-limerick-26870643.html|title=Banner dig deep to see off Limerick|date=30 June 2012|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}} Byrnes subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team. He made his first appearance on 4 June 2014, however, he was sent off after receiving two yellow cards in a 2–20 to 1–14 defeat by Clare.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=6 August 2018|first=|last=}} In his second season with the team Byrnes won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over Clare in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league {{short description|Irish hurler (born 1997)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=January 2022}} {{infobox Gaelic games player |image = |name = Peter Casey |irish = Peadar Ó Cathasaigh |nickname = |occupation = |birth_date = 21 July 1997 |birth_place = [[Caherdavin]], Limerick, Ireland |height_ft = 5 |height_in = 11 |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] |cl_years = |cl_position = |cl_apps_points = |cl_county = 5 |cl_province = 2 |cl_all_ireland = 1 |colleges = |fitz = |col_years = |counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ic_years = 2017–present |ic_position = Right corner-forward |ic_apps_points = 43 (4–80) |ic_province = 6 |ic_all_ireland = 6 |nhl = 4 |all_stars = 1 |cl_update = | ic_update = 22:29, 19 July 2026 }} '''Peter Casey''' (born 21 July 1997) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a right corner-forward for club side [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. His brother, [[Mike Casey (hurler)|Mike Casey]], also plays for both teams. ==Playing career== ===College=== Casey first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. On 20 February 2016, he scored two points when Ardscoil Rís won the [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] title after an 0–11 to 0–08 defeat of Our Lady's Secondary School from [[Templemore]] in the [[2015–16 Harty Cup#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ardscoil-ris-claim-fourth-harty-cup-in-seven-years-383154.html|title=Ardscoil Rís claim fourth Harty Cup in seven years|date=20 February 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 August 2018}} ===Club=== Casey joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the under-16 and under-21 grades. He later made his senior championship debut for the club. On 11 October 2015, Casey was at left corner-forward when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] by 1–22 to 4–12 to win the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}} Later that season he won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 2–18 to 2–11 defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} On 17 March 2016, Casey won an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] by 2–25 to 2–14 in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}} On 15 October 2017, Casey won a second Limerick Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 1–22 to 2–14 in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018}} He later won a second Munster Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated Ballygunner by 3–15 to 2–10 in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/late-na-piarsaigh-surge-sweeps-aside-ballygunner-in-scrappy-munster-final-36333884.html|title=Late Na Piarsaigh surge sweeps aside Ballygunner in scrappy Munster final|date=19 November 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}} On 17 March 2018, Casey was at corner-forward when Na Piarsaigh were defeated by [[Cuala GAA|Cuala]] in the All-Ireland final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}} On 27 October 2018, Casey won a third Limerick Championship medal following Na Piarsaigh's 2–22 to 3–10 defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/boss-beary-points-to-experience-of-troops-as-na-piarsaigh-impress-again-37468758.html|title=Boss Beary points to experience of troops as Na Piarsaigh impress again|date=29 October 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=1 November 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}} Casey won his 4th county senior hurling medal in 2020 with a victory over Doon in the LIT Gaelic Grounds and a 5th medal followed in 2022 with a comprehensive victory over Kilmallock ===Inter-county=== ====Minor and under-21==== Casey first played for Limerick at minor level. On 22 July 2014, he was at left corner-forward when Limerick won their second successive [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title after a 0–24 to 0–18 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|date=23 July 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}} Casey was moved to left wing-forward for the subsequent [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] on 7 September 2014. He was held scoreless in the 2–17 to 0–19 defeat.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/wonderful-walsh-fires-cats-to-victory-over-limerick-30569083.html|title=Wonderful Walsh fires Cats to victory over Limerick|date=8 September 2014|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}} Casey's second and final season with the Limerick minor hurling team ended with an All-Ireland quarter-final defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/evan-niland-stars-as-slick-galway-see-off-limerick-344725.html|title=Evan Niland stars as slick Galway see off Limerick|date=27 July 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} In his final year on the minor team, Casey was included on the Limerick under-21 team. He won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal in his debut season after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=30 July 2018}} On 12 September 2015, Casey was introduced as a substitute when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} After surrendering their title in 2016, Casey won a second Munster Championship medal the following year after a 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018}} On 9 September 2017, Casey was at right corner-forward in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} He was later named on the Bord Gáis Energy Team of the Year for a second time.{{cite '''Michael L. Casey''' (born 25 October 1995) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a full-back for club side [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. His brother, [[Peter Casey (hurler)|Peter Casey]], also plays for both teams.

==Playing career==
===College===

Casey first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. On 22 February 2014, he won a [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] medal following a 2–13 to 0–04 defeat of Scoil na Trionoide Naofa.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/210165|title=Harty Cup final: Ardscoil Ris rout local rivals|date=22 February 2014|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

===University===

During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]], Casey was selected for the college's senior hurling team on a number of occasions. On 24 February 2018, he was introduced as a substitute when the university defeated [[DCU GAA|DCU Dóchás Éireann]] by 2–21 to 2–15 to win the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ul-victory-keeps-limerick-hurling-momentum-bubbling-467621.html|title=UL victory keeps Limerick hurling momentum bubbling|date=26 February 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Therese|last=O'Callaghan}}</ref>

===Club===

Casey joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the under-16, minor and under-21 grades. He made his senior championship debut for the club as a seventeen-year-old in 2013.

On 6 October 2013, Casey was at left corner-back when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Adare GAA|Adare]] by 0–14 to 0–12 to win the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/downes-sets-the-tone-for-na-piarsaigh-to-grind-it-out-29639434.html|title=Downes sets the tone for Na Piarsaigh to grind it out|date=7 October 2013|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> Team manager [[Seán Stack]] later said that Casey "was definitely man of the match for me".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/na-piarsaigh-young-guns-dig-it-out-and-come-of-age-245409.html|title=Na Piarsaigh young guns dig it out and come of age|date=7 October 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> Casey retained his place at corner-back for the subsequent [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]], which culminated with him winning a provincial medal after a 4–14 to 0–08 defeat of [[Sixmilebridge GAA|Sixmilebridge]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/powerful-piarsaighs-blistering-pace-too-much-for-tired-bridge-250662.html|title=Powerful Piarsaigh's blistering pace too much for tired Bridge|date=25 November 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Casey won a second Limerick Championship medal on 11 October 2015 after a 1–22 to 4–12 defeat of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> Later that season he won a second Munster medal after a 2–18 to 2–11 defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 17 March 2016, Casey won an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] by 2–25 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

On 15 October 2017, Casey won a third Limerick Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 1–22 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He later won a third Munster Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated Ballygunner by 3–15 to 2–10 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/late-na-piarsaigh-surge-sweeps-aside-ballygunner-in-scrappy-munster-final-36333884.html|title=Late Na Piarsaigh surge sweeps aside Ballygunner in scrappy Munster final|date=19 November 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, Casey was at full-back when Na Piarsaigh were defeated by [[Cuala GAA|Cuala]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

On 27 October 2018, Casey won a fourth Limerick Championship medal following Na Piarsaigh's 2–22 to 3–10 defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/boss-beary-points-to-experience-of-troops-as-na-piarsaigh-impress-again-37468758.html|title=Boss Beary points to experience of troops as Na Piarsaigh impress again|date=29 October 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=1 November 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}}</ref>

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

Casey first played for Limerick at minor level. On 23 July 2013, he was introduced as a substitute in the 39th minute when Limerick won their first [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title in 29 years after a 1–20 to 4–08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

Casey subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2015 and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 0–22 to 0–19 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 12 September 2015, Casey was at left corner-back when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Senior====

Casey joined the Limerick senior hurling team in January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/201061/18-new-faces-on-Limerick-hurling.html|title=18 new faces on Limerick hurling panel|date=9 January 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He was released from the panel prior to the start of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].

On 12 February 2017, Casey made his senior debut at left corner-back in a [[National Hurling League|National League]] defeat by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/kiely-fumes-at-ref-as-davy-gets-lift-off-442800.html|title=Kiely fumes at ref as Davy gets lift-off|date=13 February 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Later that season he made his first championship start in a 3–17 to 2-16 Munster Championship semi-final defeat by Clare.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-senior-hurling-munster-thurles-3424841-Jun2017/|title=5 youngsters to make Munster senior debuts for Limerick in Thurles on Sunday|date=2 June 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Casey was at full-back when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> He ended the season by being nominated for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=13 September 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Casey started Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] on the bench. He was introduced as a half-time substitute for [[Tom Condon (hurler)|Tom Condon]] and collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Casey won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal at full-back following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He ended the year by being nominated for a second All-Star award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-allstars-hurling-2019-4824531-Sep2019/|title=11 players from Tipperary as 8 counties feature in 2019 All-Star hurling nominations|date=26 September 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=26 September 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

'''Conor Boylan''' (born 22 March 1998) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2019/0207/1028232-five-young-hurlers-to-watch-in-2019/|title=Five young hurlers to watch in 2019|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=8 February 2019|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=|last=}}</ref> He usually lines out as a left wing-forward.

==Playing career==
===Ardscoil Rís===

Boylan first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. On 20 February 2016, he was at right wing-forward when Ardscoil Rís won the [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] title after an 0–11 to 0–08 defeat of Our Lady's Secondary School from [[Templemore]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ardscoil-ris-claim-fourth-harty-cup-in-seven-years-383154.html|title=Ardscoil Rís claim fourth Harty Cup in seven years|date=20 February 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=8 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

===University College Cork===

On 23 February 2019, Boylan was a substitute for [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] when they faced [[Mary Immaculate College]] in the [[2019 Fitzgibbon Cup|Fitzgibbon Cup final]]. He remained on the bench for the 2–21 to 0–13 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/295945|title=Fitzgibbon Cup final: UCC in a different class|date=23 February 2017|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=23 February 2019|first=|last=}}</ref>

Boylan played in a second successive [[2020 Fitzgibbon Cup#Final|Fitzgibbon Cup final]] on 12 February 2020. Lining out at centre-forward, he ended the game with a second successive winners' medal after the 0–18 to 2–11 defeat of the [[Institute of Technology, Carlow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/it-carlow-ucc-match-report-5004314-Feb2020/|title=14-man UCC come from 6 points down to win Fitzgibbon Cup final against IT Carlow|publisher=The 42|date=12 February 2020|accessdate=13 February 2020|first=Sinéad|last=Farrell}}</ref>

===Na Piarsaigh===

Boylan joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the under-16, minor and under-21 grades.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

Boylan won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Championship]] medal as a non-playing substitute on 11 October 2015 after a 1–22 to 4–12 defeat of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> Later that season he won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal, also as a non-playing substitute, after a 2–18 to 2–11 defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 17 March 2016, Boylan was on the bench when he won an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] by 2–25 to 2–14 in the [[2016 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

On 15 October 2017, Boylan won a second Limerick Championship medal after being introduced as a substitute when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 1–22 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He later won a second Munster Championship medal from midfield when Na Piarsaigh defeated Ballygunner by 3–15 to 2–10 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/late-na-piarsaigh-surge-sweeps-aside-ballygunner-in-scrappy-munster-final-36333884.html|title=Late Na Piarsaigh surge sweeps aside Ballygunner in scrappy Munster final|date=19 November 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, Boylan played as a substitute when Na Piarsaigh were defeated by [[Cuala GAA|Cuala]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

On 27 October 2018, Boylan won a third Limerick Championship medal at left wing-forward following Na Piarsaigh's 2–22 to 3–10 defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/boss-beary-points-to-experience-of-troops-as-na-piarsaigh-impress-again-37468758.html|title=Boss Beary points to experience of troops as Na Piarsaigh impress again|date=29 October 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=1 November 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Boylan made his first appearance for the Limerick minor team on 8 April 2015. He was introduced as a substitute in a 2–20 to 1–13 defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[2015 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/shane-kingston-cork-limerick-minor-hurling-2037030-Apr2015/|title=Cork minors hit 2nd half stride to see off Limerick by 10 points|publisher=The 42|date=9 April 2015|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref> On 12 July Boylan was again introduced as a substitute in Limerick's 0–20 to 0–17 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the Munster final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-minor-2212497-Jul2015/|title=Tipperary claim Munster minor hurling title to deny Limerick three-in-a-row|publisher=The 42|date=12 July 2015|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

Boylan was eligible for the minor grade again in 2016 and made his first start on 6 April in a 2–11 to 1–08 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/josh-ryan-limerick-2702502-Apr2016/|title=Super subs strike goals for Limerick to see off Clare in Munster minor hurling clash|publisher=The 42|date=6 April 2016|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 10 July, he scored two points from left wing-forward when Limerick suffered a 1–24 to 0–10 defeat by Tipperary in a second successive Munster final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/tipperary-romp-to-munster-minor-title-744074.html|title=Tipperary romp to Munster minor title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=10 July 2016|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=|last=}}</ref> On 4 September, Boyle was at right corner-forward when Limerick suffered a second defeat by Tipperary in the All-Ireland final at [[Croke Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/redemption-as-powerful-premier-get-hands-on-cup-419377.html|title=Redemption as powerful Premier get hands on cup|date=5 September 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

Boylan subsequently progressed onto the Limerick under-21 hurling team and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal on 26 July 2017 after a coming on as a substitute in Limerick's 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 9 September, he was introduced as a 38th-minute substitute for [[Cian Lynch]] in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Senior====

Boylan made his first appearance for the Limerick senior team on 14 December 2018. He was introduced as a 55th-minute substitute for [[Barry O'Connell (hurler)|Barry O'Connell]] in a 4–14 to 2–17 defeat by Tipperary in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/winning-return-for-liam-sheedy-as-tipperary-beat-all-ireland-champs-limerick-in-munster-league-37627983.html|title=Winning return for Liam Sheedy as Tipperary beat All Ireland champs Limerick in Munster League|publisher=Irish Independent|date=14 December 2018|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=Cormac|last=Liddy}}</ref> On 2 February 2019, he made his first start at left wing-forward in a 1–21 to 1–14 defeat of Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-3-4473497-Feb2019/|title=Impressive Limerick come from behind to see off Tipperary|publisher=The 42|date=2 February 2019|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=John|last=Fallon}}</ref>

'''Aaron Costello''' (born 4 July 1992) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He usually lines out as a left corner-back.

==Playing career==
===University College Cork===

As a student at University College Cork, Costello also became involved in [[Gaelic games]]. On 8 March 2012, he came on as a 16th-minute substitute to win an All-Ireland Freshers Championship medal following a 0–24 to 3–11 defeat of the [[University of Limerick]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/late-rally-sees-ucc-claim-three-in-a-row-186578.html|title=Late rally sees UCC claim three in-a-row|date=9 March 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=7 July 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

===Kilmallock===

Costllo joined the [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the minor and under-21 grades before eventually joining the club's senior team.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

On 7 October 2012, Costello was named on the bench when Kilmallock faced [[Adare GAA|Adare]] in the [[2012 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|Limerick Senior Championship]] final. He remained on the bench for the entire game but collected a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|winners' medal]] following the -15 to 0–15 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/mulcahy-strikes-to-secure-spoils-for-gritty-kilmallock-28818665.html|title=Mulcahy strikes to secure spoils for gritty Kilmallock|publisher=Irish Independent|date=8 October 2012|accessdate=20 August 2013|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 19 October 2014, Costello won his first championship medal on the field of play following a 1–15 to 0–14 defeat of reigning champions [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] in the [[2014 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/delight-for-sparrow-as-kilmallock-defy-odds-292135.html|title=Delight for 'Sparrow' as Kilmallock defy odds|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 October 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> He later won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal on 23 November 2014 following a 1–32 to 3-18 extra-time defeat of [[Cratloe GAA|Cratloe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/football/kilmallock-find-extra-gear-in-final-epic-299265.html|title=Kilmallock find extra gear in final epic|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 November 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 17 March 2015, Costello was at left corner-back when Kilmallock suffered a 1–18 to 1–06 defeat by [[Ballyhale Shamrocks GAA|Ballyhale Shamrocks]] in the [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] at [[Croke Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ballyhale-make-it-six-of-the-best-with-final-stroll-31075381.html|title=Ballyhale make it six of the best with final stroll|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 March 2015|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Senior====

On 14 December 2018, Costello was included on [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]]'s first Limerick squad for the 2019 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/four-newcomers-as-john-kiely-names-first-limerick-squad-for-2019-season/|title=Five newcomers as John Kiely names first Limerick squad for 2019 season|publisher=Sporting Limerick|date=14 December 2018|accessdate=24 February 2019|first=Jack|last=Neville}}</ref> He made his first appearance for the team on 20 December 2018 when he came on as a 48th-minute substitute for [[Lorcan Lyons]] in Limerick's 4–14 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-kerry-munster-shl-4407358-Dec2018/|title=One last win for the All-Ireland hurling champions before Christmas|publisher=The 42|date=20 December 2018|accessdate=24 February 2019|first=Murt|last=Murphy}}</ref> On 9 March 2019, Costello made his first appearance in the [[2019 National Hurling League|National League]] when he came on as a half-time substitute for [[Tom Condon (hurler)|Tom Condon]] in the 2–22 to 0–11 defeat [[Laois GAA|Laois]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/laois-v-limerick-quarter-final-report-4532782-Mar2019/|title=Six All-Ireland winners start as Limerick storm into league semi-final with 17-point win over Laois|publisher=The 42|date=9 March 2019|accessdate=21 June 2019|first=Steven|last=Miller}}</ref> On 31 March 2019, he was a member of the extended panel when Limerick defeated [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] by 1–24 to 0–10 to win the [[National Hurling League|National League]] title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Costello won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal as a non-playing substitute following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June
