'''Ronan Connolly''' (born 1999) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Adare GAA|Adare]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/417892/limerick-hurlers-have-a-clean-slate-and-are-attacking-the-2019-championship-connolly.html|title=Limerick hurlers have a 'clean slate and are attacking the 2019 championship': Connolly|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=18 May 2019|access-date=25 January 2020|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He usually lines out as a left corner-back.

==Career==

Connolly first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Adare GAA|Adare]] club, while also playing as a schoolboy with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]]. He won a [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] title in 2016, before [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ing Ardscoil Rís to a second Harty Cup in 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ardscoil-ris-claim-fourth-harty-cup-in-seven-years-383154.html |title=Ardscoil Rís claim fourth Harty Cup in seven years |access-date=22 February 2016 |work=[[Irish Examiner]] |date=20 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30828571.html|title=Ardscoil Rís extend Cork's wait for Harty Cup success|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=17 February 2018|access-date=17 February 2022|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Connolly later lined out with [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] and was an unused substitute when the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] title was won in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/ucc-fitzgibbon-cup-hurling-cit-4971273-Jan2020/|title=Kingston hits 0-7 as UCC book Fitzgibbon quarter-final spot with win over CIT|date=19 January 2020|publisher=The 42|access-date=4 February 2023|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/it-carlow-ucc-match-report-5004314-Feb2020/|title=14-man UCC come from 6 points down to win Fitzgibbon Cup final against IT Carlow|publisher=The 42|date=12 February 2020|accessdate=13 February 2020|first=Sinéad|last=Farrell}}</ref>

Connolly first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-minor-hurlers-3465825-Jun2017/|title=Limerick minor hurlers make two changes for tomorrow's Munster semi-final against Clare|publisher=The 42|date=27 June 2017|accessdate=13 February 2020|first=|last=}}</ref> He later spent one season with the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20 team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/cork-limerick-munster-u20-hurling-championship-4709293-Jul2019/|title=O'Regan hits 1-6 as Cork take aim at Clare after proving too strong for Limerick|publisher=The 42|date=3 July 2019|accessdate=13 February 2020|first=|last=}}</ref> Connolly was called into the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in advance of the pre-season [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling League|2019 Munster SHL]]. He was on the 41-man panel that won the [[National Hurling League]] title later that season, but was released prior to the start of the championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/417892/limerick-hurlers-have-a-clean-slate-and-are-attacking-the-2019-championship-connolly.html|title=Limerick hurlers have a 'clean slate and are attacking the 2019 championship': Connolly|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=18 May 2019|accessdate=13 February 2020|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> Connolly later returned and was part of the Limerick panel that won four successive [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] titles from 2020 to 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/1253921/limerick-hurling-team-confirmed-for-all-ireland-hurling-final-with-kilkenny.html|title=Limerick hurling team confirmed for All-Ireland hurling final with Kilkenny|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 July 2023|accessdate=23 July 2023|first=John|last=Keogh}}</ref>

'''Paul Carey''' (November 1978 – 6 November 2020) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he lined out with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and was also a member of the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==

Carey first played hurling alongside his brothers, [[Ciarán Carey|Ciarán]] and [[Pa Carey|Pa]], with the [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] club. After success in the minor and under-21 grades, he subsequently joined the club's senior team and won a total of four [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick County Championship]] medals, including one as captain of the team in [[2003 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2003]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/old-guard-command-the-well-25926060.html|title=Old guard command the 'Well|publisher=Irish Independent|date=13 October 2003|accessdate=15 October 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> At inter-county level, Carey lined out with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] minor and under-21 teams, before making his first appearance for the senior team in a pre-season South-East League game in November 1998. It would be [[2002 National Hurling League|2002]] before he made his competitive debut in a [[2002 National Hurling League|National League]] game against [[Derry GAA|Derry]]. In a brief inter-county career, Carey made just two league appearances for Limerick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/home/587251/tributes-paid-to-former-star-hurler-and-full-hearted-limerick-man.html|title=Tributes paid to former star hurler and 'full-hearted Limerick man'|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=7 November 2020|accessdate=8 November 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Carey was killed in a [[road traffic collision]] in [[Dubai]] on 6 November 2020, aged 41.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/munster/arid-40077686.html|title='Terribly sad and so sudden': Limerick hurling hero Paul Carey dies in Dubai collision|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=7 November 2020|accessdate=8 November 2020|first=David|last=Raleigh}}</ref>

'''Vivian G. Cobbe''' (26 January 1934 – 31 October 2023) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who played at club level with [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St. Patrick's]], at inter-county level with [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and at inter-provincial level with [[Munster GAA|Munster]].

==Background==
Cobbe was born in [[Mountmellick]], [[County Laois]], Ireland on 26 January 1934.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41179093.html|title=A Saint marching on: Tales and truths from the colonel of the hurling Cobbes|date=8 July 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 March 2024|first=|last=}}</ref> He died at home in [[Limerick]], [[County Limerick]], on 31 October 2023, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vivian Cobbe |url=https://rip.ie/death-notice/vivian-cobbe-limerick-limerick-city-534814 |access-date=28 October 2024 |publisher=RIP.ie |date=2 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Sadness at passing of former Limerick hurler Vivian Cobbe |url=https://limerickgaa.ie/sadness-at-passing-of-former-limerick-hurler-vivian-cobbe/ |access-date=28 October 2024 |publisher=Limerick GAA |date=1 November 2023}}</ref>

==Career==
From the [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St. Patrick's]] club, Cobbe first came to prominence on the inter-county scene with the Limerick junior team that overcame [[London GAA|London]] to win the [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|1955 All-Ireland Junior Championship]]. Promotion to the senior side followed, with Cobbe lining out in the forwards when Limerick surprised [[Clare GAA|Clare]] to win the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1955 Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/columnists/arid-20473132.html|title=Mackey, Limerick, and the decade when Hollywood documented the glories of hurling for US cinema|date=17 August 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 March 2021|first=Paul|last=Rouse}}</ref> The team, labelled "Mackey's Greyhounds" after their trainer [[Mick Mackey]], were subsequently beaten by eventual champions [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/goreyguardian/sport/farewell-mick-27348747.html|title=Farewell Mick|date=27 October 2011|publisher=Gorey Guardian|accessdate=3 March 2021|first=|last=}}</ref> Cobbe continued playing for Limerick until the 1960s, by which time he had also won two [[Railway Cup]] medals with [[Munster GAA|Munster]].

{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{infobox Gaelic games player |image = |name = Colin Coughlan |irish = Cóilín Ó Cochláin |nickname = |occupation = Student |birth_date = 1 August 2002 |birth_place = [[Clarina, County Limerick|Clarina]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] |height_ft = |height_in = |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] |cl_years = |cl_position = |cl_apps_points = |cl_county = 0 |cl_province = |cl_all_ireland = |colleges = [[University of Limerick]] |fitz = 3 |col_years = 2021-present |counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ic_years = 2021-present |ic_position = Left wing-back |ic_apps_points = 13 (0-01) |ic_province = 5 |ic_all_ireland = 4 |nhl = 2 |all_stars = 0 |cl_update = |ic_update = 23:15, 19 July 2026 }} '''Colin Coughlan''' (born 1 August 2002) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he plays with [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[Clarina, County Limerick|Clarina]], [[County Limerick]], Coughlan was educated at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick]]. He played in all grades of hurling during his time there and won a [[Dr Harty Cup]] medal in February 2018, as a panel member, following the 3–18 to 2–10 win over [[Midleton CBS Secondary School|Midleton CBS]] in the [[2017–18 Harty Cup#Final|final]].{{cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/ardscoil-ris-extend-corks-wait-for-harty-cup-success-828571.html|title=Ardscoil Rís extend Cork's wait for Harty Cup success|access-date=17 May 2018 |publisher=Irish Examiner |date=17 February 2018}} During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]] (UL), Coughlan continued his hurling development. He won a league and championship double with the freshers' team in 2022.{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/star-studded-ul-crowned-all-ireland-fresher-hurling-champions-in-final-win-over-dcu-7858239|title=Star-studded UL crowned All-Ireland Fresher hurling champions in final win over DCU|access-date=20 July 2026|publisher=Limerick Live|date=9 March 2022}} Coughlan immediately progressed to UL's [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] team and claimed a winners' medal in that competition in February 2023, after the 4–19 to 1–13 win over the [[NUI Galway GAA|University of Galway]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/sigerson-fitzgibbon-cups/four-goal-michael-kiely-fires-ul-to-fitzgibbon-cup-glory-against-university-of-galway-42348322.html|title=Four-goal Michael Kiely fires UL to Fitzgibbon Cup glory against University of Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 February 2023|accessdate=18 February 2023|first=Tomás|last=McCarthy}} He won further Fitzgibbon Cup medals in 2025 and 2026, when he [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ed UL to back-to-back titles.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41575399.html|title=UL overpower DCU to lift third Fitzgibbon Cup in four years|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 February 2025|accessdate=16 February 2025|first=Kevin|last=Egan}}{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/2015230/limerick-stars-shine-as-clinical-ul-see-off-local-rivals-mary-immaculate-college-in-fitzgibbon-cup-final.html|title=Limerick stars shine as clinical UL see off local rivals Mary Immaculate College in Fitzgibbon Cup final|publisher=Limerick Live|date=13 February 2026|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} ==Club career== Coughlan began his club career with [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]], at a time when the club had multiple successes in the juvenile and underage grades. After winning the Limerick MAHC title in 2018, he won a Limerick Premier MHC title in 2019, following an 0–18 to 0–12 win over [[Doon GAA|Doon]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/ballybrown-end-31-year-wait-for-a-premier-minor-hurling-title-8134242|title=Ballybrown end 31-year wait for a Premier Minor Hurling title|publisher=Limerick Live|date=5 October 2019|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} Coughlan collected a second consecutive winners' medal in that competition in 2020, as [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret]] were beaten by 3–23 to 0–20 .{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/back-to-back-limerick-minor-hurling-tiles-for-ballybrown-after-thrilling-final-with-mungret-8044512|title=Back-to-back Limerick minor hurling tiles for Ballybrown after thrilling final with Mungret|publisher=Limerick Live|date=16 September 2020|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} Ballybrown secured the Limerick Premier U19HC title in October 2021, with Coughlan lining out at centre-forward in the 2–30 to 1–17 win over [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/emphatic-ballybrown-power-past-monaleen-to-win-limerick-u19-premier-hurling-title-7945309|title=Emphatic Ballybrown power past Monaleen to win Limerick U19 Premier hurling title|publisher=Limerick Live|date=6 October 2021|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} He added a Limerick Premier U21HC medal to his collection in 2022, following a seven-point win over Mungret in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/ballybrown-celebrate-limerick-premier-u21-hurling-final-success-7650341|title=Ballybrown celebrate Limerick Premier U21 hurling final success|publisher=Limerick Live|date=20 November 2022|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} By this stage Coughlan had already joined the Ballybrown [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|senior team]] and made his debut in July 2020 in a 4–18 to 2–14 win over [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40022090.html|title=Limerick SHC: Ballybrown get campaign off to flying start|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=25 July 2020|accessdate=31 October 2022|first=|last=}} ==Inter-county career== Coughlan first appeared on the inter-county scene for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]]. He won a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] title in June 2019, following a 1–17 to 1–11 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2019 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-triumph-in-electric-ireland-munster-mhc-final|title=Limerick triumph in Electric Ireland Munster MHC Final|date=30 June 2019|publisher=GAA website|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} Coughlan immediately progressed to the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20 team]] and won a [[Munster Under-20 Hurling Championship|Munster U20HC]] in May 2022 following a four-point win over Tipperary.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40865447.html|title=Treaty tyros tame Tipp to add to county's dominance |date=4 May 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=20 July 2026|first=|last=}} He was at left wing-back for Limerick's 0–19 to 0–18 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2022 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland U20HC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/u-20-hurling/kilkenny-claim-all-ireland-u-20-title-after-edging-limerick-in-thrilling-final-41676137.html|title=Kilkenny claim All-Ireland U-20 title after edging Limerick in thrilling final|date=22 May 2022|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} Coughlan made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in a 0–33 to 2–19 [[National Hurling League]] defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in June 2021.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/316763|title=Four new faces in Limerick squad|date=4 May 2021|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=6 May 2021|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-gaelic-grounds-hurling-5427494-May2021/|title=Limerick call up youngsters to senior squad as All-Ireland winning defender opts out|date=4 May 2021|publisher=The 42|accessdate=6 May 2021|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40305821.html|title=Teenage debutant among seven changes as Limerick name side for Cork clash|date=3 June 2021|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=22 May 2023|first=|last=}} He later won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal, as a panel member, as Limerick claimed a third consecutive title for the first time in 85 years following a 3–21 to 2–29 win over Tipperary.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/85-year-wait-ends-as-limerick-topple-tipperary-to-win-historic-munster-hurling-title-7969390|title=85-year wait ends as Limerick topple Tipperary to win historic Munster hurling title|date=18 July 2021|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Coughlan later added an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medal to his collection, after coming on as a substitute for [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|team captain]] [[Declan Hannon]] in the 3–32 to 1–22 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40364432.html|title=Will record-breaking All-Ireland victory over Cork be Limerick's high water mark? Don't bet on it|date=22 August 2021|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Coughlan's membership of the under-20 team in 2022 impacted on his senior team appearances that season.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40864889.html|title=Munster U20 Hurling final: Three key battles|date=4 May 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Limerick retained the Munster SHC title for a fourth consecutive year in June 2022, with Coughlan being an unused substitute in the 1–29 to 0–29 extra-time win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40889036.html|title=Limerick find an extra gear to see off Clare in Munster final thriller|date=5 June 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He later won his second consecutive All-Ireland SHC medal, again as an unused substitute, in the 1–31 to 2–26 win over Kilkenny in the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40920188.html|title=Limerick secure the three-in-row with dream day in the sun|date=17 July 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Coughlan won his first National League medal in April 2023, after lining out at left wing-back in the 2–20 to 0–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 National Hurling League#Division 1|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0409/1376051-classy-limerick-claim-league-honours-with-ease/|title=Classy Limerick claim league honours with ease|date=9 April 2023|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He later claimed his third Munster SHC medal, his first on the field of play, as Limerick beat Clare by 1–23 to 1–22 to win a record-equalling fifth consecutive title.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41159863.html|title=Aaron Gillane on fire as Limerick edge Clare to secure fifth consecutive Munster title|date=11 June 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Coughlan was an unused substitute when Limerick won a record-equalling fourth consecutive All-Ireland SHC title, following a 0–30 to 2–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history |date=23 July 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Coughlan was again an unused substitute when Limerick won a record-breaking sixth consecutive Munster SHC title after a 1–26 to 1–20 win over Clare in the [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster|2024 Munster SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41412799.html|title=Six of the best: Limerick make history with Munster final win over Clare |date=9 June 2024|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} After a trophy-less 2025 season, Limerick regained the National League title with a six-point win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in April 2026, with Coughlan claiming his second winners' medal.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41822540.html|title='If you get a chance to win, you have to take it' - Kiely's call that Cork shall not pass is heard|date=6 April 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He later collected a fifth Munster SHC medal, as an unused substitute, as Limerick also regained that title with a 1–21 to 2–17 win over Cork in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/munster-shc-final-limerick-finish-strongly|title=Munster SHC Final: Limerick finish strongly|date=7 June 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Coughlan won a fourth All-Ireland SHC medal, after coming on as a substitute for [[Seán Finn]], in the 1–29 to 1–18 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2026 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite He has had a close association as a coach with [[Davy Fitzgerald]] with a number of inter-county teams.{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/seoirse-bulfin-wexford-coach-coaching-series-interview-4890109-Nov2019/|title=The first day I met him was in the LIT canteen 15 years ago and I was going, 'Jesus, I'm here with Davy Fitz'|publisher=The 42|date=17 November 2019|access-date=14 August 2022|first=|last=}} ==Playing career== Bulfin first played [[hurling]] at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] club. He eventually progressed onto the club's adult teams with whom he had a 20-year association before his retirement in 2017. As a student at [[Mary Immaculate College]], Bulfin lined out for the college's senior team in the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] and [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ed the team in his final year in 2003.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30939723.html|title=The Kieran Shannon Interview: Seoirse Bulfin on riding shotgun to Davy Fitz|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=27 July 2019|access-date=14 August 2022|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, he was goalkeeper on the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick minor hurling team]] during the [[1997 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|1997 Munster MHC]] campaign.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/i-get-a-lot-of-stick-on-the-line-nasty-stuff-ive-got-anonymous-letters-too-39093053.html|title='I get a lot of stick on the line, nasty stuff. I've got anonymous letters too'|publisher=Irish Independent|date=1 April 2020|access-date=14 August 2022|first=|last=}} ==Coaching career== Buflin's coaching career began after being appointed GAA development officer at [[Limerick Institute of Technology]] in 2003. It was here that he began his close association with [[Davy Fitzgerald]] and he was part of the LIT management team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] successes in 2005 and 2007. Bulfin joined Fitzgerald as [[Coach (sport)|coach]] to the [[Waterford senior hurling team]] in 2011 before later taking up the coaching role with the [[Clare senior hurling team]]. During his five-year tenure Clare won a first [[National Hurling League]] title in [[1977-78 National Hurling League|38 years]] as well as the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] title in [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013]].{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/maybe-it-wont-feel-as-different-when-we-get-into-it-seoirse-bulfin-on-why-wexford-are-raring-to-go-39688777.html|title='Maybe it won't feel as different when we get into it' - Seoirse Bulfin on why Wexford are raring to go|publisher=Irish Independent|date=31 October 2020|access-date=14 August 2022|first=|last=}} The Fitzgerald-Bulfin combination later brought a [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster SHC]] title to [[Wexford senior hurling team|Wexford]] in [[2019 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|2019]]. He was appointed manager of the [[Meath senior hurling team]] in August 2022, having spent the previous year as team coach.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/davy-fitzgeralds-former-right-hand-man-seoirse-bulfin-to-take-over-as-meath-hurling-manager-41904773.html|title=Davy Fitzgerald's former right-hand man Seoirse Bulfin to take over as Meath hurling manager|publisher=Irish Independent|date=11 August 2022|access-date=14 August 2022|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Limerick Institute of Technology *[[Fitzgibbon Cup]]: 2005, 2007 ;Ballyagran *Limerick Senior Camogie Hurling Championship: 2011 ;Clare *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013]] *[[National Hurling League]]: [[2016 National Hurling League|2016]] ;Wexford *[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[2019 Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|2019]] ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Seoirse Bulfin navigation boxes |list1= {{s-start}} {{s-sports}} {{succession box | before=[[Nick Weir (hurler)|Nick Weir]] | title=[[Meath county hurling team|Meath senior hurling team manager]] | years=2022–2024 | after=[[Steven Clynch]] }} {{succession box | before=[[Joe Fortune]] | title=[[Westmeath county hurling team|Westmeath senior hurling team manager]] | years=2024– | after=Incumbent }} {{s-end}} {{Clare Hurling Team 2013}} {{Meath county hurling team managers}} {{Westmeath county hurling team managers}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Bulfin, Seoirse}} [[Category:1979 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Bruff hurlers]] [[Category:Hurling coaches]] [[Category:Hurling goalkeepers]] [[Category:Hurling managers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]]

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Anthony Carmody''' (born 1966) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Carmody played hurling at all grades as a student at [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]]. He was part of the school's senior team that lost to [[St Finbarr's College, Farranferris|St Finbarr's College]] in the final of the [[Dr Harty Cup]] in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Farna turn it on in second half|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=16 April 1984|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At club level, Carmody began his career at juvenile and underage levels with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]], winning a Limerick MAHC title in 1984, before progressing to adult level. Carmody's senior career coincided with a very successful era for Patrickswell and he won 11 [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medals in a 20-year period between 1983 and 2003.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dermot-crowe-no-one-could-have-predicted-how-far-three-patrickswell-players-on-the-2008-feile-team-would-travel/a777881461.html|title=Dermot Crowe: No one could have predicted how far three Patrickswell players on the 2008 Féile team would travel|publisher=Irish Independent|date=24 December 2023|access-date=20 April 2025|first=Dermot|last=Crowe}} His other club honours include two [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] medals, while he lined out at midfield when losing to [[Glenmore GAA|Glenmore]] in the [[1991 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1991 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=7 June 2009|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dermot-crowe-fallen-giants-restoring-parish-pride-after-wilderness-years/34430005.html|title=Dermot Crowe: Fallen giants restoring parish pride after wilderness years|publisher=Irish Independent|date=7 February 2016|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Carmody first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick's last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to the under-21 team and won consecutive [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] titles, before claiming an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after a 2-15 to 3-06 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|1987 final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/109109/Limerick-s-first-All-Ireland-U.html|title=Limerick's first All Ireland U-21 hurling title in 1987|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 September 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Carmody joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in 1987. He [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|captain]]ed the team during the 1991 season. Carmody claimed his only senior silverware in 1992 when Limerick won the [[National Hurling League]] title.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Carey's senior career coincided with a very successful era for Patrickswell and he won eight [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medals between 1984 and 1997.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/double-joy-at-well-as-careys-get-green-light/26192414.html|title=Double joy at 'Well as Careys get Green light|publisher=Irish Independent|date=6 March 1998|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} His other club honours include two [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] medals, while he lined out at centre-back when losing to [[Glenmore GAA|Glenmore]] in the [[1991 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1991 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=7 June 2009|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dermot-crowe-fallen-giants-restoring-parish-pride-after-wilderness-years/34430005.html|title=Dermot Crowe: Fallen giants restoring parish pride after wilderness years|publisher=Irish Independent|date=7 February 2016|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Carey first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick's last All-Ireland minor hurling title - He claimed his only senior silverware in 1992 when Limerick won the [[National Hurling League]] title.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Carey was on and off the team over the course of the following few years before being released from the panel for the final time in 1998. Éamonn Cregan.text:
{{Short description|Irish Gaelic footballer, hurler and manager}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=September 2015}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2026}} {{Infobox Gaelic games biography | code= Hurling | image = | name = Éamonn Cregan | irish = Éamonn Ó Críagáin | birth_date = {{birth date and age|df=yes|1945|5|21}} | birth_place = [[Limerick]], Ireland | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | nickname = Blondie{{citation needed|date=June 2025}} | occupation = Retired | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] | cl_years = 1963–1988 | cl_apps_points = | cl_county_h = 3 | cl_county_f = 8 | cl_province_h = | cl_all_ireland_h = | counties = [[Limerick county football team|Limerick '''(F)''']]
[[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick '''(H)''']] | ic_position_h = Centre-back/Left corner-forward | ic_position_f= Left wing-forward | ic_years = 1965–1971
1965–1983 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province_f = 0 | ic_province_h= 4 | ic_all_ireland_h= 1 | ic_all_ireland_f =0 | all_stars_f= 0 | all_stars_h= 3 | nhl = 1 | nfl = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = }} '''Éamonn Cregan''' (born 21 May 1945) is an Irish former [[Gaelic football]]er, [[hurling|hurler]] and [[Manager (Gaelic games)|manager]]. He is best remembered for his success with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]], as a player in the 1970s and then as manager of various club and inter-county teams in the 1980s and 1990s. Cregan was inducted into the GAA Hall of Fame in 2013.{{cite web|url= http://www.joe.ie/gaa/gaa-news/gaa-open-hall-of-fame-in-croke-park-0033979-1|title= GAA open Hall of Fame in Croke Park|date=12 February 2013|work= Joe.ie|accessdate=12 February 2013 }} ==Playing career== ===Club=== Cregan played his club [[hurling]] and football with his local club in [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] and enjoyed much success. He won his first senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county title]] with the club in 1968 and added a second three years later in 1971. Cregan won a third and final county medal in 1986. This was Cregan's last appearance in a county championship final. He also won 8 [[Limerick Senior Football Championship]] titles. ===Inter-county=== Cregan first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a [[dual player]] with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] minor hurling and football teams in the early 1960s. In 1963, he was appointed [[Captain (Gaelic games)|captain]] of the Limerick hurling team. That year Cregan's side defeated [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] by 4–12 to 5–4 to win a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] title. He later led his team out in the All-Ireland MHC final; however lost to [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by a scoreline of 4–10 to 2–7. Cregan also played with the Limerick minor football team, as well as later lining out with the county's under-21 teams. He had little success in these grades. Cregan made his debut with the Limerick senior hurling team in 1964 and he impressed immediately. He later gave up playing football with the county in an effort to concentrate on his hurling. Limerick hurling was in the doldrums at the time as the county hadn't won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (SHC) title since 1955. In 1970, Limerick's hurling fortunes started to change. That year Cregan's side reached the 'home' final of the [[National Hurling League]] with [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] providing the opposition. Limerick were trounced on that occasion by 2–17 to 0–7. This was the first of five consecutive league final appearances for Limerick and for Cregan. In 1971, Limerick were back in the league final. On this occasion [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] provided the opposition and an exciting game ensued. Limerick just about won the game by 3–12 to 3–11, giving Cregan a National League medal. His side reached the next three league finals; however, Limerick lost on all three occasions. Cregan was personally honoured in 1971 when he was named in the inaugural [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Stars]] team. He won a second consecutive All-Star in 1972. Two years later, in 1973, Limerick returned to the Munster SHC final. The opponent was Tipperary, and the game proved to be an exciting and controversial affair. Tipp were the favourites going into the game and they asserted their dominance early on. In spite of this, Limerick scored three goals in the first twenty-four minutes and trailed by 2–9 to 3–2 at half-time. Tipp ploughed on in the second-half; however, Cregan scored two decisive goals to put Limerick in the lead. As the game entered the dying minutes both sides were level. A Limerick shot appeared to have gone wide before it struck a Tipperary defender. In spite of this a 70-yard free was awarded. [[Richie Bennis]] scored the winning point, in spite of some reports that it trailed wide as it went over the bar. With that Limerick claimed the victory and Cregan won his first Munster SHC medal. Limerick were far from impressive when they defeated [[London county hurling team|London]] in the next game, setting up a meeting with the reigning champion [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] in the [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1973 All-Ireland SHC final]]. Cregan was switched from his usual forward position to centre-back where he marked Kilkenny's scorer in chief [[Pat Delaney (Kilkenny hurler)|Pat Delaney]]. Kilkenny were severely hampered by the absence of some of their greatest players. Limerick went on to win that game by 1–21 to 1–14. It was Cregan's first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (SHC) medal and Limerick's first since 1940. In 1974, Limerick maintained provincial dominance. Cregan captured a second Munster SHC medal following a 6–14 to 3–9 trouncing of [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]]. This victory allowed Cregan's side to advance directly to the [[1974 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1974 All-Ireland SHC final]], with Kilkenny providing the opposition again. 'The Cats' were back to full strength and set out for revenge. In spite of this Limerick stormed into an early lead; however, this was diminished as Pat Delaney, [[Eddie Keher]] and [[Mick Brennan (hurler)|Mick Brennan]] scored goals. Limerick lost that game by 3–19 to 1–13. Cregan's side contested the Munster SHC finals of 1975 and 1976; however, Cork won on both occasions, as Limerick went into decline. They were completely trounced again in 1979 on a score line of 2–14 to 0–9 as Cork won a record-equaling fifth Munster SHC title in-a-row. In 1980, Cork were going for an unprecedented sixth consecutive Munster SHC title. For the fourth time in six years Limerick provided the opposition in the provincial decider. After an exciting seventy minutes Cork's hopes were dashed by 2–14 to 2–10 as Cregan collected a third Munster SHC medal. This victory allowed Limerick a save passage to the [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1980 All-Ireland SHC final]], with [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] as opponent. Galway got off to a good start and took a 2–7 to 1–5 lead at half-time. Cregan had other ideas and single-handedly launched the Limerick counter-attack. Over the course of the game he scored 2–7, including an overhead goal and a point in which he showed the ball to [[Conor Hayes]] and nonchalantly drove the ball over the bar. It was not enough to stem the tide and Galway went on to win the game. It was the county's first All-Ireland SHC title since 1923 and, ironically, Limerick were the defeated team on that occasion as well. In spite of the defeat, Cregan was presented with a third All-Star award. At the [[1981 Irish general election|1981 general election]], Cregan was an unsuccessful [[Fianna Fáil]] candidate in the [[Limerick East (Dáil constituency)|Limerick East constituency]].{{cite web |title=Eamonn Cregan |url=https://electionsireland.org/candidate.cfm?ID=3374 |website=ElectionsIreland.org |access-date=21 July 2023}} Limerick retained the provincial crown in 1981. Clare were defeated on that occasion by 3–12 to 2–9, giving Cregan his fourth Munster SHC medal. The subsequent All-Ireland SHC semi-final saw Limerick again take on Galway. In a low-scoring game both sides finished level and a replay was necessary. The second game took place a fortnight later at [[Croke Park]], and it turned out to be an exciting affair. Both sides upped their game; however, Limerick still lost by 4–16 to 2–17. At this stage Cregan was in his 36th year and many players would contemplate retirement from the game. Cregan, however, continued playing for his county for another few seasons; however, Cork returned as the dominant force in Munster. He eventually retired from inter-county hurling in 1983. ===Provincial=== Cregan also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial hurling competition. He first played for his province in 1968 as Munster defeated [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] giving Cregan his first [[Railway Cup]] medal. He collected a second Railway Cup title in 1969. Cregan was a regular on the team throughout the 1970s; however, Leinster dominated the competition for the majority of the decade. He won a third and final Railway Cup medal in 1980. ==Managerial career== {{Infobox Gaelic games biography | name = Éamonn Cregan | image = | alt = | caption = | irish = | birth_date = | birth_place = | death_date = | death_place = | height = | height_ft = | height_in = | nickname = | occupation = | sport = | cl_position = | ic_position = | managing_years = 2007– | managing_club = Lixnaw | managing_winning_club = | managing_cl_all_ireland = 0 | managing_cl_province = 0 | managing_cl_county = 1 | managing_ic_county = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]]
[[Offaly county hurling team|Offaly]]
Limerick | managing_ic_years = 1986–1988
1992–1996
1997–2002 | managing_winning_counties = Offaly | managing_ic_province = 2 | managing_ic_all_ireland = 2 | managing_league = 1 }} In retirement from playing Cregan became involved in coaching and training teams. He served as manager of several inter-county and club sides. ===Offaly=== Cregan took charge of the Offaly senior inter-county team in late 1992. At the time Offaly were an up-and-coming hurling team in the championship; however, it would be 1994 before Cregan's charges first tasted success. That year Offaly contested the Leinster SHC final with [[Wexford county hurling team|Wexford]] providing the opposition. That game saw Cregan's side defeated Wexford by 1–18 to 0–14, giving Offaly a first [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]] (SHC) title under Cregan's tenure. The subsequent All-Ireland SHC semi-final saw Offaly defeat [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] by 2–13 to 1–10. Ironically, the 1994 All-Ireland SHC saw Offaly take on Cregan's own native-county of Limerick. The game was a close affair; however, Limerick went five points ahead with four minutes left in the game and it looked as if they were about to win a first title in twenty-one years. The next five minutes, however, produced one of the most exciting and explosive endings to an All-Ireland SHC final ever. [[Johnny Dooley (hurler)|Johnny Dooley]] was about to take a close-in free and was given the signal from Cregan to take a point. Dooley had only one thing on his mind and scored a goal to turn the game on its head. Limerick lost possession after the puck-out and Offaly rampaged up the field for another goal courtesy of [[Pat O'Connor (hurler)|Pat O'Connor]]. Four unanswered points followed and Offaly captured the victory by 3–16 to 2–13. The victory, however, came at a cost to Cregan. He was the first outside manager to defeat his own native-county in an All-Ireland SHC final, and, naturally, he had mixed feelings about the win. He appeared very calm at the final whistle, and seemed gutted that victory had come at the cost of beating his own county in the final. In 1995, Cregan was still Offaly manager as his team won a second consecutive Leinster SHC title. Their display on that occasion saw [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] being swept off the field by 2–16 to 2–5. It was a commendable performance and one that installed Offaly as favourites to retain the All-Ireland SHC title. Cregan's side defeated [[Down county hurling team|Down]] in the penultimate game of the championship, setting up an All-Ireland SHC final meeting with [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]]. It was a first ever championship meeting of the two sides. In an exciting game both sides were level for much of the game with no side taking an extensive lead. [[Éamonn Taaffe]], who entered the game unnoticed as a substitute, score a decisive goal for Clare with four minutes left on the clock. Johnny Dooley levelled for Offaly; however, [[Anthony Daly (hurler)|Anthony Daly]] and [[Jamesie O'Connor]] scored the final points for Clare to give them a 1–13 to 2–8 victory. In 1996 Cregan's side reached a third consecutive Leinster SHC final. Wexford provided the opposition on that occasion; however, the men from the Model County were regarded as the underdogs. In spite of this the [[Réabhlóid GAA|so-called hurling revolution]] continued as Wexford won by 2–23 to 2–15. Cregan resigned as manager shortly afterwards. ===Limerick=== Cregan first became involved in team management with his own native county in the mid-1980s. It was an unhappy period for Cregan and for his Limerick team. In spite of the successes in the early 1980s, Limerick did not even reach a Munster SHC final during his first term in charge. Almost ten years later, in 1997, Cregan was back at the helm of the Limerick senior hurling team. At the time Limerick had enjoyed two recent Munster Championship victories; however, they had not won an All-Ireland SHC title. Cregan's magic touch failed to work in Limerick; however, his side did contest the 2001 Munster SHC final. Tipperary provided the opposition on that occasion; however, Cregan's side lost the game by 2–16 to 1–17. This defeat did not mean that his side were out of the championship, as Limerick had one more chance in the All-Ireland SHC quarter-final. Wexford, however, won that game and that was the end. Cregan remained on for one more season in 2002. After a poor performance in the Munster SHC, he tendered his resignation, citing disagreements between himself and the Limerick County Board over [[dual player]]s.{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/2002/0326/limerick.html|title=Cregan resigns as Limerick manager|publisher=RTÉ|date=26 March 2002|access-date=11 September 2009}} Assistant coach [[Mossie Keane]] was named as his replacement, but, a few days later, Cregan was reinstated.{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/2002/0401/limerick.html|title=Cregan reinstated as Limerick boss|publisher=RTÉ|date=1 April 2002|access-date=11 September 2009}} He finally resigned in June 2002, after Limerick's poor performance in the All-Ireland SHC qualifiers led to a first round defeat by [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]].{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2002/0629/limerick.html|title=Cregan resigns as Limerick manager|publisher=RTÉ|date=29 June 2002|access-date=11 September 2009}} ===Lixnaw=== Cregan took over as manager of [[Kerry GAA]] club side [[Lixnaw GAA|Lixnaw]]. He won the 2007 [[Kerry Senior Hurling Championship|Senior County Championship]] in his first year in charge, when Lixnaw defeated [[Kilmoyley GAA|Kilmoyley]] by 1–15 to 2–6 in the final.{{cite web |url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/lixnaw-take-the-title-in-surprise-win-1117307.html |title=Lixnaw take the title in surprise win|work=Irish Independent|date=8 October 2007|access-date=11 September 2009}} ==Media career== Included TV work for the [[1995 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final]]. ==Honours== *In 2013, Cregan was inducted into the [[GAA Hall of Fame]]. *In May 2020, '''Barry Foley''' is an Irish sportsman. He plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and was a member at inter-county level of the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]] from 1996 until 2008.<ref>{{cite web
|title=Foley, Barry
|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=44480
|accessdate=2010-07-14
|date=15 November 1996
|author=Tom Morrison
|work=[[Hogan Stand]]
}}</ref>

==Early life==
Barry Foley was born in [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]] in on 12 May 1977. He was born into a family that had a strong association with hurling. His father and uncles all played for Patrickswell and one uncle, [[Seán Foley]], won an All-Ireland medal in 1973. Foley was educated locally and later attended secondary school in [[Limerick]]. Here he won a Harty Cup medal in 1993 and was named "Man of the Match" in the final.

==Playing career==
===Club===
Foley plays his club hurling with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]]. He has enjoyed much success with the club, winning county medals at under-14, under-15, under-16, minor and under-21 levels. In 1995, he won his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|senior county]] medal. He won another two county medals in 1996 and 1997 before winning his fourth and fifth county titles in 2000 and 2003. In 2006, Foley narrowly missed out on winning a sixth medal when Patrickswell were defeated by a single point by Bruree.

===Inter-county===
In the early 1990s, Foley played for both the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] minor and under-21 hurling teams but with little success. In 1996, he made his senior debut in a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] game against [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]]. Limerick later won the Munster final and Foley had his first senior inter-county success. In the subsequent [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] final, Foley's side lost to [[Wexford county hurling team|Wexford]]. The following year he won his first [[National Hurling League]] medal. However, since then, Limerick's senior hurling fortunes have taken a downturn and Foley has failed to add any more winners' medals to his collection.

'''Mark Foley''' (born 17 April 1975 in [[Cork (city)|Cork]], Ireland) is an Irish sportsperson.  He plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Adare GAA|Adare]] and was a member at inter-county level of the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]] from 1995 until 2009.

==Early life==
Mark Foley was born in [[Cork (city)|Cork]] in 1975 and when he was nine months old his family moved to [[Adare]], [[County Limerick]].  He was born into a family that had a great interest in [[Gaelic games]].  His father would later serve as a selector with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior hurling team.  Foley was educated locally and later attended [[Mary Immaculate College]] in [[Limerick]] where he studied to be a primary school teacher.  Here he played on both the college [[hurling]] and college [[Gaelic football|football]] teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickindependent.com/sport/sport/mark-foley,-captain,-limerick-senior-hurling-team/ |title=Mark Foley, captain, Limerick senior hurling team |date=23 January 2008 |accessdate=17 September 2009 |publisher=Limerick Independent |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090109185658/http://www.limerickindependent.com/sport/sport/mark-foley,-captain,-limerick-senior-hurling-team/ |archivedate=9 January 2009 }}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Club===
Foley plays his club [[hurling]] with his local [[Adare GAA|Adare]] team.  He has had much success with the club, winning under-12, under-14, under-16 and minor county medals throughout the late 1980s and early 1990s.  In 2001 and 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2002/1013/hurling.html |title=Adare and Four Roads win hurling titles |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=13 October 2002 |accessdate=17 September 2009 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Foley won back-to-back senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] medals with Adare.  They were beaten in the 2003 final by [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]]. In 2007 he (and Adare) won a third county senior championship and a fourth in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2008/1019/gaa.html|title=A round-up of Sunday's club games|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=19 October 2008|accessdate=17 September 2009}}</ref>

In early 2013 Foley played junior hurling with Castletown/Ballyagran the very same parish as where he run's the local pub, however there was mixed fortunes for the club as they won the ''South junior hurling'' championship but were then beaten in a county semi-final by local rivals Feenagh/Kilmeedy

On 30 December 2013 Foley was announced vice-chairman of Castletown/Ballyagran GAA club .

===Inter-county===
Foley has played hurling at all levels with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]].  In the early 1990s he played on both the minor and under-21 teams, however, he had little success.  He later joined the senior side and was a member of the panel when Limerick won the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] in 1994.  The team later lost the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] final to [[Offaly county hurling team|Offaly]] in what has become known as 'the five-minute final.'  In 1995 Foley made his championship debut against [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]], however, Limerick later lost the Munster final to [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]].  The following year he won his first Munster title as a full member of the team and Limerick later qualified to play [[Wexford county hurling team|Wexford]] in the All-Ireland final.  For the second time in three years Limerick left [[Croke Park]] empty handed.  There was some consolation for Foley as his performance in the championship earned him an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award and he was also crowned the [[All Stars Young Hurler of the Year]].

In 1997 Foley won a [[National Hurling League]] medal with Limerick, however, the following decade saw Limerick's senior hurling fortunes take a dramatic downturn.  In spite of this Foley received a second All-Star award in 2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2001/1129/allstars.html |title=Tipperary win seven All Stars |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=29 November 2001 |accessdate=17 September 2009 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Six years later in 2007 Limerick had an epic battle with Tipp in the provincial championship.  After a second replay Foley's side emerged victorious and qualified to play [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]] in the Munster final.  Although Limerick lost on that occasion the team showed that they were not a pushover.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2007/0708/waterford.html|title=Waterford 3–17 Limerick 1–14|date=8 July 2007|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|accessdate=8 September 2009}}</ref> Limerick later gained their revenge on Waterford by defeating them in the All-Ireland semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2007/0812/limerick.html|title=Limerick 5–11 Waterford 2–15|date=12 August 2007|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|accessdate=8 September 2009}}</ref> This victory allowed Foley's side to play [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] in the championship decider.  Unfortunately, Limerick got off to a bad start with goalkeeper [[Brian Murray (hurler)|Brian Murray]] letting in two goals in the first ten minutes.  'The Cats', however, went on to win the game by six points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2007/0902/kilkenny.html|title=Kilkenny 2–19 Limerick 1–15|date=2 September 2007|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|accessdate=8 September 2009}}</ref>

In the 2009 All-Ireland Championship quarter-final against [[Dublin county hurling team|Dublin]], Foley became Limerick's most "capped" player of all time.  It was his 46th Championship appearance for Limerick, overtaking [[Timmy Ryan]]'s record which had stood since 1946.<ref name="trib caps"/> He led his team as far as the All-Ireland semi-finals before being knocked out by Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/corbett-adds-insult-to-limerick-humiliation-1861686.html|title=Corbett adds insult to Limerick humiliation|date=17 August 2009|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|accessdate=17 September 2009}}</ref>

===Provincial===
Foley has also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the [[Railway Cup]] inter-provincial competition.  He captured a winners medal in this competition in 1997 as Munster defeated [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]].

'''Paudie Fitzmaurice''' (born 16 November 1949) is a [[hurling|hurler]] from [[Killeedy]] in [[County Limerick]], Ireland, who featured in [[Limerick GAA#Hurling|Limerick hurling]] teams of the 1970s. Fitzmaurice was part of the [[Limerick county hurling team]] which won the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] in 1973,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.doonbleisce.com/limerick_1973_all.htm |title=LIMERICK 1973 ALL |publisher=Doonbleisce.com |date=2 September 1973 |accessdate=18 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gaa.ie/page/hurling_results_1971_1990.html |title=Hurling Results 1971–1990 | Cumann Lúthchleas Gael Official Website |publisher=GAA.ie |accessdate=18 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120208095019/http://gaa.ie/page/hurling_results_1971_1990.html |archivedate=8 February 2012 }}</ref>) as well as in the 1974, 1980 and 1981 teams. He was captain when Limerick won the [[1981 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final]].<ref>[http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/seniorhurling.html Munster Senior Hurling Teams – Munster GAA Web Site] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070830175225/http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/seniorhurling.html |date=30 August 2007 }}</ref> He is a two-time National League winner,<ref>[http://www.sligoweekender.ie/news/story.asp?j=11140 Sligo Weekender: Paudie’s new dawn?] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927235227/http://www.sligoweekender.ie/news/story.asp?j=11140 |date=27 September 2007 }}</ref> and finished as top scorer when captaining [[Maynooth College]] to victory in the Fitzgibbon Cup in 1974.<ref>[http://cao.gaa.ie/fitz_scorers.html Fitzgibbon Cup Final Top Scorers<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070831154228/http://cao.gaa.ie/fitz_scorers.html |date=31 August 2007 }}</ref><ref>[http://cao.gaa.ie/fitz_capt.html Fitzgibbon Cup Winning Captains<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070831154029/http://cao.gaa.ie/fitz_capt.html |date=31 August 2007 }}</ref> His achievements as a player were recognised in 1984 when Fitzmaurice received an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gaa.ie/page/hurling_all_stars_80s.html |title=Hurling All Stars 80's | Cumann Lúthchleas Gael Official Website |publisher=GAA.ie |accessdate=18 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090427092500/http://www.gaa.ie/page/hurling_all_stars_80s.html |archivedate=27 April 2009 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Fitzmaurice continued to play competitive hurling for his native [[Killeedy]] until 1996.<ref>[http://newcastlewestgaa.csn.ul.ie/1996(JB).htm 1996]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070513040120/http://newcastlewestgaa.csn.ul.ie/1996%28JB%29.htm |date=13 May 2007 }}</ref>

Fitzmaurice was named manager of the [[Sligo GAA|Sligo hurling team]] in January 2003.{{cn|date=September 2026}} but resigned after harsh criticism in May of that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/2003/0506/sligo.html |title=RTÉ Sport: Fitzmaurice quits Sligo hurling post |publisher=RTÉ |date=6 May 2003 |accessdate=18 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://archives.tcm.ie/sligoweekender/2003/05/13/story12467.asp |title=Sligo Weekender – 2003/05/13: Chairman seeks to end crisis |publisher=Archives.tcm.ie |accessdate=18 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120510102738/http://archives.tcm.ie/sligoweekender/2003/05/13/story12467.asp |archivedate=10 May 2012 }}</ref>

He trained for the priesthood in [[St. Patrick's College, Maynooth]], as did his brother Fr. [[Willie Fitzmaurice]], who also played hurling for Limerick.

==Teaching==
Fitzmaurice attended [[Trinity College Dublin]],{{Citation needed|date=October 2007}} and is a former member of staff at [[St. Munchin's College]], where he taught mathematics, applied mathematics and physics. He currently{{when|date=March 2021}} teaches mathematics and hurling at [[Castletroy College]] in Limerick. Before that, he served as institute chaplain at [[Limerick Institute of Technology]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20030430062646/http://www.lit.ie/pdf%20files/95-98.pdf Annual Reports of the Regional Technical College of Limerick 1995-1998]</ref>

==Hurling style==
Paudie and his brother [[Willie Fitzmaurice|Willie]] were noted for their unusual hurling technique. When striking the [[sliotar]], the Fitzmaurice brothers did not bend their elbows.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AgAKhf4soZM  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/AgAKhf4soZM |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=1980 All-Ireland Hurling Final Galway Limerick 1st half |via=YouTube |date=13 February 2011 |accessdate=18 December 2011}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sioFyPJMnLc  |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/sioFyPJMnLc |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=1980 All-Ireland Hurling Final Galway Limerick 2nd half |via=YouTube |accessdate=18 December 2011}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

'''Willie Fitzmaurice''' (born 4 December 1946) was a [[hurling|hurler]] from [[Killeedy]], south of [[Limerick]], who played with the Limerick teams in the 1970s and 1980s<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/seniorhurling.html |title=Munster Senior Hurling Teams – Munster GAA Web Site<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=15 May 2008 |archive-date=19 July 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719154803/http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/seniorhurling.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 1998, he became a county team selector along with former teammates [[Éamonn Cregan]] and [[David Punch]]<ref>[http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1998/04/28/shead.htm Irish Sport News, 25 April 1998<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> and advocated the retention of the back-door system.<ref>[http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1998/10/15/shead.htm Irish Sport News, 15 October 1998<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

He was the parish priest in [[Kilmallock]] in 2008;<ref>{{Cite news |title=The bells of progress|last=Connor |first=John O |work=The Munster Express |date=1 May 2008 |url= https://www.munster-express.ie/opinion/tales-of-the-tellurians/from-moyross-to-the-dunmore-road/}}</ref>  as such he celebrated the mass of his deceased niece, Elizabeth Gubbins, who died in the controversial Vernelli hit-and-run case in [[Rome]].<ref>[http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/2008/03/26/story58683.asp Irish Examiner - 2008/03/26: Hit-and-run pictures ‘intensified pain and loss’<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[http://www.limerickblogger.org/blog/2008/04/17/new-twist-in-vernarelli-hit-and-run-case The Limerick Blogger - latest Limerick news and Limerick events » Blog Archive » New twist in Vernarelli Hit-and-run case<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

He is the brother of Limerick hurler [[Paudie Fitzmaurice]].{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

==Hurling style==
The Fitzmaurice brothers were noted for their unusual hurling technique: when striking the [[sliotar]], the Fitzmaurice brothers did not bend their elbows, making it difficult for their opponents to hook them.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AgAKhf4soZM YouTube - 1980 All-Ireland Hurling Final Galway Limerick 1st half<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sioFyPJMnLc YouTube - 1980 All-Ireland Hurling Final Galway Limerick 2nd half<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

'''Leonard Enright''' (1 July 1953 – 2 November 2018) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a full-back for club side [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]], at inter-county level with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]] and at inter-provincial level with [[Munster GAA|Munster]].

==Playing career==
===Patrickswell===

Enright first played for [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] at under-16 level on a team trained by [[Richie Bennis]]. He subsequently progressed onto the club's minor and under-21 teams before eventually making his breakthrough at senior level.

On 23 September 1979, Enright was at right wing-back when he won his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Championship]] medal after a 2-16 to 0-16 defeat of [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/galway-entering-the-lion-s-den-1.649526|title=Galway entering the lion's den|publisher=Irish Times|date=11 September 2010|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Tom|last=Humphries}}</ref>

After surrendering their title and failing to make the final stage over the following two seasons, Patrickswell qualified for the final once again on 12 September 1982. Enright was at full-back for that game and won a second County Championship medal after a 0-17 to 0-15 defeat of [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/underdogs-bruree-hope-to-humble-fancied-well-15782.html|title=Underdogs Bruree hope to humble fancied ’Well|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=14 October 2006|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Enright was appointed captain of the Patrickswell senior hurling team for the 1983 season. On 11 September 1983, he won a third County Championship medal when he captained the team to a 1-13 to 1-07 defeat of [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/220521/limerick-shc-final-preview-recalling-ballybrown-and-patrickswell-in-1983.html|title=Limerick SHC final preview – recalling Ballybrown and Patrickswell in 1983|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=20 October 2016|access-date=3 November 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

Patrickswell secured a third successive County Championship title on 14 October 1984, with Enright winning his fourth championship title overall after a 4-13 to 3-05 defeat of [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] in the final.

On 13 September 1987, Enright won a fifth County Championship medal following Patrickswell's 1-17 to 3-10 defeat of Ballybrown in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/magnificent-patrickswell-still-pride-of-the-parish-427216.html|title=Magnificent Patrickswell still pride of the parish|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=24 October 2016|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

Patrickswell retained the championship on 16 October 1988 following a 4-10 to 2-06 defeat of Cappamore in a final replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/cappamore-club-anniversary-sparks-thoughts-of-better-times-192023.html|title=Cappamore club anniversary sparks thoughts of better times|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=27 April 2012|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> It was Enright's sixth championship winners' medal. He ended the year by winning a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club Championship]] medal after Patrickswell's 3-13 to 2-13 defeat of [[Mount Sion GAA|Mount Sion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/cork-champions-move-in-on-target-1.395788|title=Cork champions move in on target|publisher=Irish Times|date=28 November 2003|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

Enright won his seventh and final County Championship medal on 21 October 1990 after a 1-15 to 1-12 defeat of [[Adare GAA|Adare]]. He later claimed a second Munster Club Championship medal following an 0-08 to 0-06 defeat of [[Éire Óg, Inis GAA|Éire Óg]]. On 17 March 1991, Patrickswell lined out against [[Glenmore GAA|Glenmore]] in the [[1991 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]]. Enright scored a point from play, however, Patrickswell suffered a 1-13 to 0-12 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/trip-down-memory-lane-for-cregan-1.138123|title=Trip down memory lane for Cregan|publisher=Irish Times|date=4 March 1998|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Seán|last=Moran}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Enright first played for Limerick when he was selected in goal for the minor team. He enjoyed little success in this grade before progressing onto the Limerick under-21 team in 1972. His three-year tenure in this grade also ended without championship success.

====Senior====

Enright made his first appearance for the Limerick senior hurling team when he lined out in goal on 7 March 1971 in a 1-17 to 2-07 defeat of [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[National Hurling League]]. He ended the campaign by winning his first league medal as a substitute. Enright was dropped from the Limerick team at the end of 1972 and missed out on the team's [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] success in 1973.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/bennis-recalls-the-heroes-of-73-231789.html|title=Bennis recalls the heroes of ’73|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 May 2013|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

After a three-year gap, Enright returned to the Limerick panel and made his [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] debut at midfield in a 2-16 to 3-13 draw with [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] on 6 July 1975. After two seasons at midfield he became disillusioned and left the panel. Enright gave up hurling altogether, switched codes to [[rugby union]] and played with [[Young Munster]] in 1977 and 1978.

A career-ending eye injury to [[Pat Hartigan]] in 1979 paved the way for Enright's return to the Limerick senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/sad-tales-of-unlimited-heartbreak-have-hurt-limerick-for-over-four-decades-37227927.html|title=Sad tales of unlimited heartbreak have hurt Limerick for over four decades|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 August 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}</ref> He initially played in his usual position at midfield before later becoming the first-choice full-back in succession to the injured Hartigan.

On 20 July 1980, Enright won his first Munster Championship medal after a 2-14 to 2-10 defeat of reigning champions [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final. This victory secured Limerick a place in the [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] against [[Galway GAA|Galway]] on 7 September 1980. Enright played at full-back, however, in spite of a personal scoring tally of 2-07 for [[Éamonn Cregan]], Limerick suffered a 2-15 to 3-09 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/one-day-in-september-1980-galway-s-day-of-deliverance-1.3599495|title=One day in September 1980: Galway’s day of deliverance|publisher=Irish Times|date=18 August 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Keith|last=Duggan}}</ref> Enright ended the season by winning his first [[GAA All Stars Awards|All Star award]].

Enright won a second successive Munster Championship medal on 5 July 1981 after a 3-12 to 2-09 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final. He ended the season with a second successive All Star award.

Enright was appointed captain of the Limerick senior team for the 1983 season. After losing the National League final to [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], Limerick's season came to an end with a Munster semi-final replay defeat by Cork. In spite of a trophy-less season, Enright ended the year by winning a third All Star award in four seasons.

After retaining the captaincy for the 1984 season, Enright guided the Limerick team to a second successive league final appearance. A 3-16 to 1-09 defeat of Wexford gave Enright a second National League medal and a first won on the field of play.

On 14 April 1985, Enright won a third National League medal following Limerick's 3-12 to 1-07 defeat of Clare in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/dual-dilemma-the-limerick-experience-1.313622|title=Dual dilemma: The Limerick experience|publisher=Irish Times|date=18 June 2001|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>  It was his second successive title as captain of the team.

Enright played his last championship game for Limerick on 5 June 1988, when he captained the team to a 0-16 to 0-08 defeat by Tipperary.

===Munster===

Enright was first selected at full-back for the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] team in 1981. He retained his position on the team for five successive seasons and won three [[Railway Cup]] medals during that time after defeats of [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] in 1981 and 1984 and [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] in 1985.

==Personal life==

Outside of his sporting life Enright worked as a caretaker with [[Mary Immaculate College]]. He was married to Birdie and had three sons and a daughter.

Enright died at the Milford Care Centre on 2 November 2018, just hours after his induction into the [[GAA Hall of Fame]] was celebrated at the annual All Star Awards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/former-limerick-hurler-leonard-enright-passes-away-aged-65-882992.html|title=Former Limerick hurler Leonard Enright passes away aged 65|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 November 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Denise|last=O'Donoghue}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-legend-and-threetime-all-star-leonard-enright-passes-away-37487977.html|title=Limerick legend and three-time All Star Leonard Enright passes away|publisher=Irish Independent|date=3 November 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/leonard-enright-rip-4320895-Nov2018/|title=Limerick legend: Three-time All-Star hurler Leonard Enright dies aged 65|publisher=The 42|date=3 November 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Paul|last=Dollery}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/292120?county=National|title="A hero, a legend" - three-time Limerick All-Star Leonard Enright passes away|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=3 November 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/1102/1008358-former-limerick-hurler-leonard-enright-dies-aged-65/|title= Former Limerick hurler Leonard Enright dies aged 65|publisher=RTÉ News|date=3 November 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-star-limerick-full-back-leonard-enright-dies-aged-65-1.3685633|title=All Star Limerick full back Leonard Enright dies aged 65|publisher=Irish Times|date=3 November 2018|accessdate=3 November 2018|first=Seán|last=Moran}}</ref>
