'''Edmond "Ned" Cregan''' (25 January 1901 – 23 August 1972) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a left wing-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://homepage.eircom.net/~monageagaa/page25.html|title=Ned Cregan (1901-1972)|publisher=Monagea GAA|date=|accessdate=5 May 2011}}</ref>

Cregan joined the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1928|1928 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement prior to the start of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1936|1936 championship]]. During that time he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and two [[National Hurling League]] medals. Cregan was an All-Ireland runner-up on two occasions.

At club level Cregan enjoyed a lengthy career with [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]].

Cregan's son, [[Éamonn Cregan|Éamonn]], was an All-Ireland medallist with Limerick in 1973.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/martin-kiely-column-eamon-cregan-the-greatest-of-them-all-1-4838393|title=Éamonn Cregan, the greatest of them all|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=2 March 2013|accessdate=20 May 2013|first=Martin|last=Kiely}}</ref> His other sons, Mickey and Conor, also played with Limerick.

==Playing career==
===Club===

Cregan played his club hurling with [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]] and enjoyed some success during a career that spanned three decades.

His activities during the [[Irish War of Independence|War of Independence]] impacted on his club hurling career, however, he won a number of West Limerick championship medals during the club's most successful period.

===Inter-county===

Cregan first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the Limerick junior hurling team in 1927. It was a successful year for the team as a 4-4 to 2-2 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the decider gave him a [[Munster Junior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal. Limerick were later defeated by [[Meath GAA|Meath]] in the "home" All-Ireland final.

The following year Cregan made his debut in the senior ranks with Limerick. The team had gone into decline since last winning the provincial crown in 1923 as [[Cork GAA|Cork]] dominated the southern province in the late twenties.

In 1933 Limerick made the breakthrough. A 3-7 to 2-2 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] gave Cregan his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal. Although the game was played in [[Thurles]] the result was decided in [[Clonmel]] as the game had to be abandoned because of a pitch invasion. Since Limerick were winning the game comfortably the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]] decided to award the Munster title to Limerick. Cregan's side subsequently faced reigning champions [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland decider. The game was a close one; however, Kilkenny sealed the victory with a great solo-run goal by [[Johnny Dunne]] in the last ten minutes. A 1-7 to 0-6 score line gave Kilkenny a second consecutive All-Ireland victory.

1934 began with Limerick bouncing back from this defeat by claiming the [[National Hurling League]] title. Cregan later collected a second Munster medal following a 4-8 to 2-5 defeat of Waterford. [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] provided Limerick's opposition in the subsequent All-Ireland final and, as it turned out, the game was a dramatic spectacle. Dublin trailed by five points with five minutes left, however, they fought back to draw 2-7 to 3-4. The replay turned out to be an even closer affair as well with both sides level with two minutes to go. Points from [[Mick Mackey]] and [[Jackie O'Connell]] and a fourth goal from [[Dave Clohessy]] secured a 5-2 to 2-6 victory for Limerick and an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal for Cregan.

Cregan captured a second consecutive National League medal in 1935 before Limerick completely powered their way through the provincial series of games. A 5-5 to 1-4 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the provincial decider gave him a third successive Munster medal. Kilkenny turned out to be Limerick's opponents in the subsequent All-Ireland final and, once again, the game was a close affair. Limerick were the red-hot favourites as they were the reigning National League and All-Ireland champions and had played a remarkable 31 games without defeat. In spite of rain falling throughout the entire game both sides served up a great game. At the beginning of the second-half [[Lory Meagher]] sent over a huge point from midfield giving Kilkenny a lead which they would not surrender. Mick Mackey smashed a free to the net, however, his final attack to secure a win was foiled by [[Paddy Larkin]]. Kilkenny held on to win the game on a score line of 2-5 to 2-4.

Cregan retired from hurling following the completion of a tour of the [[United States]] in early 1936

'''Peter Cregan''' (13 May 1918 – 12 August 2004) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a goalkeeper for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=40501|title=Peter Cregan|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=31 August 2004|accessdate=7 May 2011}}</ref>

Born in [[Croom, County Limerick]], Cregan first appeared on the inter-county scene at the age of sixteen with the Limerick minor team. He made his senior debut during the [[1937 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1937 championship]]. Cregan immediately became a regular member of the starting fifteen and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals, one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal and one [[National Hurling League]] medal.

As a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team on a number of occasions, Cregan won four [[Railway Cup]] medals. At club level he was twice a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medallist with [[Croom GAA|Croom]].

Cregan retired before to the start of the [[1947 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1947 championship]].

'''Kevin Downes''' (born 14 October 1991) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He usually lines out as a full-forward.

==Playing career==
===Ardscoil Rís===

Downes first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. Having played in every grade as a hurler, he was full-forward on the college's senior hurling team. On 11 March 2010, Downes scored 1-02 from play when Ardscoil Rís defeated Thurles CBS in the final of the [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ard-scoil-ris-end-harty-cup-marathon-with-historic-victory-114301.html|title=Ard Scoil Rís end Harty Cup marathon with historic victory|date=12 March 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 3 April, he was switched to left wing-forward for the All-Ireland final against [[St. Kieran's College]]. Downes was held scoreless in the 2–11 to 2–08 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/brennans-strike-foils-ardscoil-bid-26646769.html|title=Brennan's strike foils Ardscoil bid|date=4 April 2010|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

===NUI Galway===

During his studies at [[NUI Galway]], Downes was selected for the college's senior hurling team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/ucc-ucd-ul-fitzgibbon-cup-wit-nuig-775579-Jan2013/|title=Here's your 2013 Fitzgibbon Cup Guide: Part 2|date=31 January 2013|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He was a regular member of the starting fifteen during the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] and also served as chairman of the club.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

===Na Piarsaigh===

Downes joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the under-21 grades as a [[dual player]] before eventually joining the club's top adult teams.

On 2 October 2011, Downes scored 1-01 from full-forward in Na Piarsaigh's 2–18 to 0–13 defeat of [[Adare GAA|Adare]] to win their very first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Championship]] title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dowling-fires-na-piarsaigh-to-promised-land-26778085.html|title=Dowling fires Na Piarsaigh to promised land|date=3 October 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keyes}}</ref> On 4 December 2012, he won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal following a 1–13 to 0–09 defeat of [[Crusheen GAA|Crusheen]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/piarsaigh-young-guns-come-of-age-176100.html|title=Piarsaigh young guns come of age|date=5 December 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=9 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

After surrendering their titles the following year, Downes won a second Limerick Championship medal after lining out at centre-forward when Na Piarsaigh defeated Adare by 0–14 to 0–12 on 6 October 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/downes-sets-the-tone-for-na-piarsaigh-to-grind-it-out-29639434.html|title=Downes sets the tone for Na Piarsaigh to grind it out|date=7 October 2013|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> He was retained at centre-forward for the subsequent [[2013–14 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]], which culminated on 24 November 2014 with him winning a second provincial medal after scoring a goal in the 4–14 to 0–08 defeat of [[Sixmilebridge GAA|Sixmilebridge]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/powerful-piarsaighs-blistering-pace-too-much-for-tired-bridge-250662.html|title=Powerful Piarsaigh's blistering pace too much for tired Bridge|date=25 November 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Downes won a third Limerick Championship medal on 11 October 2015 after a 1–22 to 4–12 defeat of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in the final. He top scored with 1-05 and ended the game as [[man of the match]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> Downes missed Na Piarsaigh's subsequent Munster Championship final defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]] due to a concussion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 17 March 2016, he won an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] medal after scoring 1–02 in Na Piarsaigh's 2–25 to 2–14 defeat of [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] in the [[2016 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

On 15 October 2017, Downes won a fourth Limerick Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 1–22 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He won a third Munster Championship medal on 19 November when Na Piarsaigh defeated Ballygunner by 3–15 to 2–10 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/late-na-piarsaigh-surge-sweeps-aside-ballygunner-in-scrappy-munster-final-36333884.html|title=Late Na Piarsaigh surge sweeps aside Ballygunner in scrappy Munster final|date=19 November 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, Downes was named at full-forward by played much of the match at left corner-forward when Na Piarsaigh suffered a 2–17 to 1–17 defeat by [[Cuala GAA|Cuala]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

On 27 October 2018, Downes won a fifth Limerick Championship medal following Na Piarsaigh's 2–22 to 3–10 defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/boss-beary-points-to-experience-of-troops-as-na-piarsaigh-impress-again-37468758.html|title=Boss Beary points to experience of troops as Na Piarsaigh impress again|date=29 October 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=1 November 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Downes first played for Limerick when he was selected for the minor team in advance of the [[2008 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2008 Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=93906|title=Minor side named|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=29 April 2008|accessdate=13 June 2011}}</ref> He made his first appearance on 30 April when he scored seven points in a 3–21 to 1–12 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. Limerick's championship ended with a defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in a play-off, however, Downes ended the season as Limerick's top scorer.

Downes was eligible for the minor grade again the following year. After a second consecutive defeat to Tipperary at the quarter-final stage, he played his last game for Limerick on 5 June 2009 in a 4–08 to 1–14 defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in a play-off.

After progressing onto the Limerick under-21 team, he made his first appearance on 14 July 2010 when he came on as a substitute and scored two points in Limerick's 1–15 to 1–12 defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2010 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].

Downes broke onto the starting fifteen of the Limerick under-21 team during the [[2011 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2011 Munster Championship]] and was appointed captain of the team. On 3 August, he scored a point from full-forward when Limerick defeated Cork by 4–20 to 1–27 after extra-time to win the Munster Championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hannon-on-the-mark-to-edge-thriller-26758064.html|title=Hannon on the mark to edge thriller|date=4 August 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

Downes played his last game for the Limerick under-21 team on 18 July 2012. He scored two points from full-forward in a 1–16 to 1–11 defeat by Tipperary in the Munster Championship semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20201283.html|title=Maher ends Treaty defence|date=19 July 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

====Senior====

On 13 February 2011, Downes made his first appearance for the Limerick senior team. He scored a point in Limerick's 2–09 to 0–06 defeat of Clare in the [[2011 National Hurling League|National League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-step-up-to-the-plate-for-ogrady-26695360.html|title=Limerick step up to the plate for O'Grady|date=14 February 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 30 April, he scored 1-02 from play when Limerick defeated Clare by 4–12 to 2–13 to win the Division 2 title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}}</ref> Downes made his first championship appearance on 12 June. He top scored for Limerick 2–01 in the 3–15 to 3–14 defeat by Waterford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-mop-up-mullanes-late-winner-keeps-waterford-alive-154390-Jun2011/|title=GAA Mop-up: Mullane's late winner keeps Waterford alive|date=12 June 2011|publisher=The 42|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=Niall|last=Kelly}}</ref>

On 14 July 2013, Downes lined out in his first [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster Championship final]]. He started the game on the bench but was introduced as a 65th-minute substitute and scored two points in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of Cork and a first title in 17 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

On 2 August 2016, Downes tore his cruciate in a club football game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/kevin-downes-munster-hurling-3707007-Nov2017/|title=From torn cruciate in club football game to Munster hurling champion in the space of 15 months|date=20 November 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> The injury ruled him out of Limerick's 2017 league and championship campaigns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/kevin-downes-counting-his-blessings-after-cruciate-woe/|title=Kevin Downes counting his blessings after cruciate woe|date=14 March 2018|publisher=GAA website|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

Downes rejoined the Limerick senior panel in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-panel-john-kiely-3700398-Nov2017/|title=Downes back from cruciate, Reidy back from Kildare and U21 winners added to Limerick panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, he was an unused substitute when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

On 2 February 2019, Downes made his first appearance for Limerick in over 30 months when he lined out at full-forward in Limerick's 1–21 to 1–14 defeat of Clare in the [[2019 National Hurling League|National League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-3-4473497-Feb2019/|title=Impressive Limerick come from behind to see off Tipperary|publisher=The 42|date=2 February 2019|accessdate=24 March 2019|first=John|last=Fallon}}</ref>

'''Patrick Enright''' (11 April 1926 – 12 October 2009) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a full-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/community/paddy_enright_rip_1_2190632|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120903160903/http://www.limerickleader.ie/community/paddy_enright_rip_1_2190632|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 September 2012|title=Paddy Enright RIP|work=The Limerick Leader|date=19 November 2009|accessdate=18 October 2011}}</ref>

Enright was a stalwart of the Limerick team throughout the 1950s. During that time he won one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/winning-teams/sh_teams/|title=Munster Senior Hurling Final Winners|work=[[Munster GAA]]|accessdate=18 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100107012735/http://munster.gaa.ie/winning-teams/sh_teams/|archive-date=7 January 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At club level, Enright won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|club championship]] winners' medal with his local [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] club.

'''Shane Dowling''' (born 21 February 1993) is an Irish hurler who plays as a goalkeeper for club side [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and previously as a half-forward at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==
===College===

Dowling first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. Having played in every grade as a hurler, he was centre-forward on the college's senior hurling team. On 11 March 2010, Dowling scored a point from play when Ardscoil Rís defeated Thurles CBS in the final of the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ard-scoil-ris-end-harty-cup-marathon-with-historic-victory-114301.html|title=Ard Scoil Rís end Harty Cup marathon with historic victory|date=12 March 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref>

On 27 February 2011, Dowling was again at centre-forward when Ardscoil Rís retained the Harty Cup title after a 3–19 to 0–03 defeat of [[C.B.S. Charleville]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/awesome-ardscoil-storm-to-harty-title-26709031.html|title=Awesome Ardscoil storm to Harty title|date=28 February 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref>

===Club===

Dowling joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the under-16, minor and under-21 grades.

On 2 October 2011, Dowling scored 1-10 from right corner-forward in Na Piarsaigh's 2–18 to 0–13 defeat of [[Adare GAA|Adare]] to win their first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/the-famine-finishes-for-na-piarsaigh-in-fine-style-1.612851|title=The famine finishes for Na Piarsaigh in fine style|date=3 October 2011|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=31 July 2018}}</ref> He later won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal following a 1–13 to 0–09 defeat of [[Crusheen GAA|Crusheen]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/piarsaigh-young-guns-come-of-age-176100.html|title=Piarsaigh young guns come of age|date=5 December 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=9 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

After surrendering their titles the following year, Dowling won a second Limerick Championship medal at midfield when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Adare GAA|Adare]] by 0–14 to 0–12 on 6 October 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/downes-sets-the-tone-for-na-piarsaigh-to-grind-it-out-29639434.html|title=Downes sets the tone for Na Piarsaigh to grind it out|date=7 October 2013|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> He was switched to full-forward for the subsequent Munster Championship, which culminated with him winning a second provincial medal after a 4–14 to 0–08 defeat of [[Sixmilebridge GAA|Sixmilebridge]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/powerful-piarsaighs-blistering-pace-too-much-for-tired-bridge-250662.html|title=Powerful Piarsaigh's blistering pace too much for tired Bridge|date=25 November 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Dowling won a third Limerick Championship medal on 11 October 2015 after a 1–22 to 4–12 defeat of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> Later that season he won a third Munster medal after scoring 1–04 in a 2–18 to 2–11 defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 17 March 2016, Dowling won an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] by 2–25 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

On 15 October 2017, Dowling won a fourth Limerick Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 1–22 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018}}</ref> He was substituted in the 43rd minute after picking up an injury. Scans initially showed cartilage damage, but during surgery a fracture was also discovered inside his knee which ended his participation in the Munster Championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/piarsaigh-talisman-shane-dowling-out-of-rockies-clash-462148.html|title=Piarsaigh talisman Shane Dowling out of Rockies clash|date=3 November 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Dowling's participation in the All-Ireland series was also in doubt, however, he was introduced as a substitute in the All-Ireland semi-final against [[Slaughtneil GAC|Slaughtneil]] and set up a goal for [[Kevin Downes (hurler)|Kevin Downes]] before scoring his own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/shane-dowling-limerick-hurling-3845662-Feb2018/|title='This day last week I broke down to tears in Na Piarsaigh' - from injury to All-Ireland semi-final win|date=11 February 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, he was at midfield when Na Piarsaigh were defeated by [[Cuala GAA|Cuala]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

On 27 October 2018, Dowling won a fifth Limerick Championship medal after scoring 0–12 in Na Piarsaigh's 2–22 to 3–10 defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/boss-beary-points-to-experience-of-troops-as-na-piarsaigh-impress-again-37468758.html|title=Boss Beary points to experience of troops as Na Piarsaigh impress again|date=29 October 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=1 November 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}}</ref>
He coaches the under 14’ at his club and has brought them to win one county championships in under 13 and feile in under 14

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

Dowling first played for Limerick at minor level as a sixteen-year-old. He made his first appearance for the team on 29 April 2009, replacing [[John Fitzgibbon (Limerick hurler)|John Fitzgibbon]] at half-time in a 1–21 to 0–11 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/banner-day-for-mcgrath-as-vins-go-through-26532352.html|title=Banner day for McGrath as Vins go through|date=30 April 2009|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=8 August 2018}}</ref> He was eligible for the minor grade for the following two seasons, however, Limerick faced respective defeats by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] and Waterford.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/131104|title=Munster MHC: Banner book final spot|date=26 June 2010|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=8 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/bennett-edges-deise-home-in-epic-battle-159057.html|title=Bennett edges Déise home in epic battle|date=27 June 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 August 2018|first=John|last=Murphy}}</ref>

In his final year on the minor team, Dowling was drafted onto the Limerick under-21 team. On 3 August 2011, he scored seven points, including six frees, when Limerick defeated [[Cork GAA|Cork]] by 4–20 to 1–27 in the [[2011 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|final]] of the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hannon-on-the-mark-to-edge-thriller-26758064.html|title=Hannon on the mark to edge thriller|date=4 August 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

Dowling was appointed captain of the Limerick under-21 hurling team during his fourth and final season on the team in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/shane-dowling-limerick-u21-1497303-Jun2014/|title=Senior star Dowling to captain Limerick U21 team that includes 3 Munster minor winners|date=3 June 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

====Senior====

Dowling made his senior debut for Limerick on 25 February 2012 in a 2–24 to 1-13 [[2012 National Hurling League|National Hurling League]] defeat by Clare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/banner-avalanche-levels-limerick-185216.html|title=Banner 'avalanche' levels Limerick|date=27 February 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> Later that season he made his first [[2012 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] appearance in a 2–20 to 1–19 defeat by Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaelic-football/dowling-set-for-limerick-debut-26856922.html|title=Dowling set for Limerick debut|date=24 May 2012|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/treaty-debuts-for-allis-and-dowling-194968.html|title=Treaty debuts for Allis and Dowling|date=24 May 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2012, Dowling scored 3–09 in an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship qualifiers|All-Ireland Qualifier]] defeat of [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/article/index/172363|title=SHC Qualifier: Limerick demolish Antrim with record win|date=30 June 2012|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=8 August 2018}}</ref> It was the highest personal tally for any player in that year's championship.

After playing a number of games for Limerick after returning from club duty during the [[2013 National Hurling League|2013 National League]], Dowling was surprisingly dropped from the starting fifteen by team manager [[John Allen (hurler)|John Allen]] for the team's opening championship game against Tipperary. Recalling being left on the bench, he later said: "I took that very hard at the time. Growing up I was never a sub on any team I had ever played for so, at the time, John Allen was the demon, the big bad wolf. I genuinely thought my inter-county career was over. I was devastated."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/shane-dowling-ive-lost-friends-and-relationships-because-of-hurling-855073.html|title=Shane Dowling: I've lost friends and relationships because of hurling|date=13 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Stephen|last=Barry}}</ref> Dowling was introduced as a 49th-minute substitute for [[Séamus Hickey]] and scored two points in a three-point victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-stun-tipp-in-thriller-597021.html|title=Limerick stun Tipp in thriller|date=9 June 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 August 2018}}</ref> On 14 July 2013, he scored three points from play after being introduced as a substitute in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Dowling returned to the Limerick starting fifteen under new joint-managers [[Dónal O'Grady]] and [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J. Ryan]] in [[2014 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2014]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-team-cork-shane-dowling-1316884-Feb2014/|title=Shane Dowling thrown straight back in for Limerick's Division 1B opener|date=14 February 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Niall|last=Kelly}}</ref> After scoring 2–09 in Limerick's Munster Championship defeat of Tipperary on 1 June 2014, he later revealed how he had been the subject of an abusive text message: "Last week, the chairman of the club showed me a text message from a journalist in Limerick. I’ve no problem with someone voicing their opinion. That particular person personally abused me in that text message. I don’t say that lightly. Thank God, that we answered that today."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/ace-marksman-dowling-delighted-to-shoot-down-limerick-critics-270696.html|title=Ace marksman Dowling delighted to shoot down Limerick critics|date=2 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref> On 24 October 2014, Dowling was named on the [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/hurling-allstars-2014-1745105-Oct2014/|title=Here's the 2014 Allstar hurling team - 7 for Tipperary, 6 for Kilkenny, 2 for Limerick|date=24 October 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 10 June 2018, Dowling's tally of 0–15 in a Munster Championship game allowed him to replace [[Gary Kirby]] as Limerick's all-time top championship scorer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limerick-secure-place-in-all-ireland-series-after-13-point-win-over-waterford-847960.html|title=Limerick secure place in All-Ireland series after 13-point win over Waterford|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=10 June 2018|access-date=8 August 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Dowling scored a goal after coming on as a substitute when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/my-life-probably-would-have-been-ruined-allireland-defeat-unthinkable-for-limerick-hero-dowling-37239459.html |title ='My life probably would have been ruined' - All-Ireland defeat unthinkable for Limerick hero Dowling|date=21 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Dowling started Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] on the bench. He was introduced as a 64th-minute substitute for [[Tom Morrissey (hurler)|Tom Morrissey]] and collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Dowling won his first Munster Championship medal in six years after coming on as a 66th-minute substitute for [[Gearóid Hegarty]] in Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 2 July 2020, Dowling announced his retirement from inter-county hurling due to degenerative knee and cartilage issues.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0702/1150943-shane-dowling-retires-from-inter-county-hurling-at-27/|title = Limerick's Shane Dowling retires from inter-county hurling at 27|date=2 July 2020|work=RTE Sport|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/shane-dowling-retire-knee-injury-5139243-Jul2020/|title = 'I still hardly believe this is happening': Limerick star Shane Dowling forced to retire aged 27|date=2 July 2020|work=The 42|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

In November 2024, it was announced that Dowling would come out of retirement to be part of the Limerick senior hurling panel as a goalkeeper after playing the last two years in goal for his club.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/john-kiely-on-drafting-shane-dowling-back-into-limerick-fold-nickie-quaids-blow-and-incredible-response-from-trialists/a568075226.html|title=John Kiely on drafting Shane Dowling back into Limerick fold, Nickie Quaid’s blow and ‘incredible response’ from trialists|date=16 December 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=17 December 2024}}</ref>

===Inter-provincial===

Dowling was selected for the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team for the first time on 17 February 2013. He later won a [[Railway Cup]] medal following a 1–22 to 0–15 defeat of [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/munster-players-cherish-medals-224440.html|title=Munster players 'cherish' medals|date=4 March 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref> Dowling was also selected for the Munster team in 2016.

'''Hugh Flavin''' is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a centre-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Flavin joined the team during the [[National Hurling League 2007|2007 National League]] and was a semi-regular member of the starting fifteen over the following two seasons. He enjoyed little success in the senior grade and was an unused substitute in Limerick's All-Ireland final defeat in 2007.

At club level Flavin plays with [[Croom GAA|Croom]].

==Playing career==

===Club===

Flavin plays his club hurling with Croom and has enjoyed some success.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

In 2001 he lined out in a county under-21 championship decider. [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] were the opponents, however, a comprehensive 1–12 to 0–4 victory gave Flavin an under-21 championship medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=18579|title=Long wait for Croom ends|publisher=Hogan Stand website|accessdate=4 November 2012|date=14 December 2001}}</ref>

===Inter-county===

Flavin made his senior debut for Limerick in a National League game against [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=74971|title=Limerick omit captain|publisher=Hogan Stand website|accessdate=4 November 2012|date=30 March 2007}}</ref> He played a number of games during that campaign and was subsequently included on Limerick's championship panel, making his debut in a Munster semi-final defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].  Flavin was an unused substitute for Limerick during their 2–19 to 1–15 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the 2007 All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2007/0902/1188603379646.html|title=Kilkenny overpower Limerick to retain title|date=2 September 2007|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref>

Flavin played a number of National League games for Limerick again in 2008, however, he left the panel after that year's championship.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=89416|title=Five call ups by Treaty men|publisher=Hogan Stand website|accessdate=4 November 2012|date=13 February 2008}}</ref>

'''Eoin Foley''' (born 1981) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a centre-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Foley made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2001|2001 championship]] and was a regular member of the panel for a number of seasons until his retirement after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2009|2009 championship]] . A two-time [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medalist in the under-21 grade, he enjoyed little success as a member of the county senior team. Foley ended up an All-Ireland runner-up as a substitute on one occasion.

At club level Foley is a two-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county club championship]] medalist with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]].Limerick City All star player at all underage levels

==Playing career==

===Club===

Foley played his club hurling with Patrickswell and has enjoyed much success.

In 2000 he lined out in his first championship decider when he came on as a substitute. [[Doon GAA|Doon]] provided the opposition, however, a narrow 0–16 to 0–15 victory gave Foley his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/veteran-kirby-fires-well-to-final-glory-364742.html|title=Veteran Kirby fires 'Well to final glory|date=9 October 2000|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=4 November 2012}}</ref>

After surrendering their title in 2001, Patrickswell were back in the championship decider again in 2003. A 1–13 to 0–14 defeat of [[Adare GAA|Adare]] saw Foley add a second championship medal to his collection.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/old-guard-command-the-well-200135.html|title=Old guard command the 'Well|date=13 October 2003|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=4 November 2012}}</ref>

===Inter-county===

Foley first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2001. He won his first [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal that year as Limerick retained their provincial title following a 3–14 to 2–16 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. Limerick later went on to defeat [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by just a single point to retain their All-Ireland title.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/gaa-limerick-wins-the-u21-all-ireland-hurling-final-23931.html|title=Limerick wins the U21 All-Ireland hurling final|date=16 September 2001|publisher=Breaking News website|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref> It was Foley's first [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal.

Limerick retained the provincial title again in 2002 with Foley winning his second Munster medal following a 1–20 to 2–14 defeat of Tipperary. A subsequent 3–17 to 0-8 trouncing of Galway gave Foley a second consecutive All-Ireland medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-make-history-292955.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120803155256/http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-make-history-292955.html |url-status=dead |archive-date= 3 August 2012 |title=Limerick make history |date=16 September 2002 |publisher=Irish Independent |accessdate=4 November 2012 |first=Martin |last=Breheny }}</ref>

By this stage Foley had joined the Limerick senior hurling team. He made his senior championship debut as a substitute in an All-Ireland quarter-final defeat by Wexford in 2001.

Foley was a regular in the National League and championship over the next few seasons, however, Limerick hurling went onto decline and he played no part in the 2004 and 2005 campaigns.

In 2006 Foley returned to the Limerick panel.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=63089|title=Hurlers welcome back U21 medallists|date=30 June 2006|publisher=Hogan Stand website|accessdate=4 November 2012}}</ref> He was an unused substitute the following year as Limerick faced a 2–19 to 1–15 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2007/0902/1188603379646.html|title=Kilkenny overpower Limerick to retain title|date=2 September 2007|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref>

Foley played his last game for Limerick in a 0–25 to 0-17 Munster semi-final defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in 2009.

'''James Flood''' (8 October 1875 – 30 November 1918) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://finbarrconnolly.com/limerick-1897/|title=Jim Flood|date=|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|accessdate=10 July 2017|first=|last=|archive-date=9 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170209011744/https://finbarrconnolly.com/limerick-1897/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Born in Caherline, [[County Limerick]], Flood first played competitive hurling in his youth. He quickly established himself on the [[Caherline GAA|Caherline]] team and won [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]] medals in 1896,<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=26 October 1996 |pages=27}}</ref> 1905<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=23 September 1995 |pages=26}}</ref> and 1907.<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=12 December 1959 |pages=13}}</ref>

After success at club level, Flood joined the Limerick senior team. He was part of the team that won [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]], [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] and Croke Cup titles in 1897.

Flood was also the Great Great Grandfather of English footballer [[Harry Kane]]. Flood was Kane’s Father’s Mother’s Grandfather.<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=18 August 2018 |pages=75}}</ref> 

Flood died on 30 November 1918 as a result of the [[1918 flu pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Limerick Leader |date=2 December 1918 |pages=3}}</ref>

'''John Fitzgibbon''' (born 21 September 1992) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a midfielder for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://limerickgaa.ie/limerick-squad-cat/senior-hurlers/|title=Senior Panel|publisher=Limerick GAA|access-date=12 March 2016}}{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

He enjoyed [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] success at colleges level with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] while simultaneously enjoying championship successes at underage levels with the [[Adare GAA|Adare]] club. Fitzgibbon has won one [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

Fitzgibbon made his debut on the inter-county scene at the age of sixteen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team. He later lined out with the under-21 team. Fitzgibbon made his senior debut during the [[2015 Waterford Crystal Cup]]. He has since gone on to become a regular member of the Limerick senior team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

'''Seán Finn''' (born 24 January 1996) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he plays with [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Early life==

Born and raised in [[Bruff]], [[County Limerick]], Finn was educated at Coláiste Iósaef in [[Kilmallock]] and played in all grades of hurling during his time there.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/the-best-christmas-present-of-all-arrives-in-county-limerick-school-8264496|title=The best Christmas present of all arrives in County Limerick school|date=23 December 2018|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=5 August 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]] (UL), he continued his hurling development. Finn won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal in February 2028, following UL's 2–21 to 2–15 defeat of [[Dublin City University]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0224/943259-ul-pull-away-to-claim-fitzgibbon-cup-glory/|title=UL pull away to claim Fitzgibbon Cup glory|date=29 February 2016|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref> He was later named on the Fitzgibbon Cup Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-trio-in-fitzgibbon-cup-team-of-the-year-8327651|title=Limerick trio in Fitzgibbon Cup Team of the Year|date=17 April 2018|publisher=Limerick Live|accessdate=5 August 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Club career==

Finn began his club career at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] club, before progressing to adult level. He was just out of the minor grade when he won a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick PIHC]] medal in October 2014, after scoring 1–02 in the 2–14 to 0–16 win over [[Croom GAA|Croom]] in the [[2014 Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship#Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/watch-sean-finn-feels-its-the-right-time-for-bruff-to-return-to-limerick-senior-hurling-7675350|title=WATCH: Sean Finn feels 'it's the right time' for Bruff to return to Limerick senior hurling|publisher=Limerick Live|date=27 October 2022|access-date=24 September 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Finn was also [[man of the match]] in the final and was named on the ''[[Limerick Leader]]'''s Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/bruff-lead-the-way-on-our-premier-ihc-team-of-the-year-8537111|title=Bruff lead the way on our Premier IHC team of the year|publisher=Limerick Live|date=31 October 2014|access-date=24 September 2020|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Inter-county career==

Finn first appeared on the inter-county scene for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]]. He won a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] title in July 2013, Limerick's first in 29 years, following a 1–20 to 4–08 win over [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[2013 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> Finn was eligible for the minor grade again the following year and won a second consecutive Munster MHC medal after a second consecutive 0–24 to 0–18 defeat of Waterford in a replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref> He subsequently lined out at right corner-back in Limerick's 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#All-Ireland final|2014 All-Ireland MHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-minors-savour-all-ireland-success-against-spirited-limerick-1.1920852|title=Kilkenny minors savour All-Ireland success against spirited Limerick|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 September 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}}</ref>

Finn immediately progressed to Limerick's under-21 team and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] medal in June 2015 after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2015 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster finals|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=30 July 2018}}</ref> He was later at corner-back when Limerick beat [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0–26 to 1–07 in the [[2015 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|2015 All-Ireland U21HC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> After returning to the panel following a prolnged injury, Finn won a second Munster U21HC medal in 2017 following a 0–16 to 1–11 win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He added a second All-Ireland U21HC medal to his collection after lining out at right corner-back in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|2017 All-Ireland U21HC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Finn ended the season by being named on the Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-u21-hurling-all-ireland-gillane-3626268-Oct2017/|title=Gillane the star man as Limerick, Kilkenny, Galway and Cork players make U21 team of the year|date=2 October 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

Finn was just 19-years-old when he was drafted onto the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] by manager [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J Ryan]] in 2016. He played a number of pre-season games in the [[Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]], however, it was revealed in February 2016 that Finn would miss the rest of the season after tearing his cruciate ligament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/clare-earn-dramatic-one-point-win-munster-final-2564550-Jan2016/|title=Clare earn dramatic one-point victory in Munster final|publisher=The 42|date=23 January 2016|accessdate=25 December 2020|first=Eoin|last=Brennan}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/sean-finn-limerick-u21-hurling-cruciate-2594332-Feb2016/|title=One of Limerick's All-Ireland U21 winning heroes tears cruciate and will miss 2016 senior season|publisher=The 42|date=9 February 2016|accessdate=26 December 2020|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> Finn recovered and returned to the team under new manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-senior-hurling-panel-3057187-Nov2016/|title=Two Munster senior winners not in Limerick 2017 hurling squad as attacker recalled|publisher=The 42|date=1 November 2016|accessdate=26 December 2020|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He made his debut in a 1–25 to 3–15 [[National Hurling League]] defeat of [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in March 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-offaly-hurling-3271304-Mar2017/|title=Dooley hits 2–11 for Offaly but 14-man Limerick finish strong to win at Gaelic Grounds|date=4 March 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> 

Finn was selected at right corner-back when Limerick played [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2018 All-Ireland SHC final]] and ended the game with his first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medal following the 3–16 to 2–18 win, with Limerick claiming their first title in [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|45 years]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> He ended the season by being named as the [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star ]] right corner-back position on the .<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/1101/1008065-lynch-is-hurler-of-year-fenton-wins-footballer-of-year/|title=Lynch is Hurler of Year, Fenton wins Footballer of Year|date=2 November 2018|publisher=RTE}}</ref> Finn added a National League medal to his collection in March 2019, when Limerick beat Waterford by 1–24 to 0–19 to win the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He won his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal in June 2019, following a 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> Finn the season by claiming a second consecutive All-Star.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-allstar-hurling-2019-awards-4872163-Oct2019/|title=7 for champions Tipperary and 3 for Kilkenny – the 2019 All-Star Hurling team|date=31 October 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 December 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

After retaining the National League title in a [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games|COVID-delayed]] final in October 2020, Finn later won a second consecutive Munster SHC after a four-point win over Waterford in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He claimed his second All-Ireland SHC medal in December 2020, as Waterford were once again beaten by 0–30 to 0–19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Limerick show consistency in a world gone mad to claim All-Ireland honours|date=13 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Finn was later named as the All-Star right corner-back for the third consecutive year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-dominate-2020-pwc-hurling-all-stars-selection|title=Limerick dominate 2020 PwC Hurling All-Stars selection|date=20 February 2021|publisher=GAA website|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Finn won his third Munster SHC medal in July 2021, as Limerick claimed a third consecutive title for the first time in 85 years following a 3–21 to 2–29 win over Tipperary in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/85-year-wait-ends-as-limerick-topple-tipperary-to-win-historic-munster-hurling-title-7969390|title=85-year wait ends as Limerick topple Tipperary to win historic Munster hurling title|date=18 July 2021|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later added a third All-Ireland SHC medal to his collection, again from right corner-back, in the 3–32 to 1–22 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40364432.html|title=Will record-breaking All-Ireland victory over Cork be Limerick's high water mark? Don't bet on it|date=22 August 2021|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Finn ended the season by being presented with a fourth consecutive All-Star, as well as being a [[GAA/GPA Hurler of the Year]] nominee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/news/record-breaking-limerick-dominate-2021-pwc-all-stars-hurling-team|title=Record-breaking Limerick dominate 2021 PwC All-Stars hurling team|date=9 December 2021|publisher=GAA website|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Limerick retained the Munster SHC title for a fourth consecutive year in June 2022, with Finn collecting his fourth winners' medal following the 1–29 to 0–29 extra-time win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40889036.html|title=Limerick find an extra gear to see off Clare in Munster final thriller|date=5 June 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later won his third consecutive All-Ireland SHC medal, once again in his usual right corner-back position, in the 1–31 to 2–26 win over [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40920188.html|title=Limerick secure the three-in-row with dream day in the sun|date=17 July 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He ended the season with his fourth consecutive All-Star.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-s-dozen-lead-the-way-in-2022-pwc-all-star-hurling-nominations|title=Limerick’s dozen lead the way in 2022 PwC All-Star Hurling nominations|date=8 September 2022|publisher=GAA website|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> 

Finn won his third National League medal in April 2023, after a 2–20 to 0–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 National Hurling League#Division 1|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0409/1376051-classy-limerick-claim-league-honours-with-ease/|title=Classy Limerick claim league honours with ease|date=9 April 2023|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He damaged his anterior cruciate ligament in Limerick's Munster SHC defeat of Clare in April 2023 and, for the second time in his career, was ruled out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41131879.html|title=Seàn Finn to miss remainder of championship due to ACL injury|date=4 May 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Limerick retained their Munster SHC title, before winning a record-equalling fourth consecutive All-Ireland SHC title, with Finn collecting winners' medals as a member of the extended panel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41159863.html|title=Aaron Gillane on fire as Limerick edge Clare to secure fifth consecutive Munster title|date=11 June 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history |date=23 July 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Finn returned to the team in March 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2024/03/22/finn-returns-for-limerick/|title=Finn returns for Limerick|date=22 March 2024|publisher=Limerick Post|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He was a non-playing substitute when Limerick won a record-breaking sixth consecutive Munster SHC title after a 1–26 to 1–20 win over Clare in the [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster|2024 Munster SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41412799.html|title=Six of the best: Limerick make history with Munster final win over Clare |date=9 June 2024|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> After a trophy-less 2025 season, Limerick regained the National League title with a six-point win over Cork in April 2026, with Finn claiming his fourth winners' medal in that competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41822540.html|title='If you get a chance to win, you have to take it' - Kiely's call that Cork shall not pass is heard|date=6 April 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later collected a seventh Munster SHC medal, as Limerick also regained that title with a 1–21 to 2–17 win over Cork in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/munster-shc-final-limerick-finish-strongly|title=Munster SHC Final: Limerick finish strongly|date=7 June 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Finn won a sixth All-Ireland SHC medal in July 2022, after a 1–29 to 1–18 win over Galway in the [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2026 All-Ireland SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41882305.html|title=Dominant Limerick reclaim All-Ireland title with final victory over Galway|date=19 July 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Personal life==

His father, [[Brian Finn (hurler)|Brian Finn]], also played with Limerick and was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] runner-up in [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1994]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2023/04/05/finn-looks-to-open-his-limerick-scoring-account/|title=Finn looks to open his Limerick scoring account |date=5 April 2023|work=Limerick Post|accessdate= 25 February 2026}}</ref> Finn is a cousin of [[YouTube]]r [[Nogla|Daithi De Nogla]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2023/11/19/my-mom-is-still-my-boss-profits-at-limerick-millionaires-miracle-youtube-business-increase-to-e3-22m/|title=‘My mom is still my boss’: Profits at Limerick millionaire’s ‘miracle’ YouTube business increase to €3.22m|date=19 November 2023|work=Limerick Post|accessdate= 25 February 2026}}</ref>

'''Richard English''' (born 15 March 1995) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a left corner-back for club side [[Doon GAA|Doon]] and previously at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Early life==

English was born in [[Doon, County Limerick|Doon]], [[County Limerick]]. His cousin, [[Darragh Fitzgibbon]], is a member of the [[Cork senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/home/326490/richie-and-darragh-first-cousins-to-go-toe-to-toe-in-croke-park-clash.html|title=Richie and Darragh: First cousins to go toe-to-toe in Croke Park clash|date=28 July 2018|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Donal|last=O'Regan}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===University===

During his studies at [[Mary Immaculate College]], English was selected for the college's senior hurling team and was appointed captain of the team in his second season. On 27 February 2016, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal as Mary I won their first ever title after a 1–30 to 3–22 defeat of the [[University of Limerick]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/eamonn-cregan-hails-heroic-mary-i-384649.html|title=Eamonn Cregan hails heroic Mary I|date=29 February 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> English was once again at full-back when Mary I retained the title in 2017 following a 3–24 to 1–19 defeat of [[Carlow Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/dj-carey-hails-inspirational-coach-jamie-wall-as-mary-i-retain-fitzgibbon-title-443894.html|title=DJ Carey hails inspirational coach Jamie Wall as Mary I retain Fitzgibbon title|date=27 February 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=John|last=Fallon}}</ref>

===Club===

English joined the [[Doon GAA|Doon]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in under-12, under-14 and under-15 grades. As a member of the club's minor team, he won back-to-back championship medals in 2012 and 2013 following respective defeats of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/89915/Doon-retain-Limerick-minor-hurling-title.html|title=Doon retain Limerick minor hurling title|date=14 October 2013|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> English made his senior championship debut for the club in 2012.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

English first played for Limerick at minor level in 2012, in season which ended with a defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/osullivan-sinks-cork-26849425.html|title=O'Sullivan sinks Cork|date=3 May 2012|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/banner-dig-deep-to-see-off-limerick-26870643.html|title=Banner dig deep to see off Limerick
|date=30 June 2012|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He was eligible for the minor grade once again the following year and was also appointed captain of the team. On 23 July 2013, English was at right corner-back when Limerick won their first Munster Championship title in 29 years after a 1–20 to 4–08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

English joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2014. In his second season he won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over Clare in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 12 September 2015, English was at full-back when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> He ended the season by being named the Bord Gáis Energy Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/u21-hurler-of-the-year-2366406-Oct2015/|title=Limerick's Richie English named U21 Hurler of the Year|date=3 October 2015|publisher=The 42|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

====Senior====

English joined the Limerick senior hurling team in January 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/91053/Limerick-unveil-new-senior-hurling-panel.html|title=Limerick unveil new senior hurling panel|date=9 January 2014|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He was released from the panel prior to the start of the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].

On 13 February 2016, English made his senior debut at left corner-back in a [[National Hurling League|National League]] defeat of [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/250404|title=HL1B: terrific Treaty wallop mediocre Model|date=13 February 2016|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> Later that season he made his first championship start in a 3–11 to 1-16 Munster Championship semi-final defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/first-half-goal-deluge-fires-tipperary-into-munster-final-34814650.html|title=First half goal deluge fires Tipperary into Munster final|date=19 June 2016|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, English was at left corner-back when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> Later that day he was named on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986154-limerick-rule-in-the-sunday-game-team-of-the-year/|title=Limerick rule in The Sunday Game team of the year|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=20 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> English ended the season by winning an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=13 September 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/1101/1008052-treaty-lead-the-way-with-six-hurling-all-stars/|title= Treaty lead the way with six hurling All-Stars|date=2 November 2018|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=4 November 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, English was selected at left corner-back for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> Hours after the league title victory, his father Paddy English died after a long illness.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/297538|title=Limerick star English bereaved|date=1 April 2019|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=1 April 2019|first=|last=}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, English won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal at left corner-back following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He ended the year by being nominated for a second All-Star award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-allstars-hurling-2019-4824531-Sep2019/|title=11 players from Tipperary as 8 counties feature in 2019 All-Star hurling nominations|date=26 September 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=26 September 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 23 February 2020, it was confirmed that English had been ruled out for the rest of the season with a cruciate injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/richie-english-limerick-hurling-cruciate-5018853-Feb2020/|title=Limerick All-Star winning defender out for rest of season with cruciate injury|date=23 February 2020|publisher=The 42|accessdate=24 February 2020|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 2 January 2025, English announced his retirement from inter-county hurling after nine years with Limerick.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-defender-richie-english-calls-time-on-inter-county-career/a1143470777.html|title= Limerick defender Richie English calls time on inter-county career|date=2 January 2025|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=3 January 2025}}</ref>
