{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{infobox Gaelic games biography |image = |name = Séamus Flanagan |irish = Séamus Ó Flanagáin |nickname = Sham |occupation = Sourcing manager |birth_date = 3 July 1997 |birth_place = [[Feohanagh]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] |height_ft = 6 |height_in = 3 |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] |cl_years = |cl_apps_points = |cl_county = 0 |cl_province = |cl_all_ireland = |colleges = [[UCD GAA|University College Dublin]] |fitz = 0 |col_years = |counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ic_years = 2017-present |ic_position = Full-forward |ic_apps_points = 40 (9-59) |ic_province = 5 |ic_all_ireland = 5 |nhl = 3 |all_stars = 1 |cl_update = |ic_update = 17:56, 29 April 2026 }} '''Séamus Flanagan''' (born 3 July 1997) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a full-forward for club side [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Club career== Flanagan joined the [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before eventually joining the club's top adult team. His father, [[John Flanagan (Limerick hurler)|John Flanagan]], had also played for the club and was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1980]]. His cousin, [[Paul Flanagan]], won an All-Ireland medal with the [[Clare senior hurling team]] in [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/home/317401/limerick-hurler-seamus-flanagan-inspires-a-new-generation-as-deise-clash-looms.html|title=Limerick hurler Seamus Flanagan inspires a new generation as Déise clash looms|date=8 June 2013|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Maria|last=Flannery}} ==Inter-county career== ===Minor and under-21=== Flanagan first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] when he was added to the minor panel shortly before the start of the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2014 Munster Minor Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 10 April 2014 when he lined out at right wing-forward in a 3–17 to 2–11 win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster quarter-final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20265071.html|title=Nash the main marksman as Limerick coast to showdown with Cork|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 April 2018|accessdate=23 December 2020|first=|last=}} Flanagan was switched to left wing-forward for the subsequent [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster final replay]] defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} On 7 September 2014, he scored two points from play in a 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/wonderful-walsh-fires-cats-to-victory-over-limerick-30569083.html|title=Wonderful Walsh fires Cats to victory over Limerick|date=8 September 2014|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}} Eligible for the minor grade again the following year, he was selected at full-forward when Limerick suffered defeat by Tipperary in the [[2015 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2015 Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30744074.html|title=Tipperary romp to Munster minor title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=10 July 2016|accessdate=23 December 2020|first=|last=}} After the end of his minor career, Flanagan was immediately added to the Limerick under-21 panel for the [[2016 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2016 Munster Under-21 Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 14 July 2016 in a two-point defeat by Tipperary in the [[2016 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-limerick-munster-u21-2-2878788-Jul2016/|title=Tipperary's great hurling week continues as they defeat Limerick in Munster U21 semi-final|date=14 July 2016|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} Flanagan was again called up to the squad for the 2017 championship season, however, he found it difficult to break onto the team as either a member of the starting fifteen or as a substitute. He ended the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2017 Munster Under-21 Championship]] campaign with a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|winners' medal]] as a non-playing substitute after Limerick's 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}} On 9 September 2017, Flanagan was again confined to the substitutes' bench lined for Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} For the third successive season in 2018, he earned inclusion on the under-21 panel.{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/defending-champions-limerick-name-u21-hurling-panel-2/|title=Defending Champions Limerick name U21 hurling panel|date=26 April 2018|publisher=Sporting Limerick|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Jack|last=Neville}} Flanagan made his last under-21 appearance on 21 June 2018 in a [[2018 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]] defeat by Tipperary.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-beat-limerick-munster-u21-hurling-4084964-Jun2018/|title=Clinical Tipp dethrone All-Ireland champions Limerick and book Munster final spot|date=21 June 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}} ===Senior=== ====2018 season==== In November 2017, Flanagan was entering his final year with the Limerick under-21 team when he was named on the 38-man senior panel for the upcoming [[2018 Limerick senior hurling team season|2018 season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/281970/10-additions-to-2018-limerick-hurling-panel.html|title=10 additions to 2018 Limerick hurling panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} He made his competitive debut on 30 December 2017 and scored 1-02 from play the 2–23 to 1–21 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League#Round 1|first round]] of the [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League|2019 Munster League]].{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/279425|title=Team news: Flanagan handed Limerick debut|date=29 December 2017|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-begin-2018-season-with-win-over-experimental-cork-820712.html|title=Limerick begin 2018 season with win over experimental Cork|date=30 December 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}} Flanagan ended the pre-season league as the third highest [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League#League statistics|scorer]] with 3-05, while he also collected his first silverware at senior level when Limerick defeated Clare by 0–16 to 0–10 to secure the provincial league title.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0114/933249-limerick-step-on-the-gas-to-leave-grind-down-banner/|title=Limerick grind down Clare as Kerry beat Cork, in hurling|date=14 January 2018|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}} On 28 January 2018, Flanagan made his [[National Hurling League|National League]] debut when he lined out at full-forward in a 10-point [[2018 National Hurling League#Division 1B Rounds 1 to 5|first-round]] defeat of [[Laois GAA|Laois]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/aaron-gillane-shines-on-league-debut-for-limerick-1.3371491|title=Aaron Gillane shines on league debut for Limerick|date=28 January 2018|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}} He was a regular for Limerick during the league, lining out in seven of their games, including the [[2018 National Hurling League#Division 1 Semi-Finals|semi-final]] defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperary-go-extra-mile-to-book-their-final-spot-by-seeing-off-limerick-36762800.html|title=Tipperary go extra mile to book their final spot by seeing off Limerick|date=1 April 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Dermot|last=Crowe}} On 20 May 2018, Flanagan made his first championship appearance and scored a point from play in a 1–23 to 2–14 win over Tipperary in the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limerick-finish-strongly-to-power-home-against-tipp-844022.html|title=Limerick finish strongly to power home against Tipp|date=20 May 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=John|last=Fogarty}} He established himself as Limerick's first-choice full-forward throughout the championship and was selected in that position when Limerick faced [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2018 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-team-news-all-ireland-hurling-final-4188195-Aug2018/|title=Limerick name unchanged side for All-Ireland final showdown against Galway|date=17 August 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=Emma|last=Duffy}} He was held scoreless and substituted by [[Peter Casey (hurler)|Peter Casey]] as Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}} Flanagan ended the season by being nominated for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=13 September 2018|first=|last=}} ====2019 season==== Flanagan was again an integral part of the Limerick senior team during the early stages of the 2019 season, making two appearances during Limerick's unsuccessful pre-season [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]] campaign. He was a regular match-day player during the [[2019 National Hurling League|2019 National League]], making seven appearances during their eight league games. On 31 March 2019, Flanagan was introduced as a 55th-minute substitute for [[Graeme Mulcahy]] when Limerick claimed their first [[National Hurling League#Division 1|Division 1]] title since [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] after a 1–24 to 0–19 win over [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} Flanagan found it difficult to break onto the starting fifteen during the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2019 Munster Championship]], making just one start and two substitute appearances during the four [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship#Group matches|group stage]] games. On 30 June 2019, he came on as a 66th-minute substitute for [[Peter Casey (hurler)|Peter Casey]] in Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ====2020 season==== Flanagan again found it difficult to break onto Limerick's starting fifteen, making just one appearance during their title-winning [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]] campaign.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0111/1105733-limerick-cruise-past-to-cork-to-win-munster-league/|title=Stylish Limerick cruise past Cork to win Munster league|date=11 January 2020|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=18 December 2020|first=Denis|last=Hurley}} The subsequent [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|National League]] campaign saw Flanagan line out in four of Limerick's five [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|Division 1A]] games. On 25 October 2020, he was introduced as a substitute in Limerick's 0–36 to 1–23 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed league final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=25 October 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} Flanagan made three appearances off the bench during the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2020 Munster Championship]], ending the campaign with a second successive winners' medal after the defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford for historic Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} On 29 November 2020, he received his first start of the championship when he lined out at full-forward in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]] defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40104308.html|title=Tom Morrissey points Limerick past Galway to set-up All-Ireland final with Waterford|date=29 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} On 13 December 2020, Flanagan scored three points after starting at full-forward when Limerick defeated Waterford by 0–30 to 0–19 in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Limerick show consistency in a world gone mad to claim All-Ireland honours|date=13 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} ====2026 season==== In October 2025, Flanagan was informed by Limerick manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] that we would not be part of the Limerick panel for 2026.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/1027/1540817-flanagan-cut-from-limerick-panel-for-2026/|title= Séamus Flanagan cut from Limerick panel for 2026; Shane Dowling steps away|date=27 October 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=8 June 2026}} ==Personal life== Flanaghan is married to Laurie Carey since 2022 and they have four children. He works as a Sourcing Manager for Verizon having previously worked as a radiographer at [[University Hospital Limerick]]. '''David Dempsey''' (born 13 May 1995) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a left wing-forward for club side [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/opportunity-knocks-for-limerick-and-david-dempsey-1.3046516|title=Opportunity knocks for Limerick and David Dempsey|date=13 April 2017|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=18 August 2018|first=Therese|last=O'Callaghan}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===College===

Dempsey first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. Having played in every grade as a hurler, he was an unused substitute on 27 February 2011 when Ardscoil Rís retained the [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] title after a 3–19 to 0–03 defeat of [[C.B.S. Charleville]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/awesome-ardscoil-storm-to-harty-title-26709031.html|title=Awesome Ardscoil storm to Harty title|date=28 February 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

===University===

During his studies at the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]], Dempsey was selected for the college's senior hurling team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].

===Club===

Dempsey joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the under-16, minor and under-21 grades. He made his senior championship debut for the club as a seventeen-year-old in 2013.

On 6 October 2013, Dempsey was at right wing-forward when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Adare GAA|Adare]] by 0–14 to 0–12 to win the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/downes-sets-the-tone-for-na-piarsaigh-to-grind-it-out-29639434.html|title=Downes sets the tone for Na Piarsaigh to grind it out|date=7 October 2013|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> He retained his place in the half-forward line for the subsequent [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]], which culminated with him winning a provincial medal after a 4–14 to 0–08 defeat of [[Sixmilebridge GAA|Sixmilebridge]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/powerful-piarsaighs-blistering-pace-too-much-for-tired-bridge-250662.html|title=Powerful Piarsaigh's blistering pace too much for tired Bridge|date=25 November 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Dempsey won a second Limerick Championship medal on 11 October 2015 after a 1–22 to 4–12 defeat of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> Later that season he won a second Munster Championship medal after a 2–18 to 2–11 defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 17 March 2016, Dempsey won an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] by 2–25 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

On 15 October 2017, Dempsey won a third Limerick Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 1–22 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He later won a third Munster Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated Ballygunner by 3–15 to 2–10 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/late-na-piarsaigh-surge-sweeps-aside-ballygunner-in-scrappy-munster-final-36333884.html|title=Late Na Piarsaigh surge sweeps aside Ballygunner in scrappy Munster final|date=19 November 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, Casey was named at left wing-forward but played at midfield when Na Piarsaigh were defeated by [[Cuala GAA|Cuala]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

On 27 October 2018, Dempsey won a fourth Limerick Championship medal following Na Piarsaigh's 2–22 to 3–10 defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/boss-beary-points-to-experience-of-troops-as-na-piarsaigh-impress-again-37468758.html|title=Boss Beary points to experience of troops as Na Piarsaigh impress again|date=29 October 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=1 November 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}}</ref>

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

Dempsey first played for Limerick at minor level. On 23 July 2013, he scored two points when Limerick won their first [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title in 29 years after a 1–20 to 4–08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

Dempsey subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2015 and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 0–22 to 0–19 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 12 September 2015, Dempsey was at left wing-forward when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Intermediate====

In 2016, Dempsey joined the Limerick intermediate hurling team. On 6 July 2016, he was at right corner-forward when Limerick were defeated by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/clare-limerick-intermediate-munster-2865032-Jul2016/|title=Clare crowned Munster intermediate champions after epic extra time battle with Limerick|date=6 July 2016|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoin|last=Brennan}}</ref>

====Senior====

Dempsey joined the Limerick senior hurling team in January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/201061/18-new-faces-on-Limerick-hurling.html|title=18 new faces on Limerick hurling panel|date=9 January 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Brien}}</ref> He was an unused substitute throughout the entire season.

Dempsey made his senior debut for Limerick on 12 February 2017 in a 1–14 to 0-14 [[National Hurling League]] defeat by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/kiely-fumes-at-ref-as-davy-gets-lift-off-442800.html|title=Kiely fumes at ref as Davy gets lift-off|date=13 February 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Later that season he made his first championship start, scoring 1–01 in a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/clare-made-to-sweat-for-their-win-over-limerick-792372.html|title=Clare made to sweat for their win over Limerick|date=4 June 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Dempsey was a member of the extended panel when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Dempsey was named on the bench for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal as a non-playing substitute in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

'''Patrick J. Cunneen''' (born 1936) is an Irish retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played at club level with [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St. Patrick's]] and at inter-county level with [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]].

==Career==

From the [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St. Patrick's]] club, Cunneen first came to prominence on the inter-county scene with the Limerick junior team that overcame [[London GAA|London]] to win the [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|1955 All-Ireland Junior Championship]]. Promotion to the senior side followed, with Cunneen lining out in goal when Limerick surprised [[Clare GAA|Clare]] to win the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1955 Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/columnists/arid-20473132.html|title=Mackey, Limerick, and the decade when Hollywood documented the glories of hurling for US cinema|date=17 August 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 March 2021|first=Paul|last=Rouse}}</ref> The team, labelled "Mackey's Greyhounds" after their trainer [[Mick Mackey]], were subsequently beaten by eventual champions [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/goreyguardian/sport/farewell-mick-27348747.html|title=Farewell Mick|date=27 October 2011|publisher=Gorey Guardian|accessdate=3 March 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Adam English''' (born 25 March 2003) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he plays with [[Doon GAA|Doon]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[Doon, County Limerick|Doon]], [[County Limerick]], English was educated at Scoil na Trionóide Naofa. He played in all grades of hurling during his time there and won a Munster PPS U15BHC title as [[Captain (sport)|joint-captain]] in 2018.{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/good-people-make-great-things-happen-limerick-manager-john-kiely-tells-pupils-8276135|title=‘Good people make great things happen’, Limerick manager John Kiely tells pupils|access-date=17 May 2026|publisher=Limerick Live|date=21 October 2018}} During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]] (UL), English continued his hurling development. He won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal in February 2023, after scoring two points in the 4–19 to 1–13 win over [[NUI Galway GAA|University of Galway]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/sigerson-fitzgibbon-cups/four-goal-michael-kiely-fires-ul-to-fitzgibbon-cup-glory-against-university-of-galway-42348322.html|title=Four-goal Michael Kiely fires UL to Fitzgibbon Cup glory against University of Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 February 2023|accessdate=18 February 2023|first=Tomás|last=McCarthy}} English claimed a second Fitzgibbon Cup medal two years later, following a 0–23 to 1–15 win over [[DCU GAA|DCU Dóchas Éireann]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41575399.html|title=UL overpower DCU to lift third Fitzgibbon Cup in four years|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 February 2025|accessdate=16 February 2025|first=Kevin|last=Egan}} ==Club career== English began his club career at juvenile and underage levels with [[Doon GAA|Doon]]. He was part of the club's under-21 team that won three consecutive Limerick Premier U21HC titles between 2019 and 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/hat-trick-of-limerick-u21-hurling-titles-for-doon-with-final-victory-over-na-piarsaigh-7915616|title=Hat-trick of Limerick U21 hurling titles for Doon with final victory over Na Piarsaigh|publisher=Limerick Live|date=5 December 2021|accessdate=16 February 2025|first=|last=}} English made his [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|senior team]] debut in September 2021 in a 0–27 to 1–23 win over [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40373978.html|title=Limerick SHC: Three off as Doon defeat Patrickswell, champs Na Piarsaigh lay down marker|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=5 September 2021|accessdate=16 February 2025|first=|last=}} He won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medal in October 2024, after scoring 0–11 in the one-point win over Na Piarsaigh in the [[2024 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41504720.html|title=Historic first Limerick hurling title for Doon as they take down three-in-a-row chasing Na Piarsaigh|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=27 October 2024|access-date=28 October 2024|first=Brendan|last=O'Brien}} ==Inter-county career== English first appeared on the inter-county scene for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]]. He won a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] title in June 2019, following a 1–17 to 1–11 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2019 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-triumph-in-electric-ireland-munster-mhc-final|title=Limerick triumph in Electric Ireland Munster MHC Final|date=30 June 2019|publisher=GAA website|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} English captained the team to a second consecutive Munster MHC title in December 2020, when Limerick beat [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in extra time by 2–22 to 0–25 in a [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games|COVID-delayed]] [[2020 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster final|Munster MHC final]].{{cite news |url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-limerick-munster-mhc-final-5306959-Dec2020/|title=Limerick crowned Munster minor champions after overcoming Tipperary|access-date=11 August 2021 |work=The 42|date=20 December 2020}} English immediately progressed to the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20 team]] and won a [[Munster Under-20 Hurling Championship|Munster U20HC]] in May 2022 following a four-point win over Tipperary.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40865447.html|title=Treaty tyros tame Tipp to add to county's dominance |date=4 May 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=20 July 2026|first=|last=}} He was at right wing-forward for Limerick's 0–19 to 0–18 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2022 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland U20HC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/u-20-hurling/kilkenny-claim-all-ireland-u-20-title-after-edging-limerick-in-thrilling-final-41676137.html|title=Kilkenny claim All-Ireland U-20 title after edging Limerick in thrilling final|date=22 May 2022|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} English made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in a 0–27 to 1–18 [[National Hurling League]] defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in February 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2022/0212/1279464-galway-finish-with-a-flourish-to-beat-14-man-limerick/|title=Galway finish with a flourish to beat 14-man Limerick|date=12 February 2022|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=6 May 2026|first=|last=}} His membership of the under-20 team impacted on his senior team appearances that season.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40864889.html|title=Munster U20 Hurling final: Three key battles|date=4 May 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} Limerick retained the Munster SHC title for a fourth consecutive year in June 2022, with English being an extended panel member for the 1–29 to 0–29 extra-time win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40889036.html|title=Limerick find an extra gear to see off Clare in Munster final thriller|date=5 June 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He later won his first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medal, again as an extended panel member, in the 1–31 to 2–26 win over Kilkenny in the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40920188.html|title=Limerick secure the three-in-row with dream day in the sun|date=17 July 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} English won his first National League medal in April 2023, again as a substitute, in the 2–20 to 0–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 National Hurling League#Division 1|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0409/1376051-classy-limerick-claim-league-honours-with-ease/|title=Classy Limerick claim league honours with ease|date=9 April 2023|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He later claimed his second Munster SHC medal, his first on the field of play, as Limerick beat Clare by 1–23 to 1–22 to win a record-equalling fifth consecutive title.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41159863.html|title=Aaron Gillane on fire as Limerick edge Clare to secure fifth consecutive Munster title|date=11 June 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} English was an unused substitute when Limerick won a record-equalling fourth consecutive All-Ireland SHC title, following a 0–30 to 2–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history |date=23 July 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} English came on as a substitute for [[Cian Lynch]] when Limerick won a record-breaking sixth consecutive Munster SHC title after a 1–26 to 1–20 win over Clare in the [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster|2024 Munster SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41412799.html|title=Six of the best: Limerick make history with Munster final win over Clare |date=9 June 2024|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} After a trophy-less 2025 season, Limerick regained the National League title with a six-point win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in April 2026, with English claiming his second winners' medal.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41822540.html|title='If you get a chance to win, you have to take it' - Kiely's call that Cork shall not pass is heard|date=6 April 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He later collected a fourth Munster SHC medal as Limerick also regained that title with a 1–21 to 2–17 win over Cork in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/munster-shc-final-limerick-finish-strongly|title=Munster SHC Final: Limerick finish strongly|date=7 June 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} English won a third All-Ireland SHC medal, after lining out at midfield, in the 1–29 to 1–18 win over Galway in the [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2026 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41882305.html|title=Dominant Brian Finn.text:
{{For-multi|the New Zealand musician whose first name is Brian|Tim Finn|the fictional police officer|Shark in the Park|the fictional priest|Keeping the Faith}} {{Short description|Irish hurler (born 1965)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2023}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=May 2023}} {{infobox Gaelic games player |image = |name = Brian Finn |irish = |nickname = |occupation = Secondary school teacher |birth_date = 1965 |birth_place = [[Bruff]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Ireland]] |height_ft = |height_in = |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]]
[[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] |cl_years = |cl_position = |cl_apps_points = |cl_county = 0 |cl_province = |cl_all_ireland = |colleges = [[Thomond College]] |fitz = 0 |col_years = |counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ic_years = 1985-1994 |ic_position = Right corner-back |ic_apps_points = 13 (0-03) |ic_province = 1 |ic_all_ireland = 0 |nhl = 2 |all_stars = 0 |cl_update = |ic_update = }} '''Brian Finn''' (born 1965) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he played with [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] and also lined out at inter-county level with various [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] teams. ==Career== Born in [[Bruff]], [[County Limerick]], Finn first played [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]] at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] club. He was part of the team that won the Limerick MHC title in 1983. Finn later transferred to the [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] club in [[Limerick]], before ending his career back with Bruff. Finn first appeared on the inter-county scene with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick minor team]] that lost consecutive [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster finals]] in 1982 and 1983. He progressed to the under-21 team and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] medal in his final year with the team in 1986.{{cite news|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/u21h_teams/|title=Under 21 hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|accessdate=20 June 2022}} By that stage, Finn had already joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] and won a [[National Hurling League|National League]] medal in his debut season in 1985. He claimed a second league medal in 1992.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limericks-new-generation-aim-to-banish-ghosts/37164158.html|title=Limerick's new generation aim to banish ghosts|publisher=Irish Independent|date=29 July 2018|accessdate=20 June 2022}} Finn was a non-playing substitute when Limerick suffered a defeat by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1994 All-Ireland final]]. His performances at inter-county level resulted in his selection for the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] [[Railway Cup]] team.{{cite news|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|accessdate=20 June 2022}} ==Personal life== Finn studied at [[Thomond College]] before later working as the Gaelic games development officer at [[NIHE Limerick]]. During his time here he coached the hurling team to their inaugural [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].{{cite news|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/66153|title=Brian Finn|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=3 July 1992|accessdate=20 June 2022}} Finn's son, [[Seán Finn]], has also played for Limerick.{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-sean-finn-hurling-all-ireland-5297019-Dec2020/|title='I asked him to lift the cup with me. I don't know why but I'm delighted I did' - Limerick's defensive star|publisher=The 42|date=12 December 2020|accessdate=20 June 2022}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/2022/12/24/limerick-fathers-and-sons-i-said-it-to-you-ger-years-ago-the-boys-will-win-it-for-us/|title=Limerick fathers and sons: ‘I said it to you Ger, years ago. The boys will win it for us’|publisher=Irish Times|date=24 December 2022|accessdate=20 June 2022}} ==Honours== ===Player=== ;Bruff *Limerick Minor Hurling Championship: 1983 ;Limerick *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1984]] *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1984–85 National Hurling League|1984–85]], [[1991–92 National Hurling League|1991–92]] *[[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1986 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1986]] ===Management=== ;NIHE Limerick *[[Fitzgibbon Cup]]: 1989 ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Brian Finn navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Hurling Team 1994}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Finn, Brian}} [[Category:1965 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Bruff hurlers]] [[Category:South Liberties hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]] [[Category:Hurling managers]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

Don Flynn (hurler).text:
{{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2025}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=April 2025}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Don Flynn | irish = Dónal Ó Floinn | fullname = | height_ft = | height_in = | occupation = | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Killeedy GAA|Killeedy]]
→ [[Western Gaels (Limerick) GAA|Western Gaels]] | cl_position = | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | colleges = [[University of Limerick|NIHE Limerick]] | col_years = | fitz = 0 | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Left corner-back | ic_years = 1987-1994 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 1 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = |birth_date = 1966 | birth_place=[[Killeedy]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Don Flynn''' (born 1966) is an Irish [[hurling]] coach and former player. At club level, he played with [[Killeedy GAA|Killeedy]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Playing career== Flynn first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Killeedy GAA|Killeedy]] club, before eventually progressing to adult level. He won a [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] medal in 1992 after Killeedy's 0-14 to 1-05 defeat of [[Murroe / Boher GAA|Boher]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Killeedy's class tells in the end|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=24 October 1992|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Flynn first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick's last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to the under-21 team and won consecutive [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] titles, before claiming an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after a 2-15 to 3-06 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|1987 final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/109109/Limerick-s-first-All-Ireland-U.html|title=Limerick's first All Ireland U-21 hurling title in 1987|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 September 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Flynn made his first appearance for the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in a challenge game against [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in a challenge game in January 1987.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick slip against Tipp|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=31 January 1987|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He was later part of the Limerick team that won the [[National Hurling League]] title in 1992.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Flynn also won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal and was a non-playing substitute for Limerick's defeat by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1994 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/477252/limerick-gaa-to-make-25th-anniversary-of-the-1994-munster-hurling-title-victory.html|title=Limerick GAA to make 25th anniversary of the 1994 Munster hurling title victory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=18 September 2019|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-1994-all-ireland-shc-final-offaly-v-limerick|title=Flashback: 1994 All-Ireland SHC Final - Offaly v Limerick|publisher=GAA website|date=19 March 2020|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Management career== In retirement from playing, Flynn became involved in team management and coaching. He served a two-year spell as manager of Limerick's [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship|intermediate team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/225774|title=Limerick selector resigns after a month|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=10 October 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Killeedy *[[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]]: 1992 *Limerick Junior B Hurling Championship: 2005 ;Limerick *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1994]], [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1996]] *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1991–92 National Hurling League|1991–92]], [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] *[[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|1987]] *[[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1986 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1986]], [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1987]] *[[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] *[[Munster Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] ;Munster *[[Railway Cup]]: [[1995 Railway Cup Hurling Championship|1995]], [[1996 Railway Cup Hurling Championship|1996]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title= Don Flynn navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Minor Hurling Team 1984}} {{Limerick Under 21 Team 1987}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1994}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Flynn, Don}} [[Category:1966 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Killeedy hurlers]] [[Category:Western Gaels hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

Shane Fitzgibbon.text:
{{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2025}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=April 2025}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Shane Fitzgibbon | irish = Seán Mac Giobúin | fullname = | height_ft = | height_in = | occupation = Bank official | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Adare GAA|Adare]] | cl_position = | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | colleges = [[University of Limerick|NIHE Limerick]] | col_years = | fitz = 0 | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Midfield | ic_years = 1984-1993 | ic_apps_points = (9-17) | ic_province = 2 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = |birth_date = April 1963 | birth_place=[[Adare]]
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Shane Fitzgibbon''' (born April 1963) is an Irish [[hurling]] coach and former player. At club level, he played with [[Adare GAA|Adare]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/the-gaa/oral-history/shane-fitzgibbon|title=Shane Fitzgibbon|publisher=GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/65169|title=Shane Fitzgibbon|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=17 April 1992|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Playing career== Fitzgibbon attended St Clement's College in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]], however, his hurling there was limited to the lower grades as the school's primary sport was [[rugby union]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20113260.html|title=Ardscoil star with an enviable bloodline|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=27 February 2010|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He later attended [[University of Limerick|NIHE Limerick]] and lined out in the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]]. At club level, Fitzgibbon first played for [[Adare GAA|Adare]] at juvenile and underage levels. He was part of the club's under-21 team that claimed the Limerick U21HC title after a defeat of Ardagh in 1983.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Adare take under-21 title for second time|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 November 1983|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Fitzgibbon had already joined the Adare senior team by that stage and lost four [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#List of finals|Limerick SHC finals]] in a ten-year period between 1986 and 1996.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaelic-games/141611/Limerick-SHC-Final---The.html|title=Limerick SHC Final - The day Adare finally reached their promised land|publisher=Limerick Live|date=6 October 2012|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Fitzgibbon first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]]. He progressed to the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] and won a [[National Hurling League]] medal in his debut season in 1985.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/529524/limerick-hurlers-back-to-back-national-league-champions-84-85.html|title=Limerick hurlers back-to-back National League champions 84/85|publisher=Limerick Live|date=27 March 2020|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Fitzgibbon added a second National League medal to his collection in 1992.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Fitzgibbon being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He lined out for the province on four occasions but ended his career without a [[Railway Cup]] medal.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=11 June 2009|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=|archive-date=18 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918072623/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|url-status=dead}} ==Coaching career== Fitzgibbon was still a player when he began his coaching career at club level with Adare. He coached the club's minor team to the Limerick MHC title in 1990.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30925148.html|title=The man who prepared the Limerick rocket for moon landing|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=18 May 2019|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Fitzgibbon continued his involvement at club level and also with Limerick's underage academy. ==Honours== ===Player=== ;Adare *Limerick Under-21 Hurling Championship: 1983 ;Limerick *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1984–85 National Hurling League|1984–85]], [[1991–92 National Hurling League|1991–92]] ===Management=== ;Adare *Limerick Minor Hurling Championship: 1990 ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Fitzgibbon, Shane}} [[Category:1963 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Adare hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]] [[Category:Hurling coaches]] [[Category:Hurling managers]]

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Patrick Davoren''' (born 1967) is an Irish retired [[Hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Davoren played hurling while at secondary school in [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]]. He was part of the school's senior team that lost to [[St Finbarr's College, Farranferris|St Finbarr's College]] in the final of the [[Dr Harty Cup]] in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Farna turn it on in second half|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=16 April 1984|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At club level, Davoren first played for [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] at juvenile and underage levels before progressing to adult level. He won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medal in 1989 after a 4-10 to 2-09 win over [[Doon GAA|Doon]]. Davoren later added a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] medal to his collection before lining out in the 1-16 to 0-16 defeat by [[Ballyhale Shamrocks GAA|Ballyhale Shamrocks]] in the [[1990 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1990 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=7 June 2009|access-date=15 October 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/527176/the-day-ballybrown-broke-the-mould-in-croke-park.html|title=The day Ballybrown broke the mould in Croke Park|publisher=Limerick Live|date=29 March 2020|access-date=15 October 2024}} He collected a second Limerick SHC medal in 1991.{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Limerick/ClubTitles|title=Club titles - Limerick|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=15 October 2018}} At inter-county level, Davoren first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as corner-forward on the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick's last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to the under-21 team in 1988.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick u21 hurlers in action|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=6 July 1988|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Davoren joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in 1989. He made a number of appearances over the course of the following few years and won a [[National Hurling League]] medal in 1992.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Ballybrown *[[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship]]: [[1989–90 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|1989]] *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1989 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1989]], [[1991 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1991]] ;Limerick *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1991–92 National Hurling League|1991–92]] *[[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] *[[Munster Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title= Pat Davoren navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Minor Hurling Team 1984}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Davoren, Pat}} [[Category:1967 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Ballybrown hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Fintan Fitzgerald''' (born 2005) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he plays with [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret/St Paul's]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Fitzgerald was educated at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick]] and lined out in all grades of hurling during his time there. He was a [[Dean Ryan Cup]] runner-up in 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40746660.html|title=St Flannan's clinch Dean Ryan Cup with late goal burst|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=17 November 2021|access-date=18 February 2025|first=Brendan|last=Buckley}} He later captained the school's senior to a defeat by [[St. Joseph's CBS Nenagh|St Joseph's CBS Nenagh]] in the [[2023–24 Harty Cup#Final|2024 Harty Cup final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41323939.html|title=Hoolan the hero as late, late goal ushers in Harty history for Nenagh CBS |publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 February 2024|access-date=3 February 2024|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} Fitzgerald won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal with the [[University of Limerick]] in 2026.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/2015230/limerick-stars-shine-as-clinical-ul-see-off-local-rivals-mary-immaculate-college-in-fitzgibbon-cup-final.html|title=Limerick stars shine as clinical UL see off local rivals Mary Immaculate College in Fitzgibbon Cup final|publisher=Limerick Live|date=13 February 2026|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} At club level, Fitzgerald first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret/St Paul's]]. He won a Limerick Prmeier U21HC title in 2023, before captaining the team to the Limerick Premier U20HC title in 2025.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41294809.html|title=Archer and Lynch lead Mungret St Paul's to more silverware|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 December 2023|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/1958780/senior-is-the-big-one-that-we-want-really-says-mungret-st-paul-s-u20-hurling-captain-fintan-fitzgerald.html|title=‘Senior is the big one that we want really’ says Mungret St Paul's U20 hurling captain Fintan Fitzgerald|publisher=Limerick Live|date=6 December 2025|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}} Fitzgerald first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 2022.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/electric-ireland-munster-mhc-limerick-and-clare-cruise-into-quarter-finals/41567807.html|title=Electric Ireland Munster MHC: Limerick and Clare cruise into quarter-finals|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 April 2022|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}} He later spent three seasons with the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20 team]]. Fitzgerald was part of the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]]'s pre-season training panel in 2025 before later being released.{{cite web|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/limerick-senior-hurling-pre-season-squad-2025/|title=Limerick Senior Hurling Pre Season Squad 2025|publisher=Limerick GAA website|date=|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}} He was again part of Limerick's pre-season training panel the following year and won a [[Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster SHL]] title in 2026. Fitzgerald was retained for the subsequent [[2026 National Hurling League|National Hurling League]] campaign.{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41820200.html|title=Numbers behind Limerick hurlers' spring surge as they host Cork in league final|publisher=Echo Live|date=3 April 2026|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;University of Limerick *[[Fitzgibbon Cup]] (1): [[2026 Fitzgibbon Cup|2026]] ;Mungret/St Paul's *Limerick Premier Under-21 Hurling Championship (1): 2023 *Limerick Premier Under-20 Hurling Championship (1): 2025 ;Limerick *[[National Hurling League]] (1): [[2026 National Hurling League|2026]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling League]] (1): [[2026 Munster Senior Hurling League|2026]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 2026}} {{Limerick Hurling Team}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Fitzgerald, Fintan}} [[Category:2005 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:University of Limerick hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:21st-century Irish sportsmen]]

'''Michael Herbert''' (17 May 1925 – 20 June 2006) was an Irish [[Fianna Fáil]] politician.<ref name=oireachtas_db>{{cite web|url=https://www.oireachtas.ie/en/members/member/Michael-Herbert.D.1969-07-02/|title=Michael Herbert|work=Oireachtas Members Database|access-date=5 November 2012|archive-date=2018-05-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180516110033/https://www.oireachtas.ie/en/members/member/Michael-Herbert.D.1969-07-02/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==
A [[pub]]lican from [[Castleconnell]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/ireland/cwgbeycwauoj/|work=[[Irish Examiner]]|title=Two former TDs turned publicans die|date=20 June 2006|access-date=5 November 2012|archive-date=16 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716190936/http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/ireland/cwgbeycwauoj/|url-status=live}}</ref> [[County Limerick]], he unsuccessfully contested the [[1965 Irish general election|1965 general election]] and was first elected to [[Dáil Éireann]] at the [[1969 Irish general election|1969 general election]] as a Fianna Fáil [[Teachta Dála]] (TD) for the [[Limerick East (Dáil constituency)|Limerick East]] constituency.<ref name=elecs_irl>{{cite web|url=http://electionsireland.org/candidate.cfm?ID=2791|title=Michael Herbert|work=ElectionsIreland.org|access-date=5 November 2012|archive-date=25 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120925211837/http://electionsireland.org/candidate.cfm?ID=2791|url-status=live}}</ref> He was re-elected for the constituency until the [[1981 Irish general election|1981 general election]] when he did not stand for re-election.  He was again unsuccessful in the [[November 1982 Irish general election|November 1982 election]].

While a TD, Herbert served as a [[Member of the European Parliament]] from 1973 to 1979, being appointed to Ireland's [[List of members of the European Parliament for Ireland, 1973|first delegation]], [[List of members of the European Parliament for Ireland, 1973–1977|second delegation]] and [[List of members of the European Parliament for Ireland, 1977–1979|third delegation]].

In the [[1979 European Parliament election in Ireland|first direct elections]] to the [[European Parliament]] in December 1979 he stood in the [[Munster (European Parliament constituency)|Munster]] constituency but was not elected.

He played [[hurling]] as a full-back with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick Senior Hurling team]], with whom he won a [[National Hurling League]] medal in 1947, and also with his local club [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]]. He retired prematurely from the game following a serious head injury caused by an assault with a hurley in a club match in 1949. His assailant received 12 months imprisonment. His brothers [[Seán Herbert]] and [[Tony Herbert]] were also hurlers with Limerick and his son [[Turlough Herbert]] was a member of the Limerick senior hurling panel for the 1994 [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] final.

Michael Herbert died in 2006, aged 81.

'''Pat Hartigan''' (born 1950) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] former [[Hurling|hurler]] who played for his local club [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]]<ref>{{cite news
|title=South Liberties turn it around
|author=Diarmuid O’Flynn
|newspaper=[[Irish Examiner]]
|date=23 November 2009
|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/kfaugbkfsnid/rss2/#ixzz0tymjlL8q
|access-date=2010-07-17
}}</ref> and at senior level for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]] in the 1970s. He is regarded as one of Limerick's greatest-ever players.<ref>{{cite news
|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2009/1203/limerick.html
|access-date=2010-07-17
|title=Hartigan calls for unity on Shannonside
|newspaper=[[RTÉ Sport]]
|date=3 December 2009
}}</ref>

==Early and private life==
Pat Hartigan was born in [[Drombanna]], [[County Limerick]] in 1950. He was educated locally and from an early age he showed a great interest in the game of [[hurling]], learning his skills on the roads and in the fields of his local parish where his reputation as a skilful hurler was built. It was only when Hartigan attended the [[CBS Sexton Street|Sexton Street school]] of the [[Congregation of Christian Brothers|Christian Brothers]], where one of his friends was [[J.P. McManus]], that he began to play hurling on a competitive basis. By the age of 15 Hartigan had White Cup (under fifteen and a half) and [[Dean Ryan Cup]] (Munster junior colleges) medals to his name and had broken onto the schools Harty Cup panel. In 1966 his school won a third successive Harty Cup and All-Ireland colleges' title, beating St Mary's of [[Galway]]. In 1967, after a fourth consecutive Harty Cup title was claimed, a number of the team decided to repeat the school year and attempt to capture an elusive fifth consecutive title. The prospect of making history became an obsession for Hartigan; however, his team were eventually beaten by [[Coláiste Chríost Rí]] of [[Cork (city)|Cork]].{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

Hartigan currently works as a nationals sales manager with Grasslands Irl. Ltd.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

==Playing career==
===Club===
Hartigan played his club [[hurling]] with the famous [[South Liberties GAA Club|South Liberties]] club in Limerick. He enjoyed some success at underage levels before winning a senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] title in 1972. It was the club's first county title since 1890. Hartigan won further county victories in 1976 and 1979.

===Inter-county===
Hartigan's hurling success in secondary school brought him to the attention of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] inter-county selectors. He made history in 1968 when he played on eight different Limerick teams in the space of six months - minor, under-21 and senior in [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]], as well as intermediate in hurling and junior in football. Hartigan spent a record six years playing with the Limerick under-21 hurling team before quickly establishing himself on the senior hurling and football teams. In 1971 he first tasted success when he won a [[National Hurling League]] medal. It was the first of five successive National League final appearances for Limerick; however, they only ended up successful on one occasion.

In spite of a lack of championship success Hartigan was named in the full-back position on the inaugural [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] team. It was the first of five successive All-Star awards for him. In the 1970s Limerick also contested five [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] finals, with victory coming first in 1973. That year Hartigan later claimed his first, and only, [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal when Limerick had a great victory over [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. While Hartigan played at full-back his brother, [[Bernie Hartigan|Bernie]], played in the half-forward line. In 1974 the Hartigan's won a second Munster title; however, Limerick were later defeated by Kilkenny in the All-Ireland final. The following few years proved frustrating for Limerick as [[Cork GAA|Cork]] dominated the Munster championship.

In a training session with Limerick in 1979 Hartigan was tragically injured when the sliothar spun awkwardly off a hurley and hit him in the eye. The whole incident left him blind in one eye and effectively ended his inter-county hurling career. He remained on the panel for the All-Ireland final of 1980 and the All-Ireland semi-final of 1981; however, victory went to [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] on both occasions.

==Athletics==
As well as having a successful career at [[Gaelic games]] Hartigan had a great shot-putt career for Ireland. Without any specialised training Hartigan captained Limerick AC in 1983 to a national track and field league title, before adding a second in 1985. He later went on to represent Ireland in the European club championships. In the mid-1960s Hartigan was offered a sporting scholarship to [[Boston]]; however, he declined in favour of playing Gaelic games with his native-county.

==Retirement==
In retirement from hurling and athletics Hartigan maintained a keen interest in both. He won the [[Poc Fada]] competition in 1981 and 1983<ref>{{cite web
 |url=http://www.gaa.ie/about-the-gaa/our-games/hurling/poc-fada/roll-of-honour/
 |access-date=2010-07-17
 |title=Roll of Honour: Poc Fada
 |publisher=GAA
 |url-status=dead
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100602224511/http://www.gaa.ie/about-the-gaa/our-games/hurling/poc-fada/roll-of-honour/
 |archive-date=2010-06-02
}}</ref> and also spent a period as manager of his local underage teams in the South Liberties club.

In May 2020, the ''[[Irish Independent]]'' named Hartigan at number twelve in its "Top 20 hurlers in Ireland over the past 50 years".<ref>{{cite news|first=Martin|last=Breheny|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/the-greatest-players/revealed-the-top-20-hurlers-in-ireland-over-the-past-50-years-39244506.html|title=Revealed: The Top 20 hurlers in Ireland over the past 50 years|newspaper=[[Irish Independent]]|publisher=[[Independent News & Media]]|date=30 May 2020|access-date=30 May 2020}}</ref>
