Éamonn Grimes.text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use British English|date=September 2015}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2026}} {{Infobox Gaelic games biography | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | caption = | name = Éamonn Grimes | irish = Éamonn Ó Greacháin | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 8 | nickname = | occupation = Sales representative | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[South Liberties GAA Club|South Liberties]] | cl_position = Midfield | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county =4 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = Midfield | ic_years = 1966–1981 | ic_apps_points = 30 (3-27) | ic_province = 2 | ic_all_ireland = 1 | nhl = 1 | all_stars = 2 | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_date = 1947 | birth_place=Donoughmore, [[County Limerick]], Ireland }} '''Éamonn Grimes''' (born 1947) is an Irish retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a midfielder for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17756|title=Éamonn Grimes|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=5 March 1993|accessdate=25 November 2008}} Grimes joined the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1966|1966 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1981|1981 championship]]. During that time he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, four [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals (two as a substitute), one [[National Hurling League]] medal and two [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] awards. An All-Ireland runner-up on two occasions, Grimes captained the team to the All-Ireland title in 1973. At club level Grimes was a four-time [[Limerick Senior Club Hurling Championship|county club championship]] medalist with [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]]. ==Playing career== ===Colleges=== During his secondary schooling at [[CBS Sexton Street]], Grimes became a member of the college senior hurling team.{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssextonstreet.ie/about-us.html|title=A brief history|publisher=Limerick CBS website|date=|accessdate=20 April 2013}} In 1964 he won his first [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] medal following a defeat of [[St. Flannan's College]]. The subsequent All-Ireland decider saw the Limerick side face [[St. Peter's College, Wexford]]. A 6–7 to 4–5 victory gave Grimes an [[Dr. Croke Cup|All-Ireland]] medal.{{cite web|url=http://memorylanelimerick.photoshelter.com/image/I0000mkTnQAPTYYQ|title=Limerick CBS homecoming|publisher=Memory Lane Limerick website|date=|accessdate=20 April 2013}} Grimes added a second Harty Cup medal the following year, before losing to [[St. Kieran's College]] in the All-Ireland decider on a score line of 6–9 to 6–1. In his final year with the school, Grimes won a third successive Harty Cup medal as captain of the side, following a defeat of Thurles CBS. The subsequent All-Ireland decider against St. Mary's of Galway was a rout, with a large 8–9 to 2–2 victory giving Grimes a second All-Ireland medal. ===Club=== Grimes played his club hurling, along with his brothers Lar, John, Mikey and Joe, with the [[South Liberties GAA Club]] in Limerick.{{cite web|url=http://southliberties.limerick.gaa.ie/rollofhonour.html|title=Roll of Honour|publisher=South Liberties GAA website|date=|accessdate=25 November 2008}} After playing in two losing county finals, Grimes was at midfield again when South Liberties faced [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in 1972. A 4–8 to 1–5 victory gave Grimes a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] medal. Four years later Grimes added a second championship medal to his collection following a 2–9 to 2–6 defeat of [[Killeedy GAA|Killeedy]]. South Liberties surrendered their title the following year, but they reached the final again in 1978. Grimes won a third championship medal following a 2–9 to 2–5 defeat of [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]].{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/bruree-one-stop-from-glory-by-jerome-o-connell-1-2177348|title=Bruree one stop from glory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=13 October 2006|accessdate=19 April 2013|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} In 1981 South Liberties defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 4–7 to 2–11, giving Grimes a fourth championship medal. Grimes retired from club hurling in 1986. ===Minor and under-21=== Grimes first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the Limerick minor hurling team in 1963. He was an unused substitute that year when Limerick defeated [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] by 4–12 to 5–4 to take the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship]] crown. The subsequent All-Ireland decider saw Limerick face [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]. Grimes was introduced as a substitute, but Wexford won a high-scoring game by 6–12 to 5–9. Two years later Grimes was in his final year in the grade and was a regular member of the starting fifteen. A 5–5 to 3–9 defeat of Tipperary gave him his first Munster medal on the field of play. Limerick were defeated by 4–10 to 2–7 by [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] in the subsequent All-Ireland decider. Grimes subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team; however, he had little success in this grade.{{citation needed|date=March 2017}} ===Senior=== Grimes subsequently joined the Limerick senior team, making his debut the day before he was due to sit his [[Leaving Certificate (Ireland)|Leaving Certificate]] in a Munster quarter-final defeat of Tipperary. In 1971 Limerick hurling bounced back after over a decade in the doldrums.{{tone inline|date=March 2017}} A narrow 3–12 to 3–11 defeat of Tipperary gave Grimes a [[National Hurling League]] medal. Two years later Grimes was appointed captain of the team as Limerick finally made the provincial breakthrough. A last-minute free by [[Richie Bennis]] secured a 6–7 to 2–18 defeat of Tipperary in the provincial decider and a first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal for Grimes. It was Limerick's first provincial championship since 1955. Grimes later led his team to [[Croke Park]] for an All-Ireland showdown with reigning champions and injury-ravaged [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. A [[Mossie Dowling]] goal eight minutes after half-time, together with a series of scores by Richie Bennis led Limerick to a 1–21 to 1–14 victory. This gave Grimes an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] medal, and he had the honour of collecting the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] on behalf of the team.{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/3420/TALES-OF-3973-IMMORTALS.3163953.jp?articlepage=2|title=Tales of the '73 Immortals|date=31 August 2007|work=[[Limerick Leader]]|accessdate=15 July 2010}} Following the conclusion of the championship he was presented with his first [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award, as well as being named [[Texaco Hurler of the Year]]. In 1974 Limerick maintained their provincial dominance. Grimes captured a second Munster medal following a 6–14 to 3–9 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]]. This victory allowed Grimes's side advance directly to the All-Ireland final where Kilkenny provided the opposition once again. While Kilkenny were back to full strength, Limerick went into an early lead. However, this was diminished as [[Pat Delaney (Kilkenny hurler)|Pat Delaney]], [[Eddie Keher]] and [[Mick Brennan (hurler)|Mick Brennan]] scored goals. Limerick lost the game by 3–19 to 1–13. Limerick failed to win a third provincial championship, but Grimes won a second All-Star award in 1975. By 1980 Grimes had been dropped from the starting fifteen. He was a non-playing substitute as Limerick won the Munster final by 2–14 to 2–10 that year and denied Cork a record-breaking sixth successive title. The subsequent All-Ireland decider pitted Limerick against [[Galway GAA|Galway]]; however, Grimes started the game outside of the starting fifteen once again. He was introduced to the field of play during the game. Though [[Éamonn Cregan]] scored 2–7 for Limerick, Galway went on to win the game by 2–15 to 3–9. Limerick retained their provincial crown in 1981 following a 3–12 to 2–9 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]], but Grimes was still a non-playing substitute. His career drew to an end when eventual champions [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] defeated Limerick in the subsequent All-Ireland semi-final. ===Inter-provincial=== Grimes was also selected for [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial series of games. He made his debut with the province in 1972 and was a regular at various intervals until his retirement in 1978. During that time he won two [[Railway Cup]] medals as a non-playing substitute in 1976 and 1978.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=11 June 2009|accessdate=12 March 2013|first=|last=}} ==Personal life== {{BLP unreferenced section|date=October 2018}} Grimes lives in [[Limerick]], with his wife, Helen. They married in the 1970s and have two children. After completing his education Grimes later worked as a sales representative for [[Beamish and Crawford]]. His name re-appeared in sports reports many years later when his friend and fellow member and benefactor of the South Liberties club, [[J.P. McManus]], named his successful racehorse "Grimes" in his honour. ==Honours== ===Team=== ;Sexton Street CBS *[[Dr. Croke Cup|All-Ireland Senior Colleges' Hurling Championship]] (2): [[1964 Croke Cup|1964]], [[1966 Croke Cup|1966]] (c) *[[Dr. Harty Cup|Munster Senior Colleges' Hurling Championship]] (3): 1964, 1965, 1966 (c) ;South Liberties *[[Limerick Senior Club Hurling Championship]] (4): 1972, 1976, 1978, 1981 ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (1): [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1973|1973]] (c) *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (4): [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1973#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1973]] (c), [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1974#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1974]], [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1980#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1980]] (sub), [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1981#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1981]] (sub) *[[National Hurling League]] (1): [[National Hurling League 1970-71|1970–71]] *[[Munster Minor Hurling Championship]] (2): 1963 (sub), 1965 ;Munster *[[Railway Cup]] (4): 1976 (sub), 1978 (sub) ===Individual=== ;Awards *[[Texaco Hurler of the Year]] (1): 1973 *[[GAA GPA All Stars Awards|All-Star Awards]] (2): 1974, 1975 ==References== {{reflist}} {{s-start}} {{s-sports}} {{succession box| before=[[Jim Hogan (Limerick hurler)|Jim Hogan]]| title=[[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|Limerick Senior Hurling Captain]]| years=1973| after=[[Seán Foley]] }} {{succession box| after=[[Paddy Kelly (hurler)|Paddy Kelly]]| title=[[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|Limerick Senior Hurling Captain]]| years=1975| before=[[Seán Foley]] }} {{s-ach|achievements}} {{succession box| before=[[Noel Skehan]]

[[County Limerick]], Ireland | birth_date=7 August 1864 | death_date=1920 | death_place = [[Wales]] }} '''Denis Grimes''' (7 August 1864 – 1920) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. He played with Kilfinane at club level and was the captain of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] team that won the [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1897 All-Ireland SHC]] title. ==Career== Born and raised in [[Kilfinane]], [[County Limerick]], Grimes first played hurling with Kilfinane Hurling Club in the early years of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. He [[Captain (Gaelic games)|captain]]ed the team to [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] title wins in 1897 and 1899.{{cite web|url=https://www.ouririshheritage.org/content/archive/place/kilfinane-coshlea-historical-society/topics-kilfinane-coshlea-historical-society/kilfinane-emmets-in-1897|title=Kilfinane All-Ireland Hurling Champions 1897|date=|publisher=Our Irish Heritage|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} Kilfinane were the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] representatives at inter-county level following each of those title wins.{{cite web|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/limerick-win-first-munster-senior-hurling-championship-title-in-1897/|title=Limerick win first Munster Senior Hurling Championship title in 1897|date=1 June 2022|publisher=Limerick GAA website|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} Grimes [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|captain]]ed Limerick to the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] title, following a 4–09 to 1–06 win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/hurling/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|date=|publisher=Munster GAA website|accessdate=3 August 2026|first=|last=}} Limerick subsequently had a one-goal win over [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1897 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20111948.html|title=Sleeping giants bid to rekindle magical days at headquarters|date=12 February 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} Grimes also won a Croke Cup title in July 1899, when he again captained Limerick to victory over Kilkenny. ==Personal life and death== Grimes received a limited education at the local [[National school (Ireland)|national school]] and later worked as a labourer. He moved to [[Wales]] around the turn of the 20th century and worked in the coalmines.{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Matthew |date=2023-07-20 |title=Limerick's historic links with the GAA |url=https://www.limerick.ie/council/newsroom/news/limericks-historic-links-with-the-gaa |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=Limerick City and County Council}} He never returned to Ireland. '''Seán Foley''' (born 29 October 1949) is an Irish retired [[hurling|hurler]] whose [[National Hurling League|league]] and [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] career as a left wing-back with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team spanned thirteen seasons from 1970 to 1983.

Born in [[London]], England, Foley was introduced to hurling when his family relocated to [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]]. His father, John Foley, was an [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal winner in the junior grade with Limerick in 1941. Foley enjoyed [[Dr. Croke Cup|All-Ireland]] success with the [[CBS Sexton Street]] team in 1966, while simultaneously joining the [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/204857/Ardscoil-Ris-one-final-step-from.html|title=Ardscoil Ris one final step from the top|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=28 March 2016|accessdate=1 October 2016|first=|last=}}</ref> In a club career that spanned 25 years he won two [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and eleven [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]] medals. Foley was an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up on one occasion.

Foley enjoyed an unsuccessful underage career at minor and under-21 levels with Limerick before making his senior debut during the [[1970-71 National Hurling League|1970-71 league]]. Over the course of the next thirteen seasons he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal as Limerick won the title after a long absence in 1973.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/bennis-recalls-the-heroes-of-73-231789.html|title=Bennis recalls the heroes of ’73|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 May 2013|accessdate=1 October 2016|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> Foley also won four [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals, one [[National Hurling League]] medal and was chosen as an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] in 1973. He played his last game for Limerick in June 1983.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

Foley was chosen on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team for four consecutive years between 1972 and 1975, however, he failed to win a [[Railway Cup]] medal.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

Willie Hough.text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler (1892–1976)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=July 2015}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=July 2015}} {{Infobox Gaelic games biography | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Willie Hough | irish = Liam Ó hEochaidh | height = | nickname = | occupation = National school teacher | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Monagea GAA|Monagea]]

1915-1929 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 3 | ic_all_ireland = 2 | nhl = 0 | all_stars = | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_date = {{Birth date|df=yes|1892|5|4}} | death_date = {{death date and age|df=yes|1976|4|13|1892|5|4}} | birth_place = Monagea,
[[County Limerick]], Ireland | death_place = [[Dooradoyle]],
[[Limerick (city)|Limerick]], Ireland }} '''William Hough''' (4 May 1892 – 13 April 1976) was an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]]. At club level he played with [[Monagea GAA|Monagea]], [[De La Salle GAA|St Stephen's]] and [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]], and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. Hough [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|captain]]ed Limerick to the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] title in 1918.{{cite news|url=http://www.askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/willie-hough.pdf|title=Willie Hough of Monagae|publisher=Limerick Heritage website|access-date=5 May 2012}} ==Club career== Hough made his first appearance on the club scene with [[Monagea GAA|Monagea]] in a game against [[Granagh-Ballingarry GAA|Ballingarry]] in 1910. The club later disbanded, however, by that stage Hough was living in [[Waterford]] and lined out with [[De La Salle GAA|St Stephen's]] team. He won back-to-back [[Waterford Senior Hurling Championship|Waterford SHC]] medals in 1913 and 1914.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/upsetting-hurlings-old-order/a/149513058.html|title=Upsetting hurling's old order|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 February 2011|access-date=4 October 2026}} Hough subsequently moved to [[Cork (city)|Cork]] and played with the [[UCC GAA|Collegains]] club, before transferring to [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]]. He won his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medal in 1917, following a 3–04 to 3–01 win over [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]], before claiming a second winners' medal in 1925.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41680520.html|title='There are young fellas now walking the streets with hurleys' - Newcastle West point way for west Limerick|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=30 July 2025|access-date=4 October 2026}} ==Inter-county career== Hough first appeared on the inter-county scene as [[List of Waterford senior hurling team captains|captain]] of the [[Waterford senior hurling team]] in 1913.{{cite news|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/monagea-gaa-club-to-honour-willie-hough/|title=Monagea GAA Club to Honour Willie Hough|publisher=Limerick GAA website|date=|access-date=4 October 2026}} He declined an invitation to line out with [[Cork GAA|Cork]] the following year, having moved there for employment, however, he made his [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] debut in 1915. Success at club level resulted in Hough assuming the Limerick [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|captaincy]] in 1918. He won his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal that year, after an 11–03 to 1–02 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster final|final]].{{cite news|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/hurling/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=4 October 2026}} Hough was at centre-back when he captained Limerick to a 9–05 to 1–03 win over [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1918 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite news|url=https://www.gaa.ie/centenary/match-reports/1918-match-report-all-ireland-hurling-final|title=1918 GAA Hurling Final Match Report|publisher=GAA website|access-date=4 October 2026}}{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/relatives-sought-for-re-enactment-of-limericks-1918-all-ireland-hurling-final-win-8320894|title=Relatives sought for re-enactment of Limerick's 1918 All Ireland hurling final win|publisher=Limerick Live|date=25 May 2018|access-date=4 October 2026}} The half-back line of Hough, [[Jack Keane (hurler)|Jack Keane]] and [[Dinny Lanigan]] was known for its effectiveness and was nicknamed the '[[Hindenburg Line]]'.{{cite news|url=http://www.vsopublicationsltd.ie/monagea-honours-its-native-son/|title=Monagea honours its native son|publisher=Vale Star|date=13 September 2018|access-date=4 October 2026}} Hough won his second Munster SHC medal after a 5–02 to 1–02 win over Cork in the [[Irish War of Independence|War of Independence]]-delayed [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster final|Munster final]] in May 1922. The [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1921 All-Ireland SHC final]] was delayed by 18 months, however, Hough collected a second winners' medal as [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] were beaten by 8–05 to 3–02.{{cite news|url=https://www.gaa.ie/api/images/image/upload/t_q-best/hvuoyliszmm5ab1ffluf.pdf|title=1921 GAA Hurling Final Match Report|publisher=GAA website|access-date=4 October 2026}} After surrendering their titles the following year, Hough's Limerick returned to claim their third Munster SHC title in six years in 1923, following a 2–03 to 1–00 win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the final. The [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1923 All-Ireland SHC final]] resulted in a 7–03 to 4–05 win for [[Galway GAA|Galway]] over Limerick.{{cite news|url=https://www.gaa.ie/centenary/match-reports/1923-match-report-all-ireland-hurling-final|title=1923 GAA Hurling Final Match Report|publisher=GAA website|access-date=4 October 2026}} Hough again captained Limeick during their unsuccessful Munster SHC campaign in 1926. He retired from inter-county hurling shortly after this, however, he made a return to inter-county activity for a Munster SHC game against Waterford in 1929. ==Personal life and death== Hough was born and raised in Monagea, [[County Limerick]]. His father, William Hough Snr, played both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]] in the early years of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] (GAA) and was chairman of the West Limerick Board from 1902 until 1910. Hough was educated locally and later attended the [[De La Salle College Waterford|De La Salle College]] in [[Waterford]] where he trained as a [[National school (Ireland)|national school]] teacher. His first teaching position was in [[Baltimore, County Cork|Baltimore]], [[West Cork]]. Hough took up a teaching post in Monagea National School in 1914, before serving as principal of the school from 1918 until his retirement in 1957.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport-columnists/arid-20473255.html|title=A fitting tribute to Willie Hough - a legend of Limerick hurling|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=14 September 2018|access-date=4 October 2026}} After his playing career had ended, Hough remained active in the GAA. He was an inter-county referee and took charge of many [[National Hurling League]] and Munster SHC games. Hough served as vice-chairman of the West Limerick Board from 1924 until 1928. He was appointed treasurer of the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]] in 1936 and held the position for over 25 years.{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/monagea-honours-limerick-all-ireland-winning-captain-of-1918-8302254|title=Monagea honours Limerick All-Ireland winning captain of 1918 |publisher=Limerick Live|date=2 September 2018|access-date=4 October 2026}} Hough died on 13 April 1976, at the age of 83.{{cite news|url=https://finbarrconnolly.com/1918-2/|title=The late Willie Hough|publisher=Limerick '''Brian Geary''' (born 1980) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a centre-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Geary made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1999|1999 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2012|2012 championship]]. A two-time [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medalist in the under-21 grade, he enjoyed little success as a member of the county senior team. Geary ended up an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion.

At club level Geary is a four-time [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|county football championship]] medalist with [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]].

==Playing career==

===Club===
Geary has enjoyed much success as a Gaelic footballer with the [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] club.

In 2002 Geary lined out in his first championship decider. [[Adare GAA|Adare]] provided the opposition and were hopeful of a county double. After a thrilling draw and a replay, Monaleen were the victors on a score line of 1–10 to 1–19.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/brilliant-gavin-dashes-adares-dreams-of-double-284296.html|title=Brilliant Gavin dashes Adare's dreams of double|date=4 November 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref> It was Geary's first [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|county championship]] medal.

After a three-year absence Monaleen returned to the county final again in 2005. A 0–13 to 2–5 defeat of [[St. Kieran's GAA|St. Kieran's]] gave Geary a second championship medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/dramatic-finale-but-gavins-brief-stint-saves-monaleen-233833.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130218075718/http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/dramatic-finale-but-gavins-brief-stint-saves-monaleen-233833.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 February 2013 |title=Dramatic finale but Gavin's brief stint saves Monaleen |date=3 October 2005 |publisher=Irish Independent |accessdate=31 October 2012 }}</ref>

Monaleen once again went into decline following this victory, but reached another championship decider in 2010. Adare provided the opposition, however, a 1–9 to 1–5 defeat gave Geary a third county championship medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/obrien-shines-for-monaleen-2383684.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130218043227/http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/obrien-shines-for-monaleen-2383684.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 February 2013 |title=O'Brien shines for Monaleen |date=18 October 2010 |publisher=Irish Independent |accessdate=31 October 2012 }}</ref>

After failing to retain their title on various previous occasions, Monaleen were back in the county final again in 2011. A 1–12 to 1–7 defeat of [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]] saw Monaleen retain their title, while Geary collected a fourth championship medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/collins-turns-the-screw-to-deny-wasteful-newcastle-west-2907769.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130218135713/http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/collins-turns-the-screw-to-deny-wasteful-newcastle-west-2907769.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 February 2013 |title=Collins turns the screw to deny wasteful Newcastle West |date=17 October 2011 |publisher=Irish Independent |accessdate=31 October 2012 |first=Kieran |last=McCarthy }}</ref>

===Minor and under-21===
Geary enjoyed his first inter-county success as a [[dual player]] in the under-21 grades.

In 2000 he was a key member of the Limerick under-21 football team that broke the provincial dominance of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]]. A 0–7 to 0–4 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] gave Geary a [[Munster Under-21 Football Championship|Munster]] medal in football.

That same year Geary was also a member of the successful Limerick under-21 hurling team. After a 1-13 apiece draw with Cork in the provincial decider, Limerick went on to win the replay following a stunning 4–18 to 1–6 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/brilliant-limerick-rip-cork-to-shreds-370790.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130217184255/http://www.independent.ie/sport/brilliant-limerick-rip-cork-to-shreds-370790.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 February 2013 |title=Brilliant Limerick rip Cork to shreds |date=24 August 2000 |publisher=Irish Independent |accessdate=31 October 2012 }}</ref> It was Geary's first [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal in under-21 hurling. Limerick subsequently defeated [[Galway GAA|Galway]] by 1–13 to 0–13 in the All-Ireland decider, giving Geary an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]] medal.

In 2002 Geary added a second Munster under-21 medal to his collection as Limerick retained their provincial title following a 3–14 to 2–16 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. Limerick later went on to defeat [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by just a single point to retain their All-Ireland title.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/gaa-limerick-wins-the-u21-all-ireland-hurling-final-23931.html|title=Limerick wins the U21 All-Ireland hurling final|date=16 September 2001|publisher=Breaking News website|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref> It was Geary's last game for the under-21 hurlers.

===Senior===
By this stage Geary was a key member of the Limerick senior hurling team. He made his championship debut in a Munster quarter-final defeat by Waterford in 1999.

Two years later in 2001 Geary lined out in his first Munster final at senior level. Tipperary were the opponents on that occasion, however, Limerick faced a narrow 2–16 to 1–17 defeat.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/tipps-grace-under-pressure-produces-late-victory-flourish-337367.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218111418/http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/tipps-grace-under-pressure-produces-late-victory-flourish-337367.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=18 December 2012 |title=Tipp's grace under pressure produces late victory flourish |date=2 July 2001 |publisher=Irish Independent |accessdate=31 October 2012 |first=Martin |last=Breheny }}</ref>

Limerick hurling went into decline following this defeat and faced a number of years of early championship exits.

In 2006 Geary claimed his first silverware at senior level with Limerick. A 1–19 to 3–10 defeat of the [[Waterford Institute of Technology]] secured the [[Waterford Crystal Cup]] for Geary's side.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/clear_win_for_limerick_in_crystal_hurling_final_by_colm_kinsella_at_the_gaelic_grounds_1_2175858 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120804020048/http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/clear_win_for_limerick_in_crystal_hurling_final_by_colm_kinsella_at_the_gaelic_grounds_1_2175858 |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 August 2012 |title=Tipp's grace under pressure produces late victory flourish |date=10 February 2006 |publisher=Limerick Leader |accessdate=31 October 2012 |first=Colm |last=Kinsella }}</ref>

Geary was appointed co-captain of the Limerick senior hurling team in 2007. That year he lined out in a second [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] final, this time with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] providing the opposition. A 3–17 to 1–14 defeat was Limerick's lot on that occasion.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dynamic-dan-adds-some-extra-dash-for-the-dise-995588.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120904121742/http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dynamic-dan-adds-some-extra-dash-for-the-dise-995588.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 September 2012 |title=Dynamic Dan adds some extra dash for the Déise |publisher=[[Irish Independent]] |accessdate=2 August 2012 |date=9 July 2007 |first=Martin |last=Breheny }}</ref> Limerick later gained their revenge on Waterford in the All-Ireland semi-final, thus gaining qualification to a first All-Ireland decider in eleven years for the Treaty men. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] provided the opposition and got off to a flying start with [[Eddie Brennan]] and [[Henry Shefflin]] combining to score two goals within the first ten minutes. Limerick were eventually defeated on a 2–19 to 1–15 score line.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2007/0902/1188603379646.html|title=Kilkenny overpower Limerick to retain title|date=2 September 2007|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref>

Limerick failed to build on their reasonably successful 2007 season and went into decline once again.

After indicating that he would return for one more season with the Limerick senior hurling team, Geary announced his retirement from inter-county hurling on 19 November 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=177399|title=Geary hints at staying on|date=13 September 2012|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=31 October 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=181179|title=Geary calls it a day|date=19 November 2012|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=19 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2012/1119/346327-geary-hangs-up-his-treaty-boots/|title=Limerick defender Brian Geary calls time on inter-county hurling career that began in 1999|date=19 November 2012|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=19 November 2012}}</ref>

Séamus Hickey.text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=January 2022}} {{infobox Gaelic games biography |image = |name = Séamus Hickey |irish = Séamus Ó hÍcí |nickname = |occupation = Program Manager |birth_date = {{birth date and age|1987|10|2|df=yes}} |birth_place = Boher, [[County Limerick]], [[Ireland]] |height = {{convert|1.85|m|ftin|0|abbr=on}} |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] 2005-2019
[[Croagh-Kilfinny]] 2020-present |cl_position = Midfield |cl_apps_points = |cl_county = 0 |cl_province = |cl_all_ireland = |colleges = [[University of Limerick]] |fitz = 1 |col_years = 2006-2011 |counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] |ic_years = 2006-2018 |ic_position = Left corner-back |ic_apps_points = 44 (0-08) |ic_province = 1 |ic_all_ireland = 1 |nhl = 0 |all_stars = 1 |cl_update = |ic_update = 01:48, 20 August 2018 }} '''Séamus Hickey''' (born 2 October 1987) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] sportsperson. He played [[hurling]] with his local club [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] from 2005 to 2019 and is now a member of the [[Croagh-Kilfinny]] club. Hickey was a member at inter-county level of the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]] from 2006 until 2018.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=59998|title=Limerick call on St. Flannan's starlet|date=28 April 2006|publisher=Hoganstand.com|access-date=6 February 2011}} ==Playing career== ===College=== Hickey first came to prominence as a hurler with [[St. Flannan's College]] in [[Ennis]], [[County Clare]]. Having played in every grade as a hurler and [[Gaelic football]]er, he was a left wing-back and centre-back on the college's senior hurling teams that won back-to-back [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] titles in 2004 and 2005.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/flannans-final-flourish-26012369.html|title=Flannan's final flourish|date=15 March 2004|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/st-flannans-claim-their-21st-harty-cup-26205826.html|title=St Flannan's claim their 21st Harty Cup|date=13 March 2005|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018}} On 2 May 2005, Hickey won an [[Dr. Croke Cup|All-Ireland]] medal after a 2–15 to 2–12 defeat of [[St. Kieran's College]] from [[Kilkenny (city)|Kilkenny]] in the final at [[Semple Stadium]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/oconnors-new-kids-on-block-lift-gloom-as-flannans-deliver-25983072.html|title=O'Connor's new kids on block lift gloom as Flannan's deliver|date=3 May 2005|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Cliona|last=Foley}} ===University=== During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]], Hickey immediately became involved with the university's hurling team stating: "My induction day as a fresher, they were going looking at lecture halls and timetables. I went straight for the GAA office and asked when the [[Fitzgibbon Cup|Fitzgibbon]] trials were on! I saw it as an extension of school hurling and representing where you go. For me, I thought it was natural while developing as a hurler."{{cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/inside-one-fitzgibbon-cups-greatest-ever-defences-381108|title=Inside One Of The Fitzgibbon Cup's Greatest Ever Defences|date=13 February 2018|publisher=balls.ie|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Maurice|last=Brosnan}} After losing the 2009 Fitzgibbon Cup final at left wing-back to [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] in 2009, Hickey was moved to the full-back line with [[Michael Walsh (Waterford hurler)|Michael "Brick" Walsh]] and [[Paddy Stapleton]] for UL's 1–17 to 2–11 defeat of the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]] in the final on 26 February 2011.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/ucc-taste-fitzgibbon-cup-success-401824.html|title=UCC taste Fitzgibbon Cup success|date=17 March 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/ul-overcome-local-rivals-to-win-fitzgibbon-cup-495107.html|title=UL overcome local rivals to win Fitzgibbon Cup|date=26 February 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018}} ===Club=== Hickey joined the [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels.{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/search/crawl/news/club-and-seamus-hickey-murroe-boher|title=My Club and I: Séamus Hickey - Murroe Boher|date=5 March 2015|publisher=GAA website|access-date=2 August 2018}} He played for the club's Junior B team for the first time at the age of fifteen, before becoming centre-back the following year. Hickey made his first senior appearance at the age of seventeen, marking [[Brian Geary]] in a championship game against [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]]. Hickey also played Gaelic football with the Monaleen senior team. On 16 October 2011, he won a [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|Limerick Football Championship]] medal after coming on as a substitute in Monaleen's 1–12 to 1–07 defeat of [[Newcastle West GAA|Newcastle West]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/collins-turns-the-screw-to-deny-wasteful-newcastle-west-26782679.html|title=Collins turns the screw to deny wasteful Newcastle West|date=17 October 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Kieran|last=McCarthy}} On 18 October 2017, Hickey won a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship]] medal following a 1–21 to 1–15 defeat of [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] in a replay of the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/277100/tobin-brothers-inspire-murroe-boher-to-limerick-premier-ihc-title-in-replay.html|title=Tobin brothers inspire Murroe-Boher to Limerick Premier IHC title in replay|date=18 October 2017|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} On 15 January 2020, it was announced that Hickey had transferred from his native Murroe-Boher to [[Croagh-Kilfinny]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/508837/limerick-all-ireland-hurling-winner-granted-club-transfer.html|title=Limerick All-Ireland hurling winner granted club transfer|date=15 January 2020|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=15 January 2020|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} In June 2021, Hickey added a County Junior medal to his silverware. He lined out at centre back for his new club [[Croagh-Kilfinny]], as they defeated Patrickswell in the Covid-delayed 2020 Junior A County Hurling Final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/gallery/sport/641026/croagh-kilfinny-end-118-year-wait-for-county-honour.html |title=Croagh-Kilfinny end 118 year wait for county honour |website=limerickleader.ie |access-date=2023-01-15}} ===Inter-county=== ====Minor and under-21==== Hickey first played for Limerick at minor level during the team's unsuccessful 2004 championship. He was eligible for the grade again the following year and, after being defeated by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster final]], Limerick qualified for the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] on 11 September 2005.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/cronins-accuracy-guides-cork-to-30th-minor-title-25982253.html|title=Cronin's accuracy guides Cork to 30th minor title|date=27 June 2005|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018}} Hickey scored two points from midfield in the 3–12 to 0–17 defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/galway-glee-as-goals-put-paid-to-gutsy-limerick-25965776.html|title=Galway glee as goals put paid to gutsy Limerick|date=12 September 2005|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Paddy|last=Hickey}} On 7 June 2006, Hickey made his first appearance for the Limerick under-21 hurling team in an 0–11 to 0–10 defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/match-reports/russell-wins-it-for-waterford-in-gripping-finale-5494.html|title=Russell wins it for Waterford in gripping finale|date=8 June 2006|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018}} It was the first of three unsuccessful seasons with the team. ====Senior==== On 26 March 2006, Hickey made his senior debut for Limerick when he came on as a substitute for [[Mark O'Riordan]] in a [[National Hurling League|National League]] defeat of [[Laois county hurling team|Laois]] at [[O'Moore Park]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/sub-ryan-puts-limerick-out-of-reach-26396358.html|title=Sub Ryan puts Limerick out of reach|date=27 March 2006|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018}} He later came on as a 62nd-minute substitute in Limerick's league final defeat by [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/archives/2006/0501/ireland/lethal-shefflin-fires-cats-to-title-2155.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180802223624/https://www.irishexaminer.com/archives/2006/0501/ireland/lethal-shefflin-fires-cats-to-title-2155.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 August 2018|title=Lethal Shefflin fires Cats to title|date=1 May 2006|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Jim|last=O'Sullivan}} Hickey made his first championship appearance on 14 May 2006 in a 0–22 to 2–12 defeat by [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20003418.html|title=Was this one of the great Championship displays?|date=15 May 2006|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} Hickey played in his first Munster final on 8 July 2007 in a 3–17 to 1–14 defeat by Waterford.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dynamic-dan-adds-some-extra-dash-for-the-dise-26443514.html|title=Dynamic Dan adds some extra dash for the Déise|date=9 July 2007|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Martin|last=Breheny}} After a subsequent [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]] defeat of Waterford, Hickey lined out in his first All-Ireland final on 2 September 2007.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/quickfire-limerick-pull-off-an-ambush-on-waterford-26311113.html|title=Quickfire Limerick pull off an ambush on Waterford|date=13 August 2007|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018}} Hickey had a torrid afternoon marking [[man of the match]] [[Eddie Brennan]] who scored 1-05 from play in Kilkenny's 2–19 to 1–15 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/kilkenny-handed-final-glory-on-a-plate-26315446.html|title=Kilkenny handed final glory on a plate|date=3 September 2007|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018}} Hickey later remarked: "I wouldn’t go OTT on it but I was a boy that day, I really was, playing with real men."{{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/hurling-news/limericks-defeat-kilkenny-2007-acting-2158469|title=A hard lesson learnt: Hickey's final shock spurring him on|date=13 August 2013|publisher=Irish Mirror|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Michael|last=Scully}} He ended the season by being nominated for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]] and by being named [[Vodafone Young Hurler of the Year]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2007/0927/223180-allstars/|title=Hurling All Stars nominations revealed|date=27 September 2007|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=2 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/ose-brothers-create-history-at-all-stars-332851.html|title=O'Sé brothers create history at All-Stars|date=19 October 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018}} After two disappointing seasons, Limerick manager [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]] dropped several high-profile players from the panel in October 2009.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/mccarthy-wields-the-axe-at-limerick-104495.html|title=McCarthy wields the axe at Limerick|date=30 October 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Martin|last=Kiely}} Over the course of the winter, many more players, including Hickey, withdrew from the panel and refused to play while McCarthy and his management team remained in place.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/2.823/four-more-players-quit-the-limerick-squad-1.1238677|title=Four more players quit the Limerick squad|date=2 January 2010|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=2 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/mccarthy-dispute-gets-silent-treatment-1.1244613|title=McCarthy dispute gets silent treatment|date=19 January 2010|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=2 August 2018}} The Limerick County Board refused to remove McCarthy and contested the league and championship with a new group of players. Hickey, who spent much of the championship season in [[Boston]], admitted: "It was a difficult decision. My ambition since I was knee high was to wear the green and white. But I stood up for something I believed in. I had stood shoulder to shoulder with many of the great men to wear Limerick jerseys over the last 10 years and I felt the treatment we were getting and the deal we were dealt wasn’t fair."{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-star-hickey-stands-by-decision-to-quit-152742.html|title=Limerick star Hickey stands by decision to quit|date=28 April 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} Hickey made his return to the Limerick team on 13 February 2011 in a National League defeat of [[Clare county hurling team|Clare]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-step-up-to-the-plate-for-ogrady-26695360.html|title=Limerick step up to the plate for O'Grady|date=14 February 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=2 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} On 30 April 2011, he won a National League Division 2 medal after a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of Clare in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}} On 14 July 2013, Hickey scored a point from left wing-forward in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] in the Munster final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} In the subsequent All-Ireland semi-final against Clare, he was forced off injured after just 14 minutes with a knee injury. Damage to his cruciate ligament was later diagnosed.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/90383/Cruciate-injury-confirmed-for-Limerick-s.html|title=Cruciate injury confirmed for Limerick's Hickey|date=20 August 2013|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} Hickey returned to the Limerick team in May 2014.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/optimism-and-drive-fire-hickey-back-in-limerick-reckoning-268170.html|title=Optimism and drive fire Hickey back in Limerick reckoning|date=10 May 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=John|last=Kelly}} On 10 August 2014, Hickey was named man of the match in Limerick's 2–13 to 0–17 defeat by Kilkenny in the All-Ireland semi-final.{{cite web|url=https://www.balls.ie/gaa/video-seamus-hickey-sunday-game-interview-132263|title=Video: Seamus Hickey Gave A Heartrending Man Of The Match Interview|date=11 August 2014|publisher=balls.ie|access-date=3 August 2018|first=P. 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=3 August 2018}} He ended the season by being named in the left corner-back position on the All-Star team.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/hurling-allstars-2014-1745105-Oct2014/|title=Here's the 2014 Allstar hurling team - 7 for Tipperary, 6 for Kilkenny, 2 for Limerick|date=24 October 2014|publisher=The '''Séamus Horgan''' (born 1946) is an Irish retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a goalkeeper for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Horgan made his first appearance for the team during the [[National Hurling League 1972-73|1972-73 National League]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1976|1976]]. During that time he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] winners' medal and two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medals.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=County profile: Limerick|work=Hogan Stand website|access-date=25 June 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archive-date=25 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Munster Senior Hurling Winning Teams|work=Munster GAA website|accessdate=25 June 2012}}</ref>

At club level Horgan played with [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]] in a career that spanned four decades.

==Playing career==

===Club===

Horgan played his club [[hurling]] with his local [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]] club.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/farmleader/Sideline-View---.3821827.jp|title=Sideline View . . . with Martin Kiely|date=27 February 2008|work=[[Limerick Leader]]|accessdate=15 July 2010}}</ref>  He enjoyed some success as he minded the Tournafulla net for four decades.  One of his last games was a county final at intermediate level in 1994 when Horgan was 48 years old.

===Inter-county===

Horgan first came to prominence as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team in the early 1970s.  He took over in the number one position in the 1972-73 National Hurling League which Limerick lost to [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].  In spite of this loss Limerick went on to win the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] for the first time since 1955, giving Horgan his first provincial medal.  Limerick later faced [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final, however, the Munster champions were burdened with the underdogs tag.  In spite of this Limerick powered to a seven-point victory, giving Horgan an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/3420/TALES-OF-3973-IMMORTALS.3163953.jp?articlepage=2|title=Tales of the '73 Immortals|date=31 August 2007|work=[[Limerick Leader]]|accessdate=15 July 2010}}</ref>

In 1974 Horgan won a second consecutive Munster title before lining out in a second consecutive All-Ireland final.  Once again Kilkenny provided the opposition.  Limerick stormed to an early lead, however, a [[Pat Delaney (Kilkenny hurler)|Pat Delaney]] shot from midfield bounced on the wet [[Croke Park]] surface and between Horgan's legs for a goal.  Two more goals for Kilkenny put an end to Limerick's hopes of victory as 'the Cats' emerged the winners by twelve points.

Horgan continued hurling at inter-county level until 1976 when he was replaced by [[Tommy Quaid]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.student.dcu.ie/~saundem2/WebProject/Counties/limerick/County%20Legends.html|title=County Legends: Tommy Quaid|work=Dublin City University website|accessdate=25 June 2012}}</ref>

===Inter-provincial===

Horgan was sub-goalkeeper to [[Séamus Durack]] on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] team that lost the [[Railway Cup]] final to [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] in 1974.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup Hurling|work=Munster GAA website|accessdate=25 June 2012}}</ref>

{{Short description|Irish hurler (1899–1995)}} {{Use British English|date=May 2015}} {{Use dmy dates|date=May 2026}} {{Infobox Gaelic games biography | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Garrett Howard | irish = Gearóid Ó hÍomhair | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 11 | occupation = Garda | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Croom GAA|Croom]]

1924–1929
1929–1932
1933–1936 | ic_apps_points = | ic_munster = 5 | ic_leinster = 3 | ic_all_ireland = 5 | nhl = 4 | all_stars = 1 | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_place=[[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]], Ireland | birth_date={{Birth date|df=yes|1899|12|10}} | death_date={{death date and age|df=yes|1995|1|20|1899|12|10}} | death_place=[[Borrisokane]], [[County Tipperary]], Ireland }} '''Garrett Howard''' (10 December 1899 – 20 January 1995) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a left wing-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]], [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] and [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] senior teams.{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1921.htm#934685488|title=1921 All-Ireland champions: Garrett Howard|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|access-date=24 April 2014}}{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/documents/garrett-howard.pdf|title=Great Limerick Athletes: Garrett Howard of Croom|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=24 April 2014|first=Séamus|last=Ó Ceallaigh|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140424024436/http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/documents/garrett-howard.pdf|archive-date=24 April 2014|url-status=dead}} Born in [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]], Howard first arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of twenty-one when he first linked up with the Limerick senior team, before later lining out with the Dublin and Tipperary sides before returning to the Limerick colours. He made his senior debut in the [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1921 championship]]. Howard went on to enjoy a fifteen-year inter-county career, and won five [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals, five [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals, three [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster]] medals and four [[National Hurling League]] medals. He was an All-Ireland runner-up on two occasions. Howard represented the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] and [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] inter-provincial teams at various times, winning two [[Railway Cup]] medals during that period. At club level he won eight championship medals, playing with a host of clubs including [[Croom GAA|Croom]], [[Garda GAA|Garda]] and [[Toomevara GAA|Toomevara]]. With Ireland Howard won two [[Tailteann Games (Irish Free State)|Tailteann Games]] medals, while he also represented his country in [[shinty]]. His retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1936 championship]]. In retirement from playing, Howard became involved in team management and coaching. At inter-county level he guided [[Clare GAA|Clare]] to an [[Oireachtas Tournament|Oireachtas Cup]] as well as a first Munster final appearance in seventeen years. At club level he trained Carrick Swan GAA, [[Feakle GAA|Feakle]] and [[Burgess GAA|Burgess]]-[[Kildangan GAA|Kildangan]]. Howard also served as a club referee. Howard was the third recipient of the [[GAA All-Time All-Star Award (Hurling)|All-Time All-Star Award]] in 1982, and holds the record of being the only Limerick man to have won five All-Ireland medals. ==Playing career== ===Club=== Howard enjoyed his first success in club hurling with Croom in 1919. A narrow 1–1 to 1–0 defeat of [[Fedamore GAA|Fedamore]] gave him a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] medal.{{cite web|url=http://croom.wordpress.com/2007/11/09/croom-v-adare/|title=Croom v Adare: the facts|publisher=Croom website|access-date=23 April 2014}} A move to [[Dublin]] saw Howard join the [[Garda GAA|Garda]] club which enjoyed an unprecedented run of success in the late twenties. Five successive [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] titles were annexed between 1925 and 1929, with Howard lining out in each of these victories.{{cite web|url=http://www.gardagaaclub.ie/index.php/2-uncategorised|title=Garda GAA: History|publisher=Garda GAA website|access-date=23 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924020728/http://www.gardagaaclub.ie/index.php/2-uncategorised|archive-date=24 September 2015|url-status=dead}} Howard finished his club hurling career with [[Toomevara GAA|Toomevara]]. In 1930 he won a [[Tipperary Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal following a 4–1 to 1–0 defeat of [[Boherlahan-Dualla GAA|Boherlahan]] in a replay of the decider Toomevara retained their championship title in 1931, with Howard collecting a second consecutive championship medal following a 5–4 to 2–0 defeat of [[Moycarkey-Borris GAA|Moycarkey-Borris]]. ===Inter-county=== ====Beginnings==== Howard joined the Limerick senior team in 1921, at a time when the championship was severely hampered by the [[Irish War of Independence|War of Independence]]. As a result of this disruption only [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and Limerick contested the southern provincial championship. A 5–2 to 1–2 defeat of the reigning champions gave Howard his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal. The subsequent All-Ireland final was delayed until 4 March 1923, with Howard included on the Limerick team to face [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]. Limerick captain [[Bob McConkey]] scored a hat-trick of goals in the opening half, before adding a fourth after the interval. Limerick eventually powered to an 8–5 to 3–2 victory. It was Howard's first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal.{{cite web|url=https://www.crokepark.ie/getmedia/89c0bd0d-09c9-41c6-8a46-5b18d7beec77/All-Ireland-Glory.pdf|title=All-Ireland Glory|publisher=Croke Park website|access-date=23 April 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328014304/https://www.crokepark.ie/getmedia/89c0bd0d-09c9-41c6-8a46-5b18d7beec77/All-Ireland-Glory.pdf|archive-date=28 March 2012|df=dmy-all}} ====Success with Dublin==== In 1924 Howard transferred to the [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] senior team. Success was immediate as he captured a [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster]] medal following a 4–4 to 3–1 defeat of first-time finalists [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]. The subsequent All-Ireland final was played on 14 December 1924, with reigning champions [[Galway GAA|Galway]] providing the opposition. The westerners had the measure of Dublin for much of the game, however, Dublin got back on level terms when Howard drove the Galway goalkeeper into and under the net before scoring a second goal. Dublin eventually won the game on a score line of 5–3 to 2–6 and Howard collected his second All-Ireland medal. Three years later in 1927 Howard won a second Leinster medal following a 7–7 to 4–6 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. On 4 September 1927 Dublin faced reigning champions Cork in the All-Ireland decider. Howard was one of nine members of the [[Garda Síochána]] on the Dublin team who took a 2–3 to 0–1 lead at half-time. Cork fought back in the third quarter, however, Howard collected his third All-Ireland medal following a 4–8 to 1–3 victory. Howard added a third Leinster medal to his collection in 1928 following a 9–7 to 4–3 defeat of Offaly. In 1930 Howard's Dublin renewed their rivalry with Cork, this time in the final of the [[National Hurling League]]. A 7–4 to 5–5 victory gave him his first league medal. ====Move to Tipperary==== A transfer to [[Toomevara]], [[County Tipperary]] in his duties as a Garda saw Howard link up with the Tipperary senior team. He played two championship campaigns with Tipp in 1931 and 1932 without success, however, he did win a [[Thomond Feis]] medal. ====Return to Limerick==== In 1933 overtures were made to Howard encouraging him to rejoin an up-an-coming Limerick senior team. Howard agreed and played championship hurling with his native county after an absence of a decade. His return in green and white saw an upsurge in Limerick's fortunes as the team reached the provincial decider against [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in 1933. With eight minutes left in the game, some spectators invaded the pitch and the match was abandoned. Since Limerick were winning by 3–7 to 1–2, the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]] declared them the champions and Howard collected his second Munster medal. The subsequent All-Ireland final on 3 September 1933 saw a record crowd of 45,176 travel to [[Croke Park]] to see Limerick face Kilkenny. After being level at the interval, the game remained close in the second half until a solo-run goal by [[Johnny Dunne]] sealed a 1–7 to 0–6 victory for Kilkenny. The league campaign in 1933–34 saw Limerick reach the decider against Dublin. In spite of home advantage, Limerick had to battle hard for a 3–6 to 3–3 victory. It was Howard's second league medal. The subsequent provincial championship saw Limerick reach the decider, where they played Waterford for the second year in-a-row. The result was much the same, with Howard collecting a third Munster medal following a 4–8 to 2–5 victory. The All-Ireland final on 2 September 1934 was a special occasion as it was the golden jubilee final of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. Dublin were the opponents and a close game developed. After leading by a point at the interval, Limerick went five clear with time running out. Dublin fought their way back to secure a remarkable draw. The replay on 30 September turned out to be an even closer affair, with both sides level with two minutes to go. Points from [[Mick Mackey]] and [[Jackie O'Connell]] and a remarkable four goals from [[Dave Clohessy]] secured a 5–2 to 2–6 victory for Limerick. The win gave Howard a fourth All-Ireland medal. Howard added a third National League medal to his collection in 1935, as Limerick retained their title in a straightforward league format. Limerick dominated the provincial series of games once again, and lined out in the decider against Tipperary. Howard collected a fourth Munster medal following a 5–5 to 1–4 victory. Kilkenny were Limerick's opponents in the subsequent All-Ireland final on 1 September 1935 and, once again, the game was a close affair. Limerick were the favourites, and a record crowd of over 46,000 turned up to the game. At the beginning of the second-half [[Lory Meagher]] sent over a huge point from midfield giving Kilkenny a lead which they would not surrender. The game ended in controversial circumstances for Mick Mackey when Limerick were awarded a close-in free to level the game. Jack Keane issued an instruction from the sideline that [[Timmy Ryan]], the team captain, was to take the free and put the sliotar over the bar for the equalising point. As he lined up to take it, Mackey pushed him aside and took the free himself. The shot dropped short and into the waiting hands of the Kilkenny goalkeeper and was cleared. The game ended shortly after with Kilkenny triumphing by 2–5 to 2–4. Limerick began 1936 by retaining their league title, having won seven of their games and drawing one. It was Howard's fourth league medal. As a result of a tour to the United States, Limerick were awarded a bye into the Munster final. Tipperary provided the opposition in the provincial final, however, Limerick captain Mick Mackey ran riot and scored 5–3. The 8–5 to 4–6 victory gave Howard a fifth Munster medal. For the third time in four years the lure of a Kilkenny-Limerick clash brought a record crowd of over 50,000 to Croke Park for the All-Ireland decider on 6 September 1936. The first half produced a game that lived up to the previous clashes, and Limerick had a two-point advantage at half-time. [[Jackie Power]] scored two first-half goals, while a solo-run goal by captain Mackey in the second-half helped Limerick to a 5–6 to 1–5 victory. It was Howard's fifth All-Ireland medal, a record for a Limerick player. This was his last appearance for Limerick as he retired shortly afterwards. ===Inter-provincial=== Howard's inter-county performances ensured his selection on the inaugural [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] team for the inter-provincial championship. A 7–6 to 3–5 defeat of [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] gave him a [[Railway Cup]] medal. Leinster faced defeat at the hands of [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the deciders of 1928 and 1929. Howard's return to Limerick saw him included on the Munster team in 1931. A 1–12 to 2–6 defeat of Leinster gave him a second Railway Cup medal. ===International=== With the [[Tailteann Games (Irish Free State)|revival of the Tailteann Games]] in 1924, Howard received the ultimate honour by being one of fifteen hurlers chosen to make up an Irish hurling team. Ireland defeated a United States selection on that occasion. That same year he also played against [[Scotland]] in a [[shinty]] international. In 1928 Howard was once again included on the Irish hurling team for the Tailteann Games. The United States were defeated by the Irish selection once again. ==Coaching career== ===Clare=== At inter-county level Howard was trainer of the Clare senior hurling team for a brief period in the fifties. In 1954 he guided the team to a 3–6 to 0–12 defeat of All-Ireland runners-up [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the final of the [[Oireachtas Tournament|Oireachtas Cup]]. In 1955 Clare defeated Cork and Tipperary in the provincial championship and were hot favourites to take the Munster title. An unfancied Limerick team upset the odds and defeated Howard's side by 2–16 to 2–6. ===Naomh Pádraig=== At club level Howard took charge of Naomh Pádraig, a combined [[Burgess GAA|Burgess]] and [[Kildangan GAA|Kildangan]] under-21 team in the 1970s. Under him the club won back-to-back under-21 championships in 1970 and 1971. Howard also trained the [[Feakle GAA|Feakle]] hurling team for a time. ==Recognition== As a hurler who claimed every honour in the game, Howard became (in 1982) the third recipient of the [[All-Time All Star Award (hurling)|GAA All-Time All-Star Award]]. ==Personal life== Howard was born in Fanningstown Castle, [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]] on 10 December 1899, the second eldest son to Martin and Kate Howard who were farmers Educated locally, Howard joined the newly formed [[Garda Síochána]] in his early twenties and served in Dublin, Toomevara, [[Portroe]], [[Carrick-on-Suir]] and [[Feakle]] over the next forty years. Howard was married to Josephine "Josie" Barry (1912–1990), herself a niece of Tipperary hurler [[Frank McGrath (hurler)|Frank McGrath]], and the couple had six children: Kathleen, Patricia 'Pat', Josephine 'Jo', [[Liz Howard|Liz]], Ann and Garrett 'Garry'. Jo Howard was a [[camogie]] star in her own right and played for both Clare and Tipperary before serving as the secretary of the North Tipperary Bord na nÓg for ten years. Liz Howard was the first and only female analysts on ''[[the Sunday Game]]'', before later serving as [[Public relations officer|PRO]] of the Tipperary County Board and president of the [[Camogie Association]]. She also played camogie for Clare, Tipperary and Dublin. Pat and Ann also played camogie for Feakle. Howard's son, Garry, played under-21 hurling with Tipperary in 1972 while his grandson, also named Garrett, was a member of the Tipperary minor hurling team in 1997 and also won a Harty Cup and All Ireland Colleges title with St. Flannans College. Howard died at Dannell Nursing Home, [[Borrisokane]] on 20 January 1995, the last surviving member of the All-Ireland-winning Limerick and Dublin teams of the 1920s and 1930s. ==Honours== ===Player=== '''Bernard Hartigan''' (born 1943) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a midfielder for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Hartigan made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1964|1964 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting for the next decade. During that time he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and one [[National Hurling League]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=Limerick GAA profile|publisher=Hogan Stand website|accessdate=28 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archive-date=25 May 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|accessdate=28 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721124423/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=21 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At club level, Hartigan was a one-time [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|county football championship]] medalist with [[Old Christians GAA|Old Christians]].

Hartigan's brother, [[Pat Hartigan|Pat]], was also an All-Ireland medalist with Limerick.
