[[Mallow GAA|Mallow]] | cl_position = Forward | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | colleges = [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] | col_years = 1987-1991 | fitz = 3 | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Full-back | ic_years = 1989–2003 | ic_apps_points = 9 (3-05) | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | birth_date={{Birth date and age|1970|1|2|df=yes}} | birth_place=[[Kilfinane]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Pat Heffernan''' (born 2 January 1970 in [[Kilfinane]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]) is an Irish [[hurling]] selector and former player. He is a former selector with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior hurling team. He is currently manager of Mullinahone Senior Hurling team and teaches geography at the Patrician Academy Mallow Secondary School. An effective forward, Heffernan enjoyed a reasonably successful playing career at club level with [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]], [[UCC GAA|UCC]] and [[Mallow GAA|Mallow]] and at inter-county level with Limerick. He was a key member of the latter team during the 1990s and collected one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] title. In retirement from playing Heffernan has become involved in team management. He gained early experience at club level with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]], [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]], [[Bride Rovers]] and with his own Blackrock club. He took charge of the [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] senior hurling team between 2007 and 2008, while later serving as a selector with the Limerick intermediate team. Heffernan was appointed as a selector on the Limerick senior hurling team in September 2010.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/Donal-OGrady-set-to-be.6541550.jp|title=Donal O'Grady set to be new Limerick hurling manager|publisher=[[Limerick Leader]]|date=21 September 2010|accessdate=2010-09-22}} ==Club career== Heffernan began his playing career with his local club [[Blackrock GAA|Blackrock]] and enjoyed some initial success. He won a county junior title in the early 1990s, however, after a brief period in the senior ranks Blackrock returned to junior status once again. A move to Mallow in the early 2000s saw Heffernan join the [[Mallow GAA|local club]] there, where he won a junior league title in 2007. In 2009 Heffernan transferred back to his home club Blackrock where he joined the team as goalkeeper. It was a successful return as Blackrock secured the county junior title that year. Heffernan's club later represented the county in the provincial series of games and even reached the final. Cork champions [[Fermoy GAA|Fermoy]] provided the opposition on that occasion, however, it was Blackrock who secured a narrow 1–12 to 0–14 victory and Heffernan collected a [[Munster Junior Club Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medal.{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/jhclub_teams/|title=Munster Junior Club Hurling Champions|publisher=[[Munster GAA]]|accessdate=2010-09-24}} An All-Ireland final with [[St. Colmcille's GAA|St. Colmcille's]] of Tyrone providing the opposition. Blackrock had little difficulty in disposing of the Ulstermen on a score line of 1–18 to 0–9. Heffernan kept a clean sheet again while also collecting an [[All-Ireland Junior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] club winners' medal.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickindependent.com/sport/sport/mighty-blackrock-come-from-nowhere-to-the-top-of-the-pile/ |title=Mighty Blackrock come from nowhere to the top of the pile |work=Limerick Independent|date=19 February 2010 |accessdate=2010-09-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713210720/http://www.limerickindependent.com/sport/sport/mighty-blackrock-come-from-nowhere-to-the-top-of-the-pile/ |archivedate=13 July 2011 }} ==Inter-county career== Heffernan first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior hurling team in the early 1990s. He made his championship debut in 1991, however, he remained a fringe player for his first few seasons on the team. By 1994 Heffernan was a key member of the full-forward line and played in his first Munster final. Provincial whipping boys [[Clare GAA|Clare]] were the opponents and a rout took place. A 0–25 to 2–10 score line gave Limerick the win and gave Heffernan his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medal.{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Munster Senior Hurling Champions|publisher=[[Munster GAA]]|accessdate=2010-09-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328073637/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=28 March 2019|url-status=dead}} Limerick subsequently qualified to meet [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the All-Ireland final. It looked as if Heffernan's side were going to make history and claim the title as Limerick had a five-point lead with as many minutes left. Offaly suddenly sprang to life following a [[Johnny Dooley (hurler)|Johnny Dooley]] goal from a close-in free. Following the puck-out Offaly worked the ball upfield and [[Pat O'Connor (hurler)|Pat O'Connor]] struck for a second goal. The Offaly forwards scored another five unanswered points in the time remaining to secure a 3–16 to 2–13 victory. It was a bitter blow for Limerick who looked as if they had one hand on the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]]. Limerickregrouped and contested the a second Munster final in succession in 1995. Clare were the opponents once again, however, the roles were reversed on this occasion with victory going to the men from the banner county. Heffernan left the inter-county set up following this defeat. He returned briefly in 2003 at the behest of new manager [[Pad Joe Whelahan]], however, his second coming was short-lived.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2003/1222/heffernanp.html |title=Pat Heffernan recalled to Limerick hurling team |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=23 December 2003 |accessdate=2009-03-06 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==Management career== ===Early experience=== After retiring Heffernan pursued a career in coaching, gaining experience in his native Limerick where he became involved with several clubs, including [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]], [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] and his native Blackrock. He enjoyed little success with these early endeavours. In 2007 Heffernan took charge of [[Bride Rovers]] GAA Club in east Cork and guided the team to the semi-finals of the [[Cork Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]].{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2008/1231/kerry.html|title=Heffernan resigns as Kerry hurling boss|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=31 December 2008|accessdate=2009-03-04}} ===Kerry=== In late 2007 Heffernan was appointed manager of the [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] senior hurling team for a one-year term.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Kerry/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=87337|title=Heffernan to meet Kerry players|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=4 January 2008|accessdate=2009-03-06}} His first season in charge got off to a good start as 'the Kingdom' only lost one game in the group stage of the [[National Hurling League]]. This allowed Heffernan's side to advance to the semi-final of the competition, however, [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]] won the game by 1–19 to 3–4.{{cite web|url=http://www.corkgaaresults.com/national-hurling-league-2008.html|title=National Hurling League 2008|publisher=Cork GAA Results|accessdate=2010-09-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724025904/http://www.corkgaaresults.com/national-hurling-league-2008.html|archive-date=24 July 2011|url-status=usurped}} In the subsequent [[Christy Ring Cup]] Kerry topped their group and qualified for a home quarter-final against old rivals Carlow. It was one of the toughest draws and, in spite of home advantage, Kerry were heavily defeated by 2–4 to 1–14. Heffernan failed to secure silverware but was reappointed as manager for a second season at the end of 2008.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Kerry/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=103497|title=Heffernan reappointed Kerry hurling boss|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=11 November 2008|accessdate=2010-09-25}} This reappointment was short-lived as Heffernan subsequently stepped down before the start of the season citing personal reasons.{{cite web|url=http://www.kerrygaa.ie/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=369&Itemid=78|title=Pat Heffernan steps down|publisher=[[Kerry GAA]]|accessdate=2009-03-04}} ===St. Brendan's Ardfert=== In 2010 Heffernan was appointed trainer of the [[St. Brendan's Ardfert]] Club in County Kerry. He managed them to the semi-final stage of the County Championship where St. Brendan's were defeated by Ballyduff. ===Mallow=== In 2010 Heffernan took charge of the Mallow Intermediate Hurling Team. After initial success with a victory over [[Castlelyons]] in the Championship, Heffernan's side were defeated in the second round. In the 2011 Heffernan was appointed as the Mallow U21 Hurling Manager. ===Limerick=== In September 2010 Heffernan was named as a selector along with former teammates [[Ciarán Carey]] and [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J. Ryan]] in [[Dónal O'Grady]]'s new management team to oversee the Limerick Senior Hurling Team for 2011. ===Mullinahone=== In 2012 he was appointed manager of Mullinahone Senior Hurling Team. '''Seán Herbert''' (1923–1993) was an Irish sportsperson. He played [[hurling]] with his local club [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] and with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team from 1942 until 1953.

==Playing career==
===Club===
Herbert played his club hurling with the famous [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] club in Limerick, and won his first senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county title]] in 1942 in the company of fellow player [[Mick Mackey]].  It was the first of seven county championship victories in-a-row for Herbert and his club.  He won an eighth county medal in 1955.

===Inter-county===
Herbert's performances with his club brought him to the attention of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] selectors.  He made his senior debut for the team in 1942.

Two years later in 1944 Herbert lined out in his first Munster final.  [[Cork GAA|Cork]], a team attempting to capture a fourth successive All-Ireland title, provided the opposition.  The game was an exciting one with thousands of people walking to the match in [[Thurles]] as a result of war-time travel restrictions.{{citation needed|date=June 2017}}  The spectators were not disappointed, however, the game ended in a draw – Cork 4–13, Limerick 6–7.  Cork however won the replay.

In 1945 Herbert played in his second Munster final.  [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] were the opponents on that occasion, however, for the second time he ended up on the losing side.  Tipp claimed the victory by 4–3 to 2–6.

The year 1946 saw Herbert play in a third provincial decider.  Cork, the victors at the same stage two years earlier, provided the opposition once again.  Limerick, however, had defeated All-Ireland champions Tipperary in the Munster semi-final and looked a good bet to take the title.{{original research inline|date=June 2017}} Cork however won the game by 3–8 to 1–3.

In 1947, Herbert had his only success with the Limerick team as he captured a [[National Hurling League]] medal.  Once again his side reached the Muster final as the All-Ireland champions Cork played the League champions.  The game was a close affair, however, for the fourth year in-a-row Limerick were defeated.

Two years later in 1949 Herbert was back in his fifth Munster final.  Once again it looked as if Limerick might claim the victory.  Tipperary were the opponents on this occasion and it was that team that claimed a 1–16 to 2–10 victory.  This was Herbert's last big occasion with Limerick.  He continued playing with his county until 1953.

===Provincial===
Herbert also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial hurling competition.  He captured his first [[Railway Cup]] title in 1946 as Munster defeated [[Ulster GAA|Ulster]].  Herbert captured further Railway Cup medals in 1948, 1949, 1952 and 1953.

==Death==
On 12 September 1993, it was announced that Herbert had died at the age of 70.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sean Herbert |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/sunday-independent-dublin-ed-sean-her/204456069/ |access-date=23 August 2026 |publisher=Sunday Independent |date=12 September 1993 |pages=5}}</ref>

{{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Mike Houlihan | irish = Mícheál Ó hUallacháin | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 10 | occupation = Publican, politician | nickname = Houla | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] | cl_position = Midfield | cl_years = 1985-2006 | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 2 | cl_province= 2 | cl_all_ireland = 0 | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Midfield | ic_years = 1988-1999 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 2 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 2 | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_date = February 1969 | birth_place=[[Kilmallock]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Michael Houlihan''' (born February 1969) is an Irish politician, [[hurling]] coach and former player. At club level, he played with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Playing career== Houlihan first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club, and was part of the club's minor team that won the Limerick MAHC title in 1987.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Kilmallock abú!|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=19 September 1987|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to adult level and won [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medals in 1992 and 1994, when he [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ed the team.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/128541/1992--When-Kilmallock-conquered-Limerick.html|title=1992: When Kilmallock conquered Limerick and Munster|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=20 November 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Both of these titles were subsequently followed by [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] titles.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Houlihan also lined out in Kilmallock's 1-17 to 2-07 defeat by [[Sarsfields GAA (Galway)|Sarsfields]] in the [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1993 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-ireland-club-hurling/26713575.html|title=All-Ireland Club Hurling|publisher=Irish Independent|date=15 March 2011|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Houlihan first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 1986 and 1987. He immediately progressed to the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]], but ended his underage inter-county career without silverware.{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/66177|title=Mike Houlihan|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=8 May 1992|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Houlihan joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] during the [[1987–88 National Hurling League|1987–88 National League]]. It was in that competition that he collected his first silverware when Limerick claimed the league title in 1992.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Houlihan won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals in 1994 and 1996, however, Limerick faced subsequent All-Ireland final defeats by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] respectively.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40370429.html|title=A player-by-player guide to Wexford's All-Ireland 25 years on: 'We laughed as much as we hurled'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=1 September 2021|access-date=2 January 2025|first=|last=}} He also claimed [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] awards in both of those seasons. Houlihan added a second National League medal to his collection in 1997.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/945696/limerick-county-final-day-to-honour-25th-anniversary-of-1997-hurling-league-title-victory.html|title=Limerick county final day to honour 25th anniversary of 1997 hurling league title victory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 October 2022|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Nash being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won a [[Railway Cup]] medal in 1992 after a defeat of [[Ulster GAA|Ulster]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Management career== In retirement from playing, Houlihan became involved in team management and coaching at club level with Kilmallock. He has coached all levels at juvenile and underage, from under-14 to under-16, as well as training the club's senior team in 2007.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/inside-back-where-are-they-now-mike-houlihan/30953964.html|title=Where are they now? Mike Houlihan|publisher=Irish Independent|date=1 February 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Political career== Houlihan was elected to [[Limerick County Council]] as a [[Fine Gael]] candidate in the [[2009 Irish local elections|2009 local elections]]. He failed to be re-elected at the following election in [[2014 Irish local elections|2014]].{{cite web|url=https://electionsireland.org/candidate.cfm?ID=9869|title=Mike Houihan|publisher=Elections Ireland website|date=|access-date=12 March 2013|first=|last=}} ==Personal life== His son, [[Micheál Houlihan]], has also played for Kilmallock and the Limerick senior hurling team.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-davy-fitzs-of-the-world-want-to-change-the-game-if-you-take-hurling-out-of-hurling-its-not-the-same/40978833.html|title=‘The Davy Fitzs of the world want to change the game. If you take hurling out of hurling, it’s not the same’|publisher=Irish Independent|date=24 October 2021|access-date=12 March 2025|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Kilmallock *[[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship]]: [[1992–93 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|1992]], [[1994–95 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|1994]] (c) *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1992 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1992]], [[1994 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1994]] (c) *Limerick Minor A Hurling Championship: 1987 ;Limerick *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1994]], [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1996]] *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1991–92 National Hurling League|1991–92]], [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] ;Munster *[[Railway Cup]]: [[1992 Railway Cup Hurling Championship|1992]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title= Mike Houlihan navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Hurling Team 1994}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1996}} {{Munster Hurling Team 1992}} {{1994 Hurling All Stars}} {{1996 Hurling All Stars}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Houlihan, Mike}} [[Category:1969 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Kilmallock hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]]

'''Michael Galligan''' (born 17 January 1968) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who played for club side [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/49045|title=Mike Galligan|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=7 June 1991|access-date=3 April 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Career==

Galligan first played competitive hurling at primary school in [[Caherdavin]] before lining out for [[CBS Sexton Street]] team in the [[Dr. Harty Cup]]. His early club career with [[Claughaun GAA|CLaughaun]] yielded county championship titles in every juvenile and underage grade before winning his only [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Championship]] title at senior level in 1986. Galligan's first inter-county experience came during a two-year spell with the Limerick minor team, which was followed by two seasons with the under-21 team. He made his senior debut against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] during the [[1989–90 National Hurling League|1989–90 league]]. Galligan was a stalwart of the team for much of the following decade and was included on the Limerick teams that lost the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland finals]] in [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1994]] and [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1996]]. His career honours include two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medals, two [[National Hurling League|National League]] titles and a [[Railway Cup]] medal with [[Munster GAA|Munster]]. Galligan retired from inter-county hurling in December 2000.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/18591|title=Galligan calls it a day|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=20 December 2000|access-date=3 April 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Galligan was born in [[Cork (city)|Cork]] but was raised in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]] after his family relocated there shortly after he was born. His father, [[Billy Galligan]], won a [[Cork Senior Hurling Championship|Cork County Championship]] title with [[Blackrock GAA|Blackrock]] in 1961 and also lined out with the [[Cork senior hurling team]]. Galligan's uncle, Tommy Joy, was a prominent player with [[London Irish]] [[rugby union]] team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

'''Ger Hegarty''' (born 1966) is an Irish retired [[Hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Old Christians GAA Club|Old Christians]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Career==

Hegarty played hurling at all grades as a student at [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]]. He was part of the school's senior team that lost to [[St Finbarr's College, Farranferris|St Finbarr's College]] in the final of the [[Dr Harty Cup]] in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Farna turn it on in second half|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=16 April 1984|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> 

At club level, Hegarty first played for [[Old Christians GAA Club|Old Christians]] at juvenile and underage levels, before eventually progressing to adult level. He won a [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] medal in 1991, after scoring 0-07 in the final against [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Historic win for Gallant Old Christians|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=11 November 1991|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

At inter-county level, Hegarty first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick’s last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He progressed to the under-21 team and won consecutive [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] titles, before claiming an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after a 2-15 to 3-06 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|1987 final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/109109/Limerick-s-first-All-Ireland-U.html|title=Limerick’s first All Ireland U-21 hurling title in 1987|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 September 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Hegarty joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] during the [[1985–86 National Hurling League|1985–86 National League]]. It was in that competition that he collected his first silverware when Limerick claimed the league title in 1992.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Hegarty later won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal, before lining out in Limerick's defeat by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1994 All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-1994-all-ireland-shc-final-offaly-v-limerick|title=Flashback: 1994 All-Ireland SHC Final - Offaly v Limerick|publisher=GAA website|date=19 March 2020|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

A series of injuries severely impacted on Hegarty's inter-county career. A [[cruciate ligament]] tear occurred in his left knee in a challenge game against [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in 1992. Hegarty suffered a similar injury in his right knee in 1995.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gearoid-hegarty-limerick-hurler-of-the-year-2-5364510-Feb2021/|title=The Limerick footballer who became Hurler of the Year|publisher=The 42|date=25 February 2021|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Hegarty being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He made his only appearance in 1991 but failed to win a [[Railway Cup]] medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Personal life==

His son, [[Gearóid Hegarty]], has won six [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medals with Limerick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/1253701/limerick-great-ger-hegarty-happy-to-fade-into-family-background.html|title=Limerick great Ger Hegarty happy to fade into family background|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=20 July 2023|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

1944–1954 | ic_apps_points = | ic_munster = 1 | ic_leinster = 2 | ic_all_ireland = 1 | nhl = 0 | all_stars = | cl_update = | ic_update = 17:42, 29 March 2014 }} '''Matthew Anthony Herbert''' (9 August 1920 – 6 March 2014) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Fianna Fáil]] politician and [[Hurling|hurler]], who played as a full-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/herberttony.pdf|title=Tony Herbert of Ahane|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=19 March 1955|access-date=6 May 2011}} ==Biography== Born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], Herbert first played competitive hurling while at school in [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]]. He arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of seventeen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team. He made his senior debut during the [[Oireachtas Tournament|1939 Oireachtas Cup]]. Herbert went on to play a key role for Limerick for a brief period, before later joining the [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] senior team, and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, two [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster]] medals and one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal. He was an All-Ireland runner-up on two occasions. As a member of the [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] inter-provincial team at various times throughout his career, Herbert ended his career without a [[Railway Cup]] medal. At club level he won five [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|hurling championship]] and four [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|football championship]] with [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]], before later winning five [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|hurling championship]] medals with [[Faughs GAA|Faughs]]. Herbert's retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1954 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1954 championship]]. Whilst still a player, Herbert became involved in team management and coaching. He trained and coached the Dublin minor hurling team to [[Leinster Minor Hurling Championship|Leinster]] success in 1952. His uncle, Paddy Kenneally, was an [[All-Ireland Senior Football Championship|All-Ireland]] medalist with [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] in [[Gaelic football]]. Herbert's brothers, [[Seán Herbert|Seán]] and [[Michael Herbert|Michael]], and his nephew, [[Turlough Herbert|Turlough]] all played with Limerick. Herbert was elected to [[Seanad Éireann]] in 1977 by the [[Labour Panel]].{{cite web|url=https://www.oireachtas.ie/en/members/member/Anthony-Herbert.S.1980-04-16/|title=Anthony Herbert|work=Oireachtas Members Database|access-date=17 January 2012}} He lost his seat at the 1981 election but was re-elected to the [[16th Seanad]] at the 1982 election. He lost his seat again at the 1983 election. At the time of his death Herbert was Limerick's oldest All-Ireland medalist, while he was also the last surviving member of the 1940 All-Ireland-winning team.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/community/limerick-s-last-1940-all-ireland-winner-passes-away-1-5921032|title=Limerick's last 1940 All-Ireland winner passes away|publisher=Limerick '''Declan Hannon''' (born 25 November 1992) is an Irish former [[Hurling|hurler]] who played for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Adare GAA|Adare]] and previously at inter-county level as [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|captain]] of the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He captained Limerick to the All Ireland hurling title in 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 becoming the first Limerick captain since [[Mick Mackey]] to captain Limerick to victory more than once. He is the only hurling captain to lift the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] a record four times as well as lifting the Mackey cup in the Munster hurling final six times. He is the most successful hurling captain in hurling history. He usually lined out as a centre-back.

==Early life==

Hannon attended Scoil Naomh Iosaf, an all boys school situated in the village of Adare. Hurling was a pillar of the education system in the school, pushed by two Tipperary men, Brother Cathal Duane (Kilruane) and Principal Barry O'Riordan (Nenagh).
Hannon was born in [[Adare]], [[County Limerick]]. His granduncle, [[Pat Stakelum]], captained [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] to the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 1949.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/moran-hannon-has-great-potential-105775.html|title=Moran: Hannon has 'great potential'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=17 November 2009|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Ardscoil Rís===

Hannon first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. Having played in every grade as a hurler, he was centre-back on the college's senior hurling team. On 11 March 2010, Hannon scored three points from play when Ardscoil Rís defeated Thurles CBS in the final of the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ard-scoil-ris-end-harty-cup-marathon-with-historic-victory-114301.html|title=Ard Scoil Rís end Harty Cup marathon with historic victory|date=12 March 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref>

On 27 February 2011, Hannon was again at centre-back when Ardscoil Rís retained the Harty Cup title after a 3–19 to 0–03 defeat of [[C.B.S. Charleville]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/awesome-ardscoil-storm-to-harty-title-26709031.html|title=Awesome Ardscoil storm to Harty title|date=28 February 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref>

===Mary Immaculate College===

During his studies at [[Mary Immaculate College]], Hannon was selected for the college's senior hurling team. On 27 February 2016, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal as Mary I won their first ever title after a 1–30 to 3–22 defeat of the [[University of Limerick]] after two periods of extra-time. Hannon, in spite of being substituted in the 79th minute, ended as the game's top scorer. He said of the game "That was one of the most unbelievable games I have played in. We had it won and lost so many times throughout the game, but we’d have stayed until midnight to win."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/eamonn-cregan-hails-heroic-mary-i-384649.html|title=Eamonn Cregan hails heroic Mary I|date=29 February 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

===Adare===

Hannon joined the [[Adare GAA|Adare]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels. He enjoyed championship success in the under-14 and under-16 grades before making his championship debut with the club's senior team as a sixteen-year-old. On 18 October 2009, Hannon scored three points from right wing-forward when Adare defeated [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] by 1–17 to 0–03 in the final of the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/adare-swat-na-piarsaigh-aside-to-claim-limerick-title-430709.html|title=Adare swat Na Piarsaigh aside to claim Limerick title|date=18 October 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Hannon first played for Limerick at minor level. He made his first appearance on 25 June 2010 in a 1–17 to 2–12 defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/property/arid-10123480.html|title=Arthur's accuracy the catalyst as Clare march on|date=26 June 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018|archive-date=24 August 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130824213725/http://www.irishexaminer.com/archives/2010/0626/world/arthurs-accuracy-the-catalyst-as-clare-march-on-123480.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Hannon subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team. On 3 August 2011, he scored 1-04 from play when Limerick defeated [[Cork GAA|Cork]] by 4–20 to 1–27 in the final of the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hannon-on-the-mark-to-edge-thriller-26758064.html|title=Hannon on the mark to edge thriller|date=4 August 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

====Senior====

On 17 April 2010, Hannon made his senior debut at right wing-forward for Limerick in a [[National Hurling League|National League]] defeat of [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] at [[Loughguile]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/limerick-stride-on-1.575231|title=Limerick stride on|date=18 April 2010|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref> He later won a National League Division 2 medal after a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of Clare in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-long-road-to-unparalleled-glory-how-captain-declan-hannon-is-following-career-path-of-stephen-cluxton-41838650.html|title= The long road to unparalleled glory … how captain Declan Hannon is following career path of Stephen Cluxton|date=14 July 2022|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=14 July 2022}}</ref>

On 14 July 2013, Hannon was at full-forward in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

Hannon's performances during the 2011 and 2014 seasons earned him [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] nominations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaelic-football/and-the-winners-are-gaa-and-gpa-announce-nominees-26781291.html|title=And the winners are ... GAA and GPA announce nominees|publisher=Irish Independent|date=12 October 2011|access-date=3 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/tipperary-earn-more-hurling-all-stars-than-the-cats-as-richie-hogan-and-james-odonoghue-land-top-awards-30691087.html|title=Tipperary earn more hurling All Stars than the Cats as Richie Hogan and James O'Donoghue land top awards|publisher=Irish Independent|date=24 October 2014|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Cormac|last=Byrne}}</ref>

In December 2017, Hannon was appointed captain of the Limerick senior hurling team for the 2018 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/declan-hannon-limerick-captain-3754141-Dec2017/|title=Limerick confirm Declan Hannon as new hurling skipper|publisher=The 42|date=16 December 2017|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Cormac|last=Byrne}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, he scored two points from play and captained Limerick to their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> Later that day Hannon was named on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986154-limerick-rule-in-the-sunday-game-team-of-the-year/|title=Limerick rule in The Sunday Game team of the year|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=20 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/redemption-relief-and-joy-for-limerick-captain-declan-hannon-863219.html |title =Redemption, relief, and joy for Limerick captain Declan Hannon|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref> He ended the season by winning an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=13 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/1101/1008052-treaty-lead-the-way-with-six-hurling-all-stars/|title= Treaty lead the way with six hurling All-Stars|date=2 November 2018|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=4 November 2018}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Hannon was selected at centre-back for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal and the cup after contributing with a point in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Hannon won his first Munster Championship medal in six years after captaining Limerick to a 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

Hannon won a second successive National League medal on 25 October 2020, after captaining Limerick to a 0–36 to 1–23 defeat of Clare in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed 2020 league final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=25 October 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> On 15 November 2020, he won a third Munster Championship medal after captaining Limerick to a 0–25 to 0–21 win over [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford to defend Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=15 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> Hannon was the first Limerick player since [[Mick Mackey]] to captain the team to two provincial title successes.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

Hannon entered the history books in [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2022]] when he became the first hurling captain to lift the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] on four occasions.

He won a fifth All-Ireland medal in [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2023]], but missed the All-Ireland semi-final and [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|final]] with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.gaa.ie/article/hannon-determined-to-make-up-for-lost-time|title=Hannon determined to make up for lost time|date=17 April 2024|work=GAA.ie|accessdate=17 April 2024}}</ref>

In October 2025, Hannon announced his retirement from inter-county hurling after 15 years with the Limerick Senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/1021/1539846-decorated-all-ireland-winning-captain-hannon-retires/|title=Five-time All-Ireland winning captain Declan Hannon retires from inter-county hurling|date=21 October 2025|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://limerickgaa.ie/statement-on-behalf-of-declan-hannon/|title=Statement on behalf of Declan Hannon|date=21 October 2025|work=Limerick GAA|accessdate=22 October 2025}}</ref>

===Munster===

On 19 February 2012, Hannon was an unused substitute in [[Munster GAA|Munster]]'s 3–14 to 1-16 [[Railway Cup]] semi-final defeat by [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/early-leinster-damage-decisive-184406.html|title=Early Leinster damage decisive|date=20 February 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|archive-date=24 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324150511/https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/early-leinster-damage-decisive-184406.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In September 2023, Hannon married radio presenter Louise Cantillon with the reception at [[Adare Manor]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/home/1293201/inside-the-fairytale-wedding-of-limerick-hurling-captain-declan-hannon-and-his-love-louise.html|title=Inside the fairytale wedding of Limerick hurling captain Declan Hannon and his love Louise|date=21 October 2025|work=Limerick Leader|accessdate=22 October 2025}}</ref>

'''William Joseph Gleeson''' (1893 – 18 November 1975) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a midfielder for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerick.ie/media/gleesonbill79.pdf|title=Great Limerick Athletes: No 79 - Bill Gleeson|publisher=Limerick website|accessdate=3 October 2011}}</ref>

== Career ==
Gleeson made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1915|1915 championship]] and became a regular player over the next decade. During that time he won two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] winner's medals and three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] winner's medals

At club level, Gleeson played with [[Fedamore GAA|Fedamore]] and [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]] and won four [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] winners' medals in a career that spanned three decades.

Gleeson also won a [[Railway Cup]] winners' medal when he was chosen on the first two [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial teams and also represented Ireland in the [[Tailteann Games (Irish Free State)|Tailteann Games]].

In retirement from playing Gleeson enjoyed a distinguished career as a referee while he was also a long-serving representative with the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]].

Jack Keane (hurler).text:
{{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Irish English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox GAA player | code = Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Jack Keane | irish = Seán Ó Catháin | height_ft = | height_in = | occupation = Farmer | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Castleconnell GAA|Castleconnell]]
[[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]]
[[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 2 | cl_province = | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Right wing-back | ic_years = 1912-1927 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 3 | ic_all_ireland = 2 | nhl = | all_stars = | cl_update = | ic_update = 17:09, 18 April 2014 | birth_date = 19 April 1892 | birth_place = [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], [[Ireland]] | death_date = 24 April 1978 (aged 86) | death_place = [[Dooradoyle]], [[Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''John Keane''' (19 April 1892 – 24 April 1978) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]]. His [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] career with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team lasted from 1912 until 1927.{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1918.htm|title=1918 All-Ireland hurling champions|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|access-date=21 April 2014}}{{cite news|url=http://www.askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jack-keane.pdf|title=Jack Keane of Castleconnell|publisher=Limerick Heritage website|access-date=23 April 2012}} Born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], Keane first played competitive hurling in various club tournament games in his youth. After a year in the [[United States]] he returned to Ireland and joined the [[Castleconnell GAA|Castleconnell]] club. After the club failed to field a championship team in 1918, Keane joined the [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]] club. He won [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]] medals in 1920 and 1922, before ending his career with the newly founded [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] club.{{fact|date=December 2021}} Keane made his senior debut for Limerick in a tournament game in 1912 and quickly established himself as a regular member of the team. His partnership with [[Willie Hough]] and [[Dinny Lanigan]] in the half-back line became known as the [[Hindenburg Line]] of hurling. Over the course of a fifteen-year inter-county career he won [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals in 1918 and 1921, as well as three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals. Keane retired from inter-county hurling following Limerick's exit from the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1927|1927 championship]]. Keane was also involved as a selector for the Limerick senior team during the 30s, with Limerick winning the championship in 1934 and 1936.{{fact|date=December 2021}} ==Honours== ;Young Irelands *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] (2): 1920, 1922 ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (2): [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1918|1918]], [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1921|1921]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (3): [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1918]], [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1921]], [[1923 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1923]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes colour |title= Jack Keane navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Hurling Team 1918}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1921}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keane, Jack}} [[Category:1892 births]] [[Category:1978 deaths]] [[Category:Young Irelands (Limerick) hurlers]] [[Category:Ahane hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship winners]] [[Category:People from Castleconnell]]

Jimmy Humphreys.text:
{{short description|Irish hurler}} {{for|the American baseball player, manager, and owner|Jimmie Humphries}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Irish English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic Athletic Association player | code = Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = File:Art_work_depicting_the_Hurling_Captain_Jimmy_Humphrys_at_the_Tailteann_Games,_Dublin,_1924.jpg | name = Jimmy Humphreys | irish = | height_ft = | height_in = | occupation = Farmer | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]]
[[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 1 | cl_province = | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = Midfield | ic_years = 1910s-1920s | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 3 | ic_all_ireland = 2 | nhl = | all_stars = | cl_update = | ic_update = 15:38,5 May 2012 | birth_date = 10 February 1894 | birth_place = [[Murroe]], [[County Limerick]], Ireland | death_date = 23 December 1956 (aged 62) | death_place = Murroe, County Limerick, Ireland }} '''James Humphreys''' (10 February 1894 – 23 December 1956) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a midfielder for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].{{cite news|url=http://humphrysfamilytree.com/Humphrys/jimmy.glenstal.html|title=Jimmy Humphrys, of Glenstal|publisher=Family tree website|access-date=5 May 2012}} == Early life == Jimmy Humphreys was born 10 February 1894 at Glenstal, Murroe, Co. Limerick, Ireland, from Tim Humphreys and Bridget Lane of Quinpool. Humphreys came from a family with a strong hurling tradition; his father, Tim, had been instrumental in forming the first Murroe hurling team shortly after the formation of the GAA, which later won the first Limerick senior county hurling title.{{Cite news |date=5 January 1957 |title=Jimmy Humphreys of Murroe, part 1, Great Limerick Sportsmen No. 196 |url=https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-1.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030070203/https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-1.pdf |archive-date=30 October 2017 |work=Limerick Leader |location=Limerick City Library (AskAboutIreland database)}} He was a grandson of [[James Humphrys]] of Glenstal, known as "the Squire".{{Cite web|url=http://humphrysfamilytree.com/Humphrys/james.squire.html|title=James Humphrys, "The Squire", of Glenstal|website=humphrysfamilytree.com|access-date=2026-05-02}} == Playing career == Humphreys was a regular member of the starting fifteen for over a decade from the 1910s until the 1920s. During that time he won two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals and three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals.{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=Limerick GAA profile|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=5 May 2012|archive-date=25 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=5 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328073637/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=28 March 2019|url-status=dead}} He captined the Irish hurling team that travelled to [[New York City|New York]] in 1921. He was also captain of the Ireland team during the 1924 [[Tailteann Games (Irish Free State)|Tailteann Games]],{{Cite journal |last=Doyle |first=Siobhán |date=2024-04-17 |title=The rise and fall of the Tailteann Games |url=https://www.rte.ie/brainstorm/2024/0417/1444020-tailteann-games-ireland-1924-1928-1932-sports-culture-identity-legacy/ |journal=RTE |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Newspapers (Firm) |first=Independent |date=1924 |title=[Tailteann Games. Captains of Irish and American hurling teams shake hands] |url=https://catalogue.nli.ie/Record/vtls000249016 |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=catalogue.nli.ie}}{{Cite web |last=nli |title=Marking the Centenary of the Tailteann Games |url=https://www.nli.ie/news-stories/stories/marking-centenary-tailteann-games |access-date=2025-05-31 |website=www.nli.ie |language=en}} which was the first international hurling competition featuring teams representing the [[United States]], [[England]], [[Scotland]], and [[Wales]]. He was presented with a silver cup presented by [[John Devoy]]. At club level Humphreys played with both [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] and [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]], winning a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] medal with the latter. The Senior Colleges Cup and the GAA playing fields in Murroe are named after Humphreys. === 1918 All-Ireland title === Humphreys was part of the Limerick team that won the [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], defeating [[Wexford county hurling team|Wexford]] in a final played at Croke Park on 26 January 1919 after a lengthy delay caused by the political disruption of the period. === 1919–1920: disrupted championships === The 1919 championship saw Limerick reach the Munster final, where they were beaten by [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]].{{Cite news |date=12 January 1957 |title=Jimmy Humphreys of Murroe, part 2, Great Limerick Sportsmen No. 196 |url=https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-2.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030070203/https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-2.pdf |archive-date=30 October 2017 |work=Limerick Leader |location=Limerick City Library (AskAboutIreland database)|access-date=2026-06-15}} The 1920 championship was played against the backdrop of the [[Irish War of Independence]]; a Munster semi-final against [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] went ahead in secret outside Cork city, which was then under martial law and where the British authorities had prohibited the fixture, before Limerick lost the final to Cork in a match repeatedly postponed and not completed until April 1922.{{Cite news |date=19 January 1957 |title=Jimmy Humphreys of Murroe, part 3, Great Limerick Sportsmen No. 196 |url=https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-3.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030070203/https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-3.pdf |archive-date=30 October 2017 |work=Limerick Leader |location=Limerick City Library (AskAboutIreland database)|access-date=2026-06-15}} === 1921 All-Ireland title === Limerick won the 1921 Munster final against Cork, eventually played on 28 May 1922, and went on to win the [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final]] against [[Dublin county hurling team|Dublin]], a fixture delayed by the [[Irish Civil War]] and not played until 4 March 1923, with the ball thrown in by the opera singer [[Joseph O'Mara]].{{Cite news |date=26 January 1957 |title=Jimmy Humphreys of Murroe, part 4, Great Limerick Sportsmen No. 196 |url=https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-4.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171030070203/https://askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/jimmy-humphreys-part-4.pdf |archive-date=30 October 2017 |work=Limerick Leader |location=Limerick City Library (AskAboutIreland database)|access-date=2026-06-15}} === 1923 Munster title and All-Ireland final === Humphreys captained Limerick to final]] against [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] at Croke Park on 14 September 1924, losing the game.{{Cite news |date=23 February 1957 |title=Jimmy Humphreys of Murroe, part 7, Great Limerick October 2017 |work=Limerick Leader |location=Limerick City Library (AskAboutIreland database)|access-date=2026-06-15}} === 1924 Munster final === Limerick were beaten by Tipperary in the 1924 Munster final, played on 5 October 1924. === Tailteann Games, 1924 === Beyond his county career, Humphreys captained both Munster and Ireland in hurling at the inaugural [[Tailteann Games (Irish Free '''Liam Hogan''' (10 March 1939 – 15 January 2014<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rip.ie/showdn.php?dn=214745|title=Death notice of Liam Hogan|publisher=[[RIP.ie]] website|date=15 January 2014|accessdate=6 February 2014|first=|last=}}</ref>) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a right wing-forward for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hurlingstats.ie/person/id/2811|title=Liam Hogan|publisher=Hurling Stats website|accessdate=6 February 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222201917/http://www.hurlingstats.ie/person/id/2811|archivedate=22 February 2014}}</ref>

Born in [[Bruree]], [[County Limerick]], Hogan first played competitive hurling whilst at school at Charleville CBS. He arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of eighteen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team, before later joining the junior side. He made his senior debut in the [[1958 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1958 championship]]. Hogan went on to play a key part for Limerick for over the next few years, however, he enjoyed little success in terms of silverware.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

As a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team for one season, Hogan won one [[Railway Cup]] medal as a non-playing substitute in 1963. At club level played with [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]].{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

Throughout his career Hogan made nine championship appearances. A serious eye injury brought an end to his career during the [[1963 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1963 championship]].

{{Short description|Limerick hurling goalkeeper}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games biography | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Barry Hennessy | irish = Barra Ó hAonghusa | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 11 | occupation = Business Development Manager | county = Limerick | province = Munster | cl_position = | club = [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 4 | cl_province= 1 | cl_all_ireland = 0 | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = Goalkeeper | ic_years = 2010–2022 | ic_apps_points = 2 (0–00) | ic_province = 4 | ic_all_ireland = 4 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = 16:30, 21 July 2022 | birth_date={{Birth date and age|df=yes|1989|10|14}} | birth_place=[[Kilmallock]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Barry Hennessy''' (born 14 October 1989) is an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]] who plays as a goalkeeper for club side [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at senior level for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2014/01/09/limerick-hurlers-return-to-action/|title=Limerick hurlers return to action|publisher=Limerick Post|date=9 January 2014|accessdate=24 May 2015|first=Donn|last=O'Sullivan}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/limerick-hurlers-name-three-debutants-for-big-munster-clash-with-clare-1.2221536|title=Limerick hurlers name three debutants for big Munster clash with Clare|publisher=Irish Times|date=22 May 2015|accessdate=24 May 2015|first=Seán|last=Moran}} ==Playing career== ===College=== Hennessy first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick]]. Having played in every grade, he was in goal on the college's senior team that reached the semi-finals of the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] for the first time.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaelic-football/honan-and-ryan-to-fore-in-ardscoil-ris-breakthrough-26346853.html|title=Honan and Ryan to fore in Ardscoil Ris breakthrough|date=24 January 2008|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=5 July 2018|first=|last=}} ===Club=== Hennessy joined the [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the minor and under-21 grades. On 3 October 2010, Hennessy lined out in his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] final. A 1–16 to 1–12 defeat of divisional side [[Emmets GAA|Emmets]] gave him his first championship medal.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/mulcahy-s-goal-helps-kilmallock-bridge-gap-1.659156|title=Mulcahy's goal helps Kilmallock bridge gap|date=4 October 2010|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}} After surrendering their championship crown in 2011, Kilmallock reached the championship decider again on 7 October 2012. [[Jake Mulcahy]] scored a vital goal to secure a 1–15 to 0–15 victory over [[Adare GAA|Adare]] and a second championship medal for Hennessy.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/mulcahy-strikes-to-secure-spoils-for-gritty-kilmallock-28818665.html|title=Mulcahy strikes to secure spoils for gritty Kilmallock|publisher=Irish Independent|date=8 October 2012|accessdate=20 August 2013|first=|last=}} On 19 October 2014, Hennessy won a third championship medal following a 1–15 to 0–14 defeat of reigning champions [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/delight-for-sparrow-as-kilmallock-defy-odds-292135.html|title=Delight for 'Sparrow' as Kilmallock defy odds|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 October 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} He later won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal following a 1–32 to 3-18 extra-time defeat of [[Cratloe GAA|Cratloe]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/football/kilmallock-find-extra-gear-in-final-epic-299265.html|title=Kilmallock find extra gear in final epic|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 November 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}} On 17 March 2015, Hennessy was in goal for Kilmallock in their 1–18 to 1–06 defeat by [[Ballyhale Shamrocks GAA|Ballyhale Shamrocks]] in the [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] at [[Croke Park]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ballyhale-make-it-six-of-the-best-with-final-stroll-31075381.html|title=Ballyhale make it six of the best with final stroll|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 March 2015|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}} ===Inter-county=== ====Minor and under-21==== Hennessy first played for the Limerick minor hurling team at the age of seventeen. He made his only appearance in that grade on 23 June 2007 in a 3–21 to 0-12 [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/match-reports/maher-fires-tipperary-to-final-as-limerick-routed-35784.html|title=Maher fires Tipperary to final as Limerick routed|date=25 June 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}} On 15 July 2009, Hennessy made his first appearance with the Limerick under-21 hurling team in a 4–22 to 2–13 defeat by Clare in the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/ryan-s-3-9-gives-clare-timely-lift-1.700796|title=Ryan's 3-9 gives Clare timely lift|date=16 July 2009|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}} His tenure with the under-21 team ended with a three-point defeat by Clare the following season.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/oconnor-inspires-banner-in-thriller-125175.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803224030/https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/oconnor-inspires-banner-in-thriller-125175.html|url-status=live|archive-date=3 August 2018|title=O'Connor inspires Banner in thriller|date=15 July 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} ====Intermediate==== Hennessy made his first appearance in goal for the Limerick intermediate hurling team in a 1–16 to 0-15 [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] on 22 June 2008.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/moloney-fires-limerick-through-1.1270887|title=Moloney fires Limerick through|date=23 June 2008|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=|last=}} He later won a Munster Championship medal following a 2–16 to 2–12 victory over Tipperary in the final at [[Semple Stadium]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/98644|title=Munster IHC: Limerick lift crown|date=24 July 2008|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=|last=}} On 30 August 2008, Hennessy was in goal when Limerick were defeated by six points by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/county/kilkenny/article/index/100392|title=All-Ireland IHC final: Cats see off Limerick|date=30 August 2008|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=|last=}} ====Senior==== Hennessy made his senior debut in goal for Limerick in a 0–19 to 2–09 defeat by [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] in the pre-season [[Waterford Crystal Cup]] on 23 January 2010.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/mccarthy-remains-quiet-on-limerick-row-as-side-are-downed-by-ucc-443310.html|title=McCarthy remains quiet on Limerick row as side are downed by UCC|date=24 January 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=|last=}} He made no further appearances that season as [[Tadhg Flynn]] became Limerick's first-choice goalkeeper. Hennessy was dropped from the panel the following season. Hennessy returned to the Limerick senior panel under manager [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J. Ryan]] for the 2014 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/91053/Limerick-unveil-new-senior-hurling-panel.html|title=Limerick unveil new senior hurling panel|date=9 January 2014|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=21 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} He was an unused substitute for the entire season. On 24 May 2015, Hennessy made his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] appearance in a 1–19 to 2–15 defeat of Clare.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-indisciplined-clare-in-munster-quarter-final-678565.html|title=Limerick beat indisciplined Clare in Munster quarter-final|date=24 May 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=John|last=Fogarty}} On 19 August 2018, Hennessy was a non-playing substitute when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}} On 31 March 2019, Hennessy was named on the bench for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal as a non-playing substitute in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} On 30 June 2019, Hennessy won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal as a non-playing substitute following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ==Personal life== Hennessy has spoken about his struggles with an eating disorder.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/my-way-of-getting-weight-down-stick-my-fingers-down-my-throat-limerick-hurling-star-on-eating-disorder-battle-42138529.html|title='My way of getting weight down? '''Patrick "Pat" Herbert''' (born 1953) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a left corner-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/herbert-in-full-command-of-oularts-destiny-28905490.html|title=Herbert in full command of Oulart's destiny|publisher=Irish Independent|date=24 November 2012|accessdate=1 June 2015|first=Cliona|last=Foley}}</ref>

Herbert was born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]]. His senior debut came during the [[1977 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1977 championship]]. Herbert immediately became a regular member of the starting fifteen and won one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal and two [[National Hurling League]] medals. He was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up on one occasion.

As a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team on a number of occasions, Herbert won two [[Railway Cup]] medals. At club level he enjoyed a lengthy career with [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]].

He made 16 championship appearances during his career, and retired following the conclusion of the [[1986 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1986 championship]].

Following his retirement from active playing, he turned to management and coaching. He guided [[Toomevara GAA|Toomevara]] and [[Oulart the Ballagh GAA|Oulart the Ballagh]] to championship successes in their respective counties.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=54901|title=Herbert takes charge of Toomevara|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=22 December 2005|accessdate=1 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref>

'''Mark Keane''' (born 1981) is a [[hurling|hurler]]. His [[National Hurling League|league]] and [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] career with the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]] spanned seven seasons from 2000 until 2006.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/keane-takes-on-his-heros-mantle-26247848.html|title=Keane takes on his hero's mantle|publisher=Irish Independent|date=1 April 2001|accessdate=5 January 2017}}</ref>

Keane made his debut on the inter-county scene at the age of sixteen when he was selected for the Limerick minor team. He spent two championship seasons with the minor team, however, he enjoyed little success during that time. Keane subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 team, winning three successive [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals from 2000 to 2002. By this stage he had also joined the Limerick senior team, making his debut in the [[2000 National Hurling League|2000 league]]. Over the course of the next seven seasons Keane became a regular member of the starting fifteen, however, he enjoyed little success in terms of silverware. He played his last game for Limerick in July 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/around-limerick-i-was-the-biggest-letdown-meet-the-hurling-prodigy-who-lost-his-way-but-overcame-his-demons-37223877.html |title ='Around Limerick, I was the biggest let-down': Meet the hurling prodigy who lost his way - but overcame his demons|date=16 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=16 August 2018}}</ref>

Keane got nerve damage and injured his right hand in 2018 after rescuing a colleague from a [[Johnson & Johnson]] machine in [[Plassey, County Limerick|Plassey]]. He got a €944,000 award,<ref>https://www.rte.ie/news/courts/2025/0401/1505228-mark-keane-damages/</ref><ref>https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/courtandcrime/arid-41604592.html</ref> reduced on a Johnson & Johnson appeal by €58,000.<ref>https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/arid-41730381.html</ref><ref>https://www.rte.ie/news/courts/2026/0623/1580031-mark-keane/</ref> He has struggled with his cycling since the injuries.<ref>https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/courtandcrime/arid-41868030.html</ref>
