'''Gearóid M. Hegarty''' (born 10 August 1994) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] and [[Gaelic football]]er who plays as a right wing-forward for club side [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St Patrick's]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior hurling team]]. He is a former member of the [[Limerick county football team|Limerick senior football team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/201061/18-new-faces-on-Limerick-hurling.html|title=18 new faces on Limerick hurling panel|date=9 January 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=19 June 2016|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/209507/Limerick-select-four-debuts-for-Munster.html|title=Limerick select four debuts for Munster SHC against Tipperary|date=16 June 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=19 June 2016|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

==Early life==

Born and raised in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]], Hegarty was educated at [[Castletroy College]] and played in all grades of hurling during his time there. In 2011, he was part of the first Castletroy team to play in the [[Dr Harty Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/castletroy-set-for-harty-cup-debut-171157.html|title=Castletroy set for Harty Cup debut|date=19 October 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]] (UL), Hegarty was selected for the college's senior hurling team, while he also lined out as a [[Gaelic football]]er in the [[Sigerson Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/sigerson-fitzgibbon-cups/gearoid-hegarty-inspires-ul-to-victory-over-dit-in-last-sigerson-quarterfinal-35438344.html|title=Gearoid Hegarty inspires UL to victory over DIT in last Sigerson quarter-final|date=9 February 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref> He won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal in February 2018 following UL's 2–21 to 2–15 win over [[DCU GAA|Dublin City University]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0224/943259-ul-pull-away-to-claim-fitzgibbon-cup-glory/|title=UL pull away to claim Fitzgibbon Cup glory|date=29 February 2016|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref>

==Club career==

Hegarty began his club career at juvenile and underage levels as a [[dual player]] with the [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St Patrick's]] club, before progressing to adult level. He was part of the St Patrick's team that lost the [[Limerick Senior Football Championship#List of finals|2014 Limerick SFC final]] to [[Ballylanders GAA|Ballylanders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/225825|title=Limerick SFC final: Jimmy Barry Murphy leads Ballylanders to glory|date=12 October 2014|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref> After losing the final to [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] in 2016, Hegarty won a [[Limerick Junior A Hurling Championship|Limerick JAHC]] medal in 2017, following a 1–10 to 0–08 win over [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] in a replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/more-limerick-junior-hurling-final-drama-as-replay-ends-level-after-extra-time-8356681|title=More Limerick junior hurling final drama as replay ends level after extra time|date=27 October 2017|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Inter-county career==

Hegarty first appeared on the inter-county scene for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in 2012. He was a member of the minor hurling team's extended panel that year, but was never selected for any matchday panel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gearoid-hegarty-following-in-family-footsteps-with-the-limerick-u-21-hurlers-8566648|title=Gearoid Hegarty following in family footsteps with the Limerick U-21 hurlers|date=10 September 2015|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later lined out with the Limerick under-21 football team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/football/hayes-content-as-cork-cut-loose-262628.html|title=Hayes content as Cork cut loose|date=20 March 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=5 July 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref> Hegarty became a dual under-21 player in 2015 and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] medal after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2015 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster finals|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=30 July 2018}}</ref> He was later at midfield when Limerick beat [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0–26 to 1–07 in the [[2015 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|2015 All-Ireland U21HC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

Hegarty's first senior appearance for Limerick came as a Gaelic footballer in February 2014, when he lined out in a 2–11 to 0–11 [[National Football League (Ireland)|National Football League]] win over [[Longford GAA|Longford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/collins-pulls-limerick-strings-29994151.html|title=Collins pulls Limerick strings|date=10 February 2014|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref> He made his [[Munster Senior Football Championship|Munster SFC]] later that season in a 2–14 to 1–11 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/football/2014/0531/620875-limerick-v-tipperary/|title=Tipp see past Limerick for long overdue win|date=31 May 2014|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=6 August 2025}}</ref> Hegarty played in the early rounds of the National Football League in 2016 before joining the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He made his debut in that code in March 2016, when he replaced Seánie O'Brien at half-time in a 6–29 to 1–12 defeat of [[Laois GAA|Laois]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limericks-perfect-warm-up-for-derby-duel-with-clare-387259.html|title=Limerick's perfect warm-up for derby duel with Clare|date=14 March 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 August 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Hegarty later made his [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] debut in a 3–12 to 1–16 defeat by Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-still-couldnt-get-past-tipperary-despite-john-odwyers-sending-off-740723.html|title=Limerick still couldn't get past Tipperary despite John O'Dwyer's sending off|date=19 June 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 August 2018|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> He left the Limerick senior football team in 2017 and committed solely to the hurlers after an end to the facilitating of dual players within the county.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://limerickgaa.ie/no-limerick-dual-players-in-2017/|title=No Limerick dual players in 2017|date=21 December 2016|publisher=Limerick GAA|access-date=6 August 2018|archive-date=6 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806210846/http://limerickgaa.ie/no-limerick-dual-players-in-2017/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hegarty was selected at right wing-forward when Limerick played [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2018 All-Ireland SHC final]]. He was held scoreless but ended the game with his first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medal following the 3–16 to 2–18 win, with Limerick claiming their first title in [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|45 years]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> Hegarty ended the season by being nominated for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=13 September 2018}}</ref> He added a [[National Hurling League]] medal to his collection in March 2019, when Limerick beat [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> Hegarty won his first Munster SHC medal in June 2019, after scoring three points from right wing-forward in the 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of Tipperary in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

After retaining the National League title in a [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games|COVID-delayed]] final in October 2020, Hegarty later won a second consecutive Munster SHC after a four-point win over Waterford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He claimed his second All-Ireland SHC medal in December 2020, as Waterford were once again beaten by 0–30 to 0–19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Limerick show consistency in a world gone mad to claim All-Ireland honours|date=13 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Hegarty was also named [[man of the match]] and ended the season by collecting his first All-Star and being named [[GAA/GPA Hurler of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gearoid-hegarty-limerick-man-of-the-match-5298598-Dec2020/|title='The one thing that kept me going over the lockdown was, 'Imagine winning an All-Ireland at Christmas time{{'}}'|date=13 December 2020|publisher=The 42|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-dominate-2020-pwc-hurling-all-stars-selection|title=Limerick dominate 2020 PwC Hurling All-Stars selection|date=20 February 2021|publisher=GAA website|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Hegarty won his third Munster SHC medal in July 2021, as Limerick claimed a third consecutive title for the first time in 85 years following a 3–21 to 2–29 win over Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/85-year-wait-ends-as-limerick-topple-tipperary-to-win-historic-munster-hurling-title-7969390|title=85-year wait ends as Limerick topple Tipperary to win historic Munster hurling title|date=18 July 2021|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> To his collection was added a third All-Ireland SHC medal, after scoring 2–02 in the 3–32 to 1–22 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40364432.html|title=Will record-breaking All-Ireland victory over Cork be Limerick's high water mark? Don't bet on it|date=22 August 2021|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Hegarty ended the season by being presented with a second consecutive All-Star.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/news/record-breaking-limerick-dominate-2021-pwc-all-stars-hurling-team|title=Record-breaking Limerick dominate 2021 PwC All-Stars hurling team|date=9 December 2021|publisher=GAA website|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Limerick retained the Munster SHC title for a fourth consecutive year in June 2022, with Hegarty scoring a goal in the 1–29 to 0–29 extra-time win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40889036.html|title=Limerick find an extra gear to see off Clare in Munster final thriller|date=5 June 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later won his third consecutive All-Ireland SHC medal, after scoring 1–05 in a man of the match display in the 1–31 to 2–26 win over [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40920188.html|title=Limerick secure the three-in-row with dream day in the sun|date=17 July 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/sunday-game-man-of-the-match-12-5819807-Jul2022/|title='A performance for the ages' - Gearóid Hegarty scoops All-Ireland hurling final Man of the Match award|date=17 July 2022|publisher=The 42|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He ended the season with his third consecutive All-Star.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-s-dozen-lead-the-way-in-2022-pwc-all-star-hurling-nominations|title=Limerick’s dozen lead the way in 2022 PwC All-Star Hurling nominations|date=8 September 2022|publisher=GAA website|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Hegarty won his third National League medal in April 2023, however, he was held scoreless in the 2–20 to 0–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 National Hurling League#Division 1|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0409/1376051-classy-limerick-claim-league-honours-with-ease/|title=Classy Limerick claim league honours with ease|date=9 April 2023|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later claimed his fifth Munster SHC medal, as Limerick beat Clare by 1–23 to 1–22 to win a record-equalling fifth consecutive title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41159863.html|title=Aaron Gillane on fire as Limerick edge Clare to secure fifth consecutive Munster title|date=11 June 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Hegarty again lined out at right wing-forward when Limerick won a record-equalling fourth consecutive All-Ireland SHC title, following a 0–30 to 2–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023 All-Ireland SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history |date=23 July 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Hegarty scored 1–02 from play when Limerick won a record-breaking sixth consecutive Munster SHC title after a 1–26 to 1–20 win over Clare in the [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster|2024 Munster SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41412799.html|title=Six of the best: Limerick make history with Munster final win over Clare |date=9 June 2024|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Limerick's attempt to win a record fifth consecutive All-Ireland SHC title ended with a [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Semi-finals|semi-final]] defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]], however, Hegarty ended the season by collecting his fourth All-Star.<ref>{{cite news|title=Conroy and O'Donnell scoop Player of the Year awards|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/football/2024/1101/1478693-conroy-and-odonnell-scoop-player-of-the-year-awards/|work=RTÉ News|date=1 November 2024|access-date=2 November 2024}}</ref>

After a trophy-less 2025 season, Limerick regained the National League title with a six-point win over Cork in April 2026, with Hegarty claiming his fourth winners' medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41822540.html|title='If you get a chance to win, you have to take it' - Kiely's call that Cork shall not pass is heard|date=6 April 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later collected a seventh Munster SHC medal, as Limerick also regained that title with a 1–21 to 2–17 win over Cork in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/munster-shc-final-limerick-finish-strongly|title=Munster SHC Final: Limerick finish strongly|date=7 June 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Hegarty won a sixth All-Ireland SHC medal in July 2022, after a 1–29 to 1–18 win over Galway in the [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2026 All-Ireland SHC final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41882305.html|title=Dominant Limerick reclaim All-Ireland title with final victory over Galway|date=19 July 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Personal life==

His father, [[Ger Hegarty]], also played with Limerick and was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up in [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1994]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/gearoid-hegarty-eyes-the-bullseye-after-so-many-near-misses-353472.html|title=Gearoid Hegarty eyes the bullseye after so many near misses|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 August 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gearoid-hegarty-limerick-hurler-of-the-year-2-5364510-Feb2021/|title=The Limerick footballer who became Hurler of the Year|date=25 February 2021|work=The 42|access-date= 25 February 2021}}</ref> Hegarty works as a business teacher at the Desmond College in [[Newcastle West]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41039246.html|title=Gearóid Hegarty Interview: Even for the masters, every day is a school day|date=2 January 2023|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 25 February 2026}}</ref> In August 2026, he married Limerick Gaelic footballer and [[camogie]] player Niamh McCarthy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40814688.html|title=Gearóid Hegarty: No reason why men and women still treated differently|date=23 February 2022|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=25 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/inside-gearoid-hegarty-and-niamh-mccarthys-very-limerick-wedding-in-the-algarve-8922346|title=Inside Gearóid Hegarty and Niamh McCarthy's very Limerick wedding in the Algarve|date=14 August 2026|work=Limerick Leader|accessdate=6 November 2026}}</ref>

'''Kyle Hayes''' (born 15 July 1998) is an Irish hurler who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Kildimo-Pallaskenry GAA|Kildimo-Pallaskenry]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]]. He usually lines out as a left wing-back. To date he has won 6 All Stars, 7 Munster Senior Hurling titles, 4 National Hurling League titles, 6 All Ireland Senior Hurling Titles and PWC GPA/GAA young hurler of the year in 2018.
He also was a part of the 2017 Munster & All Ireland Under-21 winning Limerick side.

==Club career==

Hayes joined the [[Kildimo-Pallaskenry GAA|Kildimo-Pallaskenry]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before eventually joining the club's top adult teams as both a hurler and [[Gaelic football]]er. He enjoyed his first success at adult level when, on 28 October 2017, he lined out at left wing-forward when the club's intermediate team faced [[Glenroe GAA|Glenroe]] in the final of the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick Intermediate Championship]]. He was held scoreless over the hour but ended the game with a winners' medal after the 2–13 to 0–09 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vsopublicationsltd.ie/oconnell-double-drives-kildimo-pallaskenry-to-first-title/|title=O'Connell double fires Kildimo-Pallaskenry to first title|date=2 November 2017|publisher=The Weekly Observer|access-date=30 July 2018}}</ref>

On 21 October 2018, Hayes was selected amongst the substitutes when Kildimo-Pallaskenry faced [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] in the final of the Limerick Junior Football Championship. He was introduced as a half-time substitute and ended the game with a winners' medal after the 1–15 to 2–07 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2018/10/22/watch-reaction-from-kyle-hayes-and-peter-nash-after-jafc-victory/|title=WATCH: Reaction from Kyle Hayes and Peter Nash after JAFC victory|date=22 October 2018|publisher=Limerick Post|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jack|last=Neville}}</ref>

After being beaten by [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]] in the [[2019 Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship#Results|2019 PIHC final]], Hayes lined out in a second successive [[2020 Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship#Knockout stage|final]] as team captain in 2020. Lining out at left corner-forward he scored three points in the 0–22 to 1–13 defeat of [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret/St. Paul's]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30959989.html|title=Colm O'Keeffe the hero for Blackrock as they see off Kildimo-Pallaskenry|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=26 October 2019|access-date=24 September 2020|first=Joel|last=Slattery}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40048253.html|title=Kyle Hayes leads Kildimo-Pallaskenry to senior ranks in Limerick|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=13 September 2020|access-date=23 September 2020|first=Brendan|last=Buckley}}</ref> It was their first ever championship title in this grade.

==Inter-county career==
===Minor and under-21===

Hayes first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] when he was added to the minor panel shortly before the start of the [[2015 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2015 Munster Minor Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 8 April 2015 when he lined out at midfield in a ten-point defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[2015 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster quarter-final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20323014.html|title=Denis Ring delights as Cork minor hurlers roar past Limerick|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=9 April 2015|access-date=23 June 2015|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Switched to the half-forward line as Limerick regrouped during the rest of the provincial campaign, Hayes was at right wing-forward when Limerick were beaten by three points by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2015 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20342200.html|title=Tipperary storm up final stretch against Limerick|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=13 July 2015|access-date=23 December 2020|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> Eligible for the minor grade again the following year, he was selected at centre-forward when Limerick suffered a second successive defeat by Tipperary in the [[2016 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2016 Munster final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30744074.html|title=Tipperary romp to Munster minor title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=10 July 2016|access-date=23 December 2020}}</ref> On 4 September 2016, Hayes scored a point from full-forward when Limerick were beaten by 1–21 to 0–17 by Tipperary in the [[2016 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/redemption-as-powerful-premier-get-hands-on-cup-419377.html|title=Redemption as powerful Premier get hands on cup|date=5 September 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

After the end of his minor career, Hayes was immediately added to the Limerick under-21 panel for the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2017 Munster Under-21 Championship]]. After making his first appearance for the team in an 11-point [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|quarter-final]] defeat of Tipperary, he ended the championship with a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|winners' medal]] after Limerick's 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of Cork in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018}}</ref> On 9 September 2017, Hayes lined out at centre-back in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> He ended the season by being named in the centre-back position on the Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-u21-hurling-all-ireland-gillane-3626268-Oct2017/|title=Gillane the star man as Limerick, Kilkenny, Galway and Cork players make U21 team of the year|date=2 October 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> Hayes was again eligible for the under-21 team in [[2018 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|2018]] and was also appointed team captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/defending-champions-limerick-name-u21-hurling-panel-2/|title=Defending Champions Limerick name U21 hurling panel|date=26 April 2018|publisher=Sporting Limerick|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Jack|last=Neville}}</ref> He made his last under-21 appearance on 21 June 2018 in a [[2018 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]] defeat by Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-beat-limerick-munster-u21-hurling-4084964-Jun2018/|title=Clinical Tipp dethrone All-Ireland champions Limerick and book Munster final spot|date=21 June 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}}</ref>

===Senior===
{{update section|date=January 2025}}

====2017 season====

Hayes was still just 18-years-old and out of the minor grade when he was drafted onto the senior panel by new manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] in advance of the [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling League|2017 Munster League]]. He made his first appearance of the pre-season competition on 8 January 2017, when he came on as a half-time-minute substitute for right corner-back [[Seánie O'Brien]] in a [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling League#Round 1|first-round]] defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-waterford-3176017-Jan2017/|title=Fitzgibbon and Dempsey key in helping new Limerick boss claim win over Waterford|date=8 January 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Thomas|last=Keane}}</ref> Hayes received his first competitive start on 22 January 2017 when he lined out at right wing-forward in a 24-point [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling League#Round 4|fourth-round]] defeat of [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/kerry-limerick-munster-shl-3199420-Jan2017/|title=Barry Nash bags a brace as Limerick record 24-point win over Kerry|date=22 January 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Paul|last=Brennan}}</ref> He was retained on the panel for the [[2017 National Hurling League|2017 National League]] campaign, making six appearances, including at full-forward in Limerick's ten-point defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2017 National Hurling League#Division 1 Semi-Finals|semi-final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/arid-30785982.html|title=Galway see off Limerick to advance to Division 1 final|date=16 April 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=5 August 2018}}</ref> Once again making the cut for Limerick's [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2017 Munster Championship]] panel, Hayes made his championship debut on 4 June 2017 when he scored 1-01 from play in a 3–17 to 2–16 defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Semi-finals|Munster semi-final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-john-kiely-3357178-Apr2017/?embedpost=3357178&width=600&height=460|title=Limerick cut 7 players from panel ahead of hurling championship campaign|date=25 April 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Thomas|last=Keane}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/clare-keep-limerick-at-arm-s-length-to-book-munster-final-spot-1.3107642|title=Clare keep Limerick at arm's length to book Munster final spot|date=4 June 2017|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=5 August 2018}}</ref>

====2018 season====

In November 2017, Hayes was again named on the 38-man Limerick panel for the upcoming [[2018 Limerick senior hurling team season|2018 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/281970/10-additions-to-2018-limerick-hurling-panel.html|title=10 additions to 2018 Limerick hurling panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> After playing no part in Limerick's successful [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]] campaign, he made a number of appearances throughout the subsequent [[2018 National Hurling League|National League]], including at centre-forward in a second successive [[2018 National Hurling League#Division 1 Semi-Finals|semi-final]] defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/tipperary-go-extra-mile-to-book-their-final-spot-by-seeing-off-limerick-36762800.html|title=Tipperary go extra mile to book their final spot by seeing off Limerick|date=1 April 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Dermot|last=Crowe}}</ref> Hayes established himself as Limerick's first-choice centre-forward throughout the championship and was selected in that position when Limerick faced [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2018 All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-team-news-all-ireland-hurling-final-4188195-Aug2018/|title=Limerick name unchanged side for All-Ireland final showdown against Galway|date=17 August 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=19 December 2020|first=Emma|last=Duffy}}</ref> He scored four points from play as Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> Hayes was also selected as the official [[man of the match]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kyle-hayes-wins-man-of-the-match-limerick-dominate-sunday-game-best-xv-but-galway-star-was-their-hurler-of-the-year-37231272.html|title=Kyle Hayes wins Man of the Match, Limerick dominate Sunday Game best XV but Galway star was their hurler of the year|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018}}</ref> He ended the season by being nominated for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]], while he was also named [[Vodafone Young Hurler of the Year|Young Hurler of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=13 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-sweep-the-boards-with-six-all-star-and-both-hurlers-of-the-year-1.3684585|title=Limerick sweep the boards with six All Star and both Hurlers of the Year|date=2 November 2018|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=4 November 2018|first=Seán|last=Moran}}</ref>

====2019 season====

Hayes was again a regular for Limerick during the [[2019 National Hurling League|2019 National League]], making five appearances during their eight games. He was held scoreless from centre-forward when Limerick claimed their first [[National Hurling League#Division 1|Division 1]] title since [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] after a 1–24 to 0–19 win over [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> Hayes ended the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2019 Munster Championship]] with his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|provincial winners' medal]] after scoring 1-02 from play in the 2–26 to 2–14 win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He again received an All-Star nomination at the end of the season, while he was also shortlisted for a second successive [[All Stars Young Hurler of the Year|Young Hurler of the Year]] award but lost out to [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]'s [[Adrian Mullen]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-allstars-hurling-2019-4824531-Sep2019/|title=11 players from Tipperary as 8 counties feature in 2019 All-Star hurling nominations|date=26 September 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=26 September 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/304315|title=Callanan, Horgan and Reid nominated for Hurler of the Year|date=26 September 2019|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=26 September 2019}}</ref>

====2020 season====

Commitments with the [[University of Limerick]] for the [[2020 Fitzgibbon Cup]] campaign precluded him from lining out with Limerick during their title-winning [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]] campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0111/1105733-limerick-cruise-past-to-cork-to-win-munster-league/|title=Stylish Limerick cruise past Cork to win Munster league|date=11 January 2020|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=18 December 2020|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref> The subsequent [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|National League]] campaign saw Hayes line out in three of Limerick's five [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|Division 1A]] games. On 25 October 2020, he was again at centre-forward in a 0–36 to 1–23 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed league final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=25 October 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> For the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]] against [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] on 1 November 2020, he was surprisingly switched from the forwards to defence, lining out at left wing-back with [[Cian Lynch]] taking over the centre-forward position.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40074293.html|title=Tipperary blown away as Limerick storm into Munster final|date=1 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=23 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> Hayes ended the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2020 Munster Championship]] with a second successive winners' medal after again playing at left wing-back in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]] defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford for historic Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> On 13 December 2020, he scored a point from his now customary position of left wing-back when Limerick defeated Waterford by 0–30 to 0–19 in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Limerick show consistency in a world gone mad to claim All-Ireland honours|date=13 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hayes has worked as a [[Human resources|HR officer]] since graduating from his business studies degree at the [[University of Limerick]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/898335/kyle-hayes-a-lot-of-men-see-talking-about-their-struggles-as-a-weakness-but-its-not.html|title=Kyle Hayes: 'A lot of men see talking about their struggles as a weakness but it's not'|publisher=[[Limerick Leader]]|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell|date=31 August 2022|accessdate=20 November 2023}}</ref>

===Court cases and convictions===
In November 2023, a jury was sworn in to hear a trial of Hayes and three other men who were charged with violent disorder and assault causing harm to a man at a nightclub in Limerick city in October 2019.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2023/1120/1417497-hayes-court/|title=Jury sworn in as Limerick hurler Kyle Hayes charged with assault|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|date=20 November 2023|accessdate=20 November 2023}}</ref> On 1 December, Hayes was found not guilty of assault causing harm but guilty of two charges of violent disorder at the nightclub.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/news/courts/2023/1201/1419595-kyle-hayes-assault-trial/|title=Kyle Hayes found guilty of two counts of violent disorder, acquitted of assault charge|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Teresa|last=Mannion|date=1 December 2023|accessdate=1 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/courtandcrime/arid-41281462.html|title=All-Ireland winning Limerick hurler Kyle Hayes found guilty of violent disorder|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=David|last=Raleigh|date=1 December 2023|accessdate=1 December 2023}}</ref> The trial heard Hayes was part of a "mob" that "chased", "punched", "stamped" and "kicked" a 24-year-old man, during a "vicious and sustained attack" inside and outside the nightclub.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/courts/hurling-star-kyle-hayes-found-not-guilty-of-assault-but-guilty-of-violent-disorder-at-limerick-nightclub/a522672952.html|title=Hurling star Kyle Hayes found not guilty of assault but guilty of violent disorder at Limerick nightclub|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|first=David|last=Raleigh|date=1 December 2023|accessdate=1 December 2023}}</ref> In March 2024, he was given a two-year suspended sentence, ordered to pay €10,000 in compensation, and ordered to keep the peace for that time.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.rte.ie/news/courts/2024/0320/1438893-kyle-hayes/ | title=Suspended sentence for Hayes over violent disorder | date=20 March 2024 | last1=Kane | first1=Conor | website=[[RTÉ.ie]] }}</ref>

On 14 July 2024, Hayes was arrested for dangerous driving having been recorded driving at over 150 km/h in a 100 km/h zone.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://extra.ie/2024/07/18/sport/gaa/kyle-hayes-new-court-date | title=Kyle Hayes handed court date after being charged with dangerous driving | date=18 July 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.thejournal.ie/gaa-star-arrested-for-dangerous-driving-and-set-to-appear-before-court-6438459-Jul2024/ | title=Well-known GAA star arrested for dangerous driving and set to appear before court | date=16 July 2024 }}</ref> On 10 September 2024 he was convicted of dangerous driving and disqualified from driving for two years.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.rte.ie/news/courts/2024/0910/1469341-kyle-hayes/ | title=Hurler Kyle Hayes disqualified from driving for two years | last1=Martyn | first1=Petula | website=[[RTÉ.ie]] | date=10 September 2024 }}</ref> Following his conviction, an application was made for a court decision on whether his two-year suspended sentence for violent disorder would be re-activated.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/courtandcrime/arid-41473201.html | title=Kyle Hayes may face possible violent disorder sentence re-activation | date=11 September 2024 }}</ref> The case was due in court on 7 October 2024 but was adjourned for two months pending an appeal against the dangerous driving conviction.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Ann |title=All-Ireland winner Kyle Hayes's case due back in court in Limerick on Monday |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/courtandcrime/arid-41487545.html |access-date=2 October 2024 |publisher=The Examiner |date=2 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/courtandcrime/arid-41490935.html?utm_source=push&utm_medium=mobile&utm_campaign=article | title=Appeal against dangerous driving conviction delays hearing on Kyle Hayes's suspended sentence }}</ref>

Despite these convictions, Hayes was nominated for the 2024 [[GAA/GPA Hurler of the Year]] award, a decision that was widely criticised online.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sundayworld.com/sport/gaa/gaa-slammed-after-announcing-kyle-hayes-nomination-for-hurler-of-the-year-on-x/a2124350737.html | title=GAA slammed after announcing Kyle Hayes' nomination for Hurler of the Year on X }}</ref> His receipt of a [[GAA GPA All Stars Awards|GAA/GPA All Star Award]] in 2024 also faced criticism including from the mother of the victim of Hayes' "violent disorder" who claimed that Hayes had never apologised to her son over the incident.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://m.sundayworld.com/crime/courts/backlash-after-limerick-hurler-kyle-hayes-awarded-gaa-all-star-despite-convictions/a1243945160.html|title=Backlash after Limerick hurler Kyle Hayes awarded GAA All-Star despite convictions|date=2 November 2024|website=SundayWorld.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/absolutely-disgusted-victims-mother-hits-out-after-limerick-hurler-kyle-hayes-receives-all-star-award/a193127773.html|title=‘Absolutely disgusted’ – victim’s mother hits out after Limerick hurler Kyle Hayes receives All-Star award|date=5 November 2024|website=Irish Independent}}</ref>

On 12 March 2025, Hayes lost his appeal against the dangerous driving conviction.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/news/courts/2025/0312/1501705-hurler-dangerous-driving-appeal/|title=Hayes fails in appeal over dangerous driving conviction|first=Paschal|last=Sheehy|date=12 March 2025|website=RTÉ News}}</ref> On 21 March 2025, he appeared again before [[Circuit Court (Ireland)|Limerick Circuit Criminal Court]] to consider the re-activation of his suspended sentence. The court ruled that he would not be jailed if he is deemed suitable for 180 hours of voluntary unpaid community service.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/courtandcrime/arid-41597773.html|title=Kyle Hayes will not be jailed if he is deemed suitable for community service, says judge|first=David|last=Raleigh|date=21 March 2025|website=Irish Examiner}}</ref> The [[Probation Service]] later deemed him suitable to carry out community service in lieu of a prison sentence.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/crime-and-courts/1788407/work-has-been-identified-for-limerick-hurler-kyle-hayes-for-his-community-service-court-hears.html|title=Work has been identified for Limerick hurler Kyle Hayes for his community service, court hears|first=Donal|last=O'Regan|date=28 April 2025|website=www.limerickleader.ie}}</ref> He continues to play for the Limerick Senior Hurling team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2025/0308/1500929-limerick-record-commanding-win-over-galway/|title=Limerick record commanding win over Galway|first=David|last=Byrne|date=8 March 2025|website=RTÉ News}}</ref>

Aaron Gillane.text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=January 2022}} {{infobox Gaelic games player | image = | name = Aaron Gillane | irish = Aron Ó Giolláin | nickname = | occupation = Sales rep | birth_date = 1996 | birth_place = [[Patrickswell]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | sport = Hurling | code = Hurling | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] | cl_years = 2014–present | cl_position = | cl_apps_points = 66 (22–383) | cl_county = 2 | cl_province = | cl_all_ireland = | colleges = [[Mary Immaculate College]] | fitz = 1 | col_years = 2017–present | col_apps_points = 9 (7–80) | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_years = 2017–present | ic_position = Right corner-forward | ic_apps_points = 52 (20–328) | ic_province = 7 | ic_all_ireland = 6 | nhl = 4 | all_stars = 4 | cl_update = 22:48, 2 April 2026 | ic_update = 22:16, 19 July 2026 }} '''Aaron Gillane''' (born 1996) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a right corner-forward for club side [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Early career== ===Ardscoil Rís=== Gillane first came to prominence in [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. On 22 February 2014, he was introduced as a substitute when Arscoil Rís defeated Scoil na Trionóide from [[Doon, County Limerick|Doon]] by 2–13 to 0–04 in the final of the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]].{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/ardscoil-ris-a-class-apart-in-derby-duel-259848.html|title=Ardscoil Rís a class apart in derby duel|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=24 February 2014|access-date=23 June 2015|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} ===Mary Immaculate College=== During his studies at [[Mary Immaculate College]], Gillane was selected as a forward for the college's senior hurling team. On 25 February 2017, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal as Mary I retained the title after a 3–24 to 1–19 defeat of [[Carlow Institute of Technology]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/dj-carey-hails-inspirational-coach-jamie-wall-as-mary-i-retain-fitzgibbon-title-443894.html|title=DJ Carey hails inspirational coach Jamie Wall as Mary I retain Fitzgibbon title|date=27 February 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=John|last=Fallon}} ==Club career== Gillane joined the [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels. After an unremarkable period in these grades, he was 17-years-old when he joined the club's junior team after failing to make the cut with the senior panel. A combination of not being "good enough" and the prospect of [[soccer]] success could have resulted in Gillane walking away from the game but for the intervention of club legend [[Ciarán Carey]] who coaxed him onto the senior team.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsjoe.ie/gaa/patrickswell-mary-aaron-gillane-doesnt-forget-hes-come-198744|title=Patrickswell and Mary I: Aaron Gillane doesn't forget where he's come from|publisher=Sports Joe|access-date=19 December 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsjoe.ie/gaa/aaron-gillane-173110|title=Aaron Gillane: How a junior player became a hurler of the year|publisher=Sports Joe|access-date=19 December 2020}} Gillane was in the early stages of his senior club career when Patrickswell suffered a one-point defeat by [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] in the [[2015 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|2015 county final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=19 December 2020|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}} Throughout the [[2016 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2016 Limerick County Championship]], Gillane further established himself as a key member of the starting fifteen by sharing the free-taking duties with [[Diarmaid Byrnes]]. On 23 October 2016, he scored seven points, including five frees, from right corner-forward when Patrickswell claimed their first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] in 13 years after a 19-point win over [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/patrickswell-dominate-ballybrown-to-capture-19th-limerick-shc-title-760623.html|title=Patrickswell dominate Ballybrown to capture 19th Limerick SHC title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 October 2016|access-date=15 October 2018}} Gillane lined out in a second [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|county final]] on 6 October 2019. Playing at right corner-forward he scored six points and collected a second winners' medal following the 1–17 to 0–15 defeat of [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cian-lynch-comes-to-the-fore-as-patrickswell-hold-off-na-piarsaigh-in-limerick-county-final-38567636.html|title=Cian Lynch comes to the fore as Patrickswell hold off Na Piarsaigh in Limerick county final|publisher=Irish Independent|date=6 October 2019|access-date=6 October 2019|first=Colm|last=Keys}} ==Inter-county career== ===Minor and under-21=== Gillane first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] when he was added to the minor panel shortly before the start of the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2014 Munster Minor Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 26 June 2014 when he was a late substitute for [[Séamus Flanagan]] in a two-point win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]]. Gillane was again confined to the substitutes' bench for the subsequent [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster final replay]] defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|access-date=23 June 2015}} By the time Limerick qualified for the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]], Gillane was overlooked by the management and did not make the 24-man match-day panel.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-minors-savour-all-ireland-success-against-spirited-limerick-1.1920852|title=Kilkenny minors savour All-Ireland success against spirited Limerick|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 September 2014|access-date=23 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} After a season of no underage inter-county activity, Gillane made his debut with the Limerick under-21 team on 28 June 2016 when he lined out at right corner-forward in a [[2016 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster quarter-final]] win over Cork.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/all-ireland-holders-limerick-overrun-cork-u21s-742281.html|title=All-Ireland holders Limerick overrun Cork U21s|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=28 June 2016|access-date=8 August 2018}} He was dropped from the starting fifteen for the semi-final defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-limerick-munster-u21-2-2878788-Jul2016/|title=Tipperary's great hurling week continues as they defeat Limerick in Munster U21 semi-final|publisher=The 42|date=14 July 2016|access-date=19 December 2020}} In his second and final season with the under-21 team, Gillane secured a starting fifteen berth as well as taking over the free-taking duties. He ended the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2017 Munster Under-21 Championship]] as top scorer with 0–29, while he also claimed a winners' medal after Limerick's defeat of Cork in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018}} On 9 September 2017, Gillane top scored with seven points in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} As well as ending the campaign as the championship's overall [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Top scorers|top scorer]] with 0–44, he was later named on the Bord Gáis Energy Team of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-u21-hurling-all-ireland-gillane-3626268-Oct2017/|title=Gillane the star man as Limerick, Kilkenny, Galway and Cork players make U21 team of the year|date=2 October 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ===Senior=== ====2017 season==== Gillane was in his final season with the Limerick under-21 team when he was drafted onto the senior panel by new manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] in advance of the [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling League|2017 Munster League]]. He made his only appearance of the pre-season competition on 8 January 2017 when he came on as a 54th-minute substitute for full-forward [[Seán Tobin]] in a [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling League#Round 1|first-round]] defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-waterford-3176017-Jan2017/|title=Fitzgibbon and Dempsey key in helping new Limerick boss claim win over Waterford|date=8 January 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Thomas|last=Keane}} Gillane was cut from the panel for the [[2017 National Hurling League|2017 National League]] campaign, however, his impressive form for [[Mary Immaculate College]] in the [[2017 Fitzgibbon Cup|Fitzgibbon Cup]] saw him earn a recall to the panel in advance of the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2017 Munster Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-john-kiely-3357178-Apr2017/?embedpost=3357178&width=600&height=460|title=Limerick cut 7 players from panel ahead of hurling championship campaign|date=25 April 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Thomas|last=Keane}} On 4 June 2017, he made his championship debut when he came on as a 57th-minute substitute for [[Shane Dowling (hurler)|Shane Dowling]] in a 3–17 to 2–16 defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2017 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Semi-finals|Munster semi-final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/clare-keep-limerick-at-arm-s-length-to-book-munster-final-spot-1.3107642|title=Clare keep Limerick at arm's length to book Munster final spot|date=4 June 2017|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=5 August 2018}} ====2018 season==== In November 2017, Gillane was again named on the 38-man Limerick panel for the upcoming [[2018 Limerick senior hurling team season|2018 season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/281970/10-additions-to-2018-limerick-hurling-panel.html|title=10 additions to 2018 Limerick hurling panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} He claimed his first silverware at senior level on 14 January 2018 when Limerick beat Clare by 0–16 to 0–10 to claim the [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League|2018 Munster League]] title.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/limerick-make-bold-statement-of-intent-36487975.html|title=Limerick make bold statement of intent|date=15 January 2018|work=Irish Independent|access-date=15 January 2018}} Gillane started all of Limerick's games and ended the provincial league as [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League#Top scorers|top scorer]] with 1–21. The subsequent [[2018 National Hurling League|National League]] saw him start in all seven of Limerick's games, ending the campaign as the team's top scorers with 5–57. On 2 June 2018, Gillane was red carded and received a one-match suspension for digging twice at [[Cork GAA|Cork]]'s [[Seán O'Donoghue]] in their [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling Championship#Round 3|Munster Championship Round 3]] game.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30846652.html|title=14-man Limerick hold Cork to a draw in Páirc Uí Chaoimh cracker|date=2 June 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=5 August 2018|first=John|last=Fogarty}} The decision was described as a "joke" by team manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0602/967828-it-was-a-joke-limerick-boss-slams-sending-off-call/|title='It was a joke' – Limerick boss John Kiely slams Gillane sending-off|date=3 June 2018|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=5 August 2018}} On 19 August 2018, Gillane was named at right corner-forward when Limerick faced [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-team-news-all-ireland-hurling-final-4188195-Aug2018/|title=Limerick name unchanged side for All-Ireland final showdown against Galway|date=17 August 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=19 December 2020|first=Emma|last=Duffy}} He scored three points in total, including one from a free, as Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}} Gillane was later named the [[GAA/GPA Player of the Month (hurling)|GAA/GPA Player of the Month]] for August, before ending the season by being nominated for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/aaron-gillane-and-colm-cavanagh-pick-up-august-awards-863819.html|title=Aaron Gillane and Colm Cavanagh pick up August awards|date=22 August 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=22 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=13 September 2018}} ====2019 season==== Gillane was again a regular for Limerick during the [[2019 National Hurling League|2019 National League]], starting in six of their eight games. He top scored with 1-09 from right corner-forward when Limerick claimed their first [[National Hurling League#Division 1|Division 1]] title since [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] after a 1–24 to 0–19 win over Waterford in the [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|final]]{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} His [[man of the match]] performance in the final also earned him a second GAA/GPA Player of the Month award.{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/299204|title=O'Shea and Gillane take Player of the Month gongs|date=14 May 2019|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=14 May 2019}} Gillane ended the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2019 Munster Championship]] as top scorer with 2–41, while he also claimed his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|provincial winners' medal]] after the 2–26 to 2–14 win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} He ended the year by receiving his second All-Star nomination and his first win.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-allstars-hurling-2019-4824531-Sep2019/|title=11 players from Tipperary as 8 counties feature in 2019 All-Star hurling nominations|date=26 September 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=26 September 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ====2020 season==== Gillane wasn't included on the Limerick team for the two [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League#Group 1|group stage]] games of the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League|2020 Munster League]], with [[David Reidy (Limerick hurler)|David Reidy]] taking over the free-taking duties. He was back on the team at right corner-forward for the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League#Final|final]] against [[Cork GAA|Cork]] on 11 January 2020, and scored 1–01 from play in the 1–32 to 0–20 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0111/1105733-limerick-cruise-past-to-cork-to-win-munster-league/|title=Stylish Limerick cruise past Cork to win Munster league|date=11 January 2020|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=18 December 2020|first=Denis|last=Hurley}} The subsequent [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|National League]] campaign saw Gillane score 1–28 after lining out in four of Limerick's five [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|Division 1A]] games. On 25 October 2020, he top-scored with 0–12 in a 0–36 to 1–23 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed league final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=25 October 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} Gillane ended the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2020 Munster Championship]] as top scorer with 2–28, while he also claimed a second successive winners' medal after scoring ten points in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]] defeat of Waterford.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford for historic Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} On 29 November 2020, Gillane was hospitalised overnight following a heavy collision with [[Galway GAA|Galway]] centre-back [[Gearóid McInerney]] in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/1130/1181500-gillane-recovering-at-home-following-night-in-hospital/|title=Aaron Gillane recovering at home following night in hospital|date=30 November 2020|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=19 December 2020|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} Limerick selector [[Donal O'Grady (Limerick hurler)|Donal O'Grady]] later cast doubt on his ability to recover in time for the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]]: "Aaron didn't train on Tuesday, obviously he took a heavy hit there at the weekend. We are hoping to possibly get him reassessed on Friday night, to see how he is. At the moment, 50–50 is my understanding as of today."{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-star-aaron-gillane-5050-to-play-in-all-ireland-final-39823628.html|title=Limerick star Aaron Gillane '50/50' to play in All-Ireland final, Limerick say|date=3 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} Gillane made sufficient progress in his recovery and was named at '''Robbie Hanley''' (born 1996) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He usually lines out as a midfielder.

==Playing career==
===Kilmallock===

Hanley joined the [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before eventually joining the club's top adult team.

On 19 October 2014, Hanley won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Championship]] medal after coming on as a substitute in Kilmallock's 1–15 to 0–14 defeat of reigning champions [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/delight-for-sparrow-as-kilmallock-defy-odds-292135.html|title=Delight for 'Sparrow' as Kilmallock defy odds|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 October 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 23 November, he was again introduced as a substitute as Kilmallock won the [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] following a 1–32 to 3–18 extra-time defeat of [[Cratloe GAA|Cratloe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/football/kilmallock-find-extra-gear-in-final-epic-299265.html|title=Kilmallock find extra gear in final epic|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 November 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 17 March 2015, Hanley made another cameo appearance as a substitute for Kilmallock in their 1–18 to 1–06 defeat by [[Ballyhale Shamrocks GAA|Ballyhale Shamrocks]] in the [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] at [[Croke Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ballyhale-make-it-six-of-the-best-with-final-stroll-31075381.html|title=Ballyhale make it six of the best with final stroll|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 March 2015|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Hanley first played for Limerick as a member of the minor team during the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2014 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance on 10 April when he lined out at midfield in Limerick's 3–17 to 2–11 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/nash-the-main-marksman-as-limerick-coast-to-showdown-with-cork-265071.html|title=Nash the main marksman as Limerick coast to showdown with Cork|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 April 2014|accessdate=17 February 2019|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> Hanley won a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal on 22 July after scoring a point from midfield in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–18 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|date=23 July 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref> He was again at midfield for Limerick's subsequent 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] on 7 September.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/wonderful-walsh-fires-cats-to-victory-over-limerick-30569083.html|title=Wonderful Walsh fires Cats to victory over Limerick|date=8 September 2014|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref>

After progressing onto the Limerick under-21 team, Hanley made his first appearance for the team on 22 June 2017 when he lined out at midfield in a 2–24 to 0–19 defeat of Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-u21-hurling-3458849-Jun2017/|title=Morrissey and Nash goals help Limerick impress with 11-point success over Tipp in Munster U21 clash|date=22 June 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal on 26 July following Limerick's 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 9 September, Hanley was again at midfield in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of Kilkenny in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> He was later named on the Bord Gáis Energy Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-u21-hurling-all-ireland-gillane-3626268-Oct2017/|title=Gillane the star man as Limerick, Kilkenny, Galway and Cork players make U21 team of the year|date=2 October 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

====Senior====

Hanley was added to the Limerick senior panel prior to the start of the 2019 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/352321/42-man-limerick-hurling-panel-for-2019-includes-seven-newcomers.html|title=42-man Limerick hurling panel for 2019 includes seven newcomers|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 December 2018|access-date=17 February 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He made his first appearance on 17 February 2019 when he scored a point from midfield in Limerick's 2–18 to 0–15 [[2019 National Hurling League|National League]] defeat of Kilkenny.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-crush-kilkenny-with-ruthless-twogoal-burst-as-allireland-champions-fire-another-warning-shot-to-rivals-37824175.html|title=Limerick crush Kilkenny with ruthless two-goal burst as All-Ireland champions fire another warning shot to rivals|date=17 February 2019|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=24 March 2019|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}</ref> On 31 March 2019, Hanley was named on the bench for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal as a non-playing substitute in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

At club level he played with [[Hospital-Herbertstown GAA|Hospital-Herbertstown]] and [[Ballybricken-Bohermore GAA|Ballybricken-Bohermore]] and was also a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior teams]] as a [[dual player]]. ==Career== Garvey played the majority of his adult hurling and Gaelic football with the [[Hospital-Herbertstown GAA|Hospital-Herbertstown]] club. He first appeared on the inter-county scene during a two-year stint with the Limerick minor team before progressing onto the under-21 side.{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/65174|title=Bros, Garvey|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=12 June 1992|access-date=25 August 2021|first=|last=}} Garvey played for the Limerick intermediate hurling team as well as the senior team during the [[1992-93 National Hurling League]]. He was a member of the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] at various times over a 15-year period, during which time he usually lined out as a goalkeeper. ==Career== Hogan first appeared as a 14-year-old member of the [[Adare GAA|Adare]] minor team in 1951. He simultaneously lined out with the Adare CBS team and was a member of the school team that was beaten by [[De La Salle College Waterford]] in the [[Dean Ryan Cup]] final in 1953. Hogan's working life brought him to [[Cork (city)|Cork]] and it was with the [[Sarsfields GAA (Cork)|Sarsfields]] club there that he won a [[Cork Senior Hurling Championship|County Championship]] title in 1957. He also lined out as a [[Gaelic football]]er with [[Lees GAA|Lees]] and narrowly missed out on completing [[Cork Senior Football Championship|the double]]. Hogan returned to Limerick and joined the [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] club, with whom he won further [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Championship]] titles.{{cite web|url=https://claughaungaa.com/history/|title=History|publisher=Claughaun GAA website|date=|accessdate=11 December 2021|first=|last=}} He first appeared for the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] in the Rose Cup final in 1958 and quickly established himself as a mainstay of the team. Hogan was sub-goalkeeper on the Limerick team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1973 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20231789.html|title=Bennis recalls the heroes of ’73|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 May 2013|accessdate=11 December 2021|first=|last=}}{{cite Sport|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=11 December 2021|first=|last=}} His other honours include [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] and [[National Hurling League]] medals, '''Dermot Noel Kelly''' (25 December 1932 – 22 February 2023) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. He lined out at club level with [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] and also played at inter-county level with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]].

==Career==

Kelly first played hurling as a schoolboy with [[CBS Sexton Street]] in the [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]]. He later lined out as a [[dual player]] with the [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] club and won three [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medals and two [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|Limerick SFC]] medals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/sadness-at-passing-of-popular-former-limerick-hurler-and-musician-dermot-kelly/|title=Sadness at passing of popular former Limerick hurler and musician Dermot Kelly|publisher=Limerick GAA website|date=23 February 2023|access-date=1 March 2023|first=|last=}}</ref>

Kelly first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year stint with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 1949 and 1950. He immediately progressed on the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in 1951. Kelly enjoyed his greatest success with Limerick when he scored 1–12 to beat [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1955 Munster final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40188420.html|title=The one that got away: Limeick's generation that never tasted All-Ireland success|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 December 2020|access-date=1 March 2023|first=P. M.|last=O'Sullivan}}</ref> He continued to line out with Limerick until 1959. Kelly also earned selection to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] team and won four [[Railway Cup]] medals in six seasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=1 March 2023|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==

As well as his sporting career, Kelly was also known as a songwriter and performer. He was also a member of the College Players Limerick in the 1950s and was a member of [[Conradh na Gaeilge]]. Kelly worked with the [[Bank of Ireland]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/dermot-kelly-6004462-Mar2023/|title=Dermot Kelly: Father, husband, songwriter, poet, bank manager and hurling hero|publisher=The 42|date=1 March 2023|access-date=1 March 2023|first=|last=}}</ref> His nephew, [[Stephen Lucey]], was a [[dual player]] with Limerick.

Kelly was a renowned Irish ballad songwriter and composed many notable tunes including [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oXnT8Phvkx0 The Ballad Of Joseph McHugh] about the famous Publican from [[Liscannor|Liscannor, County Clare.]] He was a past Captain and President of [[Lahinch Golf Club]].
 
Kelly died on 22 February 2023, at the age of 90.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/1044678/sadness-at-passing-of-popular-former-limerick-hurler-and-musician-dermot-kelly.html|title=Sadness at passing of popular former Limerick hurler and musician Dermot Kelly|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=23 February 2023|access-date=1 March 2023|first=|last=}}</ref>
