'''William Moore''' (born 1950) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a right corner-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior hurling team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=County profile: Limerick|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=1 December 2011|archive-date=25 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Moore made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1971|1971 championship]] and became a regular player over the next few seasons. During that time he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] winners' medal and back-to-back [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medals.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Munster Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|accessdate=1 December 2011|archive-date=21 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721124423/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At club level Moore enjoyed a lengthy career with [[Doon GAA|Doon]], however, he ended his career without claiming a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county club championship]] winners' medal.

==Playing career==
===Club===

Moore played his club hurling with his local [[Doon GAA|Doon]] club.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Inter-county===

Moore first came to prominence as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team in the early 1970s. In 1973 he won his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal, Limerick's first since 1955.  Limerick later faced [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final, however, the Munster champions were burdened with the underdogs tag.  In spite of this Limerick powered to a seven-point victory, giving Moore an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/3420/TALES-OF-3973-IMMORTALS.3163953.jp?articlepage=2|title=Tales of the '73 Immortals|date=31 August 2007|work=[[Limerick Leader]]|accessdate=15 July 2010}}</ref>

In 1974 Moore won a second consecutive Munster title before lining out in a second consecutive All-Ireland final.  Once again Kilkenny provided the opposition.  Limerick stormed to an early lead, however, a [[Pat Delaney (Kilkenny hurler)|Pat Delaney]] shot from midfield bounced on the wet [[Croke Park]] surface and between goalkeeper [[Séamus Horgan]]'s legs for a goal.  Two more goals for Kilkenny put an end to Limerick's hopes of victory as 'the Cats' emerged the winners by twelve points.

Horgan continued hurling at inter-county level until 1974.

'''Niall Moran''' (born 1 March 1983) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a centre-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], Moran first played competitive hurling whilst at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]]. He arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of eighteen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team, before later lining out with the under-21 side. He made his senior debut in the [[2003 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2003 championship]]. Moran went on to play a key part in the forwards for a decade, and won one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal and one [[National Hurling League|National Hurling League (Division 2)]] medal. He was an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

As a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team at various times, Moran won one [[Railway Cup]] medal in 2007. At club level he won two [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medals with [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]].{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

Moran's career tally of 7 goals and 97 points ranks him as Limerick's sixth highest championship scorer of all time.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

Throughout his career Moran made 44 championship appearances, making one of Limerick's most "capped" player of all time. He announced his retirement from inter-county hurling on 14 December 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=206387|title=Niall Moran retires with Munster medal|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=14 December 2013|accessdate=16 December 2013|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-sport/tributes-paid-to-retiring-limerick-hurler-niall-moran-1-5751414|title=Tributes paid to retiring Limerick hurler Niall Moran|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=15 December 2013|accessdate=16 December 2013|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

His brothers, [[Ollie Moran|Ollie]] and [[James Moran (hurler)|James]], have also played with Limerick.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

Moran has also become involved in team management and coaching. He has served as manager and selector with various hurling teams at Ardscoil Rís.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-s-niall-moran-proud-to-be-part-of-team-with-ex-pupils-1.1493355|title=Limerick’s Niall Moran proud to be part of team with ex-pupils|publisher=Irish Times|date=14 August 2013|accessdate=16 December 2013|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}}</ref>

He later joined the [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]] club and won five [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]] medals between 1920 and 1932. Impressive displays at the club level brought McConkey to the attention of the Limerick senior team selectors and he was quickly added to the team. Over the course of a sixteen-year period, he won three [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals, beginning with his first in 1918, a second as captain of the team in 1921 and a third and final winners' medal in 1934. McConkey also won four [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals. After being chosen on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team for the first time in 1927, McConkey was an automatic choice on the panel for two seasons. '''Patrick McInerney''' (30 January 1895 – 28 December 1982) was an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a corner-back for the [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary senior team]].{{Contradictory inline|date=June 2025|reason=Limerick or Tipperary?}}

McInerney made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1918|1918 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his emigration after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1925|1925 championship]]. During that time he won two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medals, three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals and one [[Thomond Feis]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=Limerick GAA profile|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=24 April 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archive-date=25 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=24 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328073637/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=28 March 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> Paddy McInerney was a contemporary of Pa "Fowler" McInerney, also of O'Callihan's Mills, who won Senior County All-Ireland Hurling Championships with Clare in 1916 and Dublin in 1932.

At club level McInerney was a double [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] medalist with [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]].

==Playing career==
===Club===

McInerney played his club hurling with his local [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]] club.  He won his first senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county title]] in 1920.  The championship was suspended in 1921; however, McInerney added a second county medal to his collection in 1922.

===Inter-county===

McInerney first came to prominence on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in the late 1910s.  In 1918 he first tasted success as, for the second year in-a-row, Limerick reached the Munster final.  [[Clare GAA|Clare]] provided the opposition on that occasion, however, McInerney’s side were the better team on the day.  The final score of 11-3 to 1-2 tells its own story as McInerney collected his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] title.  The subsequent All-Ireland final saw Limerick take on [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].  The first-half saw Limerick go on a goal-scoring spree as they took a half-time lead of 5-4 to 0-2.  The goals continued in the second half as Limerick won the game by 9-5 to 1-3, giving McInerney his first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal.

In 1919 Limerick reached their third consecutive Munster final.  [[Cork GAA|Cork]] were the opponents on that occasion, however, the All-Ireland champions were humbled with a 3-5 to 1-6 defeat.  McInerney’s side were heavily beaten by Cork again in the 1920 provincial decider.

In 1921 the Munster championship was affected by political strife.  Because of this only Cork and Limerick participated with both sides contesting the provincial final for the third consecutive year.  McInerney’s side avenged the defeats of the previous two years by beating Cork by 5-2 to 1-2.  It was his second Munster title.  The subsequent All-Ireland final pitted Limerick against [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]].  Once again, Limerick went on a goal-scoring rampage with captain [[Bob McConkey]] capturing four goals in all.  Limerick went on to win the game by 8-5 to 3-2, giving McInerney a second All-Ireland medal.

Limerick surrendered their Munster crown to Tipperary after a replay in 1922, however, they reversed that defeat in 1923 with McInerney, who wa snow captain of the team, adding a third Munster medal to his collection.  He later lined out in his third All-Ireland final as [[Galway GAA|Galway]] provided the opposition.  In spite of Galway playing in their very first All-Ireland final they had yet to win a title.  Limerick looked likely to capture a third All-Ireland title in six years, however, for the very first time the All-Ireland title went to a team from [[Connacht]].

The next few years saw Limerick go into decline in Munster and McInerney retired from inter-county hurling.

==Post-playing career==

McInerney, like many of his contemporaries was forced to give up the game of hurling in an effort to find work.  He emigrated to the United States in the 1920s and remained there for the rest of his life.

Paddy McInerney died in [[New Mexico]] in 1983.

'''Stephen McDonagh''' (born 15 October 1969) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] retired [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a left corner-back for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].

McDonagh joined the team during the [[National Hurling League 1992-93|1992-93 National League]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement prior to the start of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2004|2004 championship]]. During that time he won two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and one [[National Hurling League]] medal. McDonagh was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up on two occasions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17990|title=Limerick legend McDonagh retires|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=29 April 2004|accessdate=24 December 2008}}</ref>

At club level McDonagh was a one-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county club championship]] medalist with [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]].

==Playing career==

===Club===

McDonagh played his club hurling with Bruree and enjoyed some success in a career that spanned almost twenty-five years.

Having played in and lost the county final of 1994, it would take twelve years before McDonagh lined out in his second championship decider. As captain of the team he led his club men against club kingpins [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickwell]]. Bruree took an early lead but trailed by two points at the interval. A 49th-minute goal eventually helped the team to 1–16 to 1–15 victory. It was a first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal for McDonagh.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/at-long-last-bruree-lift-county-title-for-first-time-since-de-valera-was-a-kid-26360211.html|title=AT LONG LAST: Bruree lift county title for first time since De Valera was a kid|publisher=Irish Independent|date=16 October 2006|accessdate=19 February 2013}}</ref>

===Inter-county===

McDonagh joined the Limerick senior hurling panel during the [[National Hurling League 1992-93|1992-93 National League]] and made his debut against [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the quarter-final of the competition.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

The following year McDonagh became a regular member of the starting fifteen as Limerick qualified for the Munster final. Provincial whipping boys [[Clare GAA|Clare]] were the opponents and a rout took place.  A 0–25 to 2–10 score line gave Limerick the win and gave McDonagh his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Waterford/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=79852|title=Limerick v Waterford|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=3 July 2007|accessdate=19 February 2013}}</ref> Limerick subsequently qualified to meet [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the All-Ireland final.  It looked as if McDonagh's side were going to make history and claim a first title in twenty-one years as Limerick had a five-point lead with as many minutes left.  Offaly suddenly sprang to life following a [[Johnny Dooley (hurler)|Johnny Dooley]] goal from a close-in free.  Following the puck-out Offaly worked the ball up the field and [[Pat O'Connor (hurler)|Pat O'Connor]] struck for a second goal. The Offaly forwards scored another five unanswered points in the time remaining to secure a 3–16 to 2–13 victory.  It was a bitter blow for Limerick who looked as if they had one hand on the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/yourview/arid-10098744.html|title=Limerick: where broken dreams are a way of life|date=15 August 2009|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 February 2013}}</ref>

Two years later in 1996 McDonagh was back in the provincial decider. Limerick faced [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] on that occasion and looked to be heading out of the championship as Tipp took a ten-point lead.  McDonagh's side battled back to secure a 0–19 to 1–16 draw and a second chance to defeat their near rivals.  The replay also saw Tipperary take a decisive lead, however, Limerick's goal-scoring ability was the deciding factor.  A 4–7 to 0–16 score line gave Limerick the win and gave McDonagh a second Munster medal.  The subsequent All-Ireland final pitted Limerick against [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] for the first time in over forty years.  The game was far from a classic; however, it did provide excitement. [[Tom Dempsey (hurler)|Tom Dempsey]] was the hero of the day as he scored a goal after nineteen minutes to give Wexford a major advantage. His side led by 1–8 to 0–10 at half-time in spite of having [[Éamonn Scallan]] sent off. Wexford took a four-point lead in the second-half; however, this was whittled back to two points as Wexford hung on for the last twenty minutes. The final score of 1–13 to 0-14 provided Limerick with a second All-Ireland defeat in three seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eircomsports.eircom.net/News/Rising-from-the-Ashes-Wexford-1996.aspx|title= Rising from the Ashes: Wexford 1996|publisher=Eircom Sports|date=25 November 2009|accessdate=19 February 2013|first=Seán|last=Nolan}}</ref>

Limerick bounced back immediately in 1997 by defeating [[Galway GAA|Galway]] by 1–12 to 1–9 to take the National Hurling League title.  It was McDonagh's sole winners' medal in that competition.  The recent All-Ireland defeats, however, seemed to have damaged the team as Limerick crashed out of the provincial championship at an early stage.

This process repeated itself over the next few years and it was 2001 before McDonagh lined out in another Munster final.  Tipperary were the opponents on that occasion, however, Limerick fell by 2–16 to 1–17.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/2001/07/02/story6953.asp|title=Redemption day for Tipp|date=2 July 2001|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=22 April 2009}}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

McDonagh was now in the twilight of his career and success seemed as far away for Limerick as it did when he joined the panel. After failing to make an impact on the panel under new manager [[Pad Joe Whelehan]] in 2004, McDonagh decided to retire from inter-county hurling after a National League game against Galway.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17990|title=Limerick legend McDonagh retires|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=29 April 2004|accessdate=19 February 2013}}</ref>

He was an All-Ireland runner-up on two occasions. McCarthy represented the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team at various times during his career, winning three [[Railway Cup]] medals. Richie McCarthy.text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler (born 1987)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=January 2022}} {{infobox Gaelic games player |image = |name = Richie McCarthy |irish = Risteard Mac Cárthaigh |nickname = |occupation = Clerical officer |birth_date = {{birth date and age|1987|10|11|df=yes}} |birth_place = [[Kilfinane]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] |height = {{convert|1.8|m|ftin|0|abbr=on}} |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]]
→ [[Emmets GAA|Emmets]] |cl_years = |cl_position = Full Back |cl_apps_points = |cl_county = 0 |cl_province = |cl_all_ireland = |counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ic_years = 2009-2019 |ic_position = Full-back |ic_apps_points = 26 (1-05) |ic_province = 1 |ic_all_ireland = 1 |nhl = 0 |all_stars = 1 |cl_update = |ic_update = 18:27, 20 August 2018 }} '''Richard McCarthy''' (born 11 October 1987) is an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]]. He played for the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] for 10 years, during which time he usually lined out as a full-back. A defender who was noted for his swashbuckling style, McCarthy was considered a "Limerick hurling fans favourite".{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/496615/fans-favourite-richie-mccarthy-confirms-his-retirement-from-limerick-senior-hurling-team.html|title=Fans favourite Richie McCarthy confirms his retirement from Limerick senior hurling team|accessdate=25 November 2019|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=24 November 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} McCarthy began his hurling career at club level with Blackrock. After breaking onto the club's top adult team, he enjoyed his greatest success in [[2009-10 All-Ireland Junior Club Hurling Championship|2010]] when the club won the [[All-Ireland Junior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Junior Club Championship]]. Almost a decade later, McCarthy enjoyed further success when he won a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Premier Intermediate Championship]] medal and promotion. At inter-county level, McCarthy was part of the Limerick minor team that were [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] runners-up in [[2005 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2005]]. He later lined out for Limerick at under-21 and intermediate levels before joining the Limerick senior team in [[2009 National Hurling League|2009]]. From his debut, McCarthy lined out in a variety of positions in both defence and attack and made a combined total of 75 National League and Championship appearances in a career that ended with his last game in [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2018]]. During that time he was part of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]]-winning team in [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2018]]. McCarthy also secured a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal in 2013. He announced his retirement from inter-county hurling on 25 November 2019. McCarthy was named [[Munster Hurler of the Year]] in 2013 while he also won his only [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] that year. He claimed a further two All-Star nominations at various stages in his career. At inter-provincial level, McCarthy was also selected to play for [[Munster GAA|Munster]] but ended his career without a [[Railway Cup]] medal. ==Playing career== ===Blackrock=== McCarthy joined the [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's top adult team in the junior grade. On 8 November 2009, McCarthy enjoyed his first success at adult level when he was part of the Blackrock team that secured the [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick Junior Championship]] after a 2–18 to 1–16 defeat of [[Effin GAA|Effin]] in the final. On 13 December 2009, he lined out at left wing-forward when Blackrock faced [[Fermoy GAA|Fermoy]] in the [[2009–10 All-Ireland Junior Club Hurling Championship#Munster Junior club Hurling Championship|Munster final]]. McCarthy top scored for the team with 0-06 and ended the game with a [[Munster Junior Club Hurling Championship|winners' medal]] following the 1–12 to 0–14 victory.{{cite web |url=http://munster.gaa.ie/2009/12/13/aib-munster-gaa-junior-hurling-championship-final-fermoy-cork-v-blackrock-limerick/|title=Moloney nicks it for Blackrock|accessdate=1 March 2018 |publisher=Irish Independent |date=14 December 2009}} Blackrock subsequently qualified for the [[2009–10 All-Ireland Junior Club Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Junior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] on 13 February 2010, with McCarthy once again lining out in attack. He top scored with 0-07 and claimed an [[All-Ireland Junior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland medal]] after the 1–19 to 0–09 defeat of [[Naomh Colum Cille GAA|Naomh Colum Cille]].{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaelic-football/rock-take-title-26632271.html|title='Rock take title|accessdate=1 March 2018 |publisher=Irish Independent |date=14 February 2010}} On 6 October 2019, McCarthy lined out at full-back when Blackrock drew 0-18 apiece with [[Kildimo-Pallaskenry GAA|Kildimo-Pallaskenry]] in the [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Premier Intermediate Championship final]].{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/483922/blackrock-and-kildimo-pallaskenry-play-out-thrilling-draw-in-limerick-premier-ihc-final.html|title=Blackrock and Kildimo-Pallaskenry play out thrilling draw in Limerick Premier IHC final|access-date=25 November 2019 |publisher=Limerick Leader |date=6 October 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} He retained his position for the replay on 26 October 2019 and ended the game with a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|winners' medal]] following the 1–18 to 0–16 victory.{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/489238/blackrock-end-21-year-wait-for-senior-hurling-with-limerick-premier-ihc-title-win.html|title=Blackrock end 21 year wait for senior hurling with Limerick Premier IHC title win|access-date=25 November 2019 |publisher=Limerick Leader |date=26 October 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} ===Limerick=== ====Minor and under-21==== McCarthy first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the minor team during the [[2005 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2005 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 4 May 2005 when he came on as a substitute in Limerick's 2–14 to 1–06 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the Munster semi-final.{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/limerick-stun-tipp-to-book-final-place-25983462.html|title=Limerick stun Tipp to book final place|accessdate=25 November 2019 |publisher=Irish Independent|date=5 May 2005|first=|last=}} On 26 June 2005, McCarthy was an unused substitute when Limerick suffered a 2018 to 1–12 defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/cronins-accuracy-guides-cork-to-30th-minor-title-25982253.html|title=Cronin's accuracy guides Cork to 30th minor title|date=27 June 2005|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=24 April 2013|first=|last=}} He was again an unused substitute when Limerick suffered a 3–12 to 0–17 defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] on 11 September 2005.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/galway-glee-as-goals-put-paid-to-gutsy-limerick-25965776.html|title=Galway glee as goals put paid to gutsy Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=12 September 2005|accessdate=24 March 2019|first=Paddy|last=Hickey}} McCarthy was drafted onto the Limerick under-21 starting fifteen in advance of the [[2008 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2008 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 5 June 2008 when he lined out at full-forward in Limerick's 2–17 to 1–07 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the Munster quarter-final. Limerick's subsequent defeat by Tipperary in the semi-final was his last game in the grade. ====Intermediate==== McCarthy was added to the Limerick intermediate team prior to the start of the [[2007 All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship#Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|2007 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 10 June 2007 in a 0–17 to 0–15 defeat of Tipperary. On 7 July 2007, McCarthy lined out at full-back when Limerick suffered a 5–12 to 1–12 defeat by Waterford in the [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/match-reports/casey-fires-deise-to-historic-win-37687.html|title=Casey fires Déise to historic win|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 July 2007|accessdate=24 March 2019|first=Brendan|last=Larkin}} ====Senior==== On 8 February 2009, Condon made his first appearance for the Limerick senior team when he lined out at left corner-back in a 3–13 to 1–18 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2009 National Hurling League|National League]]. He was later included on the panel for the [[2009 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|Championship]] but remained as an unused substitute throughout the campaign. At the end of a disappointing season, Limerick manager [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]] dropped several high-profile players from the panel.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/mccarthy-wields-the-axe-at-limerick-104495.html|title=McCarthy wields the axe at Limerick|date=30 October 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=Martin|last=Kiely}} Over the course of the winter, many more players, including McCarthy, withdrew from the panel and refused to play while the management team remained in place.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/2.823/four-more-players-quit-the-limerick-squad-1.1238677|title=Four more players quit the Limerick squad|date=2 January 2010|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/mccarthy-dispute-gets-silent-treatment-1.1244613|title=McCarthy dispute gets silent treatment|date=19 January 2010|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=|last=}} The Limerick County Board refused to remove McCarthy and contested the 2010 season with a new group of players. McCarthy returned to the panel the following year and was a regular player under new manager [[Dónal O'Grady]]. On 30 April 2011, he scored four points from centre-forward when Limerick defeated Clare by 4–12 to 2–13 to win the National League Division 2 title.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}} On 14 July 2013, McCarthy lined out in his first [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]]. He was selected at full-back for Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] and a first provincial title in 17 years.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} Condon ended the season by being named in the full-back position on the [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaelicplayers.com/TabId/86/ArtMID/421/ArticleID/206/2013-Hurling-All-Star-Nominations.aspx|title=2013 Hurling All Star Nominations|date=4 October 2013|publisher=GPA website|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=|last=}} On 3 July 2014, Condon was selected at full-back when Limerick faced Cork in a second successive [[2014 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]]. He ended the game on the losing side following a 2–24 to 0–24 defeat.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/irrepressible-rebels-rule-munster-again-275363.html|title=Irrepressible Rebels rule Munster again|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=14 July 2014|accessdate=17 July 2014|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} On 19 August 2018, McCarthy was selected on the substitute's bench when Limerick lined out in their first [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] in 12 years. He was introduced as a 50th-minute substitute for [[Mike Casey (hurler)|Mike Casey]] at full-back and claimed a [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|winners' medal]] following Limerick's 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and a first championship title in 45 years.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}} Just two weeks after this victory it was revealed that McCarthy faced a lengthy spell on the sidelines after tearing his cruciate ligament.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-allireland-champion-facing-long-spell-on-the-sidelines-after-cruciate-ligament-injury-37292787.html|title=Limerick All-Ireland champion facing long spell on the sidelines after cruciate ligament injury|publisher=Irish Independent|date=7 September 2018|accessdate=25 November 2019|first=|last=}} The injury ruled him out of the [[2019 National Hurling League|2019 National League]] while he also failed to secure a place on Limerick's match-day panel for the championship. On 25 November 2019, McCarthy announced his retirement from inter-county hurling. In a statement he said: "Today I am announcing my retirement from the Limerick Senior Hurling team.{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/richie-mccarthy-retires-limerick-4905382-Nov2019/|title =Limerick All-Ireland winner McCarthy announces inter-county retirement|date=25 November 2019|work=The 42|accessdate=26 November 2019}} It has been an incredible 11-year journey but the time is right for me to now step away. It is the greatest honour for any GAA player to wear their county colours but it has also been the wild dreams of a youngster from Kilfinane."{{cite [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Patrick Kelly''' (born 1955) is an Irish [[hurling]] coach and former player. At club level, he played with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Playing career== Kelly played hurling at all levels as a student at [[C.B.S. Charleville|Charleville CBS]] and won consecutive Munster Colleges U16½HC titles in 1971 and 1972.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/cork/news/first-rice-cup-win-for-cbs-under-14-team-in-a-classic-encounter/27059227.html|title=First Rice Cup win for CBS Under 14 team in a classic encounter|publisher=Irish Independent|date=12 June 2003|access-date=29 March 2025|first=|last=}} He was also involved in athletics and won an All-Ireland underage title in the 880yd.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20212152.html|title=’All we need is a bit of luck’|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=27 October 2012|access-date=29 March 2025|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} Kelly later studied at the National College of Physical Education in [[Limerick]] and lined out in various inter-varsities hurling competitions.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/50-years-on-the-thomond-trailblazers-including-brian-mullins-pat-spillane-and-jimmy-deenihan-who-led-a-gaa-revolution/42242046.html|title=50 years on: The Thomond trailblazers, including Brian Mullins, Pat Spillane and Jimmy Deenihan, who led a GAA revolution|publisher=Irish Independent|date=24 December 2022|access-date=29 March 2025|first=Frank|last=Roche}} At club level, Kelly first played for [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] at juvenile and underage levels and was part of the club's minor team that won consecutive Limerick MHC titles.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Treaty and St. Kieran's for senior football final|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=19 November 1973|access-date=29 March 2025|first=|last=}} He was in his final year of the minor grade in 1973 when he joined Kilmallock's senior team and went on to win three consecutive [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] titles.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaelic-games/141636/Limerick-SHC-Final---Kilmallock.html|title=Limerick SHC Final - Kilmallock’s three-in-a-row success is fondly remembered|publisher=Limerick Live|date=5 October 2012|access-date=29 March 2025|first=|last=}} Kelly won six Limerick SHC titles on total, while he also claimed two [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] medals.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=29 March 2025|first=|last=}} He [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ed Kilmallock to a 1-17 to 2-07 defeat by [[Sarsfields GAA (Galway)|Sarsfields]] in the [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1993 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/128541/1992--When-Kilmallock-conquered-Limerick.html|title=1992: When Kilmallock conquered Limerick and Munster|publisher=Limerick Live|date=20 November 2014|access-date=29 March 2025|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} At inter-county level, Kelly first appeared for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] that lost consecutive [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship#List of finals|Munster MHC finals]] in 1972 and 1973. He immediately progressed to the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]] before making his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in July 1974. Kelly was later a substitute for Limerick's defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[1974 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1974 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://kilkennygaa.b-cdn.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/197475-Booklet-optimized.pdf|title=Remembering Kilkenny|publisher=Kilkenny GAA website|date=|access-date=29 March 2025|first=|last=}} Kelly won consecutive [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals in 1980 and 1981, while he was again a substitute for Limerick's defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1980 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1980 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=29 March 2025|first=|last=}} He was the team's top scorer when Limerick claimed consecutive [[National Hurling League]] titles in 1984 and 1985.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/529524/limerick-hurlers-back-to-back-national-league-champions-84-85.html|title=Limerick hurlers back-to-back National League champions 84/85|publisher=Limerick Live|date=27 March 2020|access-date=29 March 2025|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} Kelly was also honoured with an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2021/12/22/limericks-storied-history-with-the-all-star-awards-1973-2021/|title=Limerick’s Storied History with the All-Star Awards (1973-2021)|publisher=Limerick Post|date=22 December 2021|access-date=29 March 2025|first=Jack|last=Neville}} Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Kelly being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won a [[Railway Cup]] medal in 1985 when he was part of the Munster team that beat [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] by 3-06 to 1-11 in the final.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Coaching career== Kelly was involved in coaching at all levels in his role as a teacher at the [[The Abbey School (Tipperary)|Abbey CBS]] in [[Tipperary (town)|Tipperary]]. He managed the school's senior team to [[All-Ireland PPS Senior B Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Colleges SBHC]] titles in 1992 and 2002.{{cite web|url=https://www.tipperarylive.ie/news/home/923625/hon-the-lads-abbey-boys-reunite-in-tipperary-to-celebrate-past-successes.html|title=Hon the lads! '''John "Tyler" Mackey''' (23 August 1882 – 2 December 1962) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] and [[Labour Party (Ireland)|Labour Party]] politician. Mackey played as a midfielder for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://limerick.ie/media/mackeyjohntylerpts1-8-204.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120919204720/http://www.limerick.ie/media/mackeyjohntylerpts1-8-204.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 September 2012|title=John "Tyler" Mackey of Castleconnell|publisher=Limerick Heritage website|access-date=23 April 2012}}</ref> He also represented the Labour party on [[Limerick County Council]], having been elected in the [[Castleconnell]] electoral area.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=38823|title=The Late James Mackey|publisher=Limerick Leader website|access-date=21 July 2013}}</ref>

Mackey made his first appearance for the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1901|1901 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1917|1917 championship]]. During that time he won two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals, however, an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal eluded him.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=23 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328073637/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=28 March 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At club level Mackey was a one-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] medalist with [[Castleconnell GAA|Castleconnell]].{{fact|date=December 2021}}

Mackey's two sons, [[Mick Mackey|Mick]] and [[John Mackey (hurler)|John, Jnr.]], won several All-Ireland medals throughout the 1930s and 1940s.{{fact|date=December 2021}}

'''Wayne McNamara''' (born 11 June 1986) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a right wing-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

McNamara joined the team during the [[2006 Senior Hurling championship]] and became a regular member of the starting fifteen over subsequent seasons. Since then he has won one [[National Hurling League|National League (Division 2)]] medal. McNamara has ended up as an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion.

At club level McNamara is a three-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county club championship]] medalist with [[Adare GAA|Adare]].

==Playing career==
===Club===

McNamara is a [[dual player]] of both hurling and [[Gaelic football]] with the [[Adare GAA|Adare]] club and has enjoyed much success.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

In 2007, he lined out in his first hurling championship decider. [[Croom GAA|Croom]] were the opponents, however, a convincing 0–14 to 0–5 victory gave McNamara his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/sheehan-on-song-as-adare-stroll-through-final-1217153.html|title=Limerick on the rise|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 November 2012|date=12 November 2007}}</ref>

Adare reached the final once again in 2008. A 0–13 to 0–8 defeat of [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] gave McNamara a second consecutive championship medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10075193.html|title=Powerful Adare keep grip on title|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 November 2012|date=20 October 2008|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

In 2009, Adare were back in the championship decider and the chance to claim their first ever hat-trick of championship titles. [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] provided the opposition in a disappointing game. A 1–17 to 0-3 trouncing gave McNamara his third successive championship medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/adare-swat-na-piarsaigh-aside-to-claim-limerick-title-430709.html|title=Adare swat Na Piarsaigh aside to claim Limerick title|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 November 2012|date=18 October 2009}}</ref>

===Inter-county===

McNamara was drafted onto the Limerick senior hurling panel for a crucial All-Ireland qualifier against [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in 2006.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=63089|title=Hurlers welcome back U21 medallists|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=4 November 2012|date=30 June 2006}}</ref> He played no part in that game but was included on the panel again the following year, making his debut in a [[Waterford Crystal Cup]] game against the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=71017|title=Limerick have two debutants|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=3 November 2012|date=12 January 2007}}</ref>

After making some cameo appearances for Limerick, McNamara was a regular member of the starting fifteen by 2011. He won a [[National Hurling League|National League (Division 2)]] medal that year following a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of near neighbours [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-2634833.html|title=Limerick on the rise|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=3 November 2012|date=2 May 2011|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}}</ref>

'''Michael Kennedy''' (1911 – 14 May 1977) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a full-back for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=Limerick GAA profile|publisher=Hogan Stand website|accessdate=20 May 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archivedate=25 May 2012}}</ref>

== Career ==
Kennedy joined the team during the [[1933 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1933 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement almost a decade later. During that time he won three [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medals, four [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals and five [[National Hurling League]] medals. Kennedy was an All-Ireland SHC runner-up on one occasion.

At club level Kennedy played with [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]].

He made his senior debut in the [[Thomond Feis|1916 Thomond Feis]]. Lanigan went on to play a key part for Limerick during a golden age for the team, and won two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals and three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals. He was an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion. At club level Lanigan won five [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medals with [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]]. His retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1926 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1926 championship]]. In retirement from playing, Lanigan became involved in the administrative affairs of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. He served as secretary of the Limerick County Board as well as vice-president of the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]]. '''Thomas McGrath''' (1891 – 31 May 1958) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a right corner-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1918.htm|title=1918 All-Ireland hurling champions|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|date=|accessdate=21 April 2014|first=|last=}}</ref>

Born in [[Limerick City|Limerick]], McGrath first arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of twenty seven when he first linked up with the Limerick senior team. He made his senior debut in the [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1918 championship]]. McGrath went on to play a key part for Limerick during a golden age for the team, and won two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals and three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals. He was an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion.{{fact|date=December 2021}}

At club level McGrath won five [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medals with [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]].{{fact|date=December 2021}}

Cian Lynch.text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler (born 1996)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=January 2022}} {{infobox Gaelic games player |image = |name = Cian Lynch |irish = Cian Ó Loingsigh |nickname = |occupation = |birth_date = {{birth date and age|1996|1|3|df=yes}} |birth_place = [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] |height = {{convert|1.8|m|ftin|0|abbr=on}} |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] |cl_years = 2013–present |cl_position = midfield |cl_apps_points = |cl_county = 2 |cl_province = |cl_all_ireland = |colleges = [[Mary Immaculate College]]
[[NUI Galway]] |fitz = 2 |counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ic_years = 2015–present |ic_position = Centre-forward |ic_apps_points = 57 (1–70) |ic_province = 7 |ic_all_ireland = 6 |nhl = 4 |all_stars = 3 |cl_update = |ic_update = 21:58, 19 July 2026 }} '''Cian Lynch''' (born 3 January 1996) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a centre forward for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Championship]] club [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]], where he has held the role of captain, and the [[Limerick senior hurling team|Limerick senior team]]. Recognised for his skill level and team play, he is widely considered one of the best players in the current game and has often been described as a "midfield magician". He is also one of only two players to win the 'hurler of the year' award more than once, with the only other player to do so being Henry Shefflin with three wins.{{cite web|url= https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/520678/opinion-the-cian-lynch-audacious-skill-from-limerick-hurling-star-jerome-o-connell.html|title=Opinion: 'The Cian Lynch' – audacious skill from Limerick hurling star|date=27 February 2020|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=26 December 2020|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cian-lynch-still-playing-central-role-in-rise-of-limerick-hurling-1.4432167|title=Cian Lynch still playing central role in rise of Limerick hurling|date=10 December 2020|work=Irish Times|accessdate=26 December 2020|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0127/1111323-lynch-magic-can-drive-limerick-forward-niall-moran/|title=Lynch magic can drive Limerick forward – Niall Moran|date=27 January 2020|work=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=26 December 2020|first=|last=}} Lynch began his inter-county career at minor level with Limerick in 2012, with whom he won back-to-back [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Minor Championship]] titles in his last two years with the team. In 2014, he joined the Limerick under-21 team and was integral in the team's [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Under-21 Championship]] wins in [[2015 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|2015]] and [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|2017]]. Lynch joined the Limerick senior team for the 2015 season. He has since won four [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] titles, three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] titles and two [[National Hurling League]] titles with the team. In 2020, he had a significant role in Limerick becoming the first team since [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in 1961 to have a 100% winning record in all competitions in a single season. Lynch made his senior club championship debut with Patrickswell as a 17-year-old in [[2013 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2013]] and has since established himself as one of the mainstays of the team. He was a member of the Patrickswell team that won [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Championship]] titles in [[2016 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2016]] and [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2019]]. Lynch has been named on the [[GAA GPA All Stars Awards|GAA–GPA All-Star Team]] and ''[[the Sunday Game]]'' Team of the Year three times each and the Under-21 Team of the Year twice. He was also named [[GAA/GPA Player of the Month (hurling)|GAA–GPA Player of the Month]] in his first championship season and was [[All Stars Hurler of the Year|GAA–GPA All-Star Hurler of the Year]] in 2018 and 2021. ==Early career== ===Ardscoil Rís=== Lynch first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]]. Having played in every grade, he was just 15-years-old when he earned selection for the college's senior hurling team. On 27 February 2011, Lynch was introduced as a substitute when Ardscoil Rís won the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] title after a 3–19 to 0–03 defeat of [[C.B.S. Charleville]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/awesome-ardscoil-storm-to-harty-title-26709031.html|title=Awesome Ardscoil storm to Harty title|date=28 February 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}} He was also introduced as a substitute in the subsequent 2–10 to 1–11 defeat by [[St. Kieran's College]] in the [[Dr. Croke Cup|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/ohanrahan-heaps-misery-on-ardscoil-26720241.html|title=O'Hanrahan heaps misery on Ardscoil|publisher=Irish Independent|date=4 April 2011|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} On 22 February 2014, Lynch was captain of the Ardscoil Rís that defeated Scoil na Trionóide from [[Doon, County Limerick|Doon]] by 2–13 to 0–04 in the final of the Harty Cup.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/ardscoil-ris-a-class-apart-in-derby-duel-259848.html|title=Ardscoil Rís a class apart in derby duel|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=24 February 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} ===Mary Immaculate College=== During his studies at [[Mary Immaculate College]], Lynch was selected as a forward for the college's senior hurling team. On 27 February 2016, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal as Mary I won their first ever title after a 1–30 to 3–22 defeat of the [[University of Limerick]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/eamonn-cregan-hails-heroic-mary-i-384649.html|title=Eamonn Cregan hails heroic Mary I|date=29 February 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} Lynch was at full-forward when Mary I retained the title in 2017 following a 3–24 to 1–19 defeat of [[Carlow Institute of Technology]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/dj-carey-hails-inspirational-coach-jamie-wall-as-mary-i-retain-fitzgibbon-title-443894.html|title=DJ Carey hails inspirational coach Jamie Wall as Mary I retain Fitzgibbon title|date=27 February 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=John|last=Fallon}} ==Club career== Lynch joined [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] at a young age, a club with whom his family had a long tradition. His six uncles, [[Ciarán Carey|Ciarán]], [[Paul Carey (hurler)|Paul]], Pa, Seán and Nigel Carey, were senior team mainstays during a golden era for the club in the 1980s and 1990s.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limericks-cian-lynch-upholding-proud-family-tradition-331784.html|title=Limerick's Cian Lynch upholding proud family tradition|date=20 May 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=John|last=Fogarty}}{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/324027/watch-limericks-cian-lynch-on-trying-to-replicate-exploits-of-his-uncle-ciaran-carey.html|title=WATCH: Limerick's Cian Lynch on trying to replicate exploits of his uncle Ciaran Carey|date=14 July 2018|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Colm|last=Kinsella}} After an unremarkable juvenile and underage career, Lynch was 17-years-old when he joined the club's senior team, stating: "I was in fifth year at school and was with the county minors. It was my second last year minor so I was only coming and going so I didn't play that much that year. I was kind of concentrating on the minor and my own age group."{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/features/feature/club-cian-lynch-patrickswell-110243/|title=My Club: Cian Lynch – Patrickswell|date=20 August 2015|publisher=GAA website|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=|last=}} An undefeated run through the [[2015 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2015 County Championship]] campaign saw Patrickswell qualify for the [[2015 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]], with Lynch's side ultimately facing a one-point defeat by [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}} For the second successive season, Patrickswell remained undefeated on their way to the [[2016 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|2016 County Championship final]]. Lynch scored three points from play and ended the game with his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|winners' medal]] after a 1–26 to 1–07 win over [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/magnificent-patrickswell-still-pride-of-the-parish-427216.html|title=Magnificent Patrickswell still pride of the parish|date=14 October 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=6 August 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} After two unsuccessful seasons, Lynch was appointed team captain in advance of the [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2019 County Championship]]. After a third undefeated run through the [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Group 1|group stage]] in five years, Patrickswell qualified for the [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Knock-out stage|2019 final]]. Lynch ended the game with a second winners' medal after scoring three points in the 1–17 to 0–15 defeat of [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cian-lynch-comes-to-the-fore-as-patrickswell-hold-off-na-piarsaigh-in-limerick-county-final-38567636.html|title=Cian Lynch comes to the fore as Patrickswell hold off Na Piarsaigh in Limerick county final|publisher=Irish Independent|date=6 October 2019|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=Colm|last=Keys}} ==Inter-county career== ===Minor and under-21=== Lynch was just 16-years-old when he was added to the Limerick minor panel shortly before the start of the [[2012 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2012 Munster Minor Championship]]. On 2 May 2012, he made his first appearance for the team, scoring a point from left corner-forward in a 0–16 to 1–12 [[2012 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|quarter-final]] defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/treaty-super-sub-sinks-cork-192651.html|title=Treaty super sub sinks Cork|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 May 2012|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} Once again eligible for the minor grade in [[2013 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|2013]], Lynch was retained on the team by manager [[Brian Ryan (hurling manager)|Brian Ryan]]. On 23 July 2013, he lined out at wing-forward when Limerick won their first [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Minor Championship]] title in 29 years after a 1–20 to 4–08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in a replay of the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} Lynch was appointed captain of the Limerick minor team in advance of the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2014 Munster Minor Championship]]. On 22 July 2014, he won a second successive Munster Minor Championship title after a six-point win over Waterford in a final replay.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} On 7 September 2014, Lynch captained Limerick to a 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2014 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-minors-savour-all-ireland-success-against-spirited-limerick-1.1920852|title=Kilkenny minors savour All-Ireland success against spirited Limerick|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 September 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} Lynch was in his final year with the minor team when he was drafted onto the Limerick under-21 team for the [[2014 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2014 Munster Under-21 Championship]]. On 4 June 2014, he made his first appearance for the team in a 2–20 to 1–14 [[2014 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|quarter-final]] defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick |publisher=Irish Examiner|date=5 June 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} Lynch was again called up to the under-21 panel for the [[2015 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2015 Munster Under-21 Championship]], becoming the only senior panellist on the team.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-u21-hurling-team-2217744-Jul2015/|title=Lynch the sole senior panellist in Limerick U21 side for Munster semi-final|publisher=The 42|date=15 July 2015|accessdate=26 December 2020|first=|last=}} On 30 July 2015, he lined out at left corner-forward when Limerick defeated four-in-a-row hopefuls Clare by 0–22 to 0–19 to win the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Under-21 Championship]] title. On 12 September 2015, Lynch was switched to centre-forward when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0–26 to 1–07 to win the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} He ended the season by being named in the centre-forward position on the Team of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/the-all-ireland-u21-hurling-team-of-the-year-nominees-are-in-2347611-Sep2015/|title=The names are in – here are the Bord Gáis Energy Team of the Year nominees|date=23 September 2015|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Shane|last=Hannon}} After a defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in [[2016 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2016]], Lynch lined out in a fourth successive [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Under-21 Championship]] campaign the following year. On 26 July 2017, he won a second Munster Under-21 Championship title in three years after a 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}} On 9 September 2017, Lynch was at left wing-forward for Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2017 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} He was once again honoured at the end of the season by being included on the Team of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-u21-hurling-all-ireland-gillane-3626268-Oct2017/|title=Gillane the star man as Limerick, Kilkenny, Galway and Cork players make U21 team of the year|date=2 October 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ===Senior=== ====2015 season==== Lynch was just 19-years-old when he was drafted onto the Limerick senior panel by team manager [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J. Ryan]] in advance of the [[2015 Waterford Crystal Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-1871085-Jan2015/|title=5 new faces in Limerick hurling panel, 6 depart, O'Grady still captain and Moran stays on|publisher=The 42|date=8 January 2015|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} He made his first appearance for the team on 17 January 2015, scoring three points from left wing-forward in a 2–15 to 1–15 [[2015 Waterford Crystal Cup#Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] win over [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-sport/limerick-hurlers-beat-waterford-in-opening-game-of-2015-1-6527849|title=Limerick hurlers beat Waterford in opening game of 2015|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=17 January 2015|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} Lynch was a regular during the pre-season competition and ended the campaign by claiming his first senior silverware after a 3–20 to 1–16 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[2015 Waterford Crystal Cup#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-win-waterford-crystal-cup-for-first-time-in-nine-years-660379.html|title=Limerick win Waterford Crystal Cup for first time in nine years|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=31 January 2015|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} He was retained on the Limerick panel for the [[2015 National Hurling League|2015 National League]] and lined out in all six of Limerick's games after making his debut on 14 February 2015 in a 2–16 to 0–22 draw with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20312822.html|title=Waterford put on a show but Limerick make their point|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=16 February 2015|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} On 24 May 2015, Lynch made his first appearance in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] when he gave a [[man of the match]] performance in a one-point [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|quarter-final]] win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]].{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-indisciplined-clare-in-munster-quarter-final-678565.html|title= Limerick beat indisciplined Clare in Munster quarter-final|date=25 May 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=26 May 2015}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/cian-lynch-limerick-2-2123002-May2015/|title= Limerick's newest hurling star embraced playing on a 'field of legends'|date=25 May 2015|publisher=The 42|accessdate=26 May 2015}} He was later named as the [[GAA/GPA Player of the Month (hurling)|GAA/GPA Player of the Month]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-s-cian-lynch-named-gaa-gpa-hurler-of-the-month-for-may-1.2244881|title=Limerick's Cian Lynch named GAA/GPA hurler of the month for May|publisher=Irish Times|date=11 June 2015|accessdate=24 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} ====2016 season==== Lynch was again included on the Limerick panel for the 2016 season, but missed the team's two opening games in the newly created pre-season [[2016 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]]. On 23 January 2016, he scored two points from left wing-forward when Limerick were beaten by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2016 Munster Senior Hurling League#Details|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/clare-earn-dramatic-one-point-win-munster-final-2564550-Jan2016/|title=Clare earn dramatic one-point victory in Munster final|publisher=The 42|date=23 January 2016|accessdate=25 December 2020|first=Eoin|last=Brennan}} Lynch was a regular starter in Limerick's [[2016 National Hurling League|2016 National League]] campaign and made six appearances in total, including at left wing-forward in the 3–23 to 1–18 [[2016 National Hurling League#Division 1 Semi-finals|semi-final]] defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/waterford-limerick-report-2720411-Apr2016/|title=Waterford book place in league decider with impressive win over Limerick|publisher=The 42|date=23 January 2016|accessdate=25 December 2020|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} ====2017 season==== Lynch combined his [[Mary Immaculate College]] [[2017 Fitzgibbon Cup|Fitzgibbon Cup]] duties with Limerick's [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]] campaign at the start of the 2017 season. On 29 January 2017, he came on as a 60th-minute substitute for team captain [[James Ryan (hurler)|James Ryan]] in a 1–21 to 1–20 [[2017 Munster Senior Hurling League#Final|provincial league final]] defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/alan-cadogan-cork-limerick-3211597-Jan2017/|title=Cadogan hits last-gasp goal as Cork claim Munster hurling league title against Limerick|date=29 January 2017|work=The 42|accessdate=23 February 2017}} Lynch made five appearances for Limerick during the [[2017 National Hurling League|2017 National League]] campaign, including at left corner-forward in the ten-point defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2017 National Hurling League#Division 1 Semi-Finals|semi-final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/arid-30785982.html|title=Galway see off Limerick to advance to Division 1 final|date=16 April 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=|last=}} ====2018 season==== Lynch was again named on the 38-man Limerick panel for the upcoming [[2018 Limerick senior hurling team season|2018 season]], however, he missed some part of the pre-season [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]] due to [[2018 Fitzgibbon Cup|Fitzgibbon Cup]] commitments with [[Mary Immaculate College]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/281970/10-additions-to-2018-limerick-hurling-panel.html|title=10 additions to 2018 Limerick hurling panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=5 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} On 14 January 2018, he claimed his first senior silverware in three years when Limerick beat [[Clare GAA|Clare]] by 0–16 to 0–10 to claim the [[2018 Munster Senior Hurling League|pre-season tournament]] title.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/limerick-make-bold-statement-of-intent-36487975.html|title=Limerick make bold statement of intent|date=15 January 2018|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=15 January 2018}} The subsequent [[2018 National Hurling League|National League]] saw Lynch line out in all seven of Limerick's games. On 19 August 2018, he was named at right corner-forward when Limerick faced [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-team-news-all-ireland-hurling-final-4188195-Aug2018/|title=Limerick name unchanged side for All-Ireland final showdown against Galway|date=17 August 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=Emma|last=Duffy}} Lynch scored a point from play as Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}} Later that day he was named on ''[[the Sunday Game]]'' Team of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986154-limerick-rule-in-the-sunday-game-team-of-the-year/|title=Limerick rule in The Sunday Game team of the year|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=20 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=|last=}} Lynch ended the season by being named [[All Stars Hurler of the Year|Hurler of the Year]], while he also selected as midfield partner to [[Cork GAA|Cork]]'s [[Darragh Fitzgibbon]] on the [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/1101/1008065-lynch-is-hurler-of-year-fenton-wins-footballer-of-year/|title=Lynch is Hurler of Year, Fenton wins Footballer of Year|date=2 November 2018|publisher=RTE}} ====2019 season==== Lynch was again a regular for Limerick during the [[2019 National Hurling League|2019 National League]], playing a role in seven of their eight games. He scored two points from play when Limerick claimed their first [[National Hurling League#Division 1|Division 1]] title since [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] after a 1–24 to 0–19 win over Waterford in the [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} Lynch ended the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2019 Munster Championship]] with his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|provincial winners' medal]] after the 2–26 to 2–14 win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} He ended the year by receiving his second successive All-Star nomination.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-allstars-hurling-2019-4824531-Sep2019/|title=11 players from Tipperary as 8 counties feature in 2019 All-Star hurling nominations|date=26 September 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=26 September 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ====2020 season==== Lynch wasn't included on the Limerick team for the two [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League#Group 1|group stage]] games of the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League|2020 Munster League]]. He was back on the team at midfield for the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling League#Final|final]] against [[Cork GAA|Cork]] on 11 January 2020, and scored a point from play in the 1–32 to 0–20 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2020/0111/1105733-limerick-cruise-past-to-cork-to-win-munster-league/|title=Stylish Limerick cruise past Cork to win Munster league|date=11 January 2020|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=18 December 2020|first=Denis|last=Hurley}} The subsequent [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|National League]] campaign saw Lynch lining out in three of Limerick's five [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A|Division 1A]] games. On 25 October 2020, he was again at midfield for the 0–36 to 1–23 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed league final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=25 October 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} Lynch ended the [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship|2020 Munster Championship]] with a second successive winners' medal after lining out in the new position of centre-forward in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]] defeat of Waterford.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford for historic Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} He was again selected at centre-forward for the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] against Waterford on 13 December 2020, ending the game with a second title in three years after the 0–30 to 0–19 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/aaron-gillane-to-start-as-limerick-and-waterford-teams-named-for-all-ireland-final-39853753.html|title=Aaron Gillane to start as Limerick and Waterford teams named for All-Ireland final|date=11 December 2020|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=Conor|last=McKeon}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Limerick show consistency in a world gone mad to claim All-Ireland honours|date=13 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} ====2021 season==== Lynch was named on the bench for Limerick's opening [[2021 National Hurling League#Division 1 Group A Round 1|group stage]] game of the [[2021 National Hurling League|2021 National League]] against [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/john-kiely-names-first-limerick-squad-of-2021/|title=John Kiely names first Limerick squad of 2021|date=7 May 2021|publisher=Sporting Limerick|accessdate=11 September 2021|first=Jack|last=Neville}} After coming on as a substitute in the 0–20 apiece draw, he was restored to the starting fifteen for Limerick's next three games against [[Galway GAA|Galway]], [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] and [[Cork GAA|Cork]], before dropping to the subs' bench for Limerick's final group stage game against [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/640676/limerick-senior-hurling-team-named-for-allianz-league-with-westmeath.html|title=Limerick Senior hurling team named for Allianz league clash with Westmeath|date=11 June 2021|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=11 September 2021|first=|last=}} After the team came in for criticism for a poor league start, Lynch stated: "It’s just about staying focused really and working hard every week, every game that comes your way. Just doing your best as a group and team. It’s just about driving on and we’re looking forward to the summer now."{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-2021-5457006-Jun2021/|title=Discipline issues, media scrutiny and a target on their backs — Limerick's rocky start to 2021|date=5 June 2021|publisher=The 42|accessdate=11 September 2021|first=|last=}} Lynch subsequently claimed a third successive [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title as well as being named [[man of the match]] for his [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]] performance against Tipperary.{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40339985.html|title=Immense second-half turnaround sees Limerick deny Tipperary in Munster final|date=18 July 2021|publisher=Echo Live|accessdate=11 September 2021|first=|last=}} He was again named man of the match after claiming a third All-Ireland winners' medal in four seasons following the [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242237-lynch-treasuring-special-limerick-moments/|title=Lynch treasuring 'special' Limerick moments|date=22 August 2021|publisher=RTÉ
