'''John McDonogh''' (1941 - 12 September 2012) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as full-back for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaelic-games/martin-kiely-column-farewell-to-john-mcdonogh-a-great-limerick-gael-1-4291856|title=Farewell to John McDonogh, a great Limerick gael|date=23 September 2012|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Martin|last=Kiely}}</ref>

Born in [[Limerick (city)|Ballysimon, Limerick]], McDonogh first arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of sixteen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team. He joined the senior panel during the [[1963 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1963 championship]]. McDonogh was a regular member of the team over the next few years, however, he ended his career without any major success.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

At club level McDonogh hurling and [[Gaelic football]] with [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St. Patrick's]].{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

McDonogh's son, [[Stephen McDonagh|Stephen]], also played with Limerick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/mcdonagh-no-margin-for-error-285244.html|title=McDonagh: No margin for error|date=6 September 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref>

Throughout his career McDonogh made 9 championship appearances. His retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1970 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1970 championship]].{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{infobox Gaelic games player |image = |name = Tom Morrissey |irish = Tomás Ó Muireasa |nickname = |occupation = Tax assistant |birth_date ={{Birth date and age|df=yes|1996|5|29}} |birth_place = [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] |height_ft = 6 |height_in = 0 |sport = Hurling |code = Hurling |county = Limerick |province = Munster |club = [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] |cl_years = 2023-present |cl_position = |cl_apps_points = 64 (30-462) |cl_county = 0 |cl_province = |cl_all_ireland = |colleges = [[University of Limerick]] |fitz = 1 |col_years = 2014–2019 |counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] |ic_years = 2015–present |ic_position = Left wing-forward |ic_apps_points = 60 (2–146) |ic_province = 7 |ic_all_ireland = 6 |nhl = 3 |all_stars = 3 |cl_update = 16:17, 2 April 2026 | ic_update = 22:33, 19 July 2026 }} '''Thomas Morrissey''' (born 29 May 1996) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a left wing-forward for club side [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Early life== Morrissey was born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]]. His brother, [[Dan Morrissey (hurler)|Dan Morrissey]], also plays for Ahane and the Limerick senior hurling team.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/dan-morrissey-wants-limerick-to-keep-hitting-high-notes-855632.html|title=Dan Morrissey wants Limerick to keep hitting high notes|date=17 July 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}} ==Playing career== ===University=== During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]], Morrissey was selected for the college's senior hurling team. On 24 February 2018, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal following UL's 2–21 to 2–15 defeat of [[Dublin City University]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0224/943259-ul-pull-away-to-claim-fitzgibbon-cup-glory/|title=UL pull away to claim Fitzgibbon Cup glory|date=29 February 2016|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}} ===Club=== Morrissey joined the [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, winning a championship medal in the minor grade in 2014. He later joined the club's senior team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} ===Inter-county=== ====Minor and under-21==== Morrissey first played for the Limerick minor hurling team at the age of seventeen. On 23 July 2013, he scored three points from play when Limerick won their first [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title in 29 years after a 1–20 to 4–08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in a replay of the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} Morrissey was eligible for the minor grade again the following year and won a second successive Munster Championship medal after a 0–24 to 0–18 second successive defeat of Waterford in a replay of the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}} On 7 September 2014, Morrissey was at full-forward for Limerick's 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-minors-savour-all-ireland-success-against-spirited-limerick-1.1920852|title=Kilkenny minors savour All-Ireland success against spirited Limerick|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 September 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} Morrissey subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team and '''Ronan Lynch''' (born 1996) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a left corner-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-boss-ryan-delighted-with-debutant-cian-lynch-678574.html|title= Limerick boss Ryan delighted with debutant Cian Lynch|date=25 May 2015|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=26 May 2015}}</ref>

Born in [[Limerick]], Lynch first played competitive hurling during his schooling at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]]. He arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of fifteen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team before later joining the under-21 side. He joined the senior team during the [[2015 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2015 championship]].

At club level Lynch plays with [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].

==Playing career==
===College===

During his schooling at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]], Lynch established himself as a key member of the senior hurling team. In 2014 he won a [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] medal following a 2–13 to 0–4 trouncing of Limerick rivals Scoil na Trionóide, Doon.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/ardscoil-ris-a-class-apart-in-derby-duel-259848.html|title=Ardscoil Rís a class apart in derby duel|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=24 February 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref>

===Minor and under-21===

Lynch was just fifteen-years-old when he first played for Limerick as a member of the minor team on 2 May 2012. He scored 0–11 on his debut in a 0–16 to 1–12 Munster quarter-final defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/treaty-super-sub-sinks-cork-192651.html|title=Treaty super sub sinks Cork|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 May 2012|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

In 2013 Lynch was at left wing-back as Limerick faced [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the provincial decider. As Waterford looked to be heading for victory, a last-minute goal from substitute [[Tom Morrissey (hurler)|Tom Morrissey]] ensured a 2–19 apiece draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/morrisseys-lastgasp-goal-ensures-limerick-live-to-fight-another-day-for-minor-crown-29419989.html|title=Morrissey's last-gasp goal ensures Limerick live to fight another day for minor crown|publisher=Irish Independent|date=15 July 2013|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref> The replay was also a close affair, however, [[Cian Lynch]]'s first-half stoppage time goal proved decisive as Limerick ended a 29-year wait for the title with a 1–20 to 4–8 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=24 July 2013|access-date=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref> It was Lynch's first [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.

Lynch was eligible for the minor grade once again in 2014, as Waterford faced the team in the Munster final for a second year in succession. Limerick looked all set to retain their title when leading their opponents by three points in added time, however, Waterford substitute [[Shane Ryan (hurler)|Shane Ryan]] struck for a dramatic late goal to send the game to a replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-sport/limerick-minors-must-replay-munster-final-1-6176001|title=Limerick minors must replay Munster final|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=13 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Colm|last=Kinsella}}</ref> The replay was also a close affair, however, Limerick pulled away in the end to secure a 0–24 to 0–18 victory and a second Munster medal for Lynch.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref> On 7 September 2014 Limerick faced [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland decider. A 2–5 haul from Kilkenny corner-forward [[John Walsh (Kilkenny hurler)|John Walsh]] ensured a 2–17 to 0–19 defeat for Lynch's side.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-minors-savour-all-ireland-success-against-spirited-limerick-1.1920852|title=Kilkenny minors savour All-Ireland success against spirited Limerick|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 September 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}}</ref>

{{Short description|Limerick hurler and manager}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code = Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | caption = | name = John Kiely | irish = Seán Ó Cadhla | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | occupation = | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]]
[[Galbally GAA|Galbally]] | cl_position = | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county_h = 1 | cl_county_f = 2 | colleges = [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] | fitz = 0 | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = Right corner-back | ic_years = 1994-1996 | ic_apps_points = 0 (0-00) | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 0 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = 14:55, 15 September 2016 | birth_date = | birth_place = [[Galbally, County Limerick|Galbally]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''John Kiely''' is an Irish [[List of hurling managers|hurling manager]] and former [[Selector_(sport)|selector]], [[Gaelic football]]er and [[Hurling|hurler]]. He has been manager of the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] since 2016.{{cite news|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/new-manager-john-kiely-says-managing-limerick-is-a-huge-honour-754556.html|title=New manager John Kiely says managing Limerick is "a huge honour"|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=14 September 2016|access-date=15 September 2016}} He is widely considered to be one of the greatest Hurling managers of all time.{{Cite web |last=266785760017516 |date=2026-07-20 |title=John Kiely is up there as hurling's all-time greatest manager after winning SIXTH All-Ireland title as Limerick gaffer |url=https://www.thesun.ie/sport/17322100/john-kiely-babs-keating-greatest-manager-all-ireland/ |access-date=2026-07-22 |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=2026-07-17 |title=John Kiely’s journey from ‘a bit of a hothead’ to all-time great is hailed by Richie McCarthy |url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa/john-kielys-journey-from-a-bit-of-a-hothead-to-all-time-great-is-hailed-by-richie-mccarthy/a/158813726.html |access-date=2026-07-22 |website=Irish Independent |language=en-IE}} Born in [[Galbally, County Limerick|Galbally]], [[County Limerick]], Kiely first played competitive hurling and Gaelic football in his youth. After beginning his club career at juvenile and underage levels, he later became a [[dual player]] at senior level with the [[Galbally GAA|Galbally]] and [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] teams. Kiely won a total of three championship medals across both codes. He was principal of [[The Abbey School (Tipperary)|The Abbey]], a secondary school in [[Tipperary (town)|Tipperary Town]] for 10 years, before taking up the role of deputy principal in 2023. He took a one-year career break from his role as deputy principal in 2024.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/john-kiely-signs-up-for-two-more-years-as-limerick-hurling-manager-along-with-coach-paul-kinnerk/a1453510882.html|title=John Kiely signs up for two more years as Limerick hurling manager along with coach Paul Kinnerk|date=11 September 2024|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=11 September 2024}}{{cite news |first=Stephen|last=Barry|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/proof-the-classroom-is-more-conducive-to-an-inter-county-career-858120.html|title=Proof the classroom is more conducive to an inter-county career|work=Irish Examiner|date=27 July 2018|quote=Two managers still standing are in education (John Meyler, a CIT lecturer, and John Kiely, principal of the Abbey School in Tipperary).}}{{cite web |url= https://www.tippmidwestradio.com/2023/09/26/tipp-towns-abbey-school-appoints-new-principal/ |title= Tipp Town's Abbey School Appoints New Principal |author= Tipp Mid West Radio |date= 26 September 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20231109114324/https://www.tippmidwestradio.com/2023/09/26/tipp-towns-abbey-school-appoints-new-principal/ |archive-date= 9 November 2023}} In October 2024, Kiely started to work at [[JP McManus]]' Martinstown Stud in Co. Limerick. While on a leave of absence from his vice-principal job at the Abbey School in Tipperary town.{{cite news |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41494103.html|title=Limerick hurling boss John Kiely enjoying new role working for JP McManus |work=Irish Examiner|date=11 October 2024|access-date=22 June 2025}}{{cite news|url=https://www.thesun.ie/sport/15057665/john-kiely-limerick-all-ireland-senior-hurling-championship/ |title='My mind was made up' – John Kiely reveals he planned Limerick stay before SHC heartbreak against Cork |work=Irish Sun|date=16 April 2025|access-date=22 June 2025}} ==Career== Kiely made his debut on the inter-county scene at the age of seventeen when he joined the Limerick minor hurling team. After little success in this grade he later joined the under-21 team, also without championship success. Kiely was a member of the extended Limerick panel in 1994 before later winning a [[Munster Senior Football Championship|Munster]] medal as a non-playing substitute in [[1996 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|1996]]. He later captained the Limerick senior football team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} ==Management and coaching career== ===Limerick intermediate manager=== After Limerick's 6-19 to 2-07 [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]] defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in 2009, Kiely was prompted to become involved in inter-county team management with Limerick. "I rang [County Board chairman] Liam Lenihan the next day to tell him I wanted to get involved and help out at any level."{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/kiely-s-quiet-revolution-leads-limerick-back-to-the-top-table-1.3578368|title=Kiely's quiet revolution leads Limerick back to the top table|publisher=Irish Times|date=28 July 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Malachy|last=Clerkin}} Kiely was later named as the new manager of the Limerick intermediate hurling team. In his first season with the team, Limerick were beaten by eventual [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] winners [[Cork GAA|Cork]] after extra-time in the semi-final.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/world/arid-10122960.html|title=Last-gasp Conway blast breaks Limerick hearts|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=21 June 2010|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} The following year, Kiely's side lost out by two points to eventual [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] champions [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the Munster final.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/clares-keane-edge-26751420.html|title=Clare's Keane edge|publisher=Irish Independent|date=14 July 2011|access-date=20 August 2018}} ===Limerick under-21 selector=== In 2011, Kiely combined his role as intermediate manager with that of a selector with [[Leo O'Connor (hurler)|Leo O'Connor]]'s Limerick under-21 team. On 3 August 2011, he was part of the management team that guided Limerick to a 4-20 to 1-27 extra-time defeat of Cork in the final of the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hannon-on-the-mark-to-edge-thriller-26758064.html|title=Hannon on the mark to edge thriller|date=4 August 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}} ===Limerick senior selector=== After [[John Allen (hurler)|John Allen]]'s appointment as manager of the Limerick senior team in October 2012, Kiely was chosen to be part of the new management team as a selector.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/allen-ratified-as-new-limerick-manager-524037.html|title=Allen ratified as new Limerick manager|date=12 October 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=20 August 2018}} His first season as a selector ended with Limerick failing to secure promotion from Division 1B of the [[National Hurling League]] before exiting the championship after a quarter-final defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]].{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/article/index/166016|title=HL 1B final: Banner comeback floors Treaty|date=7 April 2012|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=20 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-melt-in-12-minute-maelstrom-202475.html|title=Limerick melt in 12-minute maelstrom|date=30 July 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} Limerick once again failed to secure promotion from Division 1B in Kiely's second season as a selector.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dublin-return-to-hurling-s-top-table-at-limerick-s-expense-1.1351663|title=Dublin return to hurling's top table at Limerick's expense|date=6 April 2013|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Damian|last=Cullen}} On 14 July 2013, he was a selector when Limerick defeated Cork by 0-24 to 0-15 to win the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} The management team stepped down at the end of the season. ===Limerick under-21 manager=== On 18 September 2014, Kiely was appointed manager of the Limerick under-21 team in succession to [[Ciarán Carey]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/no-opposition-as-kiely-replaces-carey-as-limerick-u21-manager-287570.html|title=No opposition as Kiely replaces Carey as Limerick U21 manager|date=19 September 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Paul|last=Keane}} He subsequently guided the team to the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title after a 0-22 to 0-19 win over Clare in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=30 July 2018}} On 12 September 2015, Kiely was in charge when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0-26 to 1-07 in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} He ended the season by being named Manager of the Year by the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]].{{cite web|url=http://limerickgaa.ie/john-kiely-is-manager-of-the-year/|title=John Kiely is Manager of the Year|date=11 December 2015|publisher=Limerick GAA website|access-date=30 July 2018}} Kiely's second season as manager of the Limerick under-21 team ended with a 2-12 to 1-13 Munster semi-final defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/tipperary-limerick-munster-u21-2-2878788-Jul2016/|title=Tipperary's great hurling week continues as they defeat Limerick in Munster U21 semi-final|date=14 July 2016|publisher=The 42|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} ===Limerick senior manager=== Kiely was named as the new manager of the Limerick senior team after a meeting of the County Board on 14 September 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/john-kiely-installed-limerick-manager/|title=John Kiely installed as Limerick manager|date=13 September 2016|publisher=GAA website|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Cian|last=O'Connell}} In his first season in charge, Limerick reached the semi-finals of the National League, losing by 1-11 to 1-21 to eventual champions [[Galway GAA|Galway]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/galway-see-off-limerick-to-advance-to-division-1-final-785982.html|title=Galway see off Limerick to advance to Division 1 final|date=16 April 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018}} Kiely's side were later beaten by Clare in the Munster Championship, before exiting the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] following a three-point defeat by Kilkenny.{{cite web|url= http://www.the42.ie/clare-limerick-match-report-3416130-Jun2017/|title=Goals from O'Donnell and McGrath key as Clare reach first Munster hurling final since 2008|date=4 June 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=8 June 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/kilkenny-limerick-hurling-3474079-Jul2017/|title=Kilkenny survive late Limerick rally to return to winning ways on home soil|date=1 July 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=8 June 2017}}{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/john-kiely-limerick-hurling-9-5815421-Jul2022/|title= John Kiely: 'Nights when I was pacing the yard out the back, wondering, 'Am I the right man for this job?'|date=13 July 2022|work=The 42|accessdate=13 July 2022}} In his second season in charge, Kiely's side secured promotion to Division 1A of the National League after securing maximum points in their five group stage games.{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-promotion-division-1a-galway-hurling-all-ireland-champions-3897807-Mar2018/|title=Limerick return to top tier for first time since 2010 with defeat of All-Ireland champions|date=11 March 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=20 August 2018}} Limerick later narrowly missed out on a place in the Munster final, but their third-place finish in the new Munster Championship group stage allowed Limerick to qualify for the All-Ireland Championship.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/second-half-surge-crucial-as-clare-leapfrog-limerick-to-seal-munster-final-place-37019612.html|title=Second half surge crucial as Clare leapfrog Limerick to seal Munster final place|date=17 June 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Martin|last=Breheny}} Subsequent defeats of [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]], [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] and [[Cork GAA|Cork]] secured a place in the All-Ireland final. On 19 August 2018, Kiely guided Limerick to their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3-16 to 2-18 victory over Galway in the [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/i-said-it-after-the-game-this-is-not-the-end-its-the-beginning-john-kiely-on-the-future-of-limerick-hurling-863435.html |title ='I said it after the game, this is not the end. It's the beginning' - John Kiely on the future of Limerick hurling|date=20 August 2018|work=Irish Examiner|access-date=21 August 2018}} On 31 March 2019, Kiely guided Limerick to a first [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] appearance since [[2005 National Hurling League|2005]]. A 1-24 to 0-19 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] secured a first league title for Limerick since [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]]. In Munster, Limerick qualified for the Munster Final against Tipperary. The All Ireland Semi-Final saw Limerick face Kilkenny. Limerick were favourites but struggled as Kilkenny took a commanding lead and while Limerick fought back to reduce the lead to a point, they lost by the minimum and went out of the championship. Limerick were hotly tipped to win back the All-Ireland in 2020. When the championship started in October, having been postponed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Limerick retained their Munster title by defeating [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final. Victory over Galway put Kiely's team into a second [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|All-Ireland final]] in three years. Again they faced Waterford and went on to win on a scoreline of 0-30 to 0-19. This victory gave them back the All-Ireland crown and also ensured that Kiely's Limerick side went through all competitions in 2020 unbeaten.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/gaa-hurling-all-ireland-senior-championship/limerick-waterford/1739657/|title=LIMERICK 0-30 WATERFORD 0-19|date=13 December 2020|work=GAA.ie|accessdate= 11 May 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2020/1213/1184174-all-ireland-shc-final-limerick-v-waterford-build-up/|title=All-Ireland SHC final recap: Limerick 0-30 Waterford 0-19|date=13 December 2020|work=RTE Sport|accessdate= 11 May 2021}} In 2021, Limerick surrendered their league crown but went on to retain the Munster title following a dramatic comeback against [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the final, with Kiely's side coming back from ten points down to win by five. Victory over Waterford put Limerick into a second consecutive All-Ireland final. In the [[2021 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|All-Ireland final]] Limerick defeated Cork on a scoreline of 3-32 to 1-22. With that victory Limerick retained the All-Ireland for the first time in their history and marked the highest winning score ever achieved in an All-Ireland Hurling final.{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0822/1242236-limerick-crush-cork-to-claim-back-to-back-all-irelands/|title=Limerick crush Cork to claim back-to-back All-Irelands|publisher=[[RTÉ News and Current Affairs]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40364432.html|title=Record-breaking Limerick retain All-Ireland title after powerful win over Cork|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|first=John|last=Fogarty|date=22 August 2021|accessdate=22 August 2021}} 2022 saw Limerick set out to capture three-in-a-row. After going through the Munster round robin unbeaten, Limerick beat [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the Munster final after extra time. On 3 July, Limerick defeated Galway in the All-Ireland Semi-Final by 0-27 to 1-21 to get back to the final. [[2022 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|The final]] played on 18 July saw Limerick face Kilkenny. Limerick won the game by 1-31 to 2-26 to claim their fourth title in five years and their first ever three-in-a-row. 2023 saw Limerick try to equal Cork and Kilkenny's record by winning 4 in a row. From the start of the year, Limerick laid out their intentions by winning the League final against Kilkenny. On the 29th April, Limerick's unbeaten run in the Championship came to an end when Clare defeated them in The Munster Round Robin at the Gaelic Grounds by 1-24 to 2-20. However they met again in the Munster Final and Limerick turned the tables on them by winning by a single point, 1-23 to 1-22, giving Kiely's side a fifth Munster title in a row. After a win over Galway in the All Ireland Semi Final, Limerick faced Kilkenny in the final for the second year in a row. While Limerick struggled in the first half, they trailed by only a goal at half time. The second half saw Limerick take complete control as they outscored the Cats by 0-21 to 1-06, eventually winning by 0-30 to 2-15 to win the four in a row, becoming only the third team ever to accomplish it.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honors in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}{{cite news|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2022/0717/1310723-resilient-limerick-see-off-cats-to-claim-three-in-a-row/|title=Resilient Limerick see off Kilkenny to claim three-in-a-row|publisher=[[RTÉ News]]|first=Eoin|last=Ryan|date=17 July 2022|accessdate=17 July 2022}} In September 2024, Kiely signed on for another two years as Limerick manager.{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/0911/1469473-kiely-and-kinnerk-back-for-more-with-limerick/|title=John Kiely and Paul Kinnerk back for more with Limerick|date=11 September 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=11 September 2024}} On July 19th 2026, Kiely led Limerick to a 6th All-Ireland title since taking over in 2016, cementing both himself and the team as one of the greatest of all '''Andrew La Touche Cosgrave''' (born 1996) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a centre-back for club side [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==
===College===

La Touche Cosgrave first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Castletroy College]] in [[Limerick]]. Having played in every grade, he was at left wing-back on the college's senior team that contested the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/touche-of-class-steals-unlikely-win-for-castletroy-30927765.html|title='Touche' of class steals unlikely win for Castletroy|date=22 January 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=5 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

===University===

During his studies at the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]], La Touche Cosgrave was selected for the college's senior hurling team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/sigerson-fitzgibbon-cups/mary-i-remain-on-course-to-regain-independentie-fitzgibbon-cup-title-by-defeating-davy-fitzgeralds-lit-35480112.html|title=Mary I remain on course to regain Independent.ie Fitzgibbon Cup title by defeating Davy Fitzgerald's LIT|date=24 February 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

===Club===

La Touche Cosgrave joined the [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's top adult team. On 9 October 2016, he won a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Premier Intermediate Championship]] medal following a 1–17 to 2–11 defeat of [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] in the final.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

La Touche Cosgrave first played for the Limerick minor hurling team at the age of fifteen. On 23 July 2013, he was at centre-back when Limerick won their first [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title in 29 years after a 1–20 to 4–08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in a replay of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

La Touche Cosgrave was eligible for the minor grade again the following year and won a second successive Munster Championship medal after a 0–24 to 0-18 second successive defeat of Waterford in a replay of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref> On 7 September 2014, La Touche Cosgrave was at centre-back for Limerick's 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-minors-savour-all-ireland-success-against-spirited-limerick-1.1920852|title=Kilkenny minors savour All-Ireland success against spirited Limerick|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 September 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}}</ref>

La Touche Cosgrave subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal in his first season after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 12 September 2015, La Touche Cosgrave was introduced as a substitute for [[Pat Ryan (Limerick hurler)|Pat Ryan]] when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0–26 to 1–07 in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

After surrendering their titles in 2016, La Touche Cosgrave won a second Munster Championship medal after a 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the 2017 final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 9 September 2017, he came on as a substitute for [[Tom Morrissey (hurler)|Tom Morrissey]] in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Under-25====

In 2017, La Touche Cosgrave joined the Limerick under-25 hurling team. On 18 June 2017, he was at centre-back when Limerick defeated [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] by 4–12 to 1–19 to win the [[Munster Under-25 Reserve Hurling Competition|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-waterford-u25-3450745-Jun2017/|title=Oisin O'Reilly hat-trick leads Limerick past Waterford to Munster U25 reserves hurling crown|date=18 June 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

====Senior====

La Touche Cosgrave first played for the Limerick senior team in the pre-season [[Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]] against Clare on 18 January 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=265143|title=Team news: Treaty make thirteen changes|date=18 January 2017|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=21 August 2017|first=|last=}}</ref> He later made his first appearance in the [[National Hurling League]], scoring a point in a 6–21 to 3–08 defeat of [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-kerry-hurling-1b-match-report-3247973-Feb2017/|title=Ronan Lynch hits remarkable 3-11 tally as Limerick demolish Kerry|date=19 February 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> La Touche Cosgrave was later dropped from the panel prior to the start of the championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-john-kiely-3357178-Apr2017/|title=Limerick cut 7 players from panel ahead of hurling championship campaign|date=25 April 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=21 August 2017|first=|last=}}</ref>

La Touch Cosgrave rejoined the Limerick senior panel in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-panel-john-kiely-3700398-Nov2017/|title=Downes back from cruciate, Reidy back from Kildare and U21 winners added to Limerick panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=21 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, he was a member of the extended panel when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

'''Daniel Morrissey''' (born 20 April 1993) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a left wing-back for club side [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Early life==

Morrissey was born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]]. His brother, [[Tom Morrissey (hurler)|Tom Morrissey]], also plays for Ahane and the Limerick senior hurling team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/dan-morrissey-wants-limerick-to-keep-hitting-high-notes-855632.html|title=Dan Morrissey wants Limerick to keep hitting high notes|date=17 July 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===University===

During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]], Morrissey was selected for the college's senior hurling team. On 11 March 2015, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal as UL defeated the [[Waterford IT GAA|Waterford Institute of Technology]] by 2–18 to 1–14 in a replay of the final at [[Páirc Uí Rinn]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ul-crowned-the-independentie-fitzgibbon-cup-champions-after-replay-win-over-wit-31059883.html|title=UL crowned the Independent.ie Fitzgibbon Cup champions after replay win over WIT|date=11 March 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Cóilín|last=Duffy}}</ref>

===Club===

Morrissey joined the [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's senior team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

Morrissey first played for Limerick at minor level. He made his first appearance on 25 June 2010 in a 1–17 to 2–12 defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/property/arid-10123480.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130824213725/http://www.irishexaminer.com/archives/2010/0626/world/arthurs-accuracy-the-catalyst-as-clare-march-on-123480.html|url-status=live|archive-date=24 August 2013|title=Arthur's accuracy the catalyst as Clare march on|date=26 June 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> Morrissey was eligible for the minor grade again in 2011, however, his season ended with a 4–17 to 3–15 defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/bennett-edges-deise-home-in-epic-battle-159057.html|title=Bennett edges Déise home in epic battle|date=27 June 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=John|last=Murphy}}</ref>

Morrissey subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team. He made his first appearance on 18 July 2012 in a 1–16 to 1–11 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20201283.html|title=Maher ends Treaty defence|date=19 July 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=6 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> Morrissey's three successive seasons with the team ended without success.

====Senior====

Morrissey made his senior debut for Limerick on 23 February 2014, replacing [[Gavin O'Mahony]] for the final 12 minutes of a [[National Hurling League]] game against [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] at the [[Gaelic Grounds]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limericks-lethal-forwards-run-riot-259822.html|title=Limerick's lethal forwards run riot|date=24 February 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=6 August 2018|first=Brendan|last=Buckley}}</ref> He was an unused substitute for the subsequent championship campaign.

On 12 March 2017, Morrissey scored his first point for Limerick in a 6–33 to 1–19 defeat of [[Laois GAA|Laois]] in the National League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/hegarty-wreaks-havoc-in-ruthless-limericks-demolition-job-35522460.html|title=Hegarty wreaks havoc in ruthless Limerick's demolition job|date=12 March 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=6 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

Morrissey was named [[man of the match]], beating [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]'s [[Eoin Murphy (Kilkenny hurler)|Eoin Murphy]] and his brother Tom, following Limerick's [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland quarter-final]] defeat of Kilkenny on 15 July 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/all-ireland-shc-hurling-man-of-the-match-winners-4129659-Jul2018/|title=Do you agree with the All-Ireland SHC quarter-final man-of-the-match winners?|date=16 July 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=6 August 2018|first=Emma|last=Duffy}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Morrissey was at left wing-back when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> He ended the season by winning an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=13 September 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/1101/1008052-treaty-lead-the-way-with-six-hurling-all-stars/|title= Treaty lead the way with six hurling All-Stars|date=2 November 2018|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=4 November 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Morrissey was selected at left wing-back for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Morrissey won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal at left wing-back following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 25 October 2020, Morrissey won a second successive National League medal after Limerick's 0–36 to 1–23 win over Clare in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> Later that season he claimed a second successive Munster Championship medal after lining out at full-back in the 0–25 to 0–21 [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]] defeat of Waterford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford for historic Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref>

Morrissey won an [[GAA GPA All Stars Awards|All Star]] in 2020, 2023 and 2024.<ref>{{cite news|title=Conroy and O'Donnell scoop Player of the Year awards|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/football/2024/1101/1478693-conroy-and-odonnell-scoop-player-of-the-year-awards/|work=[[RTÉ News]]|date=1 November 2024|access-date=2 November 2024}}</ref>

He usually lines out as a left corner-forward. Lyons is a former member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]].{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-championship-squad-3942332-Apr2018/|title=Lynch not part of Limerick's 36-man championship panel as Kiely shows his hand|date=5 April 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=18 August 2018|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}} ==Playing career== ===Castletroy College=== Lyons first came to prominence as a hurler with [[Castletroy College]] in [[Limerick]]. Having played in every grade, he was at midfield on the college's senior team that contested the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/14-man-castletroy-prevail-296547.html|title=14-man Castletroy prevail|date=6 November 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=5 July 2018|first=Therese|last=O'Callaghan}} ===Limerick Institute of Technology=== During his studies at the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]], La Touche Cosgrave was selected for the college's senior hurling team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/ul-fitzgibbon-cup-hurling-3219563-Feb2017/|title=Tipp's McGrath and Waterford's Bennett both hit 1-5 as UL reach Fitzgibbon Cup last eight|date=2 February 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Eoin|last=Brennan}} ===Monaleen=== Lyons joined the [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's top adult team. On 9 October 2016, he won a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Premier Intermediate Championship]] medal following a 1–17 to 2–11 defeat of [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] in the final. ===Limerick=== ====Minor and under-21==== Lyons first played for the Limerick minor hurling team at the age of seventeen. '''James McCarthy''' (15 December 1917 – 12 April 1982) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] and medical doctor.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/My_Beautiful_Obsession_Chasing_the_Kerry/-wiWDwAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22Jim+McCarthy%22+(hurler)&pg=PT52&printsec=frontcover|title=
My Beautiful Obsession - Chasing the Kerry Dream|first= Weeshie|last=Fogarty|year= 2012|isbn=9781848899827|publisher=Weeshie Fogarty}}</ref> His career included two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] success with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==

McCarthy first played hurling for the [[Feenagh-Kilmeedy GAA|Feenagh]] junior team as an 11-year-old before gaining further experience as a boarder at [[Rockwell College]]. Here he lined out in back-to-back [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] finals in 1934 and 1935 before winning an All-Ireland medal as part of a star-studded Munster Colleges team that also featured [[Jack Lynch]], [[John Keane (hurler)|John Keane]] and [[Connie Buckley]]. As a medical student at [[University College Dublin]], McCarthy was involved in several [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] campaigns and claimed a winners' medal in 1941. After lining out at midfield in the early part of his career he switched to being a goalkeeper on the Limerick junior team that won the [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|1935 All-Ireland Junior Championship]]. McCarthy's performances at junior level earned at immediate call-up to the Limerick senior team with whom he won [[National Hurling League|National League]], [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] and [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] honours in his debut season in 1936. He won a further two National League medals over the course of the following two seasons before winning a [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick Junior Championship]] with Feenagh in 1938. McCarthy won a second set of Munster and All-Ireland medals as a full member of the starting fifteen in [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1940|1940]]. He also earned inclusion on the [[Munster GAA|Munster inter-provincial team]] and won back-to-back [[Railway Cup]] medals in [[1942 Railway Cup Hurling Championship|1942]] and [[1943 Railway Cup Hurling Championship|1943]].{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

'''Patrick Mackey''' (19 January 1920 – 19 February 1941) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]]. His brief career included [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] success with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==

Mackey first played [[hurling]] for the [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] club, winning one [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick County Championship]] medal. The [[1939 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] success saw Mackey drafted onto the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. In his one full season with the team, he won [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] honours as a substitute in the [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1940 All-Ireland Hurling Championship]], having earlier won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Hurling Championship]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/columnists/arid-20473132.html|title=Mackey, Limerick, and the decade when Hollywood documented the glories of hurling for US cinema|date=17 August 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=14 August 2020|first=Paul|last=Rouse}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==

Mackey was born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], the fifth of eight children of [[John Mackey (Tyler)|John]] and Mary (née Carroll). His father, nicknamed Tyler, was a former [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|captain of the Limerick senior hurling team]] who won two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] titles. Mackey's brothers, [[Mick Mackey|Mick]] and [[John Mackey (hurler)|John]], also hurled with Limerick. All three Mackey brothers were member of Limerick's [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1940 All-Ireland Championship]]-winning team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/38823|title=Death of James Mackey|date=30 March 2003|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=14 August 2020}}</ref>

Mackey joined the [[Irish Army]] where he held the rank of corporal. He died on 19 February 1941 from [[uremia]] at the age of 21.{{citation needed|date=January 2021}}

'''Thomas P. McGarry''' (1937 – 2 December 2021) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]], [[Association football|football]]er and [[rugby union]] player. An all-round sportsman he played with a number of teams in all codes, including the [[Limerick senior hurling team]], [[Cork Celtic]] and [[Young Munster]].

==Career==

McGarry first came to sporting prominence as a hurler. A member of the [[Treaty Sarsfields GAA|Treaty Sarsfields]] club, he also represented [[CBS Sexton Street]] in the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] while also enjoying a two-year spell with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick minor hurling team]]. McGarry made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior]] debut in 1956, however, his seven-year career coincided with a barren spell for Limerick.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/legends-of-the-ash-1.139525?mode=sample&auth-failed=1&pw-origin=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.irishtimes.com%2Fsport%2Flegends-of-the-ash-1.139525|title=Legends Of The Ash|publisher=Irish Times|date=20 December 1997|access-date=4 December 2021|first=|last=}}</ref> In spite of this he earned selection on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] team and won five [[Railway Cup]] medals in a six-year period.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=4 December 2021|first=|last=}}</ref> McGarry also played rugby and association football at a high level. Playing in the centre, he captained [[Young Munster]] when they played [[Garryowen Football Club|Garryowen]] in the [[Munster Senior Cup (rugby union)|1970-71 Munster Senior Cup final]]. McGarry also played [[League of Ireland]] soccer with [[Limerick F.C.]] and [[Cork Celtic]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/702917/sadness-at-the-passing-of-one-of-limerick-s-finest-sporting-all-rounders-tom-mcgarry.html|title=Sadness at the passing of one of Limerick's finest sporting all-rounders Tom McGarry|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=2 December 2021|access-date=4 December 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Death==

McGarry died on 2 December 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40758156.html|title=Tom McGarry, Railway Cup winner, League of Ireland player and Young Munster captain, dies|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=2 December 2021|access-date=4 December 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

At club level, he played with [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Mulcahy played hurling at all grades as a student at John the Baptist Community School in [[Hospital, County Limerick|Hospital]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Hospital|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=8 November 1997|access-date=9 May 2025|first=|last=}} He later studied at [[Limerick Institute of Technology]] and lined out with LIT in the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/82613|title=Limerick come of age|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=29 August 2007|access-date=9 May 2025|first=|last=}} At club level, Mulcahy first played for [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]] as a [[dual player]] in the juvenile and underage grades, before progressing to adult level. He was at midfield when Knockainey claimed the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] title in 2001 after a 2–13 to 1–09 win over [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret]] in a final replay.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=47 year wait over for Knockainey|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=29 October 2001|access-date=9 May 2025|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Mulcahy first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 1999. He subsequently progressed to the under-21 team and won three consecutive [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medals between 2000 and 2002.{{cite [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Patrick Kirby''' (born 1985) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Kirby played hurling at all grades as a student at John the Baptist Community School in [[Hospital, County Limerick|Hospital]]. He later transferred to [[St Colman's College, Fermoy|St Colman's college]] in [[Fermoy]] and won back-to-back [[Dr Harty Cup]] titles in 2002 and 2003.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/our-ladys-well-beaten/27447106.html|title=Our Ladys well beaten|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 March 2002|access-date=17 February 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10094977.html|title=Historic win for St Colman’s|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=31 March 2003|access-date=17 February 2018|first=Brendan|last=Larkin}} Kirby also won an [[Dr Croke Cup|All-Ireland Colleges SHC]] medal following an 0–11 to 2–4 win over [[St Kieran's College]] in the [[2002 Croke Cup#Final|2002 All-Ireland colleges final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/st-colmans-resolve-wins-battle-of-nerves/26053132.html|title=St Colman's resolve wins battle of nerves|publisher=Irish Independent|date=29 April 2002|access-date=26 June 2023|first=John|last=Harrington}} At club level, Kirby first played for [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]] as a [[dual player]] in the juvenile and underage grades, before progressing to adult level. At just 16-years-old, he wasp art of the team when Knockainey claimed the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] title in 2001 after a 2–13 to 1–9 win over [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret]] in a final replay.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=47 year wait over for Knockainey|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=29 October 2001|access-date=9 May 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gifted-teenagers-too-good-to-ignore-1.360952|title=Gifted teenagers too good to ignore|publisher=Irish Times|date=31 May 2003|access-date=9 May 2025}} Kirby first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a three-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145462/Limerick-minor-hurlers---trying.html|title=Limerick minor hurlers - trying since 1985|publisher=Limerick Live|date=7 September 2014|access-date=9 May 2025}} He was just 17 and in his second year of the minor grade when he was drafted onto the Limerick under-21 team in 2002. Kirby won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] medal that year before later collecting an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after the 3–17 to 0–8 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2002 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|2002 All-Ireland under-21 final]].{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-make-history-26034660.html|title=Limerick make history|date=16 September 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=13 October 2013|first=Martin|last=Breheny}} He made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in 2003 and made a number of appearances before leaving the panel in 2006.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gifted-teenagers-too-good-to-ignore-1.360952|title=Gifted teenagers too good to ignore|publisher=Irish Times|date=31 May 2003|access-date=9 May 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/82613|title=Limerick come of age|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=29 August 2007|access-date=9 May 2025}} ==Honours== ;St Colman's College *[[Dr Croke Cup]]: [[2002 Croke Cup|2002]] *[[Dr Harty Cup]]: [[2001–02 Harty Cup|2002]], [[2002–03 Harty Cup|2003]] ;Knockainey *[[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]]: 2001 ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[2002 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|2002]] *[[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[2002 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2002]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title= Patrick Kirby navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Under 21 Team 2002}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kirby, Patrick}} [[Category:1985 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Dual players]] [[Category:Knockainey Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:Knockainey hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:21st-century Irish sportsmen]]

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Clement Smith''' (born 1975) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Smith played hurling at all grades as a student at [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]]. He was part of the school's senior team that won the [[Dr Harty Cup]] title in 1993, after beating [[St Flannan's College]] by 5–05 to 1–12 in the final.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=O'Donnell Abú for Sexton's|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=22 March 1993|access-date=26 June 2023|first=|last=}} At club level, Smith first played for [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] in the juvenile and underage grades, before progressing to adult level. He won his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medal in 1998, before [[Captain (sport)|captaining]] the team when they retained the title in 1999.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/memories-of-mackey-as-ahane-end-famine-26174934.html|title=Memories of Mackey as Ahane end famine|publisher=Irish Independent|date=21 September 1998|access-date=15 October 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/tempers-flare-as-ahane-win-26134015.html|title=Tempers flare as Ahane win|publisher=Irish Independent|date=4 October 1999|access-date=15 October 2018}} Smith won a third and final Limerick SHC title when, in 2004, Ahane beat [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] by 1–11 to 0–13 in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/late-moran-point-shatters-garryspillane-25892336.html|title=Late Moran point shatters Garryspillane|publisher=Irish Independent|date=11 October 2004|access-date=31 October 2018}} Smith first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 1993.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145462/Limerick-minor-hurlers---trying.html|title=Limerick minor hurlers - trying since 1985|publisher=Limerick Live|date=7 September 2014|access-date=9 May 2025|first=|last=}} He later spent one season with the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]] in 1996. Smith was drafted onto the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in 1997 and was part of Limerick's [[National Hurling League]]-winning panel that year.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/945696/limerick-county-final-day-to-honour-25th-anniversary-of-1997-hurling-league-title-victory.html|title=Limerick county final day to honour 25th anniversary of 1997 hurling league title victory|publisher=Limerick Live|date=30 October 2022|access-date=9 May 2025|first=|last=}} He was appointed captain of the team for the 2000 season. Smith retired from inter-county hurling in March 2005.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30195635.html|title=Limerick's Smith to retire from inter-county hurling|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=29 March 2005|access-date=31 October 2018}} ==Honours== ;Limerick CBS *[[Dr Harty Cup]]: 1993 ;Ahane *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1998 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1998]], [[1999 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1999]], [[2004 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2004]] ;Limerick *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1997 National Hurling League|1997]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kirby, Patrick}} [[Category:1975 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Ahane hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:21st-century Irish sportsmen]]

'''Darragh Langan''' (born 2005) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he plays with [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Career==

Fitzgerald was educated at [[Castletroy College]] in [[Limerick]] and lined out in all grades of hurling during his time there. He was a Munster PPS SBHC runners-up in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/extra-time-heartbreak-for-limericks-castletroy-college-in-munster-final/|title=Extra-time heartbreak for Limerick’s Castletroy College in Munster final|publisher=Sporting Limerick|date=|accessdate=18 July 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Langan won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal with the [[University of Limerick]] in 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/2015230/limerick-stars-shine-as-clinical-ul-see-off-local-rivals-mary-immaculate-college-in-fitzgibbon-cup-final.html|title=Limerick stars shine as clinical UL see off local rivals Mary Immaculate College in Fitzgibbon Cup final|publisher=Limerick Live|date=13 February 2026|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> At club level, he first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] before progressing to adult level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41294809.html|title=Archer and Lynch lead Mungret St Paul's to more silverware|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 December 2023|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

Langan first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as [[Captain (sport)|captain]] of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/electric-ireland-munster-mhc-limerick-and-clare-cruise-into-quarter-finals/41567807.html|title=Electric Ireland Munster MHC: Limerick and Clare cruise into quarter-finals|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 April 2022|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He later spent three seasons with the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20 team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/all-ireland-winner-included-as-limericl-reveal-u20-hurling-squad-for-2023-championship/|title=All-Ireland winner included as Limerick reveal U20 Hurling Squad for 2023 Championship|publisher=Sporting Limerick|date=14 March 2023|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> Langan made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in a[[National Hurling League]] game against [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] in February 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.westmeathexaminer.ie/2024/02/12/heroic-hurlers-just-fall-short-against-mighty-limerick/|title=Heroic hurlers just fall short against mighty Limerick|publisher=Westmeath Examiner|date=12 February 2024|accessdate=4 April 2026|first=|last=}}</ref> He was a substitute for Limerick's National League and [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] title wins in 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/event/2026-allianz-hurling-league-division-1a-final-limerick-v-cork/|title=2026 Allianz Hurling League Division 1A Final – Limerick 1-27 Cork 1-21|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=5 April 2026|accessdate=8 April 2026|first=|last=}}</ref>

'''Brian Murray''' (born 6 September 1984 in [[Patrickswell]], [[County Limerick]]) is an Irish sportsperson.  He plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and was a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team from 2006 until 2009.

==Playing career==

===Club===

Murray plays his club hurling with the famous [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] club just outside Limerick city.  He was born into a family that had a strong association with hurling.  His father, [[Terence Murray (referee)|Terence Murray]], was also a member of the Patrickswell club and refereed the 1987 and 1993 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship finals between [[Galway GAA|Galway]] and [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]].  After enjoying little success as minor or under-21 levels he subsequently joined the club's senior team.  After beginning as an outfield player Murray was later chosen as goalkeeper on the team and has remained in that position since 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patrickswellgaa.com/archive.htm |title=Archive |publisher=[[Patrickswell GAA]] |accessdate=1 December 2008 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512001103/http://www.patrickswellgaa.com/archive.htm |archivedate=12 May 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patrickswellgaa.com/senior.htm |title=Senior |publisher=[[Patrickswell GAA]] |accessdate=1 December 2008 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080716133405/http://www.patrickswellgaa.com/senior.htm |archivedate=16 July 2008 |url-status=dead |df=dmy }}</ref> He played in his first senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county final]] in 2006, however, victory went to [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]] on that occasion.

===Inter-county===

Murray first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team in 2005.  He lined out in a challenge game against [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in late 2005, a game which Limerick won with Murray keeping a clean sheet as goalkeeper.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=54103|title=Limerick end Tipp's good start|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=24 November 2005|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> He impressed in that game and made his competitive debut against the same opposition in a [[National Hurling League]] game in early 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=56728|title=Four to make debuts for Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=16 February 2006|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> Murray remained as the first-choice goalkeeper for all but one game of the National League.  The team remained unbeaten and qualified for the final against Kilkenny.  It was an unhappy day for Limerick as 'the Cats' won the day by 3–11 0–14.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/2006/0430/kilkenny.html|title=Kilkenny claim league title in Thurles|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=30 April 2006|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> Murray's performances were so impressive that he edged out [[Timmy Houlihan]] as the regular Limerick goalkeeper for the championship.  He made his debut in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] championship against Tipperary, however, Limerick's championship losing streak continued and they were defeated.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=60758|title=Kelly inspires Tipp to victory|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=14 May 2006|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> After moving successfully through the qualifier system Murray's side later played defending champions [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the All-Ireland quarter-final.  Although the team only lost by a point it was a game that Limerick could easily have won.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=64090|title=Cork scrape past Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=22 July 2006|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref>

In 2007 Limerick faced near neighbours Tipperary in the semi-final of the Munster championship.  That game ended in a draw with both sides scoring 1–19.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=78545|title=Tipp and Limerick in thrilling draw|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=10 June 2007|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> The replay saw Limerick in arrears by ten points at half-time, however, Murray's side rallied to level the game at the end of normal time.  A period of extra time failed to separate the sides and a score line of 1–24 to 2–21 resulted in a second replay.  Once again, Limerick looked vulnerable at times during the game, however, they grinded out a victory with a score line of 0–22 to 2–13.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=79318|title=Third time lucky for Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=24 June 2007|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> It was Limerick's first win in the Munster championship since 2001. Murray later lined out against [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the Munster final, however, they were defeated on a score line of 3–17 to 1–14.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=80125|title=Limerick haunted by Dan the man|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=8 July 2007|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> These two sides later met again in the All-Ireland semi-final, however, manager [[Richie Bennis]] had done his homework and masterminded a surprise 5–11 to 2–15 victory over the Munster champions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=81789|title=All-Ireland SHC semi-final: Goal-den Limerick stun Waterford|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=12 August 2007|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> This victory allowed Murray's side to play Kilkenny in the championship decider.  Unfortunately, Limerick got off to a bad start with Murray letting in two goals by [[Eddie Brennan]] and [[Henry Shefflin]] in the first ten minutes.  Limerick fought back, however, 'the Cats', however, went on to win the game by six points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2007/0903/tomamccarthy.html |title=RTÉ Sport: Kilkenny 2–19 Limerick 1–15, by Tomás McCarthy |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=3 September 2007 |accessdate=17 September 2008 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090915213955/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2007/0903/tomamccarthy.html |archivedate=15 September 2009 }}</ref> In spite of this loss Murray was later presented with his first [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award, marking him out as the best goalkeeper in the championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/hurlingallstars2007.html |title=Hurling All Stars 2007 |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=19 October 2007 |accessdate=1 December 2008 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080331100601/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/hurlingallstars2007.html |archivedate=31 March 2008 }}</ref>

After the highs of the previous year, 2008 proved to be a difficult year for the Limerick hurlers.  The team were trounced by 4–12 to 1–16 in opening game of the championship by [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=97023|title=Munster SHC: Banner goals see off Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=22 June 2008|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> The newly structured qualifier system pitted Murray's side against [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in a must-win game.  Limerick, however, were out of sorts as Murray left in three goals leading to a 3–19 to 0–18 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=98081|title=All-Ireland SHC: Bergin guns down Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=12 July 2008|accessdate=1 December 2008}}</ref> Limerick's involvement in the championship came to an end following this trouncing.

In 2009 [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]] took over as Limerick manager.  After a poor showing in the National League, Limerick's first championship assignment was a Munster semi-final showdown with Waterford.  That game, described by many pundits as the worst game in the history of the provincial championship, ended in a draw.  The replay was a big improvement, however, Murray ended up on the losing side by 0–25 to 0–17.  Limerick later manoeuvred through the qualifiers, narrowly defeating [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]], [[Laois GAA|Laois]] and [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]].  It was the first time that Limerick secured three championship victories in-a-row since 1996.  In the game against 'the Dubs' Murray was brought all the way up the field to convert a penalty.  A four-point victory allowed Limerick to advance to the All-Ireland semi-final against Tipperary.

===Inter-provincial===

Murray has also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the [[Railway Cup]] inter-provincial competition.  He captured a winners medal in this competition in 2007 as Munster defeated [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/railwaycuphurling.html |title=Munster Railway Cup Hurling Teams |publisher=[[Munster GAA]] |accessdate=1 December 2008 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719201124/http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/railwaycuphurling.html |archivedate=19 July 2008 |url-status=dead |df=dmy }}</ref>
