'''Mike O'Brien''' (born 1978) is an [[Republic of Ireland|Irish]] sportsperson.  He plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Glenroe GAA|Glenroe]] and with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team.

==Early & private life==

Mike O'Brien was born in [[Glenroe, County Limerick|Glenroe]], [[County Limerick]] in 1978.  He was educated locally at Glenroe NS and went on to complete a law degree at Trinity College in the 1990s, playing both Sigerson and Fitzgibbon Cup. He returned home to the land following the completion of his degree and is now a farmer by profession.<ref name="O'Flynn" />

==Playing career==
===Club===

O'Brien plays his club [[hurling]] with his local [[Glenroe GAA|Glenroe]] club and has enjoyed some success.  Although not a senior club O'Brien has won a junior county title.

===Inter-county===

O'Brien first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] intermediate hurling team.  He won both Munster and [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals at this level in 1998.  As a result of this O'Brien joined the county senior team and made his debut in an Oireachtas game against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in October 1998.  Most of the next decade proved to be disappointing for Limerick and for O'Brien.  A victory over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] in 2001 was Limerick's last provincial win until a defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] following a three-game saga in 2007.  O'Brien played in that year's Munster final, however, victory went to [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] on that occasion. He and eleven other teammates were cut in October 2009, ending a twelve-year career with the team.<ref name="O'Flynn">{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20115554.html|title=O'Brien rages at backing for McCarthy|last=O'Flynn|first=Diarmuid|date=26 March 2010|work=[[Irish Examiner]]|accessdate=20 November 2010}}</ref>

'''James O'Brien''' (1945 – 19 August 2020) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he played as a centre-back for [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]] and was the left corner-back on the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] that won the [[1973 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1973 All-Ireland Championship]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/bennis-recalls-the-heroes-of-73-231789.html|title=Bennis recalls the heroes of ’73|date=20 May 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=26 December 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

O'Brien's skill was recognised at an early age when he won a South Limerick school's medal with Bruree National School, before an unrewarding spell at [[C.B.S. Charleville|Rathluirc CBS]]. His career at club level with [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]] spanned three decades.

O'Brien won a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal with the Limerick minor hurling team in 1963, before being subsequently selected for the Limerick under-21 and junior teams. He made his first appearance for the Limerick senior hurling team during the [[1966-67 National Hurling League|1966-67 National League]] and enjoyed his greatest successes as a defender over the following decade. In 1973 O'Brien became the first Bruree clubman to win an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] medal, having earlier won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] and [[National Hurling League]] titles.

'''Conor Matthew O'Donovan''' (born 7 February 1962<ref>{{cite news|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=The cream of the Premier|publisher=Kilkenny People|date=30 August 1991|accessdate=12 August 2022|first=|last=}}</ref>) is an Irish retired [[hurling|hurler]]. His [[National Hurling League|league]] and [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] career with the [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] senior team lasted seven seasons from 1984 to 1991.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/more-than-matter-of-civic-pride-for-thurles-and-nenagh-361140.html|title=More than matter of civic pride for Thurles and Nenagh|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=24 October 2015|accessdate=27 March 2018|first=Larry|last=Ryan}}</ref>

Born in [[Effin]], [[County Limerick]], O'Donovan was raised in a strong hurling family. His uncle, [[Terry Moloney (hurler)|Terry Moloney]], was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up with Tipperary in 1960.

O'Donovan first played competitive hurling with the [[Effin GAA|Effin]] club at juvenile and underage levels. After transferring to the [[Nenagh Éire Óg GAA|Nenagh Éire Óg]] club, he immediately became a member of the club's senior team. The highlight of his club career came in 1995 when he won a [[Tipperary Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] medal as captain.

O'Donovan made his debut on the inter-county scene when he was selected for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] minor team. He enjoyed one championship season with the minor team before subsequently joining the Tipperary under-21 team. O'Donovan later joined the Tipperary senior team, making his debut during the [[1984-85 National Hurling League|1984-85 league]]. Over the course of the following six seasons he enjoyed much success, culminating with the winning of an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals in 1989 and 1990. O'Donovan also won four [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and one [[National Hurling League|National League]] medal.

After being chosen on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team for the first time in 1987, O'Donovan was an automatic choice on the starting fifteen for the following three years. He ended his career without a [[Railway Cup]] medal.

'''Michael Nash''' (born 1965) is an Irish retired [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Career==

Nash played hurling at all grades as a secondary school student at [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/the-unsung-heroes-behind-limerick-s-hurling-revolution|title=The unsung heroes behind Limerick's hurling revolution|publisher=GAA website|date=13 September 2022|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> At club level, he played hurling and [[Gaelic football]] with [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]]. Nash won consecutive Limerick U21FC titles in 1985 and 1986.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Liberties facile win|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=23 November 1985|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Finn shines in thrilling final|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=13 December 1986|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

At inter-county level, Nash joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] during the [[1987–88 National Hurling League|1987–88 National League]]. He was on and off the team over the next few years but made a permanent return in 1993. Nash won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals in 1994 and 1996, however, Limerick faced subsequent All-Ireland final defeats by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40370429.html|title=A player-by-player guide to Wexford's All-Ireland 25 years on: 'We laughed as much as we hurled'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=1 September 2021|access-date=2 January 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He added a [[National Hurling League]] medal to his collection in 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/945696/limerick-county-final-day-to-honour-25th-anniversary-of-1997-hurling-league-title-victory.html|title=Limerick county final day to honour 25th anniversary of 1997 hurling league title victory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 October 2022|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Nash being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won a [[Railway Cup]] medals in 1995 after a one-point win over [[Ulster GAA|Ulster]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Personal life==

His brother, [[Declan Nash]], played alongside him during Limerick's Munster SHC successes in 1994 and 1996.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/1253886/family-ties-continue-to-drive-limerick-hurling-team.html|title=Family ties continue to drive Limerick hurling team|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 July 2023|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> His nephew, [[Anthony Nash (hurler)|Anthony Nash]], lined out in goal with the [[Cork senior hurling team]] and won four Munster SHC medals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/200254|title=Nash's Limerick family ties|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=4 September 2013|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

'''Declan Nash''' (born 10 July 1966) is an Irish [[hurling]] selector and former player. At club level, he played with [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==

Nash played hurling at all grades as a student at [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]]. He was part of the school's senior team that lost to [[St Finbarr's College, Farranferris|St Finbarr's College]] in the final of the [[Dr Harty Cup]] in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Farna turn it on in second half|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=16 April 1984|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> At club level, Nash played hurling and [[Gaelic football]] with [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]]. He won consecutive Limerick U21FC titles in 1985 and 1986.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Liberties facile win|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=23 November 1985|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Finn shines in thrilling final|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=13 December 1986|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

At inter-county level, Nash first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick’s last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He progressed to the under-21 team and won consecutive [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] titles, before claiming an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after a 2-15 to 3-06 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|1987 final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/109109/Limerick-s-first-All-Ireland-U.html|title=Limerick’s first All Ireland U-21 hurling title in 1987|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 September 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Nash joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] during the [[1987–88 National Hurling League|1987–88 National League]]. It was in that competition that he collected his first silverware when Limerick claimed the league title in 1992.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Nash won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals in 1994 and 1996, however, Limerick faced subsequent All-Ireland final defeats by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40370429.html|title=A player-by-player guide to Wexford's All-Ireland 25 years on: 'We laughed as much as we hurled'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=1 September 2021|access-date=2 January 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He added a second National League medal to his collection in 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/945696/limerick-county-final-day-to-honour-25th-anniversary-of-1997-hurling-league-title-victory.html|title=Limerick county final day to honour 25th anniversary of 1997 hurling league title victory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 October 2022|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Nash being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won consecutive [[Railway Cup]] medals in 1995 and 1996.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Management career==

Nash served as a selector during [[Pad Joe Whelehan]]'s term as manager of the Limerick senior hurling team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/39044|title=Padjoe shakes up Limerick panel|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=22 October 2004|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> His tenure as part of the management team saw him resign twice from the role in the space of a few months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/limerick-selectors-to-stay-on-1.420260|title=Limerick selectors to stay on|publisher=Irish Times|date=4 March 2005|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10071371.html|title=Limerick selector Nash quits before Kilkenny clash|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 July 2005|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Personal life==

His brother, [[Mike Nash]], played alongside him during Limerick's Munster SHC successes in 1994 and 1996.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/1253886/family-ties-continue-to-drive-limerick-hurling-team.html|title=Family ties continue to drive Limerick hurling team|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 July 2023|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> His nephew, [[Anthony Nash (hurler)|Anthony Nash]], lined out in goal with the [[Cork senior hurling team]] and won four Munster SHC medals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/200254|title=Nash's Limerick family ties|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=4 September 2013|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

'''Leo O'Connor''' (born 1967) is an Irish [[hurling]] manager and former player. At club level, he played hurling and [[Gaelic football]] with [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==

O'Connor played hurling at all grades as a student at [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]]. He was part of the school's senior team that lost to [[St Finbarr's College, Farranferris|St Finbarr's College]] in the final of the [[Dr Harty Cup]] in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Farna turn it on in second half|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=16 April 1984|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> 

At club level, O'Connor began his career as a [[dual player]] at juvenile and underage levels with [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]], winning a Limerick MAFC title in 1985, as well as Limerick U21AHC medals in 1984 and 1987. After beginning his career as a goalkeeper, he later became an outfield player after progressing to senior level. O'Connor was part of the Claughaun teams that claimed a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|SHC]]-[[Limerick Senior Football Championship|SFC]] double in 1986. He claimed a further five Limerick SFC medals between 1988 and 1996. O'Connor ended his club career after adding a [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] medal to his collection in 2006.

At inter-county level, O'Connor first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick’s last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He progressed to the under-21 team and won consecutive [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] titles, before claiming an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after a 2-15 to 3-06 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|1987 final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/109109/Limerick-s-first-All-Ireland-U.html|title=Limerick’s first All Ireland U-21 hurling title in 1987|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 September 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

O'Connor joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in 1988, but was on and off the team over the course of the following few years. He collected his first silverware as a panel member when Limerick won the [[National Hurling League]] title in 1992.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> O'Connor later won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal, before lining out in Limerick's defeat by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1994 All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/flashback-1994-all-ireland-shc-final-offaly-v-limerick|title=Flashback: 1994 All-Ireland SHC Final - Offaly v Limerick|publisher=GAA website|date=19 March 2020|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Management career==

In retirement from playing, O'Connor became involved in team management and coaching at all levels. As Limerick's under-21 team manager, he guided them to the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] title in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=109139|title=O'Connor is new Treaty U21 boss|work=Hogan Stand website|date=27 March 2009|accessdate=26 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-lift-munster-u-21-title-after-gaelic-grounds-thriller-515270.html|title= Limerick lift Munster U-21 title after Gaelic Grounds thriller|work=Irish Examiner|date=3 August 2011|accessdate=26 November 2012}}</ref> He also became coach of the [[Mayo senior hurling team]] before returning to Limerick as minor and intermediate team manager.

O'Connor later became heavily involved with [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and managed the minor team to a defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2022 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#All-Ireland final|2022 All-Ireland minor final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/redemption-as-powerful-premier-get-hands-on-cup-419377.html|title=Redemption as powerful Premier get hands on cup|date=4 September 2016|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=6 September 2016}}</ref> He continued his association with the team as under-21 manager, however, Offaly lost the [[2023 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship Final|2023 All-Ireland under-20 final]] to [[Cork GAA|Cork]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-41154928.html|title=Cork v Offaly: All-Ireland U20 hurling glory for Rebels|date=4 June 2023|publisher=Echo Live|access-date=5 June 2023|first=|last=}}</ref> O'Connor's under-21 team claimed the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U20HC]] title  after beating Tipperary by 2-20 to 2-14 in the [[2024 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship Final|2024 All-Ireland under-21 final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41407700.html|title=Screeney and Bourke lead Offaly to famous All-Ireland U20 title|date=1 June 2024|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=1 June 2024|first=|last=}}</ref>

'''Graeme Mulcahy''' (born 2 June 1990) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a left corner-forward for club side [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and previously at inter-county level for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==
===Kilmallock===

Mulcahy joined the [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in the minor and under-21 grades. He made his senior championship debut as a seventeen-year-old during the 2007 championship.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

On 3 October 2010, Mulcahy lined out in his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] final. He scored 1-01 from play in the 1–16 to 1–12 defeat of divisional side [[Emmets GAA|Emmets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/mulcahy-s-goal-helps-kilmallock-bridge-gap-1.659156|title=Mulcahy's goal helps Kilmallock bridge gap|date=4 October 2010|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref>

After surrendering their championship crown in 2011, Kilmallock reached the championship decider again on 7 October 2012. Mulcahy was held scoreless, however, his brother, [[Jake Mulcahy]], scored a vital goal to secure a 1–15 to 0–15 victory over [[Adare GAA|Adare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/mulcahy-strikes-to-secure-spoils-for-gritty-kilmallock-28818665.html|title=Mulcahy strikes to secure spoils for gritty Kilmallock|publisher=Irish Independent|date=8 October 2012|access-date=20 August 2013}}</ref>

On 19 October 2014, Mulcahy captained Kilmallock to a third championship victory following a 1–15 to 0–14 defeat of reigning champions [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/delight-for-sparrow-as-kilmallock-defy-odds-292135.html|title=Delight for 'Sparrow' as Kilmallock defy odds|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 October 2014|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> He later won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal, scoring six points from play, following a 1–32 to 3-18 extra-time defeat of [[Cratloe GAA|Cratloe]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/football/kilmallock-find-extra-gear-in-final-epic-299265.html|title=Kilmallock find extra gear in final epic|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 November 2014|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref> On 17 March 2015, Mulcahy captained Kilmallock in their 1–18 to 1–06 defeat by [[Ballyhale Shamrocks GAA|Ballyhale Shamrocks]] in the [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] at [[Croke Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ballyhale-make-it-six-of-the-best-with-final-stroll-31075381.html|title=Ballyhale make it six of the best with final stroll|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 March 2015|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Mulcahy first played for Limerick at minor level. He made his first appearance for the team on 23 June 2007 in a 3–21 to 0–12 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/match-reports/maher-fires-tipperary-to-final-as-limerick-routed-35784.html|title=Maher fires Tipperary to final as Limerick routed|date=25 June 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref> Mulcahy was eligible for the minor grade again in 2008, however, Limerick's season ended with a 0–23 to 0–11 defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]].

Mulcahy subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team. On 3 August 2011, he scored 2-01 from play when Limerick defeated Cork by 4–20 to 1–27 in the final of the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/hannon-on-the-mark-to-edge-thriller-26758064.html|title=Hannon on the mark to edge thriller|date=4 August 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

====Senior====

On 15 February 2009, Mulcahy made his senior debut as a substitute in a [[National Hurling League|National League]] defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] at [[Nowlan Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/grace-snatches-win-for-kilkenny-1.701172|title=Grace snatches win for Kilkenny|date=16 February 2009|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref> Later that season he made his first championship appearance in a 0–25 to 0–17 defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/waterfords-pickmeup-94598.html|title=Waterford's pick-me-up|date=22 June 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

Mulcahy claimed his first silverware at senior level on 30 April 2011 when Limerick won the National League Division 2 title after a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of Clare in the final at [[Cusack Park (Ennis)|Cusack Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}}</ref>

On 14 July 2013, Mulcahy was at right corner-forward in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of Cork in the Munster final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> He ended the season by being nominated for an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/banner-headline-this-year-s-all-star-nominations-with-13-1.1548031|title=Banner headline this year's All Star nominations with 13|date=3 October 2013|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Malachy|last=Clerkin}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Mulcahy scored 1-02 from play when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref> Later that day he was named on ''[[The Sunday Game]]'' Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0819/986154-limerick-rule-in-the-sunday-game-team-of-the-year/|title=Limerick rule in The Sunday Game team of the year|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=20 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018}}</ref> Mulcahy ended the season by winning an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star Award]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=13 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/1101/1008052-treaty-lead-the-way-with-six-hurling-all-stars/|title= Treaty lead the way with six hurling All-Stars|date=2 November 2018|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=4 November 2018}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Mulcahy was selected at left corner-forward for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal after scoring three points from play in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Mulcahy won his first Munster Championship medal in six years after scoring two points from full-forward in Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He ended the year by receiving his second successive All-Star nomination.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-allstars-hurling-2019-4824531-Sep2019/|title=11 players from Tipperary as 8 counties feature in 2019 All-Star hurling nominations|date=26 September 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=26 September 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 21 October 2024, Mulcahy announced his retirement from inter-county hurling.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2024/1021/1476589-limerick-stalwart-mulcahy-calls-time-on-county-career/|title= Limerick stalwart Graeme Mulcahy calls time on county career|date=21 October 2024|work=RTE Sport|accessdate=22 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://limerickgaa.ie/retirement-announcement-graeme-mulcahy/|title= Retirement Announcement Graeme Mulcahy|date=21 October 2024|work=Limerick GAA|accessdate=22 October 2024}}</ref>

===Munster===

Mulcahy was selected for the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team for the first time on 17 February 2013. He later won a [[Railway Cup]] medal following a 1–22 to 0–15 defeat of [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/munster-players-cherish-medals-224440.html|title=Munster players 'cherish' medals|date=4 March 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref> Mulcahy was also selected for the Munster team in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/munster-reign-ended-by-tribesmen-in-disguise-258246.html|title=Munster reign ended by Tribesmen in disguise|date=10 February 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

He ended his club career with the [[Croagh-Kilfinny]] club in Limerick. His [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] career with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] and [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] senior teams lasted from 1896 until 1908.{{cite web|url=https://finbarrconnolly.com/1897-4/|title=Pat Mulcahy|date=|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|accessdate=10 July 2017|first=|last=}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Born in [[Cappamore]], [[County Limerick]], Mulcahy first played competitive hurling in his youth. He was little more than a schoolchild when he was invited to play for the [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe]] and [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Boher]] teams, however, he quickly established himself on the [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] team, winning a Murphy Cup medal in 1897. Mulcahy later played with the [[Commercials GAA (Dublin)|Commercials]] club in [[Dublin]] and won five [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]] medals. Mulcahy joined the Limerick senior team in 1896 and enjoyed much success during his brief tenure with the team. He was the full-forward on the team that won [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]], [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] and Croke Cup titles in 1897. Mulcahy later joined the Dublin senior team and added a [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster]] medal to his collection in 1902. '''Paudie O'Dwyer''' (born 1982) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who currently played as a right wing-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

O'Dwyer made his first appearance for the team during the [[National Hurling League 2003|2003 National League]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until leaving the panel after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2008|2008 championship]]. An [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medalist in the under-21 grade, he has enjoyed little success as a member of the county senior team. O'Dwyer ended up an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion.

At club level O'Dwyer is a two-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county club championship]] medalist with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]].

==Playing career==

===Club===

O'Dwyer plays his club hurling with Kilmallock and has enjoyed much success.

After losing the 2005 championship decider to [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]], it took five years for Kilmallock to return to the county final. A 1–16 to 1–12 defeat of [[Emmets GAA|Emmets]] on that occasion gave O'Dwyer his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20132561.html|title=Battling Kilmallock end title wait|date=4 November 2002|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=4 October 2010|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

After failing to retain their title, Kilmallock qualified for another championship final in 2012. [[Adare GAA|Adare]] provided the opposition on that occasion, however, a 1–15 to 0–15 victory gave O'Dwyer a second county championship medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20210161.html|title=Kilmallock stand up to torrid test|date=4 November 2002|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=8 October 2012|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

===Inter-county===

Foley first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2002. That year Limerick retained the provincial title for the third successive year with O'Dwyer winning a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal following a 1–20 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. A subsequent 3–17 to 0-8 trouncing of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] gave O'Dwyer an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-make-history-292955.html|title=Limerick make history|date=16 September 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=4 November 2012|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}</ref>

In 2003 O'Dwyer made his senior debut for Limerick in a [[National Hurling League]] game against Wexford. Later that season he was a regular at right wing-back during Limerick's unsuccessful championship campaign.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

After playing no part for Limerick in 2004, O'Dwyer was recalled to the panel for 2005.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=39044|title=Padjoe shakes up Limerick panel|date=22 October 2004|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=4 November 2012}}</ref>

In 2007 O'Dwyer came on as a substitute in Limerick's 3–17 to 1–14 defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the Munster final.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dynamic-dan-adds-some-extra-dash-for-the-dise-995588.html|title=Dynamic Dan adds some extra dash for the Déise|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|access-date=2 August 2012|date=9 July 2007|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}</ref> He was an unused substitute in Limerick's subsequent 2–19 to 1–15 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2007/0902/1188603379646.html|title=Kilkenny overpower Limerick to retain title|date=2 September 2007|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=31 October 2012}}</ref>

O'Dwyer's last game for Limerick was a Munster semi-final defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in 2008.{{citation needed|date=January 2022}}

'''Michael Mullane''' (13 April 1889 – 22 November 1962) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a left wing-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1921.htm|title=1921 All-Ireland hurling champions|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|date=|accessdate=21 April 2014|first=|last=}}</ref>

Born in [[Croom, County Limerick|Croom]], [[County Limerick]], Mullane first arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of thirty when he first linked up with the Limerick senior team. Mullane went on to play a key part for Limerick during a golden age for the team, and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal and one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.

At club level Mullane won two [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medals with [[Croom GAA|Croom]].

Jackie O'Connell.text:
{{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Jackie O'Connell | irish = Seán Cathal Ó Conaill | occupation = Employment exchange manager | birth_date = 22 January 1912 | death_date = 16 October 1997 (aged 85) | nickname = Jackie | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Croom GAA|Croom]] | cl_position = | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]
[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Centre-forward | ic_years = 1930-1932
1933-1935 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 1 | nhl = 1 | cl_update = | ic_update = 22:22, 4 May 2015 | birth_place=[[Croom, County Limerick|Banogue]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] | death_place=[[Limerick (city)|Ballinacurra, Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''John Charles O'Connell''' (26 January 1912 – 16 October 1997) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a centre-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team. Born in [[Croom, County Limerick|Banogue]], [[County Limerick]], O'Connell first played competitive hurling during his schooling at [[Rockwell College]]. He arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of eighteen when he first linked up with the Waterford senior and junior teams. He made his debut for Limerick during the [[National Hurling League 1933-34|1933-34 league]]. O'Connell immediately became a regular member of the starting fifteen and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal and one [[National Hurling League]] medal. He was an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion.{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1934.htm|title=Limerick 1934|publisher=Finbarr J. Connolly website|date=|accessdate=4 May 2015|first=|last=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505003906/http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1934.htm|archive-date=5 May 2015|url-status=dead}} At club level O'Connell was a two-time divisional championship medallist with [[Croom GAA|Croom]]. O'Connell's retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1935 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1935 championship]]. In retirement from playing O'Connell became involved in the administrative affairs of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick County Board]]. He served as secretary for 27 years before later being elected chairman and eventually life president.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/what-s-on/arts-entertainment/ledger-found-in-limerick-home-reveals-local-gaa-history-1-6049014|title=Ledger found in Limerick home reveals local GAA history|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=9 May 2014|accessdate=4 May 2015|first=Áine|last=Fitzgerald|archive-date=5 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505020954/http://www.limerickleader.ie/what-s-on/arts-entertainment/ledger-found-in-limerick-home-reveals-local-gaa-history-1-6049014|url-status=dead}} ==Playing career== ===College=== During his tenure at [[Rockwell College]] O'Connell was heavily involved in [[rugby union]] and rowing, however, he excelled as captain of the senior hurling team. In 1930 he won a [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] medal following an 8-2 to 1-1 trouncing of Mount Sion.{{cite web|url=http://www.seamusjking.com/Articles%20Full/rockwell_and_the_harty_Cup.html|title=Rockwell College and the Harty Cup|publisher=Séamus J. King website|date=|accessdate=5 May 2015|first=Séamus J.|last=King|archive-date=10 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160710002711/http://seamusjking.com/Articles%20Full/rockwell_and_the_harty_Cup.html|url-status=dead}} ===Inter-county=== During his studies in Waterford O'Connell lined out for the Déise during several league campaigns. O'Connell joined the Limerick panel during the team's successful league campaign and made his debut in the subsequent championship. That campaign saw Limerick reach the decider, where they played [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] for the second year in-a-row. The result was much the same, with O'Connell collecting a second Munster medal following a 4-8 to 2-5 victory. The All-Ireland final on 2 September 1934 was a special occasion as it was the golden jubilee final of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. Dublin were the opponents and a close game developed. After leading by a point at the interval, Limerick went five clear with time running out. Dublin fought their way back to secure a remarkable draw. The replay on 30 September turned out to be an even closer affair, with both sides level with two minutes to go. Points from [[Mick Mackey]] and O'Connell and a remarkable four goals from [[Dave Clohessy]] secured a 5-2 to 2-6 victory for Limerick. The win gave O'Connell an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal. In 1935 O'Connell added a [[National Hurling League]] medal to his collection, as Limerick retained their title in a straightforward league format. He missed Limerick's subsequent provincial triumph, however, he was back on the starting fifteen as [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] provided the opposition in the subsequent All-Ireland final on 1 September 1935. Limerick were the red-hot favourites as a record crowd of over 46,000 turned up to watch a hurling classic. In spite of rain falling throughout the entire game both sides served up a great game. At the beginning of the second-half [[Lory Meagher]] sent over a huge point from midfield giving Kilkenny a lead which they would not surrender. The game ended in controversial circumstances for Mick Mackey when Limerick were awarded a close-in free to level the game. Jack Keane issued an instruction from the sideline that [[Timmy Ryan]], the team captain, was to take the free and put the sliotar over the bar for the equalising point. As he lined up to take it, Mackey pushed him aside and took the free himself. The shot dropped short and into the waiting hands of the Kilkenny goalkeeper and was cleared. The game ended shortly after with Kilkenny triumphing by 2-5 to 2-4. A recurring knee injury brought O'Connell's career to a premature end in 1936. ==Biography== The son of a farmer and a schoolteacher, O'Connell was born in Banogue just outside [[Croom, County Limerick|Croom]], [[County Limerick]]. He was educated at the local national school before later earning a scholarship to [[Rockwell College]]. O'Connell subsequently began his teacher training at [[De La Salle College Waterford|De La Salle College]] in [[Waterford]], however, ill health forced him to abandon his studies after two years. On returning to Limerick he joined the civil service and gave over forty years of service to the [[Department of Social Protection|Department of Social Welfare]]. He was manager of the employment exchange on his retirement in 1976.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} O'Connell married his wife Eileen in 1938 and the couple had seven children: Breda, Kathleen, Brendan, Sheila, Patricia, Marie and Margaret.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} After retiring from the civil service, O'Connell and his wife spent much of their time in [[Kilkee]], [[County Clare]]. He died on 16 October 1997 at his home in Ballinacurra. At the time of his death he was the last surviving member of Limerick's 1934 All-Ireland-winning team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} ==Honours== ===Player=== ;Rockwell College *[[Dr. Harty Cup]] (1): 1930 (c) ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (1): [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1934|1934]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (1): [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1934]] *[[National Hurling League]] (1): [[National Hurling League 1934-35|1934-35]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes | title = Jackie O'Connell navigation boxes | bg = | fg = | list1 = {{Limerick Hurling Team 1934}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1935}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oconnell, Jackie}} [[Category:1912 births]] [[Category:1997 deaths]] [[Category:Croom hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship winners]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

'''Barry Nash''' (born 31 December 1996) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a left corner-back for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].

==Playing career==
===South Liberties===

Nash joined th [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's senior team.

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

Nash first played for Limerick as a member of the county's minor team. On 23 July 2013, he scored three points from play when Limerick won their first [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title in 29 years after a 1–20 to 4–08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in a replay of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20237793.html|title=Limerick end 29-year wait for Munster title in style|date=24 July 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

Nash was eligible for the minor team again in 2014 and won a second successive Munster Championship medal after a 0–24 to 0–18 second successive defeat of Waterford in a replay of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 July 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=|last=}}</ref> On 7 September 2014, Nash scored two points in Limerick's 2–17 to 0–19 [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-minors-savour-all-ireland-success-against-spirited-limerick-1.1920852|title=Kilkenny minors savour All-Ireland success against spirited Limerick|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 September 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}}</ref>

On 30 July 2015, Nash won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal with the Limerick under-21 team after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 12 September 2015, he was named [[man of the match]] when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0–26 to 1–07 in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

After surrendering their title in 2016, Nash won a second Munster Championship medal the following year after a 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 9 September 2017, Nash was at left corner-forward in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of Kilkenny in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Senior====

Nash was drafted onto the Limerick senior hurling team in January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/201061/18-new-faces-on-Limerick-hurling.html|title=18 new faces on Limerick hurling panel|date=9 January 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=19 June 2016|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He made his first appearance for the team in a 2–23 to 0–15 defeat of Wexford in the [[National Hurling League]] on 13 February 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/wexford-have-no-answer-for-prolific-limerick-1.2534336|title=Wexford have no answer for prolific Limerick|date=13 February 2016|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=8 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> Later that season, Nash made his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] appearance in a 3–12 to 1–16 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/209507/Limerick-select-four-debuts-for-Munster.html|title=Limerick select four debuts for Munster SHC against Tipperary|date=16 June 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=19 June 2016|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

On 6 February 2017, it was announced that Nash had withdrawn from the Limerick senior hurling panel for "personal reasons".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/barry-nash-departs-limerick-senior-hurling-panel-3224856-Feb2017/|title=Limerick shock as 2015 All-Ireland U21 final star Nash departs senior hurling panel|date=6 February 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=8 August 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> Team manager [[John Kiely (Limerick hurler)|John Kiely]] stated: "It is what it is. I have no doubt Barry will have a major part to play in the years ahead, who knows, maybe even at some point later this year, he may find himself in a position to return to training."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/door-always-open-for-barry-nash-insists-limerick-boss-442271.html|title=Door always open for Barry Nash, insists Limerick boss|date=7 February 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=8 August 2018|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> Just over a month after leaving the panel, Nash returned to training.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/barry-nash-limerick-3294472-Mar2017/|title=Big boost for Limerick as Nash makes u-turn and returns to training|date=18 March 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=8 August 2018|first=Ryan|last=Bailey}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Nash was a non-playing substitute when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Nash was named on the bench for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal as a non-playing substitute in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, Nash won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after coming on as a 70th-minute substitute for [[Declan Hannon]] in Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 25 October 2020, Nash won a second successive National League medal after Limerick's 0–36 to 1–23 win over Clare in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref> Later that season he claimed a second successive Munster Championship medal after lining out at left corner-back in the 0–25 to 0–21 [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]] defeat of Waterford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford for historic Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref>

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] | death_date = 12 February 1989 (aged 48) | death_place = [[Kilmallock]],
County Limerick, Ireland }} '''Anthony O'Brien''' (1940 – 12 February 1989) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Playing career== O'Brien played hurling at all levels during his time as a student at [[St Munchin's College]] in [[Limerick]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick minors the "top twenty" in 1958 Gaelic sport|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=3 January 1959|accessdate=23 March 2017|first=|last=}} He was later part of [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]]'s team in the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]]. O'Brien first played for the [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] club in the juvenile and underage grades and won a Limerick U16HC title in 1954.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=The 'Well honour late Tony O'Brien|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=1 July 1995|accessdate=23 March 2017|first=|last=}} O'Brien was still eligible for the minor grade when he won a [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick JHC]] title in 1957. He later added a Limerick JFC medal to his collection, before claiming a second in 1970. By that stage, O'Brien had his first hurling success after winning consecutive [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] titles in 1965 and 1966.{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20036696.html|title=‘We didn’t win enough’|date=7 July 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=26 December 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2017/02/11/patrickswell-gaa-club-victory-dinner/|title=Patrickswell GAA Club Victory Dinner|date=11 February 2017|publisher=Limerick Post|accessdate=11 February 2017|first=|last=}} He won six Limerick SHC titles in total, with further victories as [[Captain (sport)|team captain]] in 1969 and 1970, as well as 1977 and 1979. At inter-county level, O'Brien first appeared for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as sub-goalkeeper on the minor team that beat [[Galway GAA|Galway]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Football Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1958.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145512/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick’s last All-Ireland minor title won in Croke Park - 1958|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=4 September 2014|accessdate=23 March 2017|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} He immediately progressed to the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] and made his first appearance in a [[National Hurling League]] game against [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]] in October 1959.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick open National Hurling League campaign|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 October 1959|accessdate=23 March 2017|first=|last=}} O'Brien [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|captain]]ed Limerick to the National League title in 1971. Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in O'Brien being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won four [[Railway Cup]] medals in five seasons between 1966 and 1970.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Coaching career== In retirement from playing, O'Brien remained active in coaching at all levels with Patrickswell. He was a selector when Patrickswell beat [[Mount Sion GAA|Mount Sion]] to win the [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] title in 1988.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10068931.html|title=McGrath set to be fit for Sion’s clash with the ‘Well|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 November 2003|access-date=20 April Seán O'Connor (sports administrator).text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler, selector, referee and Gaelic games administrator}} {{more citations needed|date=December 2021}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Seán O'Connor | irish = Seán Ó Conchubhair | birth_date = 1935 | death_date = 5 February 2018 (aged 82) | height_ft = | height_in = | occupation = Aircraft mechanic | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county_h = 4 | cl_county_f = 3 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = | ic_years = 1957–1959 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 0 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | all_stars = | nhl = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = 19:24, 7 February 2018 | birth_place = [[Limerick]], Ireland | death_place = Limerick, Ireland }} '''Seán O'Connor''' (1935 – 5 February 2018) was an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]], selector, referee and [[Gaelic games]] administrator. His [[National Hurling League|league]] and [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] career at senior level with the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]] lasted two seasons from 1957 until 1959.{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/295507/sadness-at-death-of-limerick-and-claughaun-gaa-stalwart-sean-o-connor.html|title=Sadness at death of Limerick and Claughaun GAA stalwart Sean O'Connor|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=6 February 2018|access-date=7 February 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/280936|title=Sean refereed two All-Ireland SHC finals|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=6 February 2018|access-date=7 February 2018}} Born in [[Limerick]], O'Connor first played competitive hurling and [[Gaelic football]] at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] club. He eventually became a [[dual player]] with the club's senior teams, winning four [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county hurling championship]] medals and three [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|county football championship]] medals. O'Connor made his inter-county debut as a dual player with the Limerick minor teams. He joined the senior hurling team in 1957 and had two seasons as a member of the team. Following his inter-county career, O'Connor served as an administrator and referee at club and county levels. He refereed the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] finals in [[1969 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1969]] and [[1975 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1975]], a number of [[Oireachtas Cup]] finals and 22 Munster finals at varying levels in both codes. O'Connor held most administration positions with the Claughaun club, including chairman and president, while he also served as assistant treasurer of the Limerick City Divisional Board. ==Honours== ;Claughaun *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] (4): 1957, 1958, 1968, 1971 *[[Limerick Senior Football Championship]] (3): 1955, 1959, 1967 ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Seán O'Connor navigation boxes |list1= {{s-start}} {{s-ach|ach}} {{succession box | before=[[John Dowling (hurler)|John Dowling]] | title=[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC Final]]

'''David Murnane''' (30 August 1893 – 16 May 1925) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]]. Usually lining out as a full-back, he was a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] team that won the [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1921 All-Ireland Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://finbarrconnolly.com/1921-2/|title=1921|publisher=Finbarr J. Connolly website|date=|accessdate=11 June 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 27 February 2016, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal as Mary I won their first ever title after a 1–30 to 3–22 defeat of the [[University of Limerick]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/eamonn-cregan-hails-heroic-mary-i-384649.html|title=Eamonn Cregan hails heroic Mary I|date=29 February 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} O'Donovan was at right wing-forward when Mary I retained the title in 2017 following a 3–24 to 1–19 defeat of [[Carlow Institute of Technology]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/dj-carey-hails-inspirational-coach-jamie-wall-as-mary-i-retain-fitzgibbon-title-443894.html|title=DJ Carey hails inspirational coach Jamie Wall as Mary I retain Fitzgibbon title|date=27 February 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=John|last=Fallon}} ===Club=== O'Donovan joined the [[Doon GAA|Doon]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in under-12, under-14 and under-15 grades. '''William O'Donoghue''' (born 8 December 1994) is an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]] who plays as a midfielder for club side [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] which he [[Captain (Gaelic games)|captain]]s and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-john-kiely-3357178-Apr2017/|title=Limerick cut 7 players from panel ahead of hurling championship campaign|date=25 April 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Club===

O'Donoghue joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, experiencing championship success in the under-16, minor and under-21 grades.

On 6 October 2013, O'Donoghue was at right wing-forward when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Adare GAA|Adare]] by 0–14 to 0–12 to win the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/downes-sets-the-tone-for-na-piarsaigh-to-grind-it-out-29639434.html|title=Downes sets the tone for Na Piarsaigh to grind it out|date=7 October 2013|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> He was switched to midfield for the subsequent [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]], which culminated with him winning a provincial medal after a 4–14 to 0–8 defeat of [[Sixmilebridge GAA|Sixmilebridge]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/powerful-piarsaighs-blistering-pace-too-much-for-tired-bridge-250662.html|title=Powerful Piarsaigh's blistering pace too much for tired Bridge|date=25 November 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

O'Donoghue won a second Limerick Championship medal on 11 October 2015 after a 1–22 to 4–12 defeat of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> Later that season he won a second Munster medal after a 2–18 to 2–11 defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 17 March 2016, O'Donoghue won an [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] by 2–25 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

On 15 October 2017, O'Donoghue won a third Limerick Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] by 1–22 to 2–14 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He later won a third Munster Championship medal when Na Piarsaigh defeated Ballygunner by 3–15 to 2–10 in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/late-na-piarsaigh-surge-sweeps-aside-ballygunner-in-scrappy-munster-final-36333884.html|title=Late Na Piarsaigh surge sweeps aside Ballygunner in scrappy Munster final|date=19 November 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, O'Donoghue was at midfield when Na Piarsaigh were defeated by [[Cuala GAA|Cuala]] in the All-Ireland final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

On 27 October 2018, O'Donoghue won a fourth Limerick Championship medal as captain following Na Piarsaigh's 2–22 to 3–10 defeat of [[Doon GAA|Doon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/boss-beary-points-to-experience-of-troops-as-na-piarsaigh-impress-again-37468758.html|title=Boss Beary points to experience of troops as Na Piarsaigh impress again|date=29 October 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=1 November 2018|first=Darragh|last=Small}}</ref>

O'Donoghue retained the captaincy for the [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|2019 championship]], however, Na Piarsaigh surrendered their title following a 1–17 to 0–15 defeat by Patrickswell in the [[2019 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|2019 final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cian-lynch-comes-to-the-fore-as-patrickswell-hold-off-na-piarsaigh-in-limerick-county-final-38567636.html|title=Cian Lynch comes to the fore as Patrickswell hold off Na Piarsaigh in Limerick county final|publisher=Irish Independent|date=6 October 2019|access-date=6 October 2019|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

On 19 September 2020, O'Donoghue captained Na Piarsaigh in a third consecutive [[2020 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]] and their eighth overall in ten seasons. He ended the game with a fifth winners' medal after the 5–27 to 1–12 victory over [[Doon GAA|Doon]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40051733.html|title=Na Piarsaigh crush Doon in one-sided Limerick final|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 September 2020|access-date=19 September 2020|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

===Inter-county===
====Under-21====

O'Donoghue joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He later joined the Limerick under-21 [[Gaelic football]] team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/134561/Limerick-U-21-footballers-denied-shock.html|title=Limerick U-21 footballers denied shock win by barrage of Cork goals|date=11 March 2015|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

====Senior====

On 19 February 2017, O'Donoghue made his first appearance for the Limerick senior hurling team in a 6–21 to 3–8 defeat of [[Kerry county hurling team|Kerry]] in the [[National Hurling League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/kerryman/sport/gaa/hurlers-back-down-to-earth-with-a-bang-35470472.html|title=Hurlers back down to earth with a bang|date=25 February 2017|publisher=The Kerryman|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Damian|last=Stack}}</ref> In the subsequent league semi-final against [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]] he scored his first goal in a 1–21 to 1–11 defeat by Tipperary.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/galway-see-off-limerick-to-advance-to-division-1-final-785982.html|title=Galway see off Limerick to advance to Division 1 final|date=16 April 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, O'Donoghue was introduced as a 66th-minute substitute for [[Darragh O'Donovan]] when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway county hurling team|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

In December 2018, O'Donoghue was included on the Limerick panel for the upcoming season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/352321/42-man-limerick-hurling-panel-for-2019-includes-seven-newcomers.html|title=42-man Limerick hurling panel for 2019 includes seven newcomers|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 December 2018|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> Injury ruled him out of the [[2019 National Hurling League|National League]]; however, he returned to training in March 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/370994/limerick-with-pretty-full-compliment-to-select-from-as-casey-and-o-donoghue-return.html|title=Limerick with 'pretty full {{sic|compli|ment|nolink=y|expected=complement}} to select from' as Casey and O'Donoghue return|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=21 March 2019|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, O'Donoghue won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal at midfield following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of Tipperary in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He ended the year by receiving his first [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] nomination.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/gaa-allstars-hurling-2019-4824531-Sep2019/|title=11 players from Tipperary as 8 counties feature in 2019 All-Star hurling nominations|date=26 September 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=26 September 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>
