'''Barry Murphy''' (born 25 February 1997) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a centre-forward for club side [[Doon GAA|Doon]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-clare-3796057-Jan2018/|title=5 changes to Limerick team ahead of Munster league final against Clare|date=13 January 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=22 August 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===College===

Murphy first came to prominence as a hurler with Scoil na Trionóide in [[Doon, County Limerick|Doon]]. Having played in every grade as a hurler, he eventually joined the school's senior team. On 22 February 2014, Murphy was at left corner-forward when [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] defeated Scoil na Trionóide by 2–13 to 0–04 in the final of the [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/ardscoil-ris-a-class-apart-in-derby-duel-259848.html|title=Ardscoil Rís a class apart in derby duel|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=24 February 2014|accessdate=23 June 2015|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

===University===

During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]], Murphy was selected for the college's senior hurling team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/ul-fitzgibbon-cup-wit-2-3829398-Feb2018/|title=1-6 for Limerick's Murphy as UL see off WIT to set up Fitzgibbon Cup quarter-final with UCC|date=1 February 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Tomás|last=McCarthy}}</ref>

===Club===

Murphy joined the [[Doon GAA|Doon]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in under-12, under-14 and under-15 grades. As a member of the club's minor team, he also enjoyed championship success before joining the club's senior team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

Murphy first played for Limerick at minor level. On 22 July 2014, he was an unused substitute when Limerick won their second successive [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title after a 0–24 to 0–18 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|date=23 July 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref> On 7 September 2014, Murphy was introduced as a substitute for [[Thomas Grimes (hurler)|Thomas Grimes]] in Limerick's 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/wonderful-walsh-fires-cats-to-victory-over-limerick-30569083.html|title=Wonderful Walsh fires Cats to victory over Limerick|date=8 September 2014|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref>

Murphy's second and final season with the Limerick minor hurling team ended with an All-Ireland quarter-final defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/evan-niland-stars-as-slick-galway-see-off-limerick-344725.html|title=Evan Niland stars as slick Galway see off Limerick|date=27 July 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

Murphy subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2016 and played during the team's unsuccessful championship campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/all-ireland-holders-limerick-overrun-cork-u21s-742281.html|title=All-Ireland holders Limerick overrun Cork U21s|date=28 June 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> In his second season with the team he won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after coming on as a substitute for [[Tom Morrissey (hurler)|Tom Morrissey]] in Limerick's 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 9 September 2017, Murphy was named at centre-forward for Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of Kilkenny in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Senior====

Murphy joined the Limerick senior hurling panel in 2018 and made his first appearance for the team during the pre-season [[Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/281970/10-additions-to-2018-limerick-hurling-panel.html|title=10 additions to 2018 Limerick hurling panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He made his first appearance in the [[National Hurling League]] on 28 January 2018 after being introduced as a 46th-minute substitute for [[Gearóid Hegarty]] in a 1–25 to 0–18 defeat of [[Laois GAA|Laois]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/aaron-gillane-0-11-limerick-laois-3821416-Jan2018/|title=0-11 for Aaron Gillane as Limerick ease to league opener win over Laois|date=28 January 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> He made his [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] debut on 20 May 2018 and scored a goal in a 1–23 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/tipperary-limerick-munster-hurling-3-4024189-May2018/|title=Limerick begin Munster campaign in flying form with six-point victory over Tipperary|date=20 May 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=John|last=Fallon}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, Murphy was a member of the extended panel when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, Murphy started Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] on the bench. He was introduced as a 64th-minute substitute for [[Aaron Gillane]] and collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 2 June 2019, Murphy sustained a bad hamstring injury in the final minutes of Limerick's [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat of Waterford. After undergoing a number of scans and an operation, Murphy was later ruled out for the rest of season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/424406/limerick-forward-ruled-out-of-the-remainder-of-the-hurling-championship.html|title=Limerick forward ruled out of the remainder of the hurling championship|date=17 June 2019|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

'''Barry O'Connell''' (born 1994) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick Premier Championship]] club [[Kildimo-Pallaskenry GAA|Kildimo-Pallaskenry]]. He usually lines out as a right wing-forward. O'Connell is a former member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsjoe.ie/gaa/limerick-hurlers-must-youngest-senior-inter-county-team-gaa-148905|title=Limerick hurlers must be the youngest senior inter-county team in the GAA|date=27 January 2018|publisher=Sportsjoe|accessdate=22 August 2018|first=Niall|last=McIntyre}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===University===

During his studies at the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]], O'Connell was selected for the college's senior hurling team for the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/sigerson-fitzgibbon-cups/mary-i-remain-on-course-to-regain-independentie-fitzgibbon-cup-title-by-defeating-davy-fitzgeralds-lit-35480112.html|title=Mary I remain on course to regain Independent.ie Fitzgibbon Cup title by defeating Davy Fitzgerald's LIT|date=24 February 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Declan|last=Rooney}}</ref>

===Club===

O'Connell joined the [[Kildimo-Pallaskenry GAA|Kildimo-Pallaskenry]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, before eventually joining the club's top adult team.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

On 28 October 2017, O'Connell captained Kildimo-Pallaskenry to the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick Intermediate Championship]] title. He scored a point from right wing-forward in the 2–13 to 0–09 defeat of [[Glenroe GAA|Glenroe]] in the final.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

O'Connell first played for Limerick as a member of the minor team on 27 April 2011 in a 2–14 to 0-12 [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/dowling-lights-up-limerick-152811.html|title=Dowling lights up Limerick|date=28 April 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> His two seasons with the minor team ended without success.

O'Connell subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal in his first season after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 12 September 2015, he was at centre-back when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0–26 to 1–07 in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Intermediate====

O'Connell played for the Limerick intermediate hurling team for the first time on 9 June 2013 in a 0–20 to 0-15 [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/hammersley-leads-the-charge-for-tipperary-233768.html|title=Hammersley leads the charge for Tipperary|date=10 June 2013|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> He also lined out during Limerick's unsuccessful championship campaign in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/third-quarter-blitz-secures-title-for-cork-341566.html|title=Third-quarter blitz secures title for Cork|date=19 July 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Senior====

O'Connell joined the Limerick senior panel in January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/201061/18-new-faces-on-Limerick-hurling.html|title=18 new faces on Limerick hurling panel|date=9 January 2016|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He made his first appearance for the team in a 1–19 to 0-14 [[National Hurling League]] defeat of [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] on 6 March 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-set-up-promotion-showdown-with-clare-385951.html|title=Limerick set up promotion showdown with Clare|date=7 March 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Kevin|last=Egan}}</ref>

O'Connell was included on the panel again in 2017, however, he was not included on Limerick's championship panel.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-john-kiely-3357178-Apr2017/|title=Limerick cut 7 players from panel ahead of hurling championship campaign|date=25 April 2017|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

O'Connell rejoined the Limerick senior panel in 2018. On 19 August 2018, he was a member of the extended panel when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

O'Connell was a member of Limerick's extended panel once again during the [[2019 National Hurling League|2019 National League]], however, he made no appearance during Limerick's eight-game run to the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He was dropped from the panel prior to the start of the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/375181/limerick-confirm-2019-senior-hurling-championship-panel.html|title=BREAKING: Limerick confirm 2019 senior hurling championship panel|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 April 2019|accessdate=3 May 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

{{short description|Irish hurler (born 2002)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=February 2023}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=February 2023}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Aidan O'Connor | irish = Aodán Ó Conchúir | fullname = | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | nickname = | occupation = Student | county = Limerick | province = Munster | colleges = [[University of Limerick]] | col_years = 2021-present | fitz = 2 | club = [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] | cl_position = | cl_years = 2020-present | cl_apps_points = 29 (10-219) | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Centre-forward | ic_years = 2023-present | ic_apps_points = 17 (5-60) | ic_province = 3 | ic_all_ireland = 2 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 1 | cl_update = 20:05, 13 February 2022 | ic_update = 00:02, 31 October 2026 | birth_date= 26 September 2002 | birth_place=[[Clarina, County Limerick|Clarina]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Aidan O'Connor''' (born 26 September 2002) is an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he plays with [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]], while he is also a member of the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He usually lines out as a forward. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[Clarina, County Limerick|Clarina]], [[County Limerick]], O'Connor was educated at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick]]. He played in all grades of hurling during his time there, including in the [[Dr Harty Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.echolive.ie/corksport/arid-40142378.html|title=Rochestown College suffer second loss in Harty Cup to slick Ardscoil Rís|access-date=17 May 2026|publisher=Echo Live|date=6 November 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/hogwarts-of-hurling-nurtured-15-of-limericks-all-ireland-winners-39868591.html|title='Hogwarts of hurling' nurtured 15 of Limerick's All-Ireland winners|publisher=Irish Independent|date=16 December 2020|accessdate=12 February 2023|first=|last=}} During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]] (UL), O'Connor continued his hurling development. He won a league and championship double with the freshers' team in 2022.{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/star-studded-ul-crowned-all-ireland-fresher-hurling-champions-in-final-win-over-dcu-7858239|title=Star-studded UL crowned All-Ireland Fresher hurling champions in final win over DCU|access-date=20 July 2026|publisher=Limerick Live|date=9 March 2022}}{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/watch-aidan-oconnor-delight-as-ul-freshers-complete-historic-hurling-year-for-limerick-side-7857834|title=WATCH: Aidan O’Connor delight as UL freshers complete historic hurling year for Limerick side|access-date=20 July 2026|publisher=Limerick Live|date=10 March 2022}} O'Connor later progressed to UL's [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] team and claimed a winners' medal in that competition in February 2025, following a 0–23 to 1–15 win over [[DCU GAA|DCU Dóchas Éireann]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41575399.html|title=UL overpower DCU to lift third Fitzgibbon Cup in four years|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 February 2025|accessdate=16 February 2025|first=Kevin|last=Egan}} He claimd a second consecutive winners' medal in 2026, when UL retained the title after a defeat of [[Mary Immaculate College]] in the [[2026 Fitzgibbon Cup#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/2015230/limerick-stars-shine-as-clinical-ul-see-off-local-rivals-mary-immaculate-college-in-fitzgibbon-cup-final.html|title=Limerick stars shine as clinical UL see off local rivals Mary Immaculate College in Fitzgibbon Cup final|publisher=Limerick Live|date=13 February 2026|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} ==Club career== O'Connor began his club career with [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]], at a time when the club had multiple successes in the juvenile and underage grades. After winning the Limerick MAHC title in 2018, he won a Limerick Premier MHC title in 2019, following an 0–18 to 0–12 win over [[Doon GAA|Doon]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/ballybrown-end-31-year-wait-for-a-premier-minor-hurling-title-8134242|title=Ballybrown end 31-year wait for a Premier Minor Hurling title|publisher=Limerick Live|date=5 October 2019|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} O'Connor collected a second consecutive winners' medal in that competition in 2020, as [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret]] were beaten by 3–23 to 0–20 .{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/back-to-back-limerick-minor-hurling-tiles-for-ballybrown-after-thrilling-final-with-mungret-8044512|title=Back-to-back Limerick minor hurling tiles for Ballybrown after thrilling final with Mungret|publisher=Limerick Live|date=16 September 2020|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} Ballybrown secured the Limerick Premier U19HC title in October 2021, with O'Connor [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ing the team from midfield in the 2–30 to 1–17 win over [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/emphatic-ballybrown-power-past-monaleen-to-win-limerick-u19-premier-hurling-title-7945309|title=Emphatic Ballybrown power past Monaleen to win Limerick U19 Premier hurling title|publisher=Limerick Live|date=6 October 2021|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} He added a Limerick Premier U21HC medal to his collection in 2022, after top-scoring in the seven-point win over Mungret.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/ballybrown-celebrate-limerick-premier-u21-hurling-final-success-7650341|title=Ballybrown celebrate Limerick Premier U21 hurling final success|publisher=Limerick Live|date=20 November 2022|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} By this stage O'Connor had already joined the Ballybrown [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|senior team]] and made his debut in July 2020 in a 4–18 to 2–14 win over [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40022090.html|title=Limerick SHC: Ballybrown get campaign off to flying start|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=25 July 2020|accessdate=31 October 2022|first=|last=}} ==Inter-county== O'Connor first appeared on the inter-county scene for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during as a member of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]]. He won a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] title in June 2019, following a 1–17 to 1–11 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2019 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-triumph-in-electric-ireland-munster-mhc-final|title=Limerick triumph in Electric Ireland Munster MHC Final|date=30 June 2019|publisher=GAA website|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} O'Connor immediately progressed to the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20 team]] and won a [[Munster Under-20 Hurling Championship|Munster U20HC]] in May 2022 following a four-point win over Tipperary.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40865447.html|title=Treaty tyros tame Tipp to add to county's dominance |date=4 May 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=20 July 2026|first=|last=}} He was at centre-forward for Limerick's 0–19 to 0–18 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2022 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland U20HC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/u-20-hurling/kilkenny-claim-all-ireland-u-20-title-after-edging-limerick-in-thrilling-final-41676137.html|title=Kilkenny claim All-Ireland U-20 title after edging Limerick in thrilling final|date=22 May 2022|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} O'Connor was Limerick's [[2022 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship#Top scorers|top scorer]] throughout the championship. O'Connor made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in a 1–27 to 1–15 [[National Hurling League]] defeat of [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] in March 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41091295.html|title=Aaron Gillane back as Limerick have 12-points to spare over Westmeath|date=12 March 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=6 May 2026|first=|last=}} He ended the competition with a winners' medal, as a non-playing substitute in the 2–20 to 0–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 National Hurling League#Division 1|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0409/1376051-classy-limerick-claim-league-honours-with-ease/|title=Classy Limerick claim league honours with ease|date=9 April 2023|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} O'Connor later claimed his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal, again as a substitute, as Limerick beat [[Clare GAA|Clare]] by 1–23 to 1–22 to win a record-equalling fifth consecutive title.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41159863.html|title=Aaron Gillane on fire as Limerick edge Clare to secure fifth consecutive Munster title|date=11 June 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He was also an unused substitute when Limerick won a record-equalling fourth consecutive [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] title, following a 0–30 to 2–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history |date=23 July 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} O'Connor came on as a substitute for [[David Reidy (Limerick hurler)|David Reidy]] when Limerick won a record-breaking sixth consecutive Munster SHC title after a 1–26 to 1–20 win over Clare in the [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster|2024 Munster SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41412799.html|title=Six of the best: Limerick make history with Munster final win over Clare |date=9 June 2024|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} After a trophy-less 2025 season, Limerick regained the National League title with a six-point win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in April 2026, with O'Connor claiming his second winners' medal.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41822540.html|title='If you get a chance to win, you have to take it' - Kiely's call that Cork shall not pass is heard|date=6 April 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He also took over from [[Aaron Gillane]] as Limerick's primary free-taker for the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2026/0716/1583681-limericks-old-heads-primed-after-season-of-renewal/|title=Limerick's old heads primed after season of renewal|date=18 July 2026|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=21 July 2026|first=|last=}} O'Connor later collected a third Munster SHC medal, as Limerick also regained that title with a 1–21 to 2–17 win over Cork in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/article/munster-shc-final-limerick-finish-strongly|title=Munster SHC Final: Limerick finish strongly|date=7 June 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He won a second All-Ireland SHC medal, after scoring 0–3 from frees, in the 1–29 to 1–18 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2026 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2026 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41882305.html|title=Dominant Limerick reclaim All-Ireland title with final victory over Galway|date=19 {{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2023}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=June 2023}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Shane O'Brien | irish = Seán Ó Briain | fullname = | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | nickname = The Bull | occupation = Student | county = Limerick | province = Munster | colleges = [[Mary Immaculate College]] | col_years = 2022-2026 | fitz = 1 | club = [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] | cl_position = | cl_years = 2022-present | cl_apps_points = 26 (11-121) | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Right corner-forward | ic_years = 2023-present | ic_apps_points = 16 (2-34) | ic_province = 3 | ic_all_ireland = 2 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = 9:31, 20 July 2026 | birth_date= 17 June 2004 | birth_place=[[Kilmallock]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Shane O'Brien''' (born 17 June 2004) is an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he plays with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[Kilmallock]], [[County Limerick]], O'Brien was educated at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick]]. He played in all grades of hurling during his time there and was joint-captain of the school's senior team that lost the [[2021–22 Harty Cup#Final|2022 Dr Harty Cup final]] to [[St Joseph's Secondary School, Tulla|St Joseph's Secondary School, Tulla]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40801248.html|title=Gritty Tulla make dreams reality with first Harty Cup win|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=5 February 2022|access-date=17 February 2018|first=Joe|last=Ó Muircheartaigh}} He subsequently won a [[Dr Croke Cup]] medal, following a 1–17 to 0–15 win over [[St Kieran's College]] in the [[2022 Croke Cup#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40831265.html|title=Kennedy delivers killer blow as Ardscoil Rís claim historic Croke Cup|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=17 March 2022|access-date=26 June 2023|first=Paul|last=Keane}} During his studies at [[Mary Immaculate College]], O'Brien was selected for the college's senior hurling team. He won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal in February 2024 following the 2–14 to 1–15 win over the [[University of Limerick]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41334088.html|title=Underdogs Mary I claim Fitzgibbon Cup, deny UL the three in a row|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=17 February 2024|accessdate=27 February 2024|first=Murt|last=Murphy}} ==Club career== O'Brien began his club career at juvenile and underage levels with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]]. He made his [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|senior team]] debut in July 2022 in a 2–23 to 2–09 win over [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/champions-kilmallock-impress-in-limerick-shc-as-ballybrown-and-south-liberties-also-win-7745876#:~:text=In%20Newcastle%20West%2C%20the%20repeat,ahead%20and%2010%2Dminutes%20played.|title=Champions Kilmallock impress in Limerick SHC as Ballybrown and South Liberties also win|date=30 July 2022|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=20 July 2026|first=|last=}} O'Brien ended his debut season with a 3–23 to 2–15 defeat by [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] in the [[2022 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|2022 Limerick SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/na-piarsaigh-too-good-for-kilmallock-in-limerick-shc-final/|title=Na Piarsaigh too good for Kilmallock in Limerick SHC Final|publisher=GAA website|date=30 October 2022|accessdate=31 October 2022|first=|last=}} ==Inter-county career== O'Brien first appeared on the inter-county scene for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]]. He won a [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] medal in his first season in December 2020, when Limerick beat [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in extra time by 2–22 to 0–25 in a [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Gaelic games|COVID-delayed]] [[2020 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster final|Munster MHC final]].{{cite news |url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-limerick-munster-mhc-final-5306959-Dec2020/|title=Limerick crowned Munster minor champions after overcoming Tipperary|access-date=11 August 2021 |work=The 42|date=20 December 2020}} O'Brien progressed to the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20 team]] in 2022 and won a [[Munster Under-20 Hurling Championship|Munster U20HC]] following a four-point win over Tipperary.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40865447.html|title=Treaty tyros tame Tipp to add to county's dominance |date=4 May 2022|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=20 July 2026|first=|last=}} He was at right corner-forward for Limerick's 0–19 to 0–18 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2022 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship final|2022 All-Ireland U20HC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/u-20-hurling/kilkenny-claim-all-ireland-u-20-title-after-edging-limerick-in-thrilling-final-41676137.html|title=Kilkenny claim All-Ireland U-20 title after edging Limerick in thrilling final|date=22 May 2022|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} O'Brien made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in a 1–27 to 2–18 [[National Hurling League]] win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in February 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41069537.html|title=First-half supremacy paves way for Limerick victory over Clare |date=11 February 2023|publisher=Irish Examienr|access-date=22 May 2023|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41098543.html|title=Potential dilemma on the horizon for Limerick's young stars|date=22 March 2023|publisher=Irish Examienr|access-date=22 May 2023|first=John|last=Fogarty}} He made a number of appearances throughout the league campaign, including in the 2–20 to 0–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 National Hurling League#Division 1|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2023/0409/1376051-classy-limerick-claim-league-honours-with-ease/|title=Classy Limerick claim league honours with ease|date=9 April 2023|publisher=RTÉ Sport|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} O'Brien was a member of the extended panel when Limerick beat Clare by 1–23 to 1–22 to win a record-equalling fifth consecutive [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] title in June 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41159863.html|title=Aaron Gillane on fire as Limerick edge Clare to secure fifth consecutive Munster title|date=11 June 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He was again part of teh extended panel when Limerick won a record-equalling fourth consecutive [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] title, following a 0–30 to 2–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history |date=23 July 2023|publisher=Irish pass is heard|date=6 April 2026|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} He later collected a third Munster SHC medal, as Limerick also regained that title with a 1–21 to 2–17 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2026 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41882305.html|title=Dominant Limerick reclaim All-Ireland title {{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=March 2024}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=March 2024}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code = Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Patrick O'Donovan | irish = Pádraig Ó Donnabháin | fullname = | height_ft = | height_in = | occupation = Student | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Effin GAA|Effin]] | cl_position = | cl_years = 2021-present | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | colleges = [[University of Limerick]] | col_years = | fitz = 0 | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Left corner-forward | ic_years = 2022-present | ic_apps_points = 1 (0-00) | ic_province = 0 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 0 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = 19:12, 25 May 2025 | birth_date = 2003 | birth_place = [[Effin]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Patrick O'Donovan''' (born 2003) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler.]] He plays with [[Effin GAA|Effin]] at the club level and lines out with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] at the inter-county level. ==Career== O'Donovan first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Effin GAA|Effin]] club. As a schoolboy at [[CBS Charleville]], he lined out in various schools' competitions.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/home/658072/school-with-ex-pupils-on-limerick-and-cork-teams-cant-lose-on-all-ireland-day.html|title=School with ex-pupils on Limerick and Cork teams can't lose on All-Ireland day! |publisher=Limerick Live|date=21 August 2021|accessdate=27 February 2024|first=|last=}} O'Donovan eventually progressed to the Effin adult team and won a [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] medal in his debut season in 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40728234.html|title=Patrick O'Donovan steers Effin to Limerick IHC title|publisher=Irish Examinmer|date=23 October 2021|accessdate=26 October 2021|first=John|last=Keogh}} He later lined out with [[University of Limerick]] in the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41334088.html|title=Underdogs Mary I claim Fitzgibbon Cup, deny UL the three in a row|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=17 February 2024|accessdate=27 February 2024|first=Murt|last=Murphy}} O'Donovan first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year stint with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|Limerick minor hurling team]]. He won consecutive [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] titles in 2019 and 2020.{{cite news |url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-triumph-in-electric-ireland-munster-mhc-final/|title=Limerick triumph in Electric Ireland Munster MHC Final|access-date=11 August 2021 |work=GAA website|date=30 June 2019}}{{cite news |url=https://www.the42.ie/tipperary-limerick-munster-mhc-final-5306959-Dec2020/|title=Limerick crowned Munster minor champions after overcoming Tipperary|access-date=11 August 2021 |work=The 42|date=20 December 2020}} O'Donovan immediately joined the [[All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship|under-20]] team, however, a series of injuries impacted on his progress. He was at left corner-forward when [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] beat Limerick in the [[2022 All-Ireland Under-20 Hurling Championship#All-Ireland final|2022 All-Ireland under-20 final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/u-20-hurling/kilkenny-claim-all-ireland-u-20-title-after-edging-limerick-in-thrilling-final-41676137.html|title=Kilkenny claim All-Ireland U-20 title after edging Limerick in thrilling final|date=22 May 2022|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} His third and final season in the under-20 grade saw him appointed [[Captain (sport)|vice-captain]].{{cite news|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/all-ireland-winner-included-as-limericl-reveal-u20-hurling-squad-for-2023-championship/#:~:text=The%20Limerick%20U20%20Hurling%20Panel,'Donovan%20as%20vice%2Dcaptain.|title=All-Ireland winner included as Limerick reveal U20 Hurling Squad for 2023 Championship|date=14 March 2023|publisher=Sporting Limerick|accessdate=2 March 2024|first=|last=}} After being added to the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] pre-season training panel, O'Donovan made his [[Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster Hurling Cup]] debut in a defeat of [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] in 2022.{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/720523/emphatic-limerick-hurlers-have-30-points-to-spare-over-kerry-in-munster-hurling-cup.html|title=Emphatic Limerick hurlers have {{short description|Irish hurler (1873–1942)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Irish English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox GAA player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Patrick O'Brien | irish = Pádraig Ó Briain | height = | nickname = | occupation = Labourer | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = Kilfinane | cl_position = | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Right wing-back | ic_years = 1897–1899 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 1 | all_stars = | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_place=[[Kilfinane]],
[[County Limerick]], Ireland | birth_date=2 March 1873 | death_date=10 November 1942 | death_place = Kilfinane,
County Limerick, Ireland }} '''Patrick O'Brien''' (2 March 1873 – 10 November 1942) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. He played with Kilfinane at club level and was part of the [[Limerick senior hurling team|Limerick]] team that won the [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1897 All-Ireland SHC]] title. ==Career== Born and raised in [[Kilfinane]], [[County Limerick]], O'Brien first played hurling with Kilfinane Hurling Club in the early years of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. He was part of the team that secured [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] title wins in 1897 and 1899.{{cite web|url=https://www.ouririshheritage.org/content/archive/place/kilfinane-coshlea-historical-society/topics-kilfinane-coshlea-historical-society/kilfinane-emmets-in-1897|title=Kilfinane All-Ireland Hurling Champions 1897|date=|publisher=Our Irish Heritage|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} Kilfinane were the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] representatives at inter-county level in 1897.{{cite web|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/limerick-win-first-munster-senior-hurling-championship-title-in-1897/|title=Limerick win first Munster Senior Hurling Championship title in 1897|date=1 June 2022|publisher=Limerick GAA website|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} O'Brien won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal that year, following a 4–09 to 1–06 win over [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/hurling/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|date=|publisher=Munster GAA website|accessdate=3 August 2026|first=|last=}} He was again part of the Limerick team that subsequently had a one-goal win over [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1897 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20111948.html|title=Sleeping giants bid to rekindle magical days at headquarters|date=12 February 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} O'Brien won a Croke Cup title in July 1899, following another victory over Kilkenny.{{cite web|url=https://www.ouririshheritage.org/content/archive/place/kilfinane-coshlea-historical-society/topics-kilfinane-coshlea-historical-society/kilfinane-emmets-in-1897|title=Kilfinane All-Ireland Hurling Champions 1897|date=|publisher=Our Irish Heritage|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} ==Personal life and death== His great-grandson, [[Andy O'Brien (footballer)|Andy O'Brien]], is a former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played for [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. He was a member of the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] squad at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/upbeat-obrien-braced-for-a-red-onslaught/a/149685469.html|title=Upbeat O'Brien braced for a Red onslaught|date=25 March 2000|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} O'Brien died on 10 November 1942, at the age of 69.{{cite web|url=https://www.ouririshheritage.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/12/p-obrien-1942.jpg|title=Death record of Patrick O'Brien|date=|publisher=Our Irish Heritage|accessdate=31 August 2026|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Kilfinane *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] (2): [[1897 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1897]], [[1899 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1899]] ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (1): [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1897]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (1): [[1897 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling CHampionship|1897]] *Croke Cup (1): 1897 ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Patrick O'Brien navigation boxes |list1= {{Limerick Hurling Team 1897}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Obrien, Patrick}} [[Category:1874 births]] [[Category:1942 deaths]] [[Category:Kilfinane hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship winners]] [[Category:19th-century Irish sportsmen]]

A renowned [[dual player]], he played both [[hurling]] and [[Gaelic football]] with his local club [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] and with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county teams in both codes from 1935 until 1949. He later played with the [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]] senior hurling team. ==Early life== Jackie Power was born in [[Annacotty]], [[County Limerick]] in 1916. He was educated at his local [[National school (Ireland)|national school]] where he was introduced to the game of [[hurling]] by his teacher. In his teens Power showed promise at athletics, however, he decided to forfeit this interest and concentrate on [[Gaelic games]]. ==Playing career== ===Club=== Power played his club hurling and football with his local club in [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] and enjoyed much success. Ahane, spearheaded by [[Mick Mackey]], [[John Mackey (hurler)|John Mackey]] and Power, were the kingpins of Limerick hurling at the time. He won his first senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county title]] with the club as a seventeen-year-old in 1933. It was the first of seven county championship victories in-a-row for Power and his club. He won an eighth county medal in 1942, the first of another seven county victories in-a-row. Power captured his fifteenth county hurling medal with Ahane in 1955. Power also enjoyed much success as a member of the Ahane senior football team. He won five senior [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|county football titles]] in-a-row with Ahane between 1935 and 1939. ===Inter-county=== Power played junior and senior football with Limerick in the 1930s, however, it was at hurling that he had major success. He made his senior inter-county debut in 1935, winning a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal that same year. Limerick were later defeated by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the All-Ireland final. By 1936 Power was a regular fixture on the team. He won a second Munster title that year before claiming his first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal with an emphatic victory over Kilkenny. Four years later in 1940 Power won his third Munster medal which was subsequently converted into a second All-Ireland medal. 1940 was a watershed for Limerick's hurlers. It was their last Munster and All-Ireland titles for 33 years. Power continued inter-county hurling until 1949, captaining Limerick to a [[National Hurling League]] title in 1947. It was his fourth NHL medal in all, with previous victories in 1936, 1937 and 1938. He won a Munster Junior Championship medal with Limerick in 1939. ===Provincial=== Power also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial hurling competition. He collected his first [[Railway Cup]] medal in his debut year in 1940 as Munster defeated [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]]. Power later collected five inter-provincial medals in-a-row between 1942 and 1946. He won a seventh and final Railway Cup medal in 1948. ==Post-playing career== After retiring from playing Power's work with [[CIÉ]], the Irish railway company, caused him to move from Limerick to [[Tralee]]. He continued, however, to maintain a keen interest in Gaelic games and became involved with the [[Austin Stacks]] club in his adopted home. In 1969 Power's skill and talent was recognised when he was presented with the [[Cú Chulainn]] award for the outstanding hurler of the past. In the early 1970s he became involved as coach to his own native Limerick. Power first tasted success as a coach in 1971 when his team captured the National League title andboth Munster and All-Ireland victory in 1973. Power also saw his son, [[Ger Power]], win a record eight [[All-Ireland Senior Football Championship|All-Ireland]] medals with [[Kerry GAA|Kerry]]’s footballers between 1975 and 1986. His daughter Sheila Power also won an ALL-Ireland medal whilst playing for the [http://www.kerryladiesfootball.com/ Kerry Ladies] and his grandson [[Stephen McNamara]] played on the [[Clare GAA|Clare]] All-Ireland Senior Hurling winning team in 1995. In 1991 Power's reputation as one of the all-time greats was recognised yet again when he was the recipient of the All-Time [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] Award. Jackie Power died on 23 February 1994. In 1996, a life-size bronze statue of him was erected in his native Annacotty. {{s-start}} {{s-ach|aw}} {{succession box| before=[[John Joe Doyle]]
