Tommy Quaid.text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2015}} {{EngvarB|date=September 2015}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Tommy Quaid | irish = Tomás Mac Uaid | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 10 | occupation = Fitter | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]]
[[Effin GAA|Effin]] | cl_years = 1972–1994
1994–1998 | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Goalkeeper | ic_years = 1976–1993 | ic_apps_points = 36 (0-00) | ic_province = 2 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 3 | all_stars = 1 | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_place=[[Charleville, County Cork|Charleville]], County Cork, Ireland | birth_date={{Birth date|df=yes|1957|4|23}} | death_date={{death date and age|df=yes|1998|10|10|1957|4|23}} }} '''Tommy Quaid''' (23 April 1957 – 10 October 1998) was an Irish sportsperson. He played [[hurling]] at various times with his local clubs [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] and [[Effin GAA|Effin]] and was the goalkeeper on the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team from 1976 until 1993. Quaid was regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers of his generation.{{cite web|url=http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1998/10/12/shead.htm|title=Quaid loses fight for life|publisher=[[Irish Examiner]]|date=12 October 1998|access-date=6 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629073517/http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/1998/10/12/shead.htm|archive-date=29 June 2011|df=dmy-all}} ==Biography== Tommy Quaid was born in [[Charleville, County Cork]] in 1957.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17661|title=Tommy Quaid|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=1 January 1993|access-date=5 December 2008}} The son of Bridie (née Collins) and [[Jack Quaid (hurler)|Jack Quaid]], he was born into a family that had a strong association with hurling.{{cite book| first=Brendan| last=Fullam| title=Captains of the Ash| publisher=Wolfhound Press| year=2002| isbn=978-0-86327-900-3 | pages=269}} His father was one of the key players on the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] team which beat [[London GAA|London]] in the 1954 [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] junior final. He won a senior [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] title the following year when a [[Mick Mackey]]-trained team shocked [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the provincial decider.''Captains of the Ash'' p. 269 Quaid's five children all followed in their father's footsteps on the hurling field. Séamus Quaid was a stalwart of the Feohanagh club until he emigrated to Australia. John Quaid went on to represent his county at minor and under 21 levels while Pat Quaid also served as a member of the Limerick under-21 hurling panel. Noreen Quaid also represented her County and local club in Feoghangh. The Quaid family moved to [[Feohanagh]], [[County Limerick]] when Tommy was just a few years old. He was educated at the local [[National school (Ireland)|national school]] before later attending secondary school in nearby [[Newcastle West]]. Quaid trained as a fitter with the local Golden Vale company and later set up his own engineering business. In retirement from inter-county hurling he built up his business. In 1998, however, tragedy struck. While working on the [[Credit Union]] building in Charleville, the place of his birth, Quaid fell twenty feet from some scaffolding and landed on his back, hitting his head in the process. He was immediately rushed to hospital, however, he died from his injuries several days later on 10 October 1998.''Captains of the Ash'' p. 268 Quaid's sons Tomás and Nicky represented Limerick at underage levels and were members of the [[Effin]] team that lost the 2007 Limerick Junior 'A' hurling final to a [[Caherline GAA|Caherline]] team. [[Nickie Quaid]] now plays in goal for the Limerick senior hurling team. ==Playing career== ===Club=== Quaid played his club hurling with his local [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] club. In spite of being a goalkeeper at inter-county level he played as a forward during most of his club career and, more often than not, he also served as the team's free-taker. Quaid's club career got off to a less than auspicious start. After losing back-to-back minor finals he subsequently joined the club's under-21 team. Success, however, also eluded him in this grade as he suffered the heartbreak of losing four consecutive Under-21 West Division finals. Quaid's most successful hour came in 1990 when he captained Feohanagh-Castlemahon to a West Limerick senior hurling title. Unfortunately he never won a county senior title. In later years he played his club hurling with [[Effin GAA|Effin]], where he won three South Limerick junior hurling titles. ===Inter-county=== Quaid's performances at club level brought him to the attentions of the inter-county selectors. He was passed over for inter-county duty on the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] minor team in 1973, however, he joined the side the following year as goalkeeper. He spent an unsuccessful two-year spell with the Limerick minors. Quaid later joined the county under-21 hurling team, however, in spite of a disastrous [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] final appearance in 1977, he enjoyed little success.{{cite book| first=Des| last=Donegan| title=The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games| publisher=DBA Publications| year=2005| isbn=978-0-9518704-4-0 | page=48}} In 1975 Quaid joined the Limerick senior hurling team, making his debut in a [[National Hurling League]] quarter-final against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. The young goalkeeper, however, took stage fright and had a nightmare of a game. By 1976 Quaid had redeemed himself and took over from [[Séamus Horgan]] as first-choice goalkeeper for the championship. Quaid's side contested the Munster final 1976, however, Cork were victorious on that occasion as Limerick went into decline.{{cite book| first=Des| last=Donegan| title=The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games| publisher=DBA Publications| year=2005| isbn=978-0-9518704-4-0 | page=26}} They were completely trounced again in 1979 on a score line of 2–14 to 0–9 as Cork captured a record-equaling fifth Munster title in-a-row. In 1980 Cork were going for a sixth Munster Championship in succession. For the fourth time in six years Limerick provided the opposition in the provincial decider. After an exciting seventy minutes Cork's hopes were dashed by 2–14 to 2–10 as Quiad collected a first Munster winners' medal. This victory allowed Limerick a save passage to the All-Ireland final where [[Galway GAA|Galway]] were the opponents. Galway got off to a good start and took a 2–7 to 1–5 lead at half-time. [[Éamonn Cregan]] had other ideas and single-handedly launched the Limerick counter-attack. Over the course of the game he scored 2–7, including an overhead goal and a point in which he showed the ball to [[Conor Hayes]] and nonchalantly drove the ball over the bar. It was not enough to stem the tide and Galway went on to win the game.{{cite book| first=Eoghan| last=Corry| title=The GAA Book of Lists| publisher=Hodder Headline Ireland| year=2005| isbn=978-0-340-89695-2 | pages=360}} It was the county's first All-Ireland title since 1923 and, ironically, Limerick were the defeated team on that occasion as well. Limerick retained their provincial crown in 1981. Clare were defeated on that occasion by 3–12 to 2–9 giving Quiad his second Munster medal. The subsequent All-Ireland semi-final saw Limerick take on [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]. It was the first meeting of these two sides in the history of the hurling championship. In a low-scoring game both sides finished level and a replay was necessary. The second game took place a fortnight later at [[Croke Park]] and it turned out to be an exciting affair. Both sides upped their game, however, Limerick were still defeated by 4–16 to 2–17. Following back-to-back Munster triumphs Limerick went into decline in the championship. Quaid's side did have some notable victories in the National League. In 1984 he won his first National League medal following a 3–16 to 1–9 victory over [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]. The win was all the more special as it was the centenary year of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. A second National League title was collected by Quaid in 1985 following a trouncing of [[Clare GAA|Clare]]. After some time out of the limelight Quaid won a third National League medal in 1992 following a one-point victory over Tipperary. Limerick later qualified for the Munster final, however, Cork were the victors on that occasion. In spite of ending up on the losing side Quaid's championship performance earned him his first, and only, [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award. Following the completion of the 1993 Munster championship Quaid decided to retire after 18 consecutive championship seasons as goalkeeper. He was replaced on the Limerick team by his cousin, [[Joe Quaid]]. ===Interprovincial=== Quaid was also a regular on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial hurling team between 1979 and 1992. In 1981 he collected his first [[Railway Cup]] medal following a ten-point defeat of arch-rivals [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]]. A second defeat of Leinster in 1984 gave him a second Railway Cup title while [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] were accounted for in 1985. Quaid won a fourth and final Railway Cup winners' medal in 1992.{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/railwaycuphurling.html|title=Munster Railway Cup Hurling Teams|publisher=[[Munster GAA]]|access-date=5 December 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080719201124/http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/railwaycuphurling.html |archive-date = 19 July 2008}} ===Poc Fada=== Quaid also won numerous awards as an individual and in pairs competitions in the [[All-Ireland Poc Fada Championship]]. In 1983 Quaid and Joe Shortt from [[Armagh GAA|Armagh]] won the pairs competition with 154 pucks. Three years later in 1986 he collected another pairs title, this time with John Kelly of [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] as his partner. Quaid and Des Donnelly of [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] won the title in 1990, while together with Michael Sahughnessy of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] he retained the pairs competition title in 1991. That same year Quaid also won the All-Ireland title in the singles competition. ==Managerial career== In retirement from playing at inter-county level, Quaid became involved in the management side of hurling. In 1998 he guided the Limerick intermediate hurlers to a [[Munster Intermediate Hurling Championship|Munster]] title in that grade following a 2–11 to 0–15 defeat of Tipperary. Quaid's side later qualified for the All-Ireland final, with Kilkenny providing the opposition. Unfortunately, that game took place in the same week that Quaid suffered his fatal accident at work. He died on the same day that game was taking place, however, his emotion-filled Limerick team went on to win the game by 4–16 to 2–17. A poem was written by Garry McMahon in the wake of his death called ''Lament for Tommy Quaid''.{{cite web|url=http://www.bebo.com/Profile.jsp?MemberId=8539942232|title =Feohanagh-CastlemahonGAA|publisher=bebo.com|access-date=13 September 2009}} == Tommy Quaid Perpetual Cup == On 1 May 2008, the Iverahain Golf Society launched the inaugural Tommy Quaid Perpetual Cup in 'The Hurlers', [[Castletroy]], [[County Limerick]]. Membership of the society is confined to men who have worn the hurling Number 1 jersey at senior inter-county level for one of the six Munster counties. The Tommy Quaid Perpetual Cup is awarded to the winner of this annual competition and the outing will alternate between the six Munster counties over the coming years. Present and former hurling goalkeepers from the entire province have jumped at the opportunity of participating in this novel outing. The event was launched by former Clare goalkeeper [[Davy Fitzgerald]]. Also in attendance was [[Brian Murray (hurler)|Brian Murray]] (Limerick goalkeeper) and [[Donal Óg Cusack]] (Cork goalkeeper).{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickindependent.com/sport/sport/sport-in-brief-%11-14th-may-2008/1/|title=Sport in Brief – 14th May 2008 |publisher=[[Limerick Independent]]|date=14 May 2008|access-date=13 September 2009}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==Teams== {{Empty section|date=March 2013}} == External links == * [http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/ireland/1999/0127/99012700012.html Irish Times Accident Report] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20080801004015/http://www.gaa.ie/page/poc_fada.html Poc Fada Role of Honour Winners] * [http://www.irishtimes.com/newspaper/sport/1998/1014/98101400155.html Irish Times "Quaid – an appreciation"] * [https://web.archive.org/web/20080719201124/http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/railwaycuphurling.html Railway Cup] *[http://www.limerickcity.ie/Library/LocalStudies/LocalStudiesFiles/S/SportsPeople// ''Tommy Quaid in 'Sports People' file at Limerick City Library, Ireland''] {{Limerick Hurling Team 1980}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1984}} {{1992 Hurling All Stars}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Quaid, Tommy}} [[Category:1957 births]] [[Category:1998 deaths]] [[Category:Feohanagh-Castlemahon hurlers]] [[Category:Effin hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]] [[Category:Hurling goalkeepers]] [[Category:Hurling managers]] [[Category:Quaid family|Tommy]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

Joe Quaid.text:
{{Short description|Limerick hurling goalkeeper and manager}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Joe Quaid | irish = Seosamh Mac Uaid | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 10 | occupation = GAA coaching officer | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh]]
[[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] | cl_position = Goalkeeper | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = Goalkeeper | ic_years = 1991–2002 | ic_apps_points = 18 (0–0) | ic_province = 2 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 2 | cl_update = | ic_update = 22:22, 16 September 2018 | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1972|4|10|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Feohanagh]], [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Joseph M. Quaid''' (born 10 April 1972) is an Irish [[List of hurling managers|hurling manager]] and former [[hurling|player]]. He was the manager of the [[Westmeath county hurling team|Westmeath senior team]] in 2019.{{cite web|url=https://www.westmeathindependent.ie/sport/roundup/articles/2018/09/14/4161940-new-era-for-westmeath-as-cooney-and-quaid-get-the-green-light/|title=New era for Westmeath as Cooney and Quaid get the green light|date=14 September 2018|publisher=Westmeath Independent|access-date=16 September 2018|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}} Born in [[Feohanagh]], [[County Limerick]], Quaid was introduced to hurling by his father, an [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal winner with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] junior team. At schools level he played with Newcastle West Vocational School, while simultaneously playing at juvenile and underage levels with [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh]]. Eventually playing with the club's senior team, Quaid subsequently transferred to the [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] club where he won one [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|championship]] medal. Quaid made his debut on the inter-county scene when he first linked up with the Limerick minor team. He later joined the under-21 side but enjoyed little success in either of these grades. Quaid made his senior debut during the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1994 championship]]. He went on to play a key role for Limerick as goalkeeper during a relatively successful era, and won two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and two [[National Hurling League]] medals. He was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up on two occasions. As a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team, Quaid won two [[Railway Cup]] medals, one on the field of play and one as a non-playing substitute. Quaid retired from inter-county hurling following the conclusion of the [[2000 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2000 championship]], but returned two years later for one final season.{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/quaid-quits-limerick-26107386.html|title=Quaid quits Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=23 October 2000|access-date=17 February 2016|first=Martin|last=Breheny}}{{cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/limerick-s-quaid-returns-1.343001|title=Limerick's Quaid returns|publisher=Irish Times|date=20 December 2001|access-date=17 February 2016}}{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/quaid-returns-from-early-retirement-26060717.html|title=Quaid returns from early retirement|publisher=Irish Independent|date=7 January 2002|access-date=17 February 2016}} In retirement from playing, Quaid has become involved in team management and coaching. At club level he has taken charge of the Murroe-Boher senior team, guiding them to the semi-finals of the championship. At inter-county level he is a two-time All-Ireland-winning manager, firstly with the Limerick under-16 team and later with the Limerick [[All-Ireland Intermediate Camogie Championship|intermediate camogie]] team. Quaid was appointed manager of the Kildare senior team on 6 October 2015. ==Early life== Joe Quaid was born in Ahawilk [[Feohanagh]], [[County Limerick]] in 1972. He was born into a family that had a strong association with [[hurling]]. His father, [[Jim Quaid]], was a key player on the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] team which beat [[London GAA|London]] in the 1954 junior [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] final. His uncle, [[Jack Quaid (hurler)|Jack Quaid]], was also a member of this side and the brothers also won Munster Senior Hurling medals in 1955, when a young Limerick side surprised a more experienced Clare side in the final. Their first cousin, [[Seamus Quaid]], also played on Limerick senior teams and also played with Wexford, with whom he won an All Ireland senior medal in 1960. Joe succeeded his cousin playing position, [[Tommy Quaid]], who was the goalkeeper on the Limerick team from 1976 until 1993.{{fact|date=December 2021}} ==Playing career== ===Club=== Quaid played his club [[hurling]] with Feohanagh and Murroe-Boher. He enjoyed some underage success with the side but failed to win a senior [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]]. ===Inter-county=== ====Minor and under-21==== Quaid first played for Limerick at minor level.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145462/Limerick-minor-hurlers---trying.html|title=Limerick minor hurlers - trying since 1985|date=7 September 2014|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Joel|last=Slattery}} He made his first appearance for the team on 6 July 1988 in a 4-10 to 2-06 [[1988 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]] defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. On 2 July 1989, Quaid lined out in goal for Limerick's 2-13 to 2-12 defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[1989 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster final]]. His third and final season on the minor team ended with a [[1990 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final defeat]] by Clare. Quaid subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team. On 7 August 1991, he was in goal for Limerick's 0-17 to 1-07 defeat by Cork in the [[1991 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster final]]. On 23 July 1993, Quaid made his last appearance for the under-21 team when he lined out in goal in a 1-18 to 3-09 [[1993 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster final]] defeat by Cork. ====Senior==== Quaid joined the Limerick senior team during the [[1991-92 National Hurling League|1991-92 National League]] as understudy to regular goalkeeper [[Tommy Quaid]]. On 10 May 1992, he won a [[National Hurling League]] medal as a non-playing substitute after a 0-14 to 0-13 defeat of Tipperary in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/317244/the-day-waterford-hurling-legend-john-mullane-supported-limerick.html|title=The day Waterford hurling legend John Mullane supported Limerick!|date=7 June 2018|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} On 17 October 1993, Quaid made his debut with the Limerick senior team in a 1-13 to 0-13 [[National Hurling League]] defeat of Cork. Later that season he made his first appearance in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]], before winning his first provincial winners' medal after a 0-25 to 2-10 defeat of Clare in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/110719/Munster-Final---20th-anniversary.html|title=Munster Final - 20th anniversary of Limerick's Munster SHC win of 1994|date=12 July 2014|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} On 3 September 1994, Quaid lined out in goal for Limerick's [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] meeting with [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]]. With five minutes of normal time remaining, Limerick were leading by 2-13 to 1-11 and looked to be heading to their first title in 21 years when Offaly were awarded a free 20 metres from the goal. Quaid later admitted that he was to blame for the resultant goal in that he didn't organise his defence well enough to stop a low-struck free from [[Johnny Dooley (hurler)|Johnny Dooley]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/tale-of-the-sorrowful-mysteries-1.754563|title=Tale of the sorrowful mysteries|date=10 October 2009|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Keith|last=Duggan}} He was erroneously blamed for Offaly's second goal after what was described as a quick and errant puck-out leading to [[Pat O'Connor (hurler)|Pat O'Connor]] putting Offaly a point ahead. Quaid later described the puck-out: "I didn’t rush back to the goals. I went back and picked up the ball, walked behind the goals like I normally would. [[Ger Hegarty|Hegarty]] was out in the middle of the field on his own. I dropped the ball into his hand 70 yards out from goal. He caught the ball and in contact the ball squirted out of his hands." Because the television coverage was still showing a replay of the first goal, very few people got to see the build up to the second and when live transmission was resumed, the sliotar was still dropping towards Pat O'Connor leading people to assume that Quaid rushed his puck-out.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-hurling-home-to-hope-and-hardship-1.1795923|title=Limerick hurling: home to hope and hardship|date=15 May 2014|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Keith|last=Duggan}} Limerick went on to lose the game by 3-16 to 2-13.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/yourview/arid-10098744.html|title=Limerick: where broken dreams are a way of life|date=15 August 2009|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=17 September 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/offaly-limerick-1994-1653691-Sep2014/|title=20 years ago today Offaly produced THAT All-Ireland final comeback against Limerick|date=4 September 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} Quaid ended the season by winning the [[GAA All Stars Awards|All Star]] goalkeeping award. On 14 July 1996, Quaid won a second Munster Championship medal in three seasons after a 4-07 to 0-16 defeat of Tipperary in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/shannonsiders-ahead-on-the-replay-count-35204.html|title=Shannonsiders ahead on the replay count|date=16 June 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Jim|last=O'Sullivan}} He later lined out in his second [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] when Limerick faced [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] on 1 September 1996. Quaid was praised for making a series of spectacular saves during the game, however, Limerick were eventually defeated by 1-13 to 0-14.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/wexford-overcome-sending-off-to-end-long-wait-for-title-1.82255|title=Wexford overcome sending off to end long wait for title|date=2 September 1996|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Seán|last=Moran}}{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/wexford-hurlers-1996-where-are-they-now-2955096-Sep2016/|title=20 years ago today the Wexford hurlers won the All-Ireland... but where are they now?|date=1 September 2016|publisher=The 42|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} Quaid ended the season with a second All Star Award. On 27 April 1997, Quaid suffered a serious injury in a National League game against [[Laois GAA|Laois]] when the sliotar struck Quaid in the groin at high speed following a penalty attempt by [[David Cuddy]]. His right testicle exploded on impact while half of the other testicle had to be surgically removed.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/columnists/kieran-shannon/for-love-of-limerick-195205.html|title=KIERAN SHANNON: For love of Limerick|date=26 May 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Kieran|last=Shannon}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/it-all-boils-down-to-who-is-best-positioned-when-this-kilkenny-team-eventually-do-fall-29454047.html|title=It all boils down to who is best positioned when this Kilkenny team eventually do fall|date=28 July 2013|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Damian|last=Lawlor}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/last-man-standing-keeps-us-posted-on-netminders-25966438.html|title='Last Man Standing' keeps us posted on netminders|date=16 September 2005|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}} In spite of the injury, Quaid won a second National League medal on 5 October 1997 after a 1-12 to 1-09 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/revamped-limerick-can-take-league-title-1.112811|title=Revamped Limerick can take League title|date=4 October 1997|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Seán|last=Moran}} Quaid announced his retirement from inter-county hurling on 22 October 2000. At 28, he cited the growing levels of commitment required as the principal reason for his retirement.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/quaid-quits-limerick-26107386.html|title=Quaid quits Limerick|date=23 October 2000|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 September 2018|first=Martin|last=Breheny}} After a year out of the game, Quaid reversed his decision and returned to the panel in January 2002.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/limerick-s-quaid-returns-1.343001|title=Limerick's Quaid returns|date=20 December 2001|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=17 September 2018}} He made seven appearances throughout the league and championship that season before retiring for the second time at the end of the season. ===Inter-provincial=== Like both his cousin [[Tommy Quaid]] and his Uncle [[Jack Quaid (hurler)|Jack Quaid]] before him, Joe was also a member of the Munster Team in 1995 and 1997. In 1995 he won a [[Railway Cup]] medal as Munster's goalkeeper. Munster defeated Leinster 2-25 to 5-12 in the semi-final of that year, before going on to beat Ulster 0-13 to 1-09 in the final. ==Management and coaching career== ===Murroe-Boher=== Quaid first became involved in management when he took charge of the [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Morroe-Boher]] senior team, In 2007, he guided the team to the semi-final of the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Championship]] where they were defeated by [[Adare GAA|Adare]].{{cite web|url=http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/2007/10/22/story45853.asp|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120707003349/http://archives.tcm.ie/irishexaminer/2007/10/22/story45853.asp|url-status=dead|archive-date=2012-07-07|title=Fitzgerald firepower crucial as cool Adare surge into final|date=22 October 2007|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=13 September 2009}} ===Limerick=== ====Under-16==== Quaid took over as manager of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick under-16 hurling team]] in 2010. In his third season in charge he guided the team to the All-Ireland title after a 3-20 to 0-08 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final at [[Semple Stadium]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaelic-games/87956/Limerick-U-16-hurlers-claim-All.html|title=Limerick U-16 hurlers claim All Ireland glory|date=8 September 2012|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=16 September 2018}} The following day he was informed by the Limerick County Board that he had been overlooked to progress with the team as manager of the Limerick minor hurling team for 2013, a decision which prompted him to decline the position of selector.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/joe-quaid-limerick-camogie-manager-all-ireland-intermediate-final-1656170-Sep2014/|title=I'd never been to a camogie match before I took charge of the Limerick girls - Joe Quaid|date=11 September 2014|publisher=The 42|access-date=16 September 2018|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}} ====Camogie==== In 2013 Quaid took charge of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick intermediate camogie team]]. On 5 May 2013, he guided the team to a [[National Camogie League#Junior National League / Division 2|National League Division 2]] title and promotion after a 3-14 to 0-10 defeat of [[Kildare GAA|Kildare]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/191702|title=Limerick win Camogie League title|date=7 May 2013|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=16 September 2018}} On 15 September 2013, Quaid's Limerick to the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Camogie Championship|All-Ireland Intermediate Championship]] final where they were beaten by [[Galway GAA|Galway]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/galway-limerick-all-ireland-intermediate-camogie-final-report-1084408-Sep2013/|title=Galway crowned intermediate camogie champions after victory over Limerick|date=15 September 2013|publisher=The 42|access-date=16 September 2018|first=Cormac|last=O'Malley}} On 14 September 2014, Quaid's Limerick intermediate team lined out in a second successive All-Ireland Intermediate Championship final. A 1-12 to 0-10 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] secured the title and promotion to the [[All-Ireland Senior Camogie Championship|All-Ireland Senior Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/camogie/limerick-crowned-intermediate-camogie-champions-with-victory-over-kilkenny-30585747.html|title=Limerick crowned intermediate camogie champions with victory over Kilkenny|date=14 September 2014|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=16 September 2018}} Quaid's third season in charge saw Limerick finish in fourth position in Group 1 of the All-Ireland Championship. He stepped down as manager in August 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickpost.ie/2015/08/17/camogie-joe-quaid-to-leave-limerick-camogie/|title=Camogie – Joe Quaid to leave Limerick Camogie|date=17 August 2015|publisher=Limerick Post|access-date=16 September 2018|first=Donal|last=O'Sullivan}} ===Kildare=== On 6 October 2015, Quaid was appointed manager of the [[Kildare county hurling team|Kildare senior hurling team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/cian-oneill-joe-quaid-kildare-2372582-Oct2015/|title=Kildare have appointed new senior football and hurling team managers|date=7 October 2015|publisher=The 42|access-date=16 September 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} His first season in charge saw Kildare finish in fifth position in [[2016 National Hurling League#Division 2A|Division 2A]] of the [[National Hurling League]] while the team reached the semi-final of the [[2016 Christy Ring Cup|Christy Ring Cup]] where they were beaten by eventual winners [[Meath county hurling team|Meath]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/mcgowan-keeps-the-royals-on-the-march-34737383.html|title=McGowan keeps the Royals on the march|date=23 May 2016|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=16 September 2018}} Quaid's second season in charge saw Kildare finish in third position in [[2017 National Hurling League#Division 2A|Division 2A]] of the league and narrowly miss out on a place in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/sport/gaa/antrim/antrim-are-looking-up-after-showing-their-mettle-35504054.html|title=Antrim are looking up after showing their mettle|date=6 March 2017|publisher=Belfast Telegraph|access-date=16 September 2018|first=David|last=Mohan}} In the [[2017 Christy Ring Cup|subsequent Christy Ring Cup]], Kildare reached the quarter-finals where they were defeated again by eventual champions [[Carlow county hurling team|Carlow]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/0506/873022-christy-ring-nick-rackard-round-up/|title=Christy Ring: Carlow ease past depleted Kildare - Nicky Rackard and Lory Meagher round-up|date=6 May 2017|publisher=RTÉ News|access-date=16 September 2018}} Quaid's Kildare lost all of their group stage games during the [[2018 National Hurling League#Division 2A|2018 league]] and were relegated to Division 2B. On 23 June 2018, he guided Kildare to a 3-19 to 1-11 defeat of [[London county hurling team|London]] to win their second ever [[Christy Ring Cup]] title.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0623/972695-kildare-overpower-london-to-win-christy-ring-cup/|title=Kildare overpower London to win Christy Ring Cup|date=23 June 2018|publisher=RTÉ News|access-date=16 September 2018}} Quaid stepped down as Kildare manager on 29 August 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/joe-quaid-kildare-hurling-4208148-Aug2018/|title=Limerick's Quaid steps aside from Christy Ring Cup champions after three seasons in charge|date=29 August 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=16 September 2018|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}} ===Westmeath=== On 13 September 2018, Quaid was appointed manager of the [[Westmeath senior hurling team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.westmeathindependent.ie/sport/roundup/articles/2018/09/14/4161940-new-era-for-westmeath-as-cooney-and-quaid-get-the-green-light/|title=New era for Westmeath as Cooney and Quaid get the green light|date=14 September 2018|publisher=Westmeath Independent|access-date=16 September 2018|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}} He led the Midlanders to a National Hurling League Div 2A title in the spring by overcoming Kerry in the final. The win secured the Lake County's return to Division 1 hurling at the first time in 32 years. He later seen his side qualify for the [[Joe McDonagh Cup]] decider where Westmeath lost out to Laois in Corke Park. In the All-Ireland preliminary quarter-finals Quaids side went down to Cork on a 1-40 to 0-20 scoreline. He also led Westmeath to Kehoe Cup honours. Quaid left as manager of Westmeath in July 2019 after one year in charge.{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/quaid-axed-as-westmeath-boss-38341100.html|title =Quaid '''Andrew O'Shaughnessy''' (born 30 November 1984 in [[Kilmallock]], [[County Limerick]]) is an Irish sportsperson.  He plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and was a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team from 2002 to 2011.

==Biography==

Andrew O'Shaughnessy was born in [[Kilmallock]], [[County Limerick]] in 1984.  He was educated at his local primary school and later attended the famous [[St. Colman's College, Fermoy]] in [[Fermoy]], [[County Cork]], a virtual nursery for young hurling talent.

Here his hurling skills were first developed and he became a star on the college's various hurling teams.  O'Shaughnessy enjoyed a very successful hurling career, beginning by capturing three [[Dean Ryan Cup]] titles in-a-row in 2000, 2001 and 2002.  By this stage he was also a star on the St. Colman's senior hurling team.  O'Shaughnessy won his first [[Dr. Harty Cup]] winners' medal in 2001.<ref>{{cite book| first=Des| last=Donegan| title=The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games| publisher=DBA Publications| year=2005| page=227}}</ref> He later collected his first [[Dr. Croke Cup|All-Ireland]] colleges' title when St. Colman's defeated Dublin Colleges in the final of that competition.<ref name="Gaelic Games' p. 226">''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' p. 226</ref> O'Shaughnessy captured a second Harty Cup title in 2002 before later lining out in a second All-Ireland colleges' final.<ref name="Gaelic Games' p. 227">''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' p. 227</ref> His scoring exploits in that game were spectacular.  [[Gort]] [[Congregation of Christian Brothers|CBS]] provided the opposition, however, O'Shaughnessy scored 2–8 of a total score of 2–10.<ref>{{Cite news|title=An iron fist in a green, velvet glove |publisher=[[Sunday Tribune]] |date=2 September 2007 }}</ref> It was his second All-Ireland winners' medal.  2003 saw O'Shaughnessy win a third consecutive Harty Cup winners' medal.<ref name="Gaelic Games' p. 227" /> The subsequent All-Ireland final saw St. Colman's take on St. Kieran's, however, victory went to the Kilkenny team on that occasion.<ref name="Gaelic Games' p. 226" />

After completing a successful [[Irish Leaving Certificate|Leaving Certificate]] at St. Colman's O'Shaughnessy became a cadet in the [[Irish Army]].  He was commissioned as an army lieutenant and currently holds the rank of Commandant.<ref name="Irish Independent">{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/star-cadet-of-green-army-becomes-a-field-marshal-1055258.html|title=Star cadet of green army becomes a field marshal|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|date=10 July 2007|access-date=6 December 2008}}</ref>

==Playing career==

===Club===

O'Shaughnessy plays his club hurling with his local [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club and has enjoyed success.  As a member of the club's minor hurling team he captured three consecutive [[Limerick Minor Hurling Championship|county titles]] in 2000, 2001 and 2002.  The latter final saw O'Shaughnessy give a scoring exhibition once again.  In that game they beat [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] by 4–11 to 2–11. Three of their 11 points were scored in a gripping last 10 minutes, the previous 4–9 had come from the hurley of Andrew O'Shaughnessy in a glorious 50-minute spell of individual brilliance.<ref name="Irish Independent" />

O'Shaughnessy later joined the club's under-21 team, however, he enjoyed little success in this grade.  Around the same time he joined the Kilmallock senior team.  He lined out in the senior [[Limerick Minor Hurling Championship|county final]] in 2005, however, [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] were victorious on that occasion by 2–15 to 2–12.

===Minor and under-21===

O'Shaughnessy first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] minor hurling team in the early 2000s.  He had little success in this grade and later joined the county's under-21 team where he first tasted inter-county glory.  2002 saw Limerick reach the provincial decider for the third year in-a-row, however, it was O'Shaughnessy's first year as full member of the team.  After an exciting contest with [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]], which included extra-time, Limerick won the game by 1–20 to 2–14.<ref>''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' p. 48</ref> It was his O'Shaughnessy's first [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] under-21 winners' medal.  For the third year in-a-row Limerick lined out in the All-Ireland final with [[Galway GAA|Galway]] providing the opposition.  O'Shaughnessy's side powered to a 3–17 to 0–8 victory.<ref>''The Complete Handbook of Gaelic Games'' p. 42</ref> It was his first, and only, [[All-Ireland Under 21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] under-21 winners' medal.

===Senior===

In 2003 O'Shaughnessy made his senior championship debut in a Munster semi-final against [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].  Both sides drew level on that occasion, however, Limerick lost the replay and continued their streak of bad luck that had lasted since 2001 when they were dumped out of the championship in the All-Ireland qualifiers.  The next few years proved difficult for both O'Shaughnessy and for Limerick.  In spite of coming close to creating some hurling upsets, defeat seemed to be Limerick's lot.

In 2006 Limerick remained unbeaten throughout the entire [[National Hurling League]] campaign and qualified for the final against [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]].  It was an unhappy day for Limerick as 'the Cats' won the game by 3–11 0–14.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/2006/0430/kilkenny.html|title=Kilkenny claim league title in Thurles|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=30 April 2006|access-date=1 December 2008}}</ref> In spite of some success in the league, Limerick's championship form was still below par.

All this changed in 2007 when Limerick had one of their best seasons.  That year Limerick faced near neighbours Tipperary in the semi-final of the Munster championship.  That game ended in a draw with both sides scoring 1–19.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=78545|title=Tipp and Limerick in thrilling draw|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=10 June 2007|access-date=1 December 2008}}</ref> The replay saw Limerick in arrears by ten points at half-time, however, Limerick rallied to level the game at the end of normal time.  A period of extra time had to be played and O'Shaughnessy turned out to be the hero as he scored the equalising point which meant that the sides had to play for a third time.  Once again, Limerick looked vulnerable at times during the game, however, they grinded out a victory with a score line of 0–22 to 2–13.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=79318|title=Third time lucky for Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=24 June 2007|access-date=1 December 2008}}</ref> It was Limerick's first win in the Munster championship since 2001. O'Shaughnessy later lined out against [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the Munster final, however, they were defeated on a score line of 3–17 to 1–14.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=80125|title=Limerick haunted by Dan the man|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=8 July 2007|access-date=1 December 2008}}</ref> These two sides later met again in the All-Ireland semi-final, however, manager [[Richie Bennis]] had done his homework and masterminded a magnificent 5–11 to 2–15 victory over the Munster champions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=81789|title=All-Ireland SHC semi-final: Goal-den Limerick stun Waterford|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=12 August 2007|access-date=1 December 2008}}</ref> This victory allowed O'shaughnessy's side to play Kilkenny in the championship decider.  Unfortunately, Limerick got off to a bad start with goalkeeper [[Brian Murray (hurler)|Brian Murray]] letting in two goals by [[Eddie Brennan]] and [[Henry Shefflin]] in the first ten minutes.  Limerick fought back, however 'the Cats' went on to win the game by seven points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2007/0903/tomamccarthy.html |title=RTÉ Sport: Kilkenny 2–19 Limerick 1–15, by Tomás McCarthy |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=3 September 2007 |access-date=17 September 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090915213955/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2007/0903/tomamccarthy.html |archive-date=15 September 2009 |df=dmy }}</ref> In spite of this loss O'Shaughnessy was later presented with his first [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award, marking him out as one of the best players of the championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/hurlingallstars2007.html |title=Hurling All Stars 2007 |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=19 October 2007 |access-date=1 December 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080331100601/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/hurlingallstars2007.html |archive-date=31 March 2008 |df=dmy }}</ref>

After the highs of the previous year, 2008 proved to be a difficult year for the Limerick hurlers.  The team were beaten by 4–12 to 1–16 in opening game of the championship by [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=97023|title=Munster SHC: Banner goals see off Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=22 June 2008|access-date=1 December 2008}}</ref> The newly structured qualifier system pitted O'Shaughnessy's side against [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in a must-win game.  Limerick, however, were out of sorts as they suffered a surprising 3–19 to 0–18 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=98081|title=All-Ireland SHC: Bergin guns down Limerick|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=12 July 2008|access-date=1 December 2008}}</ref> Limerick's involvement in the championship came to an end following this defeat.
In late 2009 O'Shaughnessy was diagnosed with sclerosis but remained to feature during the league.
In April 2011 just three days before the National Hurling League Division 2 final, O'Shaughnessy announced his retirement from Inter-County hurling.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0428/imerick_oshaughnessy.html |title=O'Shaughnessy calls time on Treaty career |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=28 April 2011 |access-date=28 April 2011 }}{{dead link|date=January 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref name="Retirement Indo">{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/oshaughnessy-calls-it-a-day-2631790.html|title=O'Shaughnessy calls it a day|publisher=[[Irish Independent]]|date=28 April 2011|access-date=28 April 2011}}</ref>

===Provincial===

O'Shaughnessy has also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the [[Railway Cup]] inter-provincial competition.  He first lined out with his province in 2002, however, Munster were defeated by arch-rivals [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] in the final.  His inclusion on the team that year marks him out as the youngest Munster man to ever play for his province.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17836|title=O'Shaughnessy awarded National Junior honour
|publisher=www.hoganstand.com|date=13 March 2003|access-date=7 December 2008}}</ref> It was 2006 before O'Shaughnessy played with Munster again.  On that occasion [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] were the victors in the semi-final of the competition.  After an absence the following year O'Shaughnessy was back on the team in 2008.  Once again Munster reached the final, however, Leinster were the winners on that occasion.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/railwaycuphurling.html |title=Munster Railway Cup Hurling Teams |publisher=[[Munster GAA]] |access-date=7 December 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080719201124/http://munster.gaa.ie/teams/railwaycuphurling.html |archive-date=19 July 2008 |url-status=dead |df=dmy }}</ref>

2007-2009 |ic_apps_points = |ic_province_f = 0 |ic_province_h = 0 |ic_all_ireland_f = 0 |ic_all_ireland_h = 0 |nhl = 1 |nfl = 1 |all_stars_f = 0 |all_stars_h = 0 |cl_update = |ic_update = }} '''Mark O'Riordan''' (born 1980 in [[Croom, County Limerick]]) is an [[Republic of Ireland|Irish]] athlete who plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Croom GAA|Croom]] and with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team. He also plays with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior football team.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/turmoil-of-days-gone-by-holdsno-concern-for-dual-star-lucey-1848823.html|title=Turmoil of days gone by holdsno concern for dual star Lucey|last=Hogan|first=Vincent|date=1 August 2009|work=[[Irish Independent]]|accessdate=20 November 2010}} ==Playing career== ===Club=== O'Riordan plays his club [[hurling]] with his local [[Croom GAA|Croom]] club and has enjoyed some success. ===Inter-county=== ;Hurling O'Riordan first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] under-21 team. He won a Munster title at this level in 2000 before later collecting an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal following a victory over [[Galway GAA|Galway]]. The following year O'Riordan won a second set of Munster and All-Ireland under-21 honours, as Limerick completed the second leg of a three-in-a-row. By this stage he had already joined the county senior team, however, Limerick's hurling fortunes were about to take a dramatic downturn. Following the county's victory over [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] in 2001 Limerick failed to win a game in the province until their 2007 Munster semi-final victory over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. This was achieved following a three-game saga, however, O'Riordanside later lost the Munster final to [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]. Limerick later gained revenge by defeating 'the Decies' in the subsequent All-Ireland semi-final, setting up an All-Ireland final meeting with [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] on 2 September 2007. ;Football O'Riordan was part of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] team that won the Munster U21 Championship in 2000 he also played in the All Ireland Final but lost out to [[Tyrone GAA|Tyrone]]. In 2009 he played in the Munster Senior Championship final but lost out by a point [[Cork GAA|Cork]]. In 2010 he helped [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] win the National Football League Div 4 title beating [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final in [[Croke Park]]. ==Honours== Hurling * [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]] (2): 2000, 2001 * [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship]] (2): 2000, 2001 * [[National Hurling League|National Hurling League, Division 2]] (1): 2011 Football * [[Munster Under-21 Football Championship]] (1): 2000 * [[National Football League (Ireland)|National Football League, Division 4]] (1): 2010 * [[McGrath Cup]] (1): 2004 == References == {{Reflist}} {{Limerick Under 21 Football Team 2000}} {{Limerick Under 21 Team 2001}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 2007}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 2009}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Oriordan, Mark}} [[Category:1980 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Croom hurlers]] [[Category:Croom Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:Dual players]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:21st-century Irish sportsmen]] {{Limerick-hurling-bio-stub}}

'''Donie Ryan''' (born 26 December 1976) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he played with [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] and was also a member of the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He usually lined out as a forward.

==Career==

Ryan first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] club and had a career that spanned 25 years with the club's top adult team. During that time, he won three County Championship titles in three different grades, including a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|County Senior Championship]] title in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/343194/donie-ryan-s-wins-a-third-limerick-title-spanning-three-decades-with-garryspillane.html|title=Donie Ryan wins a third Limerick title spanning three decades with Garryspillane|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=22 October 2018|access-date=23 August 2021|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> Ryan first came to prominence on the inter-county scene at the underage and intermediate levels with Limerick. He joined his brother, [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J. Ryan]], on the [[Limerick senior hurling team]] for the [[Oireachtas Cup]] in 1997, however, it was 2002 before he established himself on the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20040895.html|title=Take a look through my eyes|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=27 August 2007|access-date=23 August 2021|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> Ryan was at left corner-forward when Limerick lost the [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|2007 All-Ireland final]] to [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. His inter-county career ended when he was dropped from the panel in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/allen-drops-nine-limerick-players-dropped-from-panel-256777-Oct2011/|title=Allen drops nine Limerick players from panel|publisher=The 42|date=18 October 2011|access-date=23 August 2021|first=Paul|last=Fennessy}}</ref>

'''Donal O'Grady''' (born 3 July 1980) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a midfielder and later centre back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/ogrady-can-lay-foundations-for-limerick-rebuild-2362679.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120804071027/http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/ogrady-can-lay-foundations-for-limerick-rebuild-2362679.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 August 2012 |title=O'Grady can lay foundations for Limerick rebuild |date=3 October 2010 |work=Irish Independent |access-date=20 November 2010 }}</ref>

Born in [[Ballingarry, County Limerick|Ballingarry]], [[County Limerick]], O'Grady first arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of twenty-one when he first linked up with the Limerick under-21 team. He made his senior debut in the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 2004|2004 championship]]. O'Grady has since gone on to play a key part for Limerick, and has won one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal and one [[National Hurling League|National League (Division 2)]] medal. O'Grady has been an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up on one occasion.

O'Grady has been a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team on a number of occasions and has won two [[Railway Cup]] medals. At club level he won one intermediate championship medal with [[Granagh-Ballingarry GAA|Granagh-Ballingarry]].

He attended [[St Munchin's College]], Limerick and graduated from there in 1998.

College :L.I.T

==Playing career==
===Granagh-Ballingarry===

O'Grady plays his club hurling with the [[Granagh-Ballingarry GAA|Granagh-Ballingarry]] club and has enjoyed some success.

In 2005 the club enjoyed its greatest success, with O'Grady playing a key role. After losing at the quarter-final or semi-final stage for six years in a row, the club finally reached the final of the county intermediate championship. A 4–10 to 3–10 defeat of [[Glenroe GAA|Glenroe]] gave O'Grady a championship medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=56801|title=Granagh/Ballingarry braced for senior action|date=16 February 2006|work=Hogan Stand website|access-date=12 February 2013}}</ref>

===Limerick===

O'Grady first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] under-21 team in 2001. He started in Limerick's opening game against [[Cork GAA|Cork]] but was substituted after half-an-hour and failed to regain his place on the team., In spite of this he claimed [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] and [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals as a non-playing substitute.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaelic-games/new-limerick-captain-ready-for-challenge-1-4762109|title=New Limerick captain ready for challenge|date=9 February 2013|work=Limerick Leader|access-date=12 February 2013|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

In 2004 O'Grady made his senior debut when he came on as a blood sub in Limerick's 1–18 to 2–12 defeat by Cork in the Munster semi-final. He was the first man from the Granagh-Ballingarry club to play senior hurling for Limerick.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

After becoming a regular member of the starting fifteen the following year, O'Grady lined out in his first Munster final in 2007. [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] provided the opposition, however, a 3–17 to 1–14 defeat was Limerick's lot on that occasion.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dynamic-dan-adds-some-extra-dash-for-the-dise-995588.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120904121742/http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/dynamic-dan-adds-some-extra-dash-for-the-dise-995588.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 September 2012 |title=Dynamic Dan adds some extra dash for the Déise |publisher=Irish Independent |access-date=2 August 2012 |date=9 July 2007 |first=Martin |last=Breheny }}</ref> Limerick later gained their revenge on Waterford in the All-Ireland semi-final, thus gaining qualification to a first All-Ireland decider in eleven years for the Treaty men. [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] provided the opposition and got off to a flying start with [[Eddie Brennan]] and [[Henry Shefflin]] combining to score two goals within the first ten minutes. Limerick were eventually defeated on a 2–19 to 1–15 score line.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sports/gaa/2007/0902/1188603379646.html|title=Kilkenny overpower Limerick to retain title|date=2 September 2007|publisher=Irish Times|access-date=31 October 2012}}</ref>

Limerick failed to build on their reasonably successful 2007 season and went into decline once again.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

In late 2009 and early 2010 Limerick hurling hit an all-time low when many of the senior hurling team withdrew their services in protest at the continuation of [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]] as manager.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/could-it-end-in-a-strike-1-2190539 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130413011731/http://www.limerickleader.ie/news/could-it-end-in-a-strike-1-2190539 |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 April 2013 |title=Could it end in a strike? |date=5 November 2009 |publisher=Limerick Leader |access-date=12 February 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/kfkfmhsnojql/rss2/|title=Limerick players reaffirm strike stance|date=8 March 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=12 February 2013|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref> As a result of this O'Grady played no part in the 2010 championship.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

O'Grady returned to the panel in 2011 and a new management team took over. Limerick defeated [[Clare GAA|Clare]] by 4–12 to 2–13 in the National League Division 2 final that year, giving O'Grady his first success in the senior grade.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0430/limerick_clare.html |title=Limerick 4-12 Clare 2-13 |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=30 April 2011 |access-date=13 June 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110603042348/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0430/limerick_clare.html |archive-date= 3 June 2011 }}</ref>

In 2013 O'Grady was appointed captain of the Limerick senior hurling team. It was a successful year as he won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal after guiding the team to a 0–24 to 0–15 victory over Cork in the [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 July 2013|access-date=15 July 2013|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

===Munster===

O'Grady has also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in a number of inter-provincial campaigns and has enjoyed some success.

In 2007 he was at midfield in his debut year when Munster defeated [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] by 2–22 to 2–19 to take the [[Railway Cup]] title.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2007/1027/interpro.html |title=RTÉ Sport: Munster 2-22 Connacht 2-19 |date=28 October 2007 |publisher=RTÉ Sport |access-date=12 February 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080506073543/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2007/1027/interpro.html |archive-date= 6 May 2008 }}</ref>  Further appearances for the province in 2008, 2009 and 2012 ended in defeat.

O'Grady won a second inter-provincial medal in [[2013 Inter-Provincial Hurling Championship|2013]] following Munster's 1–22 to 0–15 defeat of Connacht.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/munster-too-strong-for-connacht-586773.html|title=Munster too strong for Connacht|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 March 2013|access-date=15 July 2013}}</ref>

{{Short description|Irish hurler (1944–2021)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code = Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = Ned Rea 2013 (cropped).jpg | caption = Rea in 2013 | name = Éamonn "Ned" Rea | irish = Éamonn Ó Riabhaigh | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | occupation = Publican | nickname = Ned | county = Dublin | province = Munster | club = [[Effin GAA|Effin]]

1969–1980 | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 3 | cl_province = | cl_all_ireland = | colleges = [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] | fitz = 2 | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Full-forward | ic_years = 1963–1977 | ic_apps_points = 15 (3–08) | ic_province = 2 | ic_all_ireland = 1 | nhl = 0 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_date = May 1944 | birth_place = Glenroe, [[County Limerick]], [[Ireland]] | death_place = [[Tallaght]], [[Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] | death_date = {{death date and age|2021|11|22|1944|5||df=y}} }} '''Éamonn "Ned" Rea''' (May 1944 – 22 November 2021) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a full-forward for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=48809|title=Éamonn Rea|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=5 April 1991|accessdate=20 April 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/where-are-they-now-eamon-ned-rea-former-limerick-hurler-26701473.html|title=Where are they now?: Eamon 'Ned' Rea (Former Limerick hurler)|publisher=Irish Independent|date=21 November 2010|accessdate=20 April 2013}} Rea joined the team during the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1964|1964 championship]] and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1974|1974 championship]]. During that time he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal and two [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals. Rea was an All-Ireland runner-up on one occasion. At club level Rea was a three-time [[Dublin Senior Club Hurling Championship|county club championship]] medalist with [[Faughs GAA|Faughs]]. He began his career with [[Effin GAA|Effin]]. He attended [[St Munchin's College]], Limerick. His brother, [[Gerry Rea]], was also an inter-county hurler, while his granduncle, [[Matt Rea (Gaelic footballer)|Matt Rea]], was an [[All-Ireland Senior Football Championship|All-Ireland]] medal winner as a [[Gaelic football]]er with [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]. ==Playing career== ===Club=== Rea began his club hurling career with [[Effin GAA|Effin]] before joining Dublin club [[Faughs GAA|Faughs]] in 1968. It was with the latter club that he enjoyed his greatest success.{{cite web|url=http://faughs.ie/index.php/about/history/|title=Faughs GAA Club: History|publisher=Faughs GAA website|accessdate=21 April 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130826025705/http://faughs.ie/index.php/about/history/|archivedate=26 August 2013}} After losing the 1969 championship decider, Faughs were back in the final again the following year. A defeat of [[St Vincents GAA|St. Vincents]] gave Rea his first [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal. Faughs surrendered their title the following year but went on to win back-to-back titles in 1972 and 1973, bringing Rea's championship medal tally to three. ===Inter-county=== Rea's performances at club level brought him to the attentions of the inter-county selectors and he soon joined the Limerick senior team. In 1973, after eighteen years in the doldrums, Limerick finally made the provincial breakthrough. A last-gasp free by [[Richie Bennis]] secured a narrow 6-7 to 2-18 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the provincial decider and a first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal for Rea. Limerick later lined out as underdogs in [[Croke Park]] for an All-Ireland showdown with reigning champions and injury-ravaged [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]]. A [[Mossie Dowling]] goal eight minutes after half-time, together with play from Richie Bennis powered Limerick to a 1-21 to 1-14 victory and secured an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal for Rea.{{cite news|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/3420/TALES-OF-3973-IMMORTALS.3163953.jp?articlepage=2|title=Tales of the '73 Immortals|date=31 August 2007|work=[[Limerick Leader]]|accessdate=15 July 2010}} In 1974 Limerick maintained their provincial dominance. Rea captured a second Munster medal following a 6-14 to 3-9 trouncing of [[Clare GAA|Clare]]. This victory allowed Rea's side to advance directly to the All-Ireland final where Kilkenny provided the opposition once again. The Cats were back to full strength and set out for revenge. In spite of this Limerick stormed into an early lead, however, this was diminished as [[Pat Delaney (Kilkenny hurler)|Pat Delaney]], [[Eddie Keher]] and [[Mick Brennan (hurler)|Mick Brennan]] scored goals. Limerick lost the game by 3-19 to 1-13. ===Inter-provincial=== Rea also had the honour of being selected for [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial series of games but enjoyed little success.{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|accessdate=12 March 2013|first=|last=}} ==Personal life== Born in Glenroe, [[County Limerick]], [[Munster]], in May 1944, Rea was the eldest in a farming family of eight boys and three girls. His family moved to nearby [[Effin]] when he was an infant. Rea was a boarder at [[St Munchin's College]] in [[Limerick]] where he was a proficient rugby player and claimed three Muster junior medals and a senior schools medal. He later studied dairy science at [[University College Cork]] where he graduated before being appointed a creamery manager in [[Athlacca]] and later with Galtee Food Products. He became a publican in 1989, opening Rea’s Pub on Parkgate Street in [[Dublin]].{{cite web|url=http://www.vsopublicationsltd.ie/eamon-rea-%E2%80%93-limerick-person-of-the-year-dublin-2013/|title=Eamon Rea - Limerick person of the year|publisher=VSO Publications|date=17 April 2013|accessdate=23 November 2021|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40750500.html|title=Limerick GAA mourns passing of legend ‘Ned’ Rea|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=22 November 2021|accessdate=23 November 2021|first=John|last=Fogarty}} He died on 22 November 2021, at the age of 77 after falling ill earlier in the month.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-ireland-winner-eamonn-ned-rea-dies-aged-77-1.4735813|title=All-Ireland winner Eamonn ‘Ned’ Rea dies, aged 77|work=[[The Irish Times]]|first=Seán|last=Moran|date=22 November 2021|access-date=22 November 2021}} ==Honours== ===Player=== ;University College Cork *[[Fitzgibbon Cup]]: 1965, 1966 ;Effin *South Limerick Minor Hurling Championship: 1959 ;Kilmallock *South Limerick Minor Hurling Championship: 1961 ;Faughs *[[Dublin Senior Club Hurling Championship]]: 1970, 1972, 1973 ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1973|1973]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1973#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1973]], [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1974#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1974]] ===Selector=== ;Faughs *[[Dublin Senior Club Hurling Championship]]: 1986 ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Navboxes |title= Ned Rea navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Hurling Team 1973}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1974}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Rea, Ned}} [[Category:1944 births]] [[Category:2021 deaths]] [[Category:UCC hurlers]] [[Category:Effin hurlers]] [[Category:Kilmallock hurlers]] [[Category:Faughs hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship winners]] [[Category:People educated at St Munchin's College]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Damien Reale''' (born 17 May 1981) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Hospital-Herbertstown GAA|Hospital-Herbertstown]], divisional side [[Emmets GAA|Emmets]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== At club level, Reale first played for [[Hospital-Herbertstown GAA|Hospital-Herbertstown]] at juvenile and underage levels before progressing to adult level. He claimed his first [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] medal in 2000 following a 2–11 to 1–05 win over [[South Liberties GAA|South Liberties]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Hospital-Herbertostown return to the senior grade|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=25 September 2000|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He added a [[Limerick Junior A Hurling Championship|Limerick JAHC]] medal to his collection in 2005.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Three years of heartache finally ends|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 November 2005|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Reale won a second Limerick IHC medal after a 2–11 to 0–15 win over [[Dromin/Athlacca GAA|Dromin/Athlacca]].{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/reeling-in-the-years-limerick-gaas-2010/|title=Reeling in the Years: Limerick GAA’s 2010|publisher=Sporting Limerick|date=22 June 2020|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Reale first appeared for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 1999.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145462/Limerick-minor-hurlers---trying.html|title=Limerick minor hurlers - trying since 1985|publisher=Limerick Live|date=7 September 2014|access-date=9 May 2025|first=|last=}} He immediately progressed to the under-21 team and won three successive [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medals between 2000 and 2002.{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/young-guns-grab-glory-for-limerick-26109433.html|title=Young guns grab glory for Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=3 October 2015|date=18 September 2000}}{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/news/limerick-hold-on-to-u-21-crown-1.396923|title=Limerick hold on to U-21 crown|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=8 April 2017|date=16 September 2001}}{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-make-history-26034660.html|title=Limerick make history|date=16 September 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=13 October 2013|first=Martin|last=Breheny}} Reale made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in the [[National Hurling League]] in 2001. He was appointed [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|team captain]] in 2007, in the absence of the nominated [[James O'Brien (hurler)|James O'Brien]].{{cite web|url= https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/reale-to-lead-limerick/26281976.html|title=Reale to lead Limerick|date=25 January 2007|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=13 October 2024|first=|last=}} Reale captained the team when Limerick had a 2–17 to 1–15 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2007 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/kilkenny-handed-final-glory-on-a-plate/26315446.html|title=Kilkenny handed final glory on a plate|publisher=Irish '''Damien Quigley''' (born 1971) is an Irish [[hurling]] selector and former player. At club level, he played with [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==

Quigley was educated at [[Crescent College]] in [[Limerick]] before later studying at [[University College Cork]] (UCC). He lined with the [[UCC GAA|senior hurling team]] during his time there, and was part of UCC's [[Fitzgibbon Cup]]-winning panel in 1991.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=UCC garb late winner|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=25 February 1991|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

At club level, Quigley began his career with [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] at juvenile and underage levels. He won several Limerick MAHC and U21AHC titles between 1989 and 1990, by which time he had progressed to adult level with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Na Piarsaigh win at ease|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=11 September 1989|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Quigley claimed a [[Limerick Junior A Hurling Championship|Limerick JAHC]] medal in 1990, after scoring three points in the defeat of [[Dromcollogher/Broadford GAA|Drom/Broadford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Na Piarsaigh are county champions|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=11 September 1989|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Quigley added a [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] medal to his collection in 1994, after a 1-14 to 0-04 win over [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Na Piarsaigh crush Tour for historic win|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=11 September 1989|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He was in the twilight of his career when he claimed [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medals in 2011 and 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/damien-quigley-na-piarsaigh-1299950-Feb2014/|title=The 42 year-old at the heart of Limerick club Na Piarsaigh's march to an All-Ireland semi-final|publisher=The 42|date=5 February 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Quigley also won [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] medals following those county victories.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> 

At inter-county level, Quigley first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during an unsuccessful two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick blasted by Brian|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 August 1991|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He later progressed to the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] and won [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medals in 1994 and 1996, however, Limerick faced subsequent All-Ireland final defeats by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] and [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] respectively.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40370429.html|title=A player-by-player guide to Wexford's All-Ireland 25 years on: 'We laughed as much as we hurled'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=1 September 2021|access-date=2 January 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> Quigley was also an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] award-winner in 1994. He added a [[National Hurling League]] medal to his collection in 1997.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/945696/limerick-county-final-day-to-honour-25th-anniversary-of-1997-hurling-league-title-victory.html|title=Limerick county final day to honour 25th anniversary of 1997 hurling league title victory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 October 2022|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

Performances at inter-county level for Limerick resulted in Quigley being called up to the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won consecutive [[Railway Cup]] medals in 1995 and 1996.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

==Management career==

Quigley served as a selector during [[Pad Joe Whelehan]]'s term as manager of the Limerick senior hurling team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10102845.html|title=McKenna appointed new Limerick selector|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=13 October 2004|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref> He was later part of a three-man committee which recommended the appointments of [[Dónal O'Grady]] and [[John Allen (hurler)|John Allen]] as Limerick senior hurling team managers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20128957.html|title=Limerick refusing to rush hurling appointment|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=26 August 2010|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}</ref>

{{short description|Irish hurler (born 1989)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games biography | code = Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Nickie Quaid | irish = | fullname = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|df=y|1989|06|12}} | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | nickname = | occupation = Primary school teacher | county = Limerick | province = Munster | cl_position = | club = [[Effin GAA|Effin]]
