At club level, he plays with [[Effin GAA|Effin]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team.]] Quaid is the most decorated Limerick player of all time. ==Early life== Quaid was born in [[Effin]], [[County Limerick]], the middle child of three sons born to [[Tommy Quaid]] and Breda Grace. His father was an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] runner-up with Limerick as a goalkeeper in 1980.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=17661|title=The great Tommy Quaid|date=1 January 1993|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=2 July 2011}} His grandfather, [[Jack Quaid (hurler)|Jack Quaid]], won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal in 1955, while his cousin, [[Joe Quaid]], was the All-Ireland runner-up goalkeeper in 1994 and 1996.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} ==Playing career== ===University=== During his studies at the [[Institute of Technology, Tralee]], Quaid became involved with the institute's senior hurling team. On 26 February 2011, he was at midfield when Tralee IT defeated [[Institute of Technology, Carlow]] by 1–17 to 1–15 in the final of the [[Ryan Cup]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/kerry/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=143269|title=Ryan Cup win for Tralee IT|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=28 February 2011|accessdate=12 February 2016|first=|last=}} ===Club=== Quaid joined the [[Effin GAA|Effin]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before joining the club's junior team. On 31 October 2010, Quaid won a [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick Junior Championship]] medal following Effin's 1–16 to 1–10 defeat of [[St. Kieran's GAA|St. Kieran's]]. As a member of divisional side [[Emmets GAA|Emmets]], Quaid was at midfield when the team was defeated by [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] in the [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] final on 3 October 2010.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/mulcahy-s-goal-helps-kilmallock-bridge-gap-1.659156|title=Mulcahy's goal helps Kilmallock bridge gap|publisher=Irish Times|date=4 October 2010|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}} On 25 September 2011, Quaid was at centre-back when Effin defeated [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]] in the final of the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick Intermediate Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/132220/Moloney-the-Effin-hero-.html|title=Moloney the Effin hero|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=26 September 2011|access-date=3 August 2018|first=|last=}} His display in the subsequent 0–14 to 0–11 defeat of [[Ballyduff GAA (Kerry)|Ballyduff]] in the [[Munster Intermediate Club Hurling Championship|Munster final]] earned Quaid particular praise in the media.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/towering-quaid-display-guides-effin-to-title-glory-26794100.html|title=Towering Quaid display guides Effin to title glory|publisher=Irish Independent|date=21 November 2011|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}} ===Inter-county=== ====Minor and under-21==== Quaid first played for Limerick at minor level in 2006.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/archives/2006/0419/ireland/limerick-and-clare-ring-the-changes-ahead-of-minor-hurling-qualifier-562067934.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160216073003/http://www.irishexaminer.com/archives/2006/0419/ireland/limerick-and-clare-ring-the-changes-ahead-of-minor-hurling-qualifier-562067934.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 February 2016|title=Limerick and Clare ring the changes ahead of minor hurling qualifier|date=19 April 2006|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=2 July 2011|first=Brendan|last=Larkin}} His two seasons in the grade ended with back-to-back [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeats by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]. On 5 June 2008, Quaid made his first appearance for the Limerick under-21 hurling team, lining out in goal in Limerick's 2–17 to 1–07 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/limerick-add-to-waterford-s-woes-1.1217210|title=Limerick add to Waterford's woes|date=6 June 2008|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}} His three seasons in the under-21 grade ended with early championship defeats.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/ryan-s-3-9-gives-clare-timely-lift-1.700796|title=Ryan's 3-9 gives Clare timely lift|date=16 July 2009|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/oconnor-inspires-banner-in-thriller-125175.html|title=O'Connor inspires Banner in thriller|date=15 July 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} ====Senior==== Quaid was one of a number of new players drafted onto the Limerick senior hurling team in 2010 in place of many of the 2009 panel who refused to play under manager [[Justin McCarthy (hurler)|Justin McCarthy]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/mccarthy-dispute-gets-silent-treatment-1.1244613|title=McCarthy dispute gets silent treatment|date=19 January 2010|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}} On 21 February 2010, he made his senior debut at midfield for Limerick in a [[National Hurling League|National League]] defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] at [[FitzGerald Park, Kilmallock|FitzGerald Park]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/mccarthy-hails-defiant-display-of-treaty-men-26634617.html|title=McCarthy hails defiant display of Treaty men|date=22 February 2010|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}} Quaid made his first championship appearance on 20 June 2010 when he was introduced as a substitute for [[Andrew Brennan (hurler)|Andrew Brennan]] in the 44th minute of a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/cork-record-comfortable-win-over-limerick-462436.html|title=Cork record comfortable win over Limerick|date=20 June 2010|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=}} Following the return of many of the regular Limerick panel in 2011, Quaid was one of the few players to be retained, switching from an outfield player to goalkeeper.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-step-up-to-the-plate-for-ogrady-26695360.html|title=Limerick step up to the plate for O'Grady|date=14 February 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=2 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}} On 30 April 2011, he won a National League Division 2 medal after a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|date=2 May 2011|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}} Quaid's performances during the 2012 season earned him an [[GAA All Stars Awards|All-Star]] nomination.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/galway-top-list-with-14-as-kilkenny-earn-12-1.547428|title=Galway top list with 14 as Kilkenny earn 12|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} On 14 July 2013, Quaid was in goal in Limerick's 0–24 to 0–15 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the Munster final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|date=15 July 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=3 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} Quaid was appointed captain of the Limerick senior hurling team on 9 December 2015.{{cite web|url= http://www.hoganstand.com/hurling/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=247916|title=Quaid to captain Shannonsiders|date=9 December 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=12 February 2016}} On 30 July 2018, Quaid's injury-time save from a [[Séamus Harnedy]] shot at goal in the All-Ireland semi-final the previous day was listed by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' as its "sports highlight of the weekend".{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/examviral/us-magazine-calls-nickie-quaids-save-against-cork-the-sports-highlight-of-the-weekend-858886.html|title=US magazine calls Nickie Quaid's save against Cork the 'sports highlight of the weekend'|date=30 July 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Steve|last=Neville}} The magazine wrote: "You can’t really call yourself a sports fan if you don’t appreciate this play...Séamus Harnedy found himself in front of the net with a chance to score a potential game-winning goal. He might have been the hero if not for this jaw-dropping effort from Limerick goalie Nickie Quaid. Quaid, while diving to his right, managed to knock the ball out of mid-air before Harnedy could hit it into the net."{{cite web|url=https://www.joe.ie/sport/nickie-quaids-astonishing-save-voted-sports-highlight-weekend-massive-us-publication-635047|title=Nickie Quaid's amazing save was voted as the best sports moment of the weekend by a huge U.S. magazine|date=30 July 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=Paul|last=Moore}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-quaid-supremacy-limerick-goalkeeping-dynasty-seeking-to-add-triumph-after-going-through-tragedy-37224763.html |title =The Quaid supremacy - Limerick goalkeeping dynasty seeking to add triumph after going through tragedy|date=17 August 2018|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=17 August 2018}} On 19 August 2018, Quaid was in goal when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}} He ended the season by being nominated for a second All-Star Award.{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/290289|title=All Star hurling nominees: 15 Limerick players in contention|date=13 September 2018|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=13 September 2018|first=|last=}} On 31 March 2019, Quaid was selected in goal for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal following the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} On 30 June 2019, Quaid won his first Munster Championship medal in six years following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}} On 25 October 2020, Quaid won a second successive National League medal after Limerick's 0–36 to 1–23 win over Clare in the [[2020 National Hurling League#Division 1 Final|delayed final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40070783.html|title=Lethal Limerick storm to victory despite Tony Kelly brilliance|date=25 October 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} Later that season he claimed a second successive Munster Championship medal - the third of his career - after keeping a clean sheet in the 0–25 to 0-21 [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster final]] defeat of Waterford.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40082804.html|title=Limerick made to work by Waterford for historic Munster SHC crown|date=15 November 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 November 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} On 13 December 2020, Quaid won a second All-Ireland Championship medal after keeping a clean sheet in the 0–30 to 0–19 win over Waterford.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40189962.html|title=Limerick show consistency in a world gone mad to claim All-Ireland honours|date=13 December 2020|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=19 December 2020|first=John|last=Fogarty}} Quaid won an [[GAA GPA All Stars Awards|All Star]] at the end of the 2024 season.{{cite news|title=Conroy and O'Donnell scoop Player of the Year awards|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/football/2024/1101/1478693-conroy-and-odonnell-scoop-player-of-the-year-awards/|work=[[RTÉ News]]|date=1 November 2024|access-date=2 November 2024}} ===Inter-provincial=== On 19 February 2012, Quaid was sub goalkeeper to [[Donal Óg Cusack]] in [[Munster GAA|Munster]]'s 3–14 to 1-16 [[Railway Cup]] semi-final defeat by [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/early-leinster-damage-decisive-184406.html|title=Early Leinster damage decisive|date=20 February 2012|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=3 August 2018|first=|last=|archive-date=24 March school, Quaid later attended Mannix College in [[Charleville, County Cork|Charleville]].{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/regionals/corkman/news/mannix-pupils-reap-awards-27055044.html|title=Mannix pupils reap awards|date=6 October 2005|publisher=The Corkman|accessdate=2 July 2011}} {{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Anthony O'Riordan | irish = Antóin Ó Riordáin | birth_date = 1966 | height = | nickname = | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] | cl_position = Midfield | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 0 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_position = Centre-back | ic_years = 1987-1993 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 0 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | all_stars = 0 | nhl = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_place=[[Bruff]],
[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Anthony O'Riordan''' (born 1966) is an Irish [[hurling]] coach and former player. At club level, he played with [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Playing career== O'Riordan first played hurling at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] club. He was part of the club's minor team that beat [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] by 1-07 to 1-06 to claim the Limerick MHC title in 1983.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Bruff champs after 42 years|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=17 September 1983|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} O'Riordan later progressed to adult level as a [[dual player]]. He won a Limerick JAFC medal in 1987 when Bruff beat [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St Patrick's]] by seven points in the final.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Bruff tops in dull tie|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=7 November 1987|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, O'Riordan first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as [[Captain (sport)|captain]] of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick’s last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to the under-21 team and won consecutive [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] titles, before claiming an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after a 2-15 to 3-06 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|1987 final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/109109/Limerick-s-first-All-Ireland-U.html|title=Limerick’s first All Ireland U-21 hurling title in 1987|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 September 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} O'Riordan joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] during the [[1987–88 National Hurling League|1987–88 National League]]. He was part of Limerick's [[National Hurling League]]-winning season in 1992, however, he missed the semi-final and final as he was on his honeymoon.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Riordan could be asked to fly home|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=4 May 1992|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Management career== O'Riordan was a selector during [[Richie Bennis]]'s term as manager of the Limerick senior team.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30276624.html|title=Bennis goes full-time with Limerick|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=13 February 2006|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} His tenure included Limerick's 2-17 to 1-15 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[2007 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2007 All-Ireland final]]. O'Riordan later served as a selector with the [[All-Ireland Intermediate Hurling Championship|intermediate team]] under [[Leo O'Connor (hurler)|Leo O'Connor]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/209410/Six-from-senior-panel-bolster-Limerick.html|title=Six from senior panel bolster Limerick intermediate team|publisher=Limerick Live|date=16 June 2016|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Bruff *Limerick Junior A Football Championship: 1987 *Limerick Minor Hurling Championship: 1983 ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|1987]] *[[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1986 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1986]], [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1987]] *[[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] (c) *[[Munster Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] (c) == References == {{Reflist}} {{Navboxes |title= Anthony O'Riordan navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{s-start}} {{s-ach|achievements}} {{succession box | before=[[Anthony Cunningham]] | title=[[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Minor Hurling Final]]

'''Christopher "Christy" Ryan''' (25 December 1899 – 22 February 1978) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a right wing-back for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/chris-ryan.pdf|title=Chris Ryan of Pallasgreen|publisher=Limerick Heritage website|access-date=23 April 2012}}</ref>

Keane made his first appearance for the team in a tournament game in late 1918 and was a regular member of the starting fifteen until his retirement after the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1930|1930 championship]]. During that time he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal and one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=23 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721124423/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=21 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At club level Ryan enjoyed a lengthy career with [[Pallasgreen GAA|Pallasgreen]].

Ryan hailed from a family with a close association with [[Gaelic games]]. His uncles, [[Tom Barry (London hurler)|Tom]], [[John Barry (hurler)|John]] and [[James Barry (hurler)|James Barry]] won All-Ireland medals with [[London county hurling team|London]] in 1901. His brother, [[Dick Ryan]], won an All-Ireland medal with Limerick in 1918.

'''Kieran O'Rourke''' (born 1987) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a right corner-back for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].

O'Rourke joined the team during the [[National Hurling League 2007|2007 National League]] and was a semi-regular member of the starting fifteen over subsequent seasons.

At club level O'Rourke is a one-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county club championship]] medalist with [[Bruree GAA|Bruree]].

==Playing career==

===Club===

O'Rourke plays his club hurling with Bruree and has enjoyed much success.

In 2006 he lined out in his first hurling championship decider. [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] were the opponents, however, a narrow 1–16 to 1–15 victory gave O'Rourke a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] medal.<ref>{{Cite news |date=16 October 2006 |title=AT LONG LAST: Bruree lift county title for first time since De Valera was a kid |publisher=Irish Independent |url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/at-long-last-bruree-lift-county-title-for-first-time-since-de-valera-was-a-kid-73538.html |access-date=4 November 2012}}</ref>

===Inter-county===

O'Rourke made his senior debut for Limerick in a National League game against [[Antrim county hurling team|Antrim]] in 2007.<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 March 2007 |title=Limerick omit captain |publisher=Hogan Stand website |url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=74971 |access-date=4 November 2012}}</ref> He played a number of games during that campaign and was subsequently included on Limerick's championship panel.

After a number of seasons O'Rourke was recalled to the panel in 2010. He made his championship debut that year in a Munster semi-final defeat by [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=18 June 2010 |title=All change for Limerick |publisher=Hogan Stand website |url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=130663 |access-date=4 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=21 October 2011 |title=Allen points to youth as way forward |publisher=Hogan Stand website |url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=156852 |access-date=4 November 2012}}</ref>

'''John Reidy''' (8 November 1875 – 21 June 1910) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a goalkeeper for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Born in [[Ballingarry, County Limerick|Ballingarry]], [[County Limerick]], Reidy first played competitive hurling in his youth. He was a regular for the Limerick senior hurling team during a successful period at the end of the 19th century. During his inter-county career he won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal and one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=Limerick GAA profile|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=20 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archive-date=25 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=20 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328073637/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=28 March 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At club level Reidy was a stalwart of the [[Granagh-Ballingarry GAA|Ballingarry]] team.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

In retirement from playing Reidy became involved in the administrative affairs of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]], having served as president of the Limerick County Board.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

'''Michael Rochford''' (born 1890) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a right corner-back for the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior team.

Born in [[Limerick (city)|Limerick]], Rochford first played competitive hurling in his youth. He made his first impression on the inter-county scene when he joined the Limerick senior team during a golden age between 1918 and 1923. Rochford went on to play a key role for Limerick for a brief period, and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal and one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=1 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328073637/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=28 March 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

At club level he was a four-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medallist with [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]].

He usually lines out as a right wing-forward. ==Playing career== ===Mary Immaculate College=== During his studies at [[Mary Immaculate College]], Reidy was selected for the college's senior hurling team during his second year. On 27 February 2016, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal when Mary Immaculate College won their first ever title after a 1–30 to 3–22 defeat of the [[University of Limerick]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/eamonn-cregan-hails-heroic-mary-i-384649.html|title=Eamonn Cregan hails heroic Mary I|date=29 February 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}} ===Dromin-Athlacca=== Reidy joined the [[Dromin-Athlacca GAA|Dromin-Athlacca]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels before eventually joining the club's top adult team in the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick Intermediate Championship]].{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} On 15 October 2013, Reidy lined out at centre-forward when Dromin-Athlacca faced [[Knockaderry GAA|Knockaderry]] in the Limerick Intermediate Championship final. He scored 1-02, including a point from a free, and collected a winners' medal following a 2–18 to 1–15 victory.{{cite news|url=http://www.vsopublicationsltd.ie/2013/10/dromin-athlacca-champions-after-classic/|title=Dromin-Athlacca champions after classic final|date=17 October 2013|publisher=VSO Publications|accessdate=8 March 2018|archive-date=8 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708182607/http://www.vsopublicationsltd.ie/2013/10/dromin-athlacca-champions-after-classic/|url-status=dead}} On 27 October 2018, Reidy lined out in a second Limerick Intermediate Championship final. He top scored for Dromin-Athlacca with 0-09 and collected a second winners' medal following a 2–15 to 0–14 defeat of [[Croom GAA|Croom]].{{cite news|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/344571/dromin-athlacca-win-limerick-ihc-against-13-man-croom.html|title=Dromin-Athlacca win Limerick IHC against 13 man Croom|date=27 October 2018|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=8 March 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}} ===Limerick=== ====Minor and under-21==== Reidy first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the minor team during the [[2011 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|2011 Munster Championship]]. He made his first appearance for the team on 27 April 2011 when he lined out at right wing-forward in a 2–14 to 0–12 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/dowling-lights-up-limerick-152811.html|title=Dowling lights up Limerick|date=28 April 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=8 March 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} Reidy was drafted onto the Limerick under-21 team for the [[2013 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|2013 Munster Championship]]. He made his only appearance in the grade on 31 May 2013 when he scored a point from left wing-forward in a 2–18 to 2–11 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/193510|title=Munster U21HC: Forde drives Tipp to victory|date=1 June 2013|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=8 March 2018}} ====Senior==== Reidy was just '''Paddy O'Loughlin''' (born 6 August 1997) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a centre-forward for club side [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-championship-squad-3942332-Apr2018/|title=Lynch not part of Limerick's 36-man championship panel as Kiely shows his hand|date=5 April 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=22 August 2018|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===University College Cork===

After lining out for the [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] freshers' team in his first year at university, O'Loughlin was added to the senior team in advance of the [[2019 Fitzgibbon Cup|2020 Fitzgibbon Cup]]. On 23 February 2019, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal after lining out in UCC's 2–21 to 0–13 defeat of [[Mary Immaculate College]] in the [[2019 Fitzgibbon Cup#Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/295945|title=Fitzgibbon Cup final: UCC in a different class|date=23 February 2017|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=23 February 2019|first=|last=}}</ref>

O'Loughlin played in a second successive [[2020 Fitzgibbon Cup#Final|Fitzgibbon Cup final]] on 12 February 2020. Captaining the team from centre-back, he ended the game with a second successive winners' medal after the 0–18 to 2–11 defeat of the [[Institute of Technology, Carlow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/it-carlow-ucc-match-report-5004314-Feb2020/|title=14-man UCC come from 6 points down to win Fitzgibbon Cup final against IT Carlow|publisher=The 42|date=12 February 2020|accessdate=13 February 2020|first=Sinéad|last=Farrell}}</ref>

===Kilmallock===

O'Loughlin joined the [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, before joining the club's senior team.

On 19 October 2014, O'Loughlin won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Championship]] from centre-back following a 1–15 to 0–14 defeat of reigning champions [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/delight-for-sparrow-as-kilmallock-defy-odds-292135.html|title=Delight for 'Sparrow' as Kilmallock defy odds|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=19 October 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> He later won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 1–32 to 3–18 extra-time defeat of [[Cratloe GAA|Cratloe]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/football/kilmallock-find-extra-gear-in-final-epic-299265.html|title=Kilmallock find extra gear in final epic|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=23 November 2014|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 17 March 2015, O'Loughlin came on as a substitute for Kilmallock in their 1–18 to 1–06 defeat by [[Ballyhale Shamrocks GAA|Ballyhale Shamrocks]] in the [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]] at [[Croke Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/ballyhale-make-it-six-of-the-best-with-final-stroll-31075381.html|title=Ballyhale make it six of the best with final stroll|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 March 2015|accessdate=4 August 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

O'Loughlin first played for Limerick at minor level. On 22 July 2014, he was at full-back when Limerick won their second successive [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] title after a 0–24 to 0–18 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/limerick-blitz-shakes-off-deise-276382.html|title=Limerick blitz shakes off Déise|date=23 July 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref> On 7 September 2014, O'Loughlin was again at full-back in Limerick's 2–17 to 0–19 defeat by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/wonderful-walsh-fires-cats-to-victory-over-limerick-30569083.html|title=Wonderful Walsh fires Cats to victory over Limerick|date=8 September 2014|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref>

O'Loughlin's second and final season with the Limerick minor hurling team ended with an All-Ireland quarter-final defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/evan-niland-stars-as-slick-galway-see-off-limerick-344725.html|title=Evan Niland stars as slick Galway see off Limerick|date=27 July 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

O'Loughlin joined the Limerick under-21 team in 2016 but was an unused substitute for Limerick's unsuccessful championship campaign. After being dropped from the panel the following year, O'Loughlin made his first appearance for the team on 7 May 2018 in a 3–18 to 0–13 [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/gaa/limerick-u21s-begin-title-defence-with-comfortable-win-over-clare-841452.html|title=Limerick U21s begin title defence with comfortable win over Clare|date=7 May 2018|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Senior====

In November 2017, O'Loughlin was added to the Limerick senior hurling panel and made his first appearance for the team during the pre-season [[Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/281970/10-additions-to-2018-limerick-hurling-panel.html|title=10 additions to 2018 Limerick hurling panel|date=16 November 2017|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> He made his first appearance in the [[National Hurling League]] on 28 January 2018 in a 1–25 to 0–18 defeat of [[Laois GAA|Laois]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/aaron-gillane-0-11-limerick-laois-3821416-Jan2018/|title=0–11 for Aaron Gillane as Limerick ease to league opener win over Laois|date=28 January 2018|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, O'Loughlin was a member of the extended panel when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

On 31 March 2019, O'Loughlin was named on the bench for Limerick's [[2019 National Hurling League#Final|National League final]] meeting with [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] at [[Croke Park]]. He collected a winners' medal as a non-playing substitute in the 1–24 to 0–19 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> O'Loughlin made his [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] debut on 2 June 2019 when he lined out at left wing-back in a 2–24 to 0–10 defeat of Waterford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Limerick/Article/Index/299910|title=Team news: Two Treaty changes as O'Loughlin debuts|date=31 May 2019|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=12 June 2019|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-waterford-hurling-munster-4665494-Jun2019/|title=20-point Munster victory for Limerick as they storm past 14-man Waterford|date=2 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=12 June 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> On 30 June 2019, O'Loughlin won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal as a non-playing substitute following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

After making a substitute appearance in the [[2020 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final]], O'Loughlin withdrew from the Limerick hurling panel "for personal reasons" ahead of the 2021 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.skysports.com/gaa/hurling/news/30554/12296601/limerick-all-ireland-winner-paddy-oloughlin-opts-out-of-treaty-hurling-panel-for-2021|title=Limerick All-Ireland winner Paddy O'Loughlin opts out of Treaty hurling panel for 2021|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=5 May 2021}}</ref>

'''Oisín O'Reilly''' (born 21 August 1997) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays for [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]]. He usually lines out as a full-forward. O'Reilly is also currently a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==
===Club===

O'Reilly joined the [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, before joining the club's senior team.

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

O'Reilly first played for Limerick at minor level. On 2 July 2015, he made his first appearance for the team when he came on as a late substitute in Limerick's 1–14 to 0-14 [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-minors-deliver-late-knockout-to-cork-684856.html|title=Limerick minors deliver late knockout to Cork|date=2 July 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Therese|last=O'Callaghan}}</ref>

O'Reilly subsequently joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2016 and played during the team's unsuccessful championship campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/all-ireland-holders-limerick-overrun-cork-u21s-742281.html|title=All-Ireland holders Limerick overrun Cork U21s|date=28 June 2016|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018}}</ref> He was included on the panel again the following season and won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 0–16 to 1–11 defeat of [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-beat-cork-to-earn-second-munster-u21-hurling-title-in-three-years-799624.html|title=Limerick beat Cork to earn second Munster U21 hurling title in three years|date=26 July 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018}}</ref> On 9 September 2017, he came on as a substitute for [[Barry Murphy (Limerick hurler)|Barry Murphy]] in Limerick's 0–17 to 0–11 defeat of [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-savour-that-september-excitement-in-u21-hurling-final-458686.html|title=Limerick savour that September excitement in U21 hurling final|date=11 September 2017|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref>

====Under-25====

In 2017, O'Reilly joined the Limerick under-25 hurling team. On 18 June 2017, he scored 3-01 from play when Limerick defeated [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] by 4–12 to 1–19 to win the [[Munster Under-25 Reserve Hurling Competition|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-waterford-u25-3450745-Jun2017/|title=Oisin O'Reilly hat-trick leads Limerick past Waterford to Munster U25 reserves hurling crown|date=18 June 2017|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

====Senior====

O'Reilly joined the Limerick senior hurling panel in 2018 and made his first appearance for the team during the pre-season [[Munster Senior Hurling League|Munster League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-clare-3796057-Jan2018/|title=5 changes to Limerick team ahead of Munster league final against Clare|date=13 January 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/limerick-championship-squad-3942332-Apr2018/|title=Lynch not part of Limerick's 36-man championship panel as Kiely shows his hand|date=5 April 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=22 August 2018|first=Kevin|last=O'Brien}}</ref> He made his first appearance in the [[National Hurling League]] on 4 February 2018 in a 1–24 to 0–10 defeat of [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] at [[O'Connor Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.the42.ie/division-1b-wrap-3833892-Feb2018/|title=14-man Offaly brought back down to earth with heavy defeat to Limerick|date=4 February 2018|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 July 2018}}</ref> On 19 August 2018, O'Reilly was a member of the extended panel when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|access-date=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

O'Reilly was a member of Limerick's extended panel once again during the [[2019 National Hurling League|2019 National League]], however, he made no appearance during Limerick's eight-game run to the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-hurling-league-waterford-4569589-Mar2019/|title=Limerick end 22-year with for league honours in style with final win over Waterford|date=31 March 2019|publisher=The 42|access-date=31 March 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref> He was dropped from the panel prior to the start of the [[2019 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/375181/limerick-confirm-2019-senior-hurling-championship-panel.html|title=BREAKING: Limerick confirm 2019 senior hurling championship panel|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 April 2019|access-date=3 May 2019|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

'''Shane O'Neill''' (born 1974) is an Irish [[List of hurling managers|hurling manager]] and former [[hurling|player]] who previously was the  [[Manager (Gaelic games)|manager]] of the [[Galway senior hurling team]]. As a player he lined out with [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship]] club [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] and the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Playing career==
===Na Piarsaigh===

O'Neill joined the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying much championship success in the minor and under-21 grades.

On 25 November 1990, O'Neill was just 16-years-old when he was a member of the extended panel of the Na Piarsaigh junior team that qualified to play [[Dromcollogher/Broadford GAA|Dromcollogher/Broadford]] in the [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick Junior Championship final]]. He ended the game with a winners' medal following the 2-10 to 2-00 victory.

On 3 October 1993, O'Neill was at full-forward when Na Piarsaigh faced [[Blackrock GAA (Limerick)|Blackrock]] in the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick Intermediate Championship final]]. He scored three points but ended on the losing side after a 2-04 to 0-08 defeat.

Na Piarsaigh qualified for a second successive Limerick Intermediate Championship final on 6 November 1994, with [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]] providing the opposition. O'Neill top scored with 1-02 from full-forward and ended the game with a winners' medal after the 2-14 to 0-04 victory.

On 18 October 2009, O'Neill was at full-forward when Na Piarsaigh qualified for their very first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick Senior Championship final]]. He was held scoreless from play in the 1-17 to 0-03 defeat by [[Adare GAA|Adare]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/adare-swat-na-piarsaigh-aside-to-claim-limerick-title-430709.html|title=Adare swat Na Piarsaigh aside to claim Limerick title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=18 October 2009|accessdate=31 October 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

Na Piarsaigh qualified for a second [[2011 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|senior final]] on 2 October 2011. O'Neill lined out at left wing-forward and scored a point from play in the 2-13 to 0-13 defeat of Adare.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/the-famine-finishes-for-na-piarsaigh-in-fine-style-1.612851|title=The famine finishes for Na Piarsaigh in fine style|date=3 October 2011|publisher=Irish Times|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 4 December 2011, he won a [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal following a 1-13 to 0-09 defeat of [[Crusheen GAA|Crusheen]] in the final replay.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/piarsaigh-young-guns-come-of-age-176100.html|title=Piarsaigh young guns come of age|date=5 December 2011|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=9 August 2018|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

===Limerick===
====Minor and under-21====

O'Neill was called up for a trial with the Limerick minor team prior to the start of the 1991 season, however, he failed to make the championship panel. Again eligible for the grade the following year, he was an unused substitute on 22 April 1992 when Limerick suffered a 1-07 to 0-09 defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]].{{fact|date=January 2022}}

On 16 April 1993, O'Neill made his first appearance for the Limerick under-21 team. He scored 2-01 from play in the 5-09 to 4-08 defeat of [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]]. On 23 July 1993, O'Neill scored a goal when Limerick suffered a 1-18 to 3-09 defeat by [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in the [[1993 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster final]].{{fact|date=January 2022}}

====Senior====

O'Neill was added to the Limerick senior team during the [[1994-95 National Hurling League|1994-95 National League]]. He made a number of appearances throughout the campaign and was retained on the panel for the [[1995 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1995 Munster Championship]]. O'Neill made his championship debut on 18 June 1995 when he came on as a 62nd-minute substitute for [[Pat Heffernan]] in a 0-16 to 0-15 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the Munster semi-final. On 9 July 1995, he was an unused substitute when Limerick suffered a 1-17 to 0-11 defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[1995 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/clare-hurling-1995-2205595-Jul2015/|title=20 years ago today the Clare hurlers won a famous Munster title...but where are they now?|publisher=The 42|date=9 July 2015|accessdate=26 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

On 7 July 1996, O'Neill lined out at midfield when Limerick faced [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[1996 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|Munster final]]. He was substituted at half-time in the 0-19 to 1-16 draw. O'Neill was dropped from the starting fifteen for the replay a week later but collected a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal as an unused substitute after a 4-07 to 0-16 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/shannonsiders-ahead-on-the-replay-count-35204.html|title=Shannonsiders ahead on the replay count|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=16 June 2007|accessdate=26 July 2019|first=Jim|last=O'Sullivan}}</ref> On 1 September 1996, he was again listed amongst the substitutes when Limerick faced [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]]. He remained on the bench for the 1-13 to 0-14 defeat.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.the42.ie/wexford-hurlers-1996-where-are-they-now-2955096-Sep2016/|title=20 years ago today the Wexford hurlers won the All-Ireland... but where are they now?|publisher=The 42|date=1 September 2016|accessdate=26 July 2019|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

On 6 October 1997, O'Neill lined out at midfield when Limerick faced [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1997 National Hurling League#Knock-out stage|National League final]]. He scored a point from play and collected a [[National Hurling League|winners' medal]] after the 1-12 to 1-09 victory.

==Managerial career==
===Na Piarsaigh===

In April 2014, it was confirmed that O'Neill had replaced [[Seán Stack]] as manager of the [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]] senior team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/sean-stack-na-piarsaigh-1332886-Feb2014/|title =Sean Stack steps down as manager of Munster club hurling champions Na Piarsaigh|date=25 February 2014|publisher=The 42|accessdate=9 November 2019|first=Mikey|last=Fanning}}</ref> His debut [[2014 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship campaign]] saw Na Piarsaigh remain undefeated in the group stage and qualify for the [[2014 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]] against [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] on 19 October 2014 where his side suffered a 1-15 to 0-14 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-shc-final-2014-1733823-Oct2014/|title =Kilmallock upset the odds to win Limerick SHC title|date=19 October 2014|publisher=The 42|accessdate=9 November 2019|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref>

O'Neill guided Na Piarsaigh to a second successive [[2015 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]] on 11 October 2015. He claimed his first silverware as manager following the 1-22 to 4-12 defeat of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/downes-restores-na-piarsaigh-as-limerick-leaders-31601388.html|title=Downes restores Na Piarsaigh as Limerick leaders|date=12 October 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Donnchadh|last=Boyle}}</ref> On 22 November 2015, Na Piarsaigh won the [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] after a 2-18 to 2-11 defeat of [[Ballygunner GAA|Ballygunner]] in the [[2015–16 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/dowling-goal-puts-seal-on-na-piarsaigh-glory-trail-34224443.html|title=Dowling goal puts seal on Na Piarsaigh glory trail|date=23 November 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Jackie|last=Cahill}}</ref> On 17 March 2016, O'Neill managed Na Piarsaigh to the [[All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]] medal when the club defeated [[Ruairí Óg GAC|Ruairí Óg]] by 2-25 to 2-14 in the [[2016 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/immortality-for-na-piarsaigh-as-cushendall-rue-big-day-flop-388128.html|title=Immortality for Na Piarsaigh as Cushendall rue big-day flop|date=18 March 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}</ref>

On 15 October 2017, O'Neill guided Na Piarsaigh to a third [[2017 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|county final]] in four seasons. He claimed his second championship as manager following the 1-22 to 2-14 defeat of [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/na-piarsaigh-see-off-kilmallock-to-secure-limerick-hurling-crown-36229094.html|title=Na Piarsaigh see off Kilmallock to secure Limerick hurling crown|date=15 October 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 19 November 2017, O'Neill won a second Munster Championship as Na Piarsaigh manager after a 3-15 to 2-10 defeat of Ballygunner in the [[2017–18 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship#Munster Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/late-na-piarsaigh-surge-sweeps-aside-ballygunner-in-scrappy-munster-final-36333884.html|title=Late Na Piarsaigh surge sweeps aside Ballygunner in scrappy Munster final|date=19 November 2017|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> On 17 March 2018, he guided Na Piarsaigh to a second [[2018 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]], however, his side suffered a 2-17 to 1-17 defeat by [[Cuala CLG|Cuala]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cuala-finish-with-four-late-points-to-finally-see-off-na-piarsaigh-challenge-and-retain-allireland-title-36740558.html|title=Cuala finish with four late points to finally see off Na Piarsaigh challenge and retain All-Ireland title|date=18 March 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=31 July 2018|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> It was later confirmed that O'Neill had stepped down as manager.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/304469/shane-o-neill-departs-as-na-piarsaigh-manager.html|title=Shane O'Neill departs as Na Piarsaigh manager|date=26 March 2018|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=31 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref>

===Galway===

On 8 November 2019, O'Neill was ratified as manager of the [[Galway senior hurling team]] on a two-year term.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/305681|title =Galway confirm O'Neill appointment|date=8 November 2019|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=9 November 2019|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/galway-hurling-manager-shane-oneill-4885170-Nov2019/|title =Galway's new hurling manager confirmed as All-Ireland winning Na Piarsaigh boss|date=8 November 2019|work=The 42|accessdate=11 November 2019}}</ref>

On 2 September 2021, after two years in charge, O'Neill announced that he would not be seeking an extension to his term as Galway manager and would leave the position.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.the42.ie/galway-hurling-shane-oneill-manager-5538680-Sep2021/|title= Galway in search for new hurling manager as O'Neill departs|date=2 September 2021|work=The 42|accessdate= 3 September 2021}}</ref>

'''John Quaid''' (1932 – 22 February 2021) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who played at club level with [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]], at inter-county level with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] and at inter-provincial level with [[Munster GAA|Munster]].

==Career==

From the [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] club, Quaid first came to prominence on the inter-county scene alongside his twin brother [[Jim Quaid|Jim]] on the Limerick junior team that overcame [[London GAA|London]] to win the [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|1955 All-Ireland Junior Championship]]. Promotion to the senior side followed, with both Quaid brothers heavily involved as Limerick surprised [[Clare GAA|Clare]] to win the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1955 Munster Championship]]. The team, labelled "Mackey's Greyhounds" after their trainer [[Mick Mackey]], were subsequently beaten by eventual champions [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]]. Quaid continued playing for Limerick until the 1960s, by which time he had also won three [[Railway Cup]] medals with [[Munster GAA|Munster]].{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

==Personal life and death==

The Quaid surname has been synonymous with Limerick hurling for nearly 70 years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-quaid-supremacy-limerick-goalkeeping-dynasty-seeking-to-add-triumph-after-going-through-tragedy-37224763.html|title=The Quaid supremacy - Limerick goalkeeping dynasty seeking to add triumph after going through tragedy|date=17 August 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=23 February 2021|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> A cousin, [[Seamus Quaid|Séamus Quaid]], was a contemporary of the Quaid twins and lined out with Limerick before winning the [[1960 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1960 All-Ireland Championship]] with [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]. Jack Quaid's son, [[Tommy Quaid|Tommy]], was also a Munster Championship-winner as goalkeeper with the Limerick team between 1976 and 1993. His nephew, [[Joe Quaid]], immediately took over as goalkeeper and also won Munster Championship medals in a decade-long career. Jack Quaid's grandson, [[Nickie Quaid]], has continued the family goalkeeping tradition with Limerick and has won two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]]s.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/he-came-into-my-head-a-couple-of-times-during-the-week-of-course-i-was-thinking-of-him-nickie-quaids-tribute-to-father-37252085.html|title='He came into my head a couple of times during the week. Of course I was thinking of him' - Nickie Quaid's tribute to father|date=26 August 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=23 February 2021|first=Dermot|last=Crowe}}</ref>

'''James Quaid''' (1932 – 25 March 2021) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who played at club level with [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] and at inter-county level with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]].

==Career==

From the [[Feohanagh-Castlemahon GAA|Feohanagh-Castlemahon]] club, Quaid first came to prominence on the inter-county scene alongside his twin brother [[Jack Quaid (hurler)|Jack]] on the Limerick junior team that overcame [[London GAA|London]] to win the [[All-Ireland Junior Hurling Championship|1955 All-Ireland Junior Championship]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40232093.html|title=Former Limerick hurler Jack Quaid, grandfather of All-Star Nickie, passes away|date=23 February 2021|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 February 2021|first=John|last=Fogarty}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/315769|title=Passing of a Limerick Hurling Great|date=23 February 2021|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=23 February 2021|first=|last=}}</ref> Promotion to the senior side followed, with both Quaid brothers heavily involved as Limerick surprised [[Clare GAA|Clare]] to win the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1955 Munster Championship]]. The team, labelled "Mackey's Greyhounds" after their trainer [[Mick Mackey]], were subsequently beaten by eventual champions [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland semi-final]]. Quaid continued playing for Limerick until the 1960s.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

==Personal life==

The Quaid surname has been synonymous with Limerick hurling for nearly 70 years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/the-quaid-supremacy-limerick-goalkeeping-dynasty-seeking-to-add-triumph-after-going-through-tragedy-37224763.html|title=The Quaid supremacy - Limerick goalkeeping dynasty seeking to add triumph after going through tragedy|date=17 August 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=23 February 2021|first=Colm|last=Keys}}</ref> A cousin, [[Seamus Quaid|Séamus Quaid]], was a contemporary of the Quaid twins and lined out with Limerick before winning the [[1960 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1960 All-Ireland Championship]] with [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]]. Jim Quaid's nephew, [[Tommy Quaid|Tommy]], was also a Munster Championship-winner as goalkeeper with the Limerick team between 1976 and 1993. His son, [[Joe Quaid]], immediately took over as goalkeeper and also won Munster Championship medals in a decade-long career. Jim Quaid's grandnephew, [[Nickie Quaid]], continues the family goalkeeping tradition with Limerick and as of July 2026 has won six [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland Championship]]s.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/he-came-into-my-head-a-couple-of-times-during-the-week-of-course-i-was-thinking-of-him-nickie-quaids-tribute-to-father-37252085.html|title='He came into my head a couple of times during the week. Of course I was thinking of him' - Nickie Quaid's tribute to father|date=26 August 2018|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=23 February 2021|first=Dermot|last=Crowe}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-20 |title=WATCH: Limerick netminder Nickie Quaid savours All-Ireland victory |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/all-ireland-final/watch-limerick-netminder-nickie-quaid-savours-all-ireland-victory-8810521 |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Limerick Live |language=en}}</ref>

Jim Quaid died at [[University Hospital Limerick]] on 25 March 2021, aged 89.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/316223|title=Limerick's Jim Quaid sadly passes away just weeks after death of his twin brother Jack|date=27 March 2021|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=27 March 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

At club level, he plays with [[Crecora/Manister GAA|Crecora/Manister]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[Crecora]], [[County Limerick]], O'Neill was educated at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick]]. He played in all grades of hurling during his time there and won a [[Dr Harty Cup]] medal in February 2018, after scoring 1–03 from play in the 3–18 to 2–10 win over [[Midleton CBS Secondary School|Midleton CBS]] in the [[2017–18 Harty Cup#Final|final]].{{cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/ardscoil-ris-extend-corks-wait-for-harty-cup-success-828571.html|title=Ardscoil Rís extend Cork's wait for Harty Cup success|access-date=17 May 2018 |publisher=Irish Examiner |date=17 February 2018}} During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]] (UL), O'Neill continued his hurling development. He won a league and championship double with the freshers' team in 2022.{{cite web |url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/star-studded-ul-crowned-all-ireland-fresher-hurling-champions-in-final-win-over-dcu-7858239|title=Star-studded UL crowned All-Ireland Fresher hurling champions in final win over DCU|access-date=20 July 2026|publisher=Limerick Live|date=9 March 2022}} O'Neill was a panel member when UL beat the [[NUI Galway GAA|University of Galway]] by 4–19 to 1–13 to win the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] tite in February 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/sigerson-fitzgibbon-cups/four-goal-michael-kiely-fires-ul-to-fitzgibbon-cup-glory-against-university-of-galway-42348322.html|title=Four-goal Michael Kiely fires UL to Fitzgibbon Cup glory against University of Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=18 February 2023|accessdate=18 February 2023|first=Tomás|last=McCarthy}} He won further Fitzgibbon Cup medals in 2025 and 2026, when UL won back-to-back titles.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41575399.html|title=UL overpower DCU to lift third Fitzgibbon Cup in four years|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 February 2025|accessdate=16 February 2025|first=Kevin|last=Egan}}{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/hurling/2015230/limerick-stars-shine-as-clinical-ul-see-off-local-rivals-mary-immaculate-college-in-fitzgibbon-cup-final.html|title=Limerick stars shine as clinical UL see off local rivals Mary Immaculate College in Fitzgibbon Cup final|publisher=Limerick Live|date=13 February 2026|accessdate=13 February 2026|first=|last=}} ==Club career== O'Neill began his club career at juvenile and underage levels with [[Crecora/Manister GAA|Crecora/Manister]]. He eventually progressed to the club's adult team in the [[Limerick Premier Junior A Hurling Championship|Limerick Premier JAHC]]. ==Inter-county career== O'Neill first appeared on the inter-county scene for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year tenure with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]]. He was the team's [[2018 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Top scorers|top scorer]] in his first year with the team in 2018, as well as ending the campaign by being named on the Team of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-star-selected-on-the-minor-hurling-team-of-the-year-8282015|title=Limerick star selected on the Minor Hurling Team of the Year|date=19 September 2018|publisher=GAA website|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} O'Neill [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ed Limerick to the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster MHC]] title in June 2019, following a 1–17 to 1–11 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[2019 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/hurling/news/limerick-triumph-in-electric-ireland-munster-mhc-final|title=Limerick triumph in Electric Ireland Munster MHC Final|date=30 June 2019|publisher=GAA website|access-date=22 May 2022|first=|last=}} He was again named on the Team of the Year, while he was also named Munster Minor Hurler of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/limerick-duo-honoured-as-munster-gaa-senior-and-minor-hurlers-of-the-year-8119206|title=Limerick duo honoured as Munster GAA Senior and Minor Hurlers of the 2026|first=|last=}} O'Neill made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in a 0–26 to 1–17 [[National Hurling League]] defeat by [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in May 2021.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/article/index/316961|title=Team news: O'Neill debuts as Lynch and Hegarty named from start|date=14 May 2021|publisher=Hogan Stand|access-date=22 May 2023|first=|last=}} He later won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal, as a panel member, as Limerick claimed a third consecutive title for the first time in 85 years following a 3–21 to 2–29 win title, following a 0–30 to 2–15 win over Kilkenny in the [[2023 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|2023 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41189653.html|title=Magnificent Limerick ignite in second half to make history |date=23 July 2023|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=19 July 2026|first=|last=}} O'Neill was at centre-forward when Limerick won a record-breaking sixth consecutive Munster SHC title after a 1–26 to 1–20 win over Clare in the [[2024 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster|2024 Munster SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-41412799.html|title=Six of the best: Limerick make history with Munster final win over Clare {{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Ralph Prendergast | irish = Ráulbh de Priondragás | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 8 | nickname = | occupation = | county = Limerick | province = Munster | cl_position = | colleges = | col_years = | fitz = | club = [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]]

1958–1959 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 0 | all_stars = | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_date=1936 | birth_place=[[Limerick]], Ireland | death_date = 28 June 2024 (aged 87) | death_place = Limerick, Ireland }} '''Ralph Prendergast''' (1936 – 28 June 2024) was an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]], [[Gaelic football]]er and [[Association football|football]]er. At club level he played with [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] and at inter-county level with [[Limerick senior hurling team|Limerick]] and [[New York GAA|New York]]. Prendergast also played with [[Cork Hibernians]] in the [[League of Ireland]]. ==Career== Prendergast attended [[CBS Sexton Street|Limerick CBS]],{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/home/206663/Brotherly-love-in-air-as-CBS.html|title=Brotherly love in air as CBS marks 200 years|date=28 April 2016|publisher=Limerick Live|access-date=19 June 2023}} and was part of the school's senior team beaten by the [[North Monastery]] in the [[Dr Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] in 1955. His performances earned his inclusion on the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] colleges team he won an [[All-Ireland Colleges Interprovincial Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal after a defeat of [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Leinster boys crushed by Munster "blitz"|publisher=Irish Independent|date=4 April 1955|access-date=19 August 2023|first=|last=}} At club level with [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]], Prendergast began his career by winning a Limerick MHC title in 1954. He progressed to adult level as a [[dual player]] and won a [[Limerick Senior Football Championship|Limerick SFC]] medal in 1955. Prendergast also made his first appearance with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]], having previously played at [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor level]]. He was part of a [[Mick Mackey]]-trained team that won the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] title in 1955.{{cite web|url=https://clarechampion.ie/time-to-right-the-wrongs-of-55/|title=Time to right the wrongs of '55|date=10 June 2023|publisher=The Clare Champion|access-date=19 June 2023}} Prendergast emigrated to the [[United States]] in 1957 but continued his [[Gaelic games]] activities. He joined the Limerick club and won a [[New York Senior Hurling Championship|New York SHC]] medal in 1961. He also lined out with the [[New York GAA|New York senior team]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishcentral.com/sports/anniversary-for-hurling-heroes-2283-237625301|title=Anniversary for hurling heroes|publisher=Irish Central|date=15 March 2009|access-date=19 August 2023|first=|last=}} After returning to Ireland Prendergast resumed his Limerick career in the [[National Hurling League]], before being [[Rule 27|banned]] from the [[Gaelic Athletic Association|GAA]] after lining out with [[Cork Hibernians]] in the [[League of Ireland]]. He was later reinstated and ended his club career by winning a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]]-SFC double with Claughaun in 1971. ==Death== Prendergast died on 28 June 2024, at the age of 87.{{cite web |last= |first= |date=30 June 2024 |title=The death has occurred of Ralph Prendergast|url=https://rip.ie/death-notice/ralph-prendergast-limerick-south-circular-road-560951|access-date=8 July 2024 |website=Derry Now|language=en}} ==Honours== ;Claughaun *[[Limerick Senior Football Championship]]: 1955, 1971 *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]]: 1971 *Limerick Minor Hurling Championship: 1954 ;Limerick GAA Club, New York *[[New York Senior Hurling Championship]]: 1961 ;Limerick *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1955]] ;Munster *[[All-Ireland Colleges Interprovincial Hurling Championship]]: 1955 ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Ralph Prendergast navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Hurling Team 1955}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Prendergast, Ralph}} [[Category:1936 births]] [[Category:2024 deaths]] [[Category:Claughaun hurlers]] [[Category:Claughaun Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:New York inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Cork Hibernians F.C. players]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Michael Reale''' (born 26 June 1966{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/county/limerick/article/index/42428|title=Mike Reale|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=8 May 1992|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}}) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== At club level, Reale began his career at juvenile and underage levels with [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] as a [[dual player]]. He won a Limerick MAHC medal in 1983 before claiming a Limerick MAFC medal the following year.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Bruff champs after 42 years|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=17 September 1983|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}} Reale progressed to adult level, also as a dual player, and won a Limerick JAFC medal in 1987 after a 2-07 to 1-03 win over [[St Patrick's GAA (Limerick)|St Patrick's]].{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Bruff tops in dull tie|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=7 November 1987|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}} He won a [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] medal two years later after a defeat of [[Old Christians GAA Club|Old Christians]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Bruff celebrate first major title|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=7 November 1987|accessdate=6 October 2019|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Reale first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the minor team that beat [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] to win the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|All-Ireland MHC]] title in 1984.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145499/Limerick-s-last-All-Ireland-minor.html|title=Limerick's last All-Ireland minor hurling title - 1984|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=5 September 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to the under-21 team and won consecutive [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] titles, before claiming an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland U21HC]] medal after a 2-15 to 3-06 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|1987 final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/109109/Limerick-s-first-All-Ireland-U.html|title=Limerick's first All Ireland U-21 hurling title in 1987|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=10 September 2015|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Reale joined the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in 1988. He claimed his only senior silverware in 1992 when Limerick won the [[National Hurling League]] title.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/coming-back-from-the-dead-is-nothing-new-to-limerick/27453640.html|title=Coming back from the dead is nothing new to Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|date=30 June 2001|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Bruff *[[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]]: 1989 *Limerick Junior A Football Championship: 1987 *Limerick Minor A Football Championship: 1984 *Limerick Minor A Hurling Championship: 1983 ;Limerick *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1991–92 National Hurling League|1991–92]] *[[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|1987]] *[[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1986 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1986]], [[1987 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1987]] *[[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] *[[Munster Minor Hurling Championship]]: [[1984 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|1984]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title= Mike Reale navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Minor Hurling Team 1984}} {{Limerick Under 21 Team 1987}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Reale, Mike}} [[Category:1966 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Bruff hurlers]] [[Category:Bruff Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

At club level, he played with [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== At club level, O'Grady first played for [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] at juvenile and underage levels, and was part of the club's under-21 team that won consecutive Limerick U21AHC titles in 1996 and 1997.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=The 'Well tops in rowdy final|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=7 December 1996|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Another title for the 'Well|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=20 December 1997|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to the club's senior side and won his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medal in 2000 after a 0–16 to 0–15 win over [[Doon GAA|Doon]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/veteran-kirby-fires-well-to-final-glory-26106240.html|title=Veteran Kirby fires 'Well to final glory|publisher=Irish Independent|date=9 October 2000|accessdate=15 October 2018|first=|last=}} O'Grady added a second Limerick SHC medal to his collection in 2003 after a win over [[Adare GAA|Adare]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/old-guard-command-the-well-25926060.html|title=Old guard command the 'Well|publisher=Irish Independent|date=13 October 2003|accessdate=15 October 2018|first=|last=}} O'Grady first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]] in 1997.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/145462/Limerick-minor-hurlers---trying.html|title=Limerick minor hurlers -
