J. Ryan''' (born 12 November 1974) is an Irish [[hurling]] manager, selector and former player. At club level, he played with [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[Knocklong]], [[County Limerick]], Ryan attended the local [[National school (Ireland)|national school]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/91350/Limerick-v-Tipperary-SHC-preview-.html|title=Limerick v Tipperary SHC preview - TJ Ryan in manager’s hot seat|publisher=Limerick Live|date=29 May 2014|access-date=27 May 2026}} He later attended the Presentation De La Salle Secondary School in [[Hospital, County Limerick|Hospital]] and played hurling in all grades during his time there, including in the [[Dr Harty Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=LML19901020.1.16&srpos=5&e=01-01-1990-31-12-1991--en-20--1--img-txIN-tj+ryan+de+la+salle+hospital+hurling---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all---AND-0-0--&coordinates=594,1056,576,576|title=Harty Cup: De La Salle Hospital out|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=20 October 1990|access-date=27 May 2026}} Ryan later studied [[agricultural science]] at [[University College Galway]] and played on the university's [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] team, however, he left after two years without taking his degree.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40919465.html|title=TJ Ryan interview: Podcasting, his playing career and intercounty management|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=16 July 2022|access-date=27 May 2026}} ==Club career== Ryan began his club career at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] club. He won a Limerick U21BHC medal in 1995, when he and his brother [[Donie Ryan]] scored 2–09 in the 5–13 to 0–07 win over [[Monaleen GAA|Monaleen]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=LML19951111.1.24&srpos=1&e=01-07-1995-31-12-1995--en-20--1--img-txIN-garryspillane+under+21+hurling---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all---AND-0-0--&coordinates=0,375,576,576|title=Garryspillane bounce Monaleen in 21 decider|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=11 November 1995|access-date=27 May 2026}} By that stage, Ryan had already lined out at adult level. He was in goal when Garryspillane beat Ardagh by 4–12 to 2–07 in a replay to win the [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick IHC]] title in 1990.{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=LML19901027.1.20&srpos=3&e=01-08-1990-30-11-1990--en-20--1--img-txIN-garryspillane+ardagh+replay---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all---AND-0-0--&coordinates=780,1005,819,819|title='Bouncers prove best|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=27 October 1990|access-date=27 May 2026}} Ryan claimed a second Limerick IHC medal after a 1–10 to 0–11 win over [[Mungret/St. Paul's GAA|Mungret/St Paul's]] in 1996.{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=LML19961116.1.25&srpos=1&e=11-11-1996-16-11-1996--en-20--1--img-txIN-garryspillane+mungret+---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all--garryspillane+mungret-AND-0-0--&coordinates=921,389,684,684|title=Up the bouncers after great win|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=16 November 1996|access-date=27 May 2026}} After winning the Limerick SBHC title after an extra-time defeat of [[Knockainey GAA|Knockainey]] in 2004, Ryan was at wing-forward when Garryspillane won their first ever [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] in 2005, after a 2–15 to 2–12 win over [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] in the [[2005 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=EEC20040830.1.89&srpos=1&e=23-08-2004-31-08-2004--en-20--1--img-txIN-garryspillane+hurling+tj+ryan+---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all--garryspillane+hurling+tj+ryan-AND-0-0--&coordinates=116,0,576,576|title=Bouncers rebound in style to land title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=30 August 2004|access-date=27 May 2026}} {{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/carroll-s-just-reward-1.506589|title=Carroll's just reward|publisher=Irish Times|date=17 October 2005|access-date=31 October 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10079361.html|title=Long wait over for Garryspillane|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=17 October 2005|access-date=31 October 2024}} He played his last senior club game in September 2009 in a 1-15 to 1-09 relegation play-off defeat of [[Tournafulla GAA|Tournafulla]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=117783|title=Limerick great Ryan retires|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=13 September 2009|accessdate=10 July 2014}} ==Inter-county career== Ryan first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] during a two-year stint with the [[All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship|minor team]]. He was wing-forward when the team was beaten by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[1991 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|1991 Munster MHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=IEX19910708.1.13&srpos=2&e=08-07-1991-08-07-1991--en-20--1--img-txIN-tipperary+limerick+minor---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all---AND-0-0--&coordinates=0,802,2547,2547|title=Barrett Tipp minors' ace|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=8 July 1991|access-date=29 May 2026}} Ryan later spent three consecutive years with the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]], but ended his underage career without silverware.{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=IEX19930724.1.24&srpos=2&e=24-07-1993-24-07-1993--en-20--1--img-txIN-limerick+cork+hurling---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all---AND-0-0--&coordinates=0,799,1449,1449|title=Cork's honour after rip-roaring clash|publisher=The Cork Examiner|date=24 July 1993|access-date=29 May 2026}} Ryan was just 18-years-old when he made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in a [[National Hurling League]] game against [[Cork GAA|Cork]] in October 1993.{{cite web|url=https://irishnewsarchive.com/?a=d&d=IPR19931018.1.37&srpos=4&e=01-10-1993-31-12-1993--en-20--1--img-txIN-tj+ryan+limerick+hurling+league---------1-1-1-1-1-1-community-------INA-mr-all---AND-0-0--&coordinates=65,0,1665,1665|title=Champs shocked!|publisher=Irish Press|date=18 October 1993|access-date=29 May 2026}} He made his [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] debut against the same opposition in June 1994. Ryan won his first Munster SHC later that year, following a 0–25 to 2–10 win over [[Clare GAA|Clare]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He lined out at corner-forward in Limerick's 3–16 to 2–13 defeat by [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] in the [[1994 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1994 All-Ireland SHC final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20093934.html|title=Kirby fearful over Limerick’s lack of firepower|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=12 June 2009|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Two years later, Ryan won a second Munster SHC medal after beating Tipperary by 4–07 to 0–16 in a replay. Limerick later qualified for the [[1996 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1996 All-Ireland SHC final]], with Ryan once again lining out at corner-forward, however, [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] won the game by 1–13 to 0–14.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40370429.html|title=A player-by-player guide to Wexford's All-Ireland 25 years on: 'We laughed as much as we hurled'|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=1 September 2021|access-date=2 January 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/yourview/arid-10098744.html|title=Limerck: where broken dreams are a way of life|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 August 2009|access-date=10 July 2014}} He added a National League medal to his collection in 1997.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/gaa/945696/limerick-county-final-day-to-honour-25th-anniversary-of-1997-hurling-league-title-victory.html|title=Limerick county final day to honour 25th anniversary of 1997 hurling league title victory|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=30 October 2022|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Ryan continued to line out with Limerick for much of the following decade. He served as [[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|team captain]] in 2004 and 2006.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-10116334.html|title=Captain by accident, leader by nature|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=28 May 2004|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/ryan-determined-to-learn-lesson-from-defeat/a/148549474.html|title=Ryan determined to learn lesson from defeat|publisher=Irish Independent|date=5 May 2006|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Ryan announced his retirement from inter-county hurling in July 2006.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30269555.html|title=Limerick skipper Ryan retires|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=26 July 2006|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} ==Inter-provincial career== Ryan's performances at inter-county level resulted in him being selected for the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team. He won his first [[Railway Cup]] medal as a non-playing substitute in 2000, before claiming a second successive title in 2001, after lining out at corner-back in the 1-21 to 1-15 win over [[Connacht GAA|Connacht]] in the [[2001 Railway Cup Hurling Championship#Final|final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/munster-deluge-swamps-connacht-26067543.html|title=Munster deluge swamps Connacht|date=12 November 2001|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=30 December 2018}} ==Management career== Ryan was an unsuccessful candidate for the Limerick senior team's manager post in September 2010, however, he became a selector, alongside former teammates [[Ciarán Carey]] and [[Pat Heffernan]], under [[Dónal O'Grady]].{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/ogrady-gets-the-green-light-131620.html|title=O'Grady gets the green light|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=10 July 2014|date=23 September 2010}} The new management sought to restore order to the team, following on from a year in which the players went on strike and refused to play. Limerick went on to win the [[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 2]] title in 2011, following a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the final.{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=10 July 2014|date=1 May 2011}} The Limerick management team broke up after one year and Ryan moved to the club scene as manager of [[Kilworth GAA|Kilworth]]. He guided the team to the [[Cork Intermediate Hurling Championship|Cork IHC]] title in October 2012, after a 2-15 to 2-13 win over [[Kanturk GAA|Kanturk]].{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/kilworth-finally-end-years-of-anguish-210877.html|title=Kilworth finally end years of anguish|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=10 July 2014|date=15 October 2012|first=Therese|last=O'Callaghan}} Ryan was appointed manager of the Limerick under-21 team in November 2012 and spent one season in charge.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/sport/gaelic-games/tj-ryan-appointed-limerick-u-21-hurling-boss-1-4477467|title=TJ Ryan appointed Limerick U-21 hurling boss|publisher=Limerick Leader|accessdate=10 July 2014|date=15 November 2012}} In November 2013, Ryan was named as the joint-manager of the Limerick senior hurling team, alongside former boss Dónal O'Grady. He took over as manager in his own right in April 2014, when O'Grady stepped away when the Limerick County Board falsely claimed at a meeting that the co-managers had "apologised for the abysmal" displays of the team during the National League.{{cite web|url=http://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/hurling/shock-for-limerick-as-ogrady-quits-post-as-coach-and-co-manager-266052.html|title=Shock for Limerick as O’Grady quits post as coach and co-manager|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=10 July 2014|date=21 April 2014|first=Michael|last=Moynihan}}{{cite web|url=https://www.gaa.ie/search/crawl/news/ryan-stay-limerick-manager|title=TJ Ryan to stay on as Limerick manager|publisher=GAA website|accessdate=22 April 2014|date=23 April 2014|first=|last=}} Ryan stepped down as manager in July 2016.{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-confirm-they-will-be-looking-for-a-new-hurling-manager-for-2017-34874898.html|title=Limerick confirm they will be looking for a new hurling manager for 2017|date=11 July 2016|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=12 July 2016}}{{cite web|url= http://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/banner-blitz-signals-end-for-ryan-34872407.html|title=Banner blitz signals end for Ryan|date=11 July 2016|work=Irish Independent|accessdate=12 July 2016}} Ryan returned to club management with Garryspillane. He guided the team to the [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Limerick PIHC]] title in October 2018, after a 2–12 to 0–12 win over [[Bruff GAA|Bruff]] in the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30877092.html|title=Garryspillane get the better of Bruff in Limerick Premier IHC final|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=20 October 2018|accessdate=24 September 2020|first=|last=}} Ryan later served as trainer of the [[St Thomas' GAA|St Thomas']] team that won three consecutive [[Galway Senior Hurling Championship|Galway SHC]] titles between 2018 and 2020.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40120133.html|title=TJ Ryan dismisses links with Charleville job|date=1 December 2020|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 May 2026}} '''Tom Ryan''' (born 1944 in Ballybrown, [[County Limerick]], Ireland) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] former [[hurling]] [[Manager (Gaelic games)|manager]] and player.  He played hurling with his local club [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]]<ref name='intv'>{{cite news
|url=http://www.limerickleader.ie/interview/The-Leader-Interviewwith-Tom-Ryan.4997756.jp
|accessdate=17 July 2010
|newspaper=[[Limerick Leader]]
|title=The Leader Interview..with Tom Ryan
|author=
|date=19 February 2009
}}</ref> and was a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] senior inter-county team from 1973 until 1976.  Ryan later served as manager of both the Limerick and [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] senior inter-county teams.<ref name='west'/>

==Playing career==
===Club===

Ryan played his club hurling with his local club in [[Ballybrown GAA|Ballybrown]].<ref name='intv'/>

===Inter-county===

Ryan began his playing career with Limerick in the 1960s and went on as a substitute for [[Bernie Hartigan]] in the 1973 All Ireland Final which Limerick won, beating [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] by 1–21 to 1–14. He started the 1974 All Ireland final as a right half back but Limerick were beaten by Kilkenny 3–19 to 1–13. He also won a [[National Hurling League]]{{Clarify|date=July 2010}} as a player in 1971.

==Managerial career==
===Limerick===
Ryan took over as Limerick senior hurling manager from [[Phil Bennis]] in the late summer of 1993 and remained as manager until 1997. He won two Munster titles in 1994 and 1996 as a manager, and won a National Hurling League in 1997. He was removed immediately after that success following a frosty relationship with the Limerick county board officers. He was replaced as manager by [[Éamonn Cregan]].

===Westmeath===
Ryan was appointed manager of the [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] senior hurling team in November 2003.<ref name='west'>{{cite web |url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2003/1113/westmeath.html|title=Ryan to manage Westmeath hurlers|publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]]|date=13 November 2003|accessdate=13 September 2009}}</ref>  After two unsuccessful years in this position, he stepped down in 2005.

'''Pat Tobin''' (born 1982 in [[Murroe]], [[County Limerick]]) is an [[Republic of Ireland|Irish]] sportsperson.  He plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] and was a member at inter-county level of the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]] from 2004 until 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/battlelines-are-drawn-695587.html|title=Battlelines are drawn - Tobin equaliser whets appetite for replay after Munster thriller|last=Hogan|first=Vincent|date=11 June 2007|work=[[Irish Independent]]|accessdate=23 November 2010}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Club===

Tobin plays his club [[hurling]] with his local [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] club, however, he has yet to taste success at [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|senior level]].  Tobin's brother, [[Kevin Tobin|Kevin]], also plays on the team.

===Inter-county===

Tobin first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the successful [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] under-21 team of the early 2000s.  He came on as a substitute to win a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] title in this grade in 2000.  He later collected an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal with the team following a victory over [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the championship decider.  In 2002 Tobin won a second Munster under-21 medal.  He later came on as a substitute in the All-Ireland final against [[Galway GAA|Galway]] to capture a second consecutive All-Ireland medal.  It was Limerick's third such victory in-a-row.  Tobin later joined the county senior team, however, Limerick hurling was in the doldrums at the time.  All this changed in 2007 under the management of [[Richie Bennis]].  Limerick began their championship campaign with an epic battle with [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]].  In the first game of three Tobin contributed 1-1, however, after a second replay Limerick emerged victorious and qualified to play [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]] in the Munster final.  Although Limerick lost on that occasion the team showed that they were not a pushover.  Limerick later gained their revenge on Waterford by defeating them in the All-Ireland semi-final.  This victory allowed Tobin's side to play [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] in the championship decider. '''Kevin Tobin''' (born 1981 in Boher, [[County Limerick]]) is an [[Republic of Ireland|Irish]] sportsperson.  He plays [[hurling]] with his local club [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].<ref name="tobin">{{cite web|url=http://hoganstand.com/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=46568|title=Tobin added to Limerick squad|date=18 May 2005|work=[[Hogan Stand]]|accessdate=23 November 2010}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===Club===

Tobin plays his club [[hurling]] with his local [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] club, however, he has yet to taste success at [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|senior level]].  Tobin's brother [[Pat Tobin|Pat]] also plays on the team.<ref name="tobin" />

===Inter-county===

Tobin first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the successful [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] under-21 team of the early 2000s.  He won his first [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster]] title in this grade in 2000.  He later collected an [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal with the team following a victory over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the championship decider.  In 2001 Tobin won a second Munster under-21 medal.  He played in the All-Ireland final against [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] scoring 2 points to capture a second consecutive All-Ireland medal.  The following year Tobin added a third Munster medal to his collection.  Once again Limerick went all the way and Tobin captured a third consecutive All-Ireland medal.  It was Limerick's third such victory in-a-row.  Tobin later joined the county senior team, however, Limerick hurling was in the doldrums at the time.  All this changed in 2007 under the management of [[Richie Bennis]].  Limerick began their championship campaign with an epic battle with [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]].  Limerick went on to win the second replay and qualified to play [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]] in the Munster final.  Although Limerick lost on that occasion the team showed that they were not a pushover.  Limerick later gained their revenge on Waterford by defeating them in the All-Ireland semi-final.  This victory allowed Tobin's side to play [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] in the championship decider.  Unfortunately, Limerick got off to a bad start and conceded two goals in the first ten minutes.  'The Cats', however, went on to win the game by six points.

Timmy Ryan.text:
{{Short description|Limerick hurler}} {{For|similarly named people|Tim Ryan (disambiguation)}} {{Use dmy dates|date=November 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=November 2022}} {{multiple issues| {{more citations needed|date=March 2024}} {{POV|date=March 2024}} }} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Timmy Ryan | irish = Tadhg Ó Riain | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | nickname = Goodboy | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] | cl_position = Midfield | cl_years = 1928–1946 | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 13 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = Midfield | ic_years = 1930–1946 | ic_apps_points = 45 | ic_province = 5 | ic_all_ireland = 3 | nhl = 5 | cl_update = | ic_update = 18:57, 24 April 2014 | birth_date = 7 May 1909 | birth_place=[[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], Ireland | death_date = 28 January 1995 (aged 85) | death_place = [[Killoscully]], County Tipperary, Ireland }} '''Timothy Ryan''' (7 May 1909 – 28 January 1995) was an Irish [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a midfielder at senior level for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]].{{cite web|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1934.htm|title=1934 All-Ireland Champions|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|accessdate=24 April 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505003906/http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1934.htm|archivedate=5 May 2015|df=dmy-all}} ==Biographical overview== Born in [[Castleconnell]], [[County Limerick]], Ryan first arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of twenty, when he first linked up with the Limerick senior team. He made his senior debut in the [[1930 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1930 championship]]. Ryan went on to win three [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medals, five [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medals and five [[National Hurling League]] medals with Limerick. An All-Ireland runner-up on two occasions, Ryan also captained the team to the All-Ireland title in 1934. Ryan represented the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team at various times throughout his career, winning five [[Railway Cup]] medals. At club level, he won thirteen [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medals with [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]]. Throughout his inter-county career, Ryan made a then record of 45 championship appearances for Limerick. His retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1946 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1946 championship]]. In retirement from playing, Ryan became involved in team management and coaching. He was a selector and adviser with Ahane during their championship victory in 1955. ==Playing career== ===Club=== Ryan was sixteen years-old when the [[Ahane GAA|Ahane]] club was formed in 1926. His first success came in 1928 when a 5–1 to 2–2 defeat of [[Kilmeedy GAA|Kilmeedy]] gave him a junior championship medal. In 1929, a 1–8 to 1–2 defeat of [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] gave Ryan an intermediate championship medal. In 1931, he was a part of the Ahane team that reached the final of the senior championship. A 5–5 to 1–4 win over [[Croom GAA|Croom]] gave Ahane their first senior title, while it also gave Ryan his first [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal. Ahane failed to retain their title, however, Ryan's team returned to the championship decider once again in 1933. A 1–7 to 1–1 defeat of Croom gave him his second championship medal. Back-to-back defeats of [[Kidimo GAA|Kildimo]] in 1934 and 1935, followed by four successive defeats of Croom brought Ryan's championship medal tally to eight. Eight-in-a-row proved beyond Ahane, as Croom triumphed in 1940 and again in 1941. Ahane hurlers bounced back in 1942 to reach a tenth successive county decider. A 7–8 to 1–0 defeat of [[Rathkeale GAA|Rathkeale]] gave Ryan a ninth winners' medal in the hurling championship. Further defeats of Croom, Rathkeale (twice) and [[Granagh-Ballingarry GAA|Granagh-Ballingarry]] yielded further championships in succession. These victories brought Ryan's championship medal tally to a remarkable thirteen. ===Inter-county=== ====Beginnings==== Ryan joined the Limerick senior team in 1930. Ryan lined out in his first Munster decider in 1933, as Limerick faced [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]]. With eight minutes left in the game, some spectators invaded the pitch and the match was abandoned. Since Limerick were winning by 3–7 to 1–2, the [[Munster GAA|Munster Council]] declared them the champions and Ryan collected his first [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal.{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|title=Senior Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|accessdate=24 April 2014|archive-url=https://archive.today/20110721124423/http://munster.gaa.ie/history/sh_teams/|archive-date=2011-07-21}} The subsequent All-Ireland final on 3 September 1933, saw a record crowd of 45,176 travel to [[Croke Park]] to see Limerick face Kilkenny. After being level at the interval, the game remained close in the second half until a solo-run goal by [[Johnny Dunne]] sealed a 1–7 to 0–6 victory for Kilkenny. ====Dominance==== A successful league campaign throughout 1933–34 saw Limerick reach the decider against [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]]. In spite of home advantage, Limerick had to battle hard for a 3–6 to 3–3 victory. It was Ryan's first league medal. The subsequent provincial championship saw Limerick reach the decider, where they played Waterford for the second year in-a-row. The result was much the same, with Ryan collecting a second Munster medal following a 4–8 to 2–5 victory. The All-Ireland final on 2 September 1934, was a special occasion as it was the golden jubilee final of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]]. Dublin were the opponents and a close game developed. After leading by a point at the interval, Limerick went five clear with time running out. Dublin fought their way back to secure a remarkable draw. The replay on 30 September turned out to be an even closer affair, with both sides level with two minutes to go. Points from [[Mick Mackey]] and [[Jackie O'Connell]] and four goals from [[Dave Clohessy]] secured a 5–2 to 2–6 victory for Limerick. The win gave Ryan an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal, while he also had the honour of collecting the [[Liam MacCarthy Cup]] as captain. Ryan added a second league medal to his collection as captain in 1935, as Limerick retained their title in a straightforward league format. Limerick dominated the provincial series of games once again, and lined out in the decider against Tipperary. He collected a third Munster medal following a 5–5 to 1–4 victory. Kilkenny were Limerick's opponents in the subsequent All-Ireland final on 1 September 1935, and, once again, the game was a close affair. Limerick were the red-hot favourites as a record crowd of over 46,000 turned up to watch the match. At the beginning of the second-half [[Lory Meagher]] scored a point from midfield giving Kilkenny a lead which they would not surrender. The game ended in controversial circumstances for Mackey when Limerick were awarded a close-in free to level the game. Jack Keane issued an instruction from the sideline that Ryan was to take the free and put the sliotar over the bar for the equalising point. As he lined up to take it, Mick Mackey pushed him aside and took the free himself. The shot dropped short and into the hands of the Kilkenny goalkeeper and was cleared. The game ended shortly after with Kilkenny triumphing by 2–5 to 2–4. Limerick began 1936 by retaining their league title, having won seven of their games and drawing one. It was Ryan's third league medal. The team later embarked on a tour of the United States where they defeated a [[New York GAA|New York]] team made up of Irish expatriates. As a result of the tour Limerick were awarded a bye into the Munster final. Tipperary provided the opposition in the provincial final, however, a 5–3 haul from an injured Mick Mackey secured an 8–6 to 4–5 victory and a fourth successive Munster medal for Ryan. For the third time in four years the lure of a Kilkenny-Limerick clash brought a record crowd of over 50,000 to Croke Park for the All-Ireland decider on 6 September 1936. The first half produced a game that lived up to the previous clashes, and Limerick had a two-point advantage at half-time. [[Jackie Power]] scored two first-half goals, while a solo-run goal by Mackey in the second-half helped Limerick to a 5–6 to 1–5 victory. Ryan had won a second All-Ireland medal. ====Final success and decline==== In 1937, Ryan captured another league title, his fourth overall. Limerick's bid for a record-equalling fifth successive Munster crown came to an end in the provincial decider when Tipperary were victorious. Limerick entered the record books in 1938 as the first team to win five consecutive National League titles. It is a record which has never been equalled. Ryan played a key role in all five of the victories.{{original research inline|date=March 2024}} A period of decline followed for Limerick, with many people believing that the team's best days were behind them. This certainly seemed the case in 1940, when it took two late goals from Jackie Power and a storming display by Mick Mackey to level the Munster semi-final with Waterford. Another late rally gave Limerick a victory in the subsequent replay. Ryan's side put in another excellent performance{{original research inline|date=March 2024}} in the Munster final to draw the game with reigning provincial champions Cork.{{tone inline|date=March 2024}} At half-time in the replay Limerick looked like a spent force. Held scoreless for the entire thirty minutes, Mackey got the recovery underway in the second-half with a point from a seventy. He later moved back to the defense, where Cork were running riot with goals. A pitch invasion scuppered the game for ten minutes, however, Limerick held on to win by 3–3 to 2–4 and Ryan collected a fifth Munster medal. The subsequent All-Ireland decider, on 1 September 1940, brought Kilkenny and Limerick together. Early in the second-half Kilkenny took a four-point lead, however, a positional switch at midfield proved vital.{{original research inline|date=March 2024}} Limerick hung on to win the game on a score line of 3–7 to 1–7. The win gave Ryan his third All-Ireland medal. Limerick took a back seat to Cork and Tipperary in the Munster series of games for the next few years.{{tone inline|date=March 2024}} In 1944, Limerick squared up to Cork in the provincial final as Cork were aiming for a fourth consecutive All-Ireland final victory. Ryan was a veteran hurler by now, however, he was still a key member of the Limerick team. In the game, Cork come back to draw the game on a 4–13 to 6–7 score line. In the last fifteen minutes of the subsequent replay, Limerick were up by four points when a goal by Mick Mackey was disallowed as he was deemed to be fouled as he went through. The subsequent free hit the outside of the post and dropped wide. Only seconds remained when Cork's [[Christy Ring]] caught the sliotar and fired a fierce shot into the net to win the game. Following a defeat by Cork in the Munster decider in 1946, Ryan effectively retired from inter-county hurling. ===Inter-provincial=== Ryan also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial series of games, and enjoyed much success during an eight-year career.{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=11 June 2009|accessdate=25 April 2014|first=|last=}} He was first included on the team in 1933, however, [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] defeated Munster by 4–6 to 3–6 in the decider. Both sides renewed their rivalry the following year, with Ryan, who was now captain of the team, winning his first [[Railway Cup]] medal following a 6–3 to 3–2 victory. Munster made it two-in-a-row in 1935, with Ryan winning a second Railway Cup medal as captain. After defeat in 1936, Munster bounced back in 1937. A 1–9 to 3–1 defeat of Leinster in the decider gave Ryan a third Railway Cup medal. It was the first of four successive final defeats of Leinster, with Ryan collecting further winners' medals in 1938 and 1939. Ryan made his last appearance for Munster in 1941, however, it ended in defeat. ==Honours== ===Team=== ;Ahane *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] (13): 1931, 1933, 1934, 1935, 1936, 1937, 1938, 1939, 1942, 1943, 1944, 1945, 1946 ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (3): [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1934|1934]] (c), [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1936|1936]], [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1940|1940]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (5): [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1933#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1933]], [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1934#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1934]] (c), [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1935#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1935]] (c), [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1936#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1936]], [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1940#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1940]] *[[National Hurling League]] (5): [[National Hurling League 1933-34|1933–34]], [[National Hurling League 1934-35|1934–35]] (c), [[National Hurling League 1935-36|1935–36]] (c), [[National Hurling League 1936-37|1936–37]], [[National Hurling League 1937-38|1937–38]] ;Munster *[[Railway Cup]] (5): 1934 (c), 1935 (c), 1937, 1938, 1939 ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Timmy Ryan navigation boxes |list1= {{s-start}} {{s-sports}} {{succession box | before=[[Micky Fitzgibbon]] | title=[[List of Limerick senior hurling team captains|Limerick Senior Hurling Captain]] | years=1934–1935 | after=[[Mick Mackey]] }} {{s-ach|achievements}} {{succession box | before=[[Eddie Doyle (hurler)|Eddie Doyle]]

In retirement from playing Scanlan became a highly respected referee at club championship level. A move to Galway shortly after this victory saw Scanlan join the [[Liam Mellows GAA|Liam Mellows]] club. He won a [[Galway Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal in 1935 as Liam Mellows defeated [[Ballinderreen GAA|Ballinderreen]] in the decider. ===Inter-county=== ====Beginnings==== On 1 May 1932 Scanlan made his competitive debut for Limerick in a 5-5 to 4-1 semi-final defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the pre-season Thomond Feis. An injury ruled Scanlan out of the replay and he was replaced in goal by [[Tom Shinny]]. Limerick won at the second attempt on a score line of 5-2 to 2-6. At the beginning of the second-half [[Lory Meagher]] sent over a huge point from midfield giving Kilkenny a lead which they would not surrender. The game ended in controversial circumstances for [[Mick Mackey]] when Limerick were awarded a close-in free to level the game. The game ended shortly after with Kilkenny triumphing by 2-5 to 2-4. Held scoreless for the entire opening half, Limerick sprang to life for the second period of play. A pitch invasion scuppered the game for ten minutes, however, Limerick held on to win by 3-3 to 2-4 and Scanlan collected a fifth Munster medal. The subsequent All-Ireland decider on 1 September 1940 brought Kilkenny and Limerick together for the last great game between the two outstanding teams of the decade. Early in the second-half Kilkenny took a four-point lead, however, once Mick Mackey was deployed at midfield he proceeded to dominate the game. Limerick hung on to win the game on a score line of 3-7 to 1-7. The win gave Scanlan his second All-Ireland medal. ===Inter-provincial=== Scanlon also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial hurling competition. He won his first [[Railway Cup]] medal in 1934 as Munster defeated [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]]. Scanlon won three more Railway Cup titles in 1937, 1938 and 1940. ==Honours== ===Player=== ;Ahane *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] (3): 1931 (c), 1933, 1934 ;Liam Mellows *[[Galway Senior Hurling Championship]] (1): 1935 ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] (3): [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1934|1934]] [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1936|1936]], [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1940|1940]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (5): [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1933]], [[1934 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1934]], [[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1936]], [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1940]] *[[National Hurling League]] (4): [[National Hurling League 1933-34|1933-34]], [[National Hurling League 1934-35|1934-35]], [[National Hurling League 1936-37|1936-37]], [[National Hurling League 1937-38|1937-38]] ;Munster *[[Railway Cup]] (4): 1934, 1937, 1938, 1940 ==References== {{reflist}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1933}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1934}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1935}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1936}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1940}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Scanlon, Paddy}} [[Category:1905 births]] [[Category:1977 deaths]] [[Category:Ahane hurlers]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship winners]] [[Category:Hurling goalkeepers]] [[Category:Hurling referees]] [[Category:Irish publicans]] [[Category:Liam Mellows hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]] [[Category:People from Castleconnell]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

'''Thomas Shinny''' (1899 – 8 May 1963) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[hurling|hurler]] who played as a goalkeeper for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].

Born in Fedamore, [[County Limerick]], Shinny first arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of twenty-five when he first linked up with the Limerick senior team. He made his senior debut during a tournament game in 1925. Shinny went on to enjoy a lengthy inter-county career, and won one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal and one [[National Hurling League]] medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile.aspx|title=County profile: Limerick|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=3 October 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120525185227/http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/Profile.aspx|archive-date=25 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1934.htm|title=1934 All-Ireland champions|publisher=Finbarr Connolly website|access-date=20 April 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505003906/http://www.finbarrconnolly.com/1934.htm|archive-date=5 May 2015}}</ref>

Shinny represented the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team at various times, winning two [[Railway Cup]] medals on the field of play and a third as a substitute. At club level he won one [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal with [[Fedamore GAA|Fedamore]].

His retirement from inter-county hurling came following the conclusion of the [[National Hurling League 1935-36|1935–36 National Hurling League]].

==Playing career==
===Club===

Shinny was in goal for [[Fedamore GAA|Fedamore]] when the club reached the club championship decider in 1927. A 5–1 to 1–3 defeat of [[Young Irelands GAA (Limerick)|Young Irelands]] gave him a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]] medal.

===Inter-county===

Following some impressive performances for his club, Shinny joined the Limerick senior team and was first choice goalkeeper for the team's unsuccessful [[Thomond Feis]] campaign in 1926.

Shinny played for Limerick at a time when the team's fortunes were at a low ebb, with [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]] dominating the provincial series. He retired from inter-county hurling in 1930.

In 1934, Limerick were held to a draw by [[Dublin county hurling team|Dublin]] in the All-Ireland decider. Three days before the replay regular goalkeeper [[Paddy Scanlan (hurler)|Paddy Scanlan]] was taken ill and was forced to withdraw from the team. Shinny made a sensational return as goalkeeper. The replay turned out to be an even closer affair than the first game, with both sides level with two minutes to go. Points from [[Mick Mackey]] and [[Jackie O'Connell]] and a remarkable four goals from [[Dave Clohessy]] secured a 5–2 to 2–6 victory for Limerick. The win gave Shinny an [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal in the golden jubilee year of the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]].

Shinny remained on the team for another few years as sub goalkeeper. He won a [[National Hurling League]] medal in 1936 as Limerick remained undefeated during their eight-game campaign. Shinny retired from inter-county hurling shortly after this victory.

===Inter-provincial===

Shinny also lined out with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] in the inter-provincial series of games, and enjoyed much success during a brief career. He won his first [[Railway Cup]] medal as a non-playing substitute in 1928 as Munster defeated arch rivals [[Leinster GAA|Leinster]] by 2–2 to 1–2.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/history/railway-cup-hurling/|title=Railway Cup Hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=20 April 2014}}</ref>

In 1929 Shinny broke onto the starting fifteen as first choice goalkeeper. A 5–3 to 3–1 defeat of Leinster once again gave him a second Railway Cup medal. Munster made it three-in-a-row in 1930, with Shinny collecting a third winners' medal following a 4–6 to 2–7 defeat of Leinster once again.

'''Liam Ryan''' (1936 – 27 May 2015) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] priest, sociologist and [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a left wing-forward at senior level for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.askaboutireland.ie/aai-files/assets/libraries/limerick-city-library/reading-room/sport/liam-ryan-part-1.pdf|title=Profile of Liam Ryan|date=|publisher=The Limerick Leader|accessdate=18 October 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/irish-news/news/liam-ryan-31267003.html|title=Obituary: Liam Ryan|date=31 May 2015|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=1 June 2015|first=Barry|last=Duggan}}</ref>

Ryan made his first appearance for the team during the [[1955 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1955 championship]] and played intermittently for the team over the course of the next six seasons. During that time he won one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] winners' medal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://munster.gaa.ie/winning-teams/sh_teams/|title=Munster Senior Hurling Final Winners|date=|work=[[Munster GAA]]|accessdate=18 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100107012735/http://munster.gaa.ie/winning-teams/sh_teams/|archive-date=7 January 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was captain on that occasion and remains the youngest Munster final-winning captain.

At club level, Ryan was a three-time [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county championship]] winners' medalist with his local [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] club.

==Playing career==

===Club===
Ryan played his club hurling with the [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] club and enjoyed much success in a brief club championship career.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

He spent four years with the Cappamore minor hurling team, winning two East Limerick championship titles, however, the club narrowly missed out on a county minor title on both occasions.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

By this stage Ryan had already lined out for Cappamore's top team. He was barely sixteen when he won a county junior championship winners' medal in 1952. His inclusion on the team was as a result of a shortage of players.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

Two years later in 1954 Cappamore had reached the final of the county senior championship. A victory over [[Western Gaels GAA|Western Gaels]] gave Ryan a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|county senior championship]] winners' medal. He added two more senior medals to his collection in 1956 and 1959.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}}

===Inter-county===
Ryan first came to prominence on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] minor hurling team in 1952. He enjoyed little success in this grade, losing back-to-back [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster]] finals in 1953 and 1954.

In 1955 Ryan made his debut as captain with the Limerick senior hurling team. After beating [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]] in the opening round of the provincial campaign, Limerick later went into the Munster final as underdogs against [[Clare GAA|Clare]]. In a shock result Limerick defeated their nearest neighbours by 2-16 to 2-6. Ryan, in collecting the cup, became the youngest Munster final-winning captain. Limerick later played [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the All-Ireland semi-final, however, they were comfortably beaten by 2-12 to 2-3.

Limerick reached the provincial decider again in 1956 with [[Cork GAA|Cork]] providing the opposition. Ryan's side looked set to retain their title, however, a hat-trick of goals by [[Christy Ring]] swung the result in Cork's favour and Limerick were beaten by 5-5 to 3-5.

Ryan's studies for the priesthood impacted on his inter-county career and he missed the next three championship seasons with Limerick.

In 1960 Ryan was back with Limerick, however, as he had already been [[ordained]] a priest and was not allowed to play, he adopted the name 'Tom' Ryan and played anyhow. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] easily won that match, bringing an end to Ryan's inter-county career.

==Personal life==
Ryan was born into a family that had a strong association with hurling. His father, [[Willie Ryan (Limerick hurler)|Willie Ryan]], was a hurler with the great Limerick team of the 1918-1921 era and won two [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] winners' medals.

He was educated locally in Cappamore before later attending [[St. Flannan's College]] in [[Ennis]] where he excelled as a hurler. He won a [[Dr. Harty Cup]] winners' medal in 1952 and an inter-provincial colleges' title with [[Munster GAA|Munster]] the following year.

==Academic and Clerical career==

{{Infobox academic
| name           = Liam Ryan
| image          =
| birth_date     = 1936
| death_date     = 27 May 2015
| birth_place    = 
| death_place    =

Ryan, along with his brother Séamus Ryan, who also hurled with Limerick, subsequently studied for the priesthood at [[Maynooth College]] where he was ordained in 1960 for the [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Cashel and Emly]].<ref name="maydos">[https://www.maynoothuniversity.ie/news-events/rev-prof-liam-ryan-passes-away Rev. Prof Liam Ryan passes away] by Brian Conway, Department of Sociology, [[Maynooth University]], 8 June 2015.</ref> Ryan excelled academically earning two masters degrees and doctorates in theology (1962) and in sociology. Following his post-graduate studies (DD) in Maynooth he completed his PhD in Sociology at the [[University of Missouri–St. Louis]].<ref>[https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/news/liam-ryan-31267003.html Fr. Liam Ryan] by Barry Duggan, Irish Independent, 30 May 2015</ref>

He lectured in the Department of Sociology in [[University College Cork]]. During this time, in 1967, he published his famous ''Social Dynamite: A study of early school-leavers'',<ref>[http://www.limerickregeneration.org/Social_Dynamite.pdf Social Dynamite : A study of early school-leavers] by Rev. Liam Ryan MA DD, published by [[University College Cork]], 1967.</ref> which predicted many of the social problems which came to pass in [[Limerick]] and suggested solutions.<ref>[http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/ur079.pdf Limerick Cleric of 1960s fortold where city was headed in his report] by David Raleigh, Limerick Independent (www.limerickindependent.com, 15 July 2009.</ref>

Rev. Dr. Ryan was appointed Professor of Sociology at [[Maynooth University]] in 1969<ref name="kal">[https://maynoothcollege.ie/files/images/Kalendarium-Complete1.pdf Rev. Liam Ryan MA, LPh, DD, PhD] Kalendarium, Maynooth College</ref> holding the position until 2000.<ref name="ita">[https://www.irishtimes.com/life-and-style/people/fr-liam-ryan-1.2482483 Fr. Liam Ryan] by Mary P. Corcoran, An Appreciation, The Irish Times, 4 January 2016.</ref> He was instrumental in the setting up of the Department of Anthropology in 1983, as well as the development of the Department of Adult and Community Education. In the 1980s Ryan pioneered Sociology as part of the Oscail distance learning BA degree with other Irish universities.<ref name="ita"/> Ryan also served as vice-president of [[St Patrick's College, Maynooth]] from 1974-1976.<ref name="kal"/>

==Death and legacy==
Ryan died on 27 May 2015 and was buried in the grounds of St. Michael’s Church, [[Cappamore]] in his native Limerick.<ref>[http://seminary.maynoothcollege.ie/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/Siolta-2016-2.pdf A Priest Sociologist Recalled  A Tribute to Fr Liam Ryan] By Brian Conway, Slíota Magazine 2016, St. Patricks College, Maynooth.</ref> A memorial night of appreciation was also held Maynooth later in the year, and a booklet was produced by the sociology department,<ref>[https://www.maynoothuniversity.ie/sites/default/files/assets/document//Liam%20Ryan%20AW%202.pdf A Celebration of the Life of Professor Liam Ryan] Maynooth University</ref> which had contributions and tributes from President [[Michael D. Higgins]] and from his colleagues and former students.<ref>[https://www.irishtimes.com/news/social-affairs/religion-and-beliefs/in-memoriam-prof-liam-ryan-celebrated-at-maynooth-event-1.2455071 In memoriam: Prof Liam Ryan celebrated at Maynooth event] by Patsy McGarry, Irish Times 4 December 2015.</ref> Also in his memory, a hardback version of his book Social Dynamite was reproduced by Limerick Regeneration.

Dick Stokes (hurler).text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler}} {{More citations needed|date=January 2022}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2022}} {{Use Hiberno-English|date=January 2022}} {{Infobox Gaelic games player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Dick Stokes | irish = Risteard Stóc | birth_date = {{Birth date|1920|3|12|df=yes}} | death_date = {{death date and age|2005|11|17|1920|3|12|df=yes}} | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 10 | nickname= | occupation = Doctor | county = Dublin | province = Munster | club = [[Pallasgreen GAA|Pallasgreen]]
[[UCD GAA|UCD]] | cl_position = Midfield | cl_years = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county_h = 2 | cl_county_f = 1 | cl_province= | cl_all_ireland = | counties = [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] | ic_position = Left wing-forward | ic_years = 1940–1953 | ic_apps_points = | ic_province = 1 | ic_all_ireland = 1 | nhl = 1 | all_stars = | cl_update = | ic_update = | birth_place=[[Oola]], [[County Limerick]], Ireland | death_place=[[Nenagh]], [[County Tipperary]], Ireland }} '''Richard Stokes''' (12 March 1920 – 17 November 2005) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played as a left wing-forward for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick senior team]].{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/Limerick/ArticleForm.aspx?ID=57035|title=Dick Stokes|publisher=Hogan Stand website|date=25 November 2005|accessdate=5 May 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/stokesdick.pdf|title=Dr. Dick Stokes of Oola|publisher=Limerick City website|date=|accessdate=16 July 2013|first=Séamus|last=Ó Ceallaigh}} Born in [[Oola]], [[County Limerick]], Stokes first played competitive hurling whilst at school in Doon CBS. He arrived on the inter-county scene as a [[dual player]] with the Limerick minor hurling and [[Gaelic football|football]] teams. He made his senior hurling debut in the [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1940 championship]]. Stokes went on to win one [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] medal, one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal and one [[National Hurling League]] medal while playing for Limerick. As a member of the [[Munster GAA|Munster]] inter-provincial team at various times throughout his career, Stokes won five [[Railway Cup]] medals. At club level he won two [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|hurling championship]] medals and one [[Dublin Senior Football Championship|football championship]] medal with [[UCD GAA|University College Dublin]]. His retirement came following the conclusion of the [[1953 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1953 championship]]. In retirement from playing, Stokes became involved in team management and coaching. As selector to the Limerick senior team, he helped guide the team to the All-Ireland SHC title in 1973. ==Playing career== ===Colleges=== Stokes first played in goal for the Doon CBS secondary school team in the [[Dr Harty Cup]]. In 1938 he was moved to midfield and was a reserve on the Munster colleges team. The following year Stokes partnered [[Vin Baston]] at midfield in the All-Ireland colleges decider and played a key part in bringing the title back to Munster. ===University=== During his studies at [[University College Dublin]], Stokes played on both the university's hurling and football teams. He first experienced success on the hurling field in 1941. A 2-8 to 2-4 defeat of University College Galway and a 7-10 to 3-1 win over [[UCC GAA|University College Cork]] gave Stokes his first [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal. Three years later in 1944, UCD made a clean sweep of the series once again, giving Stokes, who was now [[Captain (Gaelic games)|captain]] of the team, a second Fitzgibbon Cup medal. In 1945, Stokes was named at full-forward on the UCD football team. A 3-8 to 0-2 defeat of UCC gave him a [[Sigerson Cup]] medal. ===Club=== Stokes began his playing career with [[Pallasgreen GAA|Pallasgreen]]; however, it was as a dual player with University College Dublin in the Dublin county championships that he experienced his greatest successes.{{original research inline|date=April 2017}} In 1943, UCD's senior football team reached the final of the county club championship. A 1-8 to 1-6 defeat of [[Seán McDermott's GAA|Seán McDermott's]] gave Stokes a [[Dublin Senior Football Championship]] medal. Four years later in 1947, Stokes was on the UCD hurling team lined out against [[Faughs GAA|Faughs]] in the county decider. A 6-12 to 4-9 of the hurling kingpins of Dublin, gave Stokes a [[Dublin Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal in the small ball code.{{cite web|url=http://www.ucd.ie/gaa/hurling/history/|title=The history of hurling at UCD|publisher=UCD website|date=|accessdate=16 July 2013|first=|last=}} UC retained the title the following year. ===Inter-county=== Stokes first appeared on the inter-county scene as a dual player at minor level; however, he experienced little success.{{original research inline|date=April 2017}} In 1940, Stokes made his debut for the Limerick senior hurling team in a tournament game against [[Cork county hurling team|Cork]]. He was subsequently included on the Limerick championship team, and made his debut in a drawn Munster semi-final against [[Waterford county hurling team|Waterford]]. It took two late goals from [[Jackie Power]] and a storming display by [[Mick Mackey]] to level the game. Another late rally gave Limerick a victory in the subsequent replay. Stokes's side put in another excellent performance in the Munster final to draw the game with Cork. At half-time in the replay Limerick looked like a spent force. Held scoreless for the entire thirty minutes, team captain Mick Mackey got the recovery underway in the second-half with a point from a seventy. He later moved back to the defence where Cork were running riot with goals. A pitch invasion scuppered the game for ten minutes, however, Limerick held on to win by 3-3 to 2-4 and Stoke collected a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal. The subsequent [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland SHC]] decider on 1 September 1940 brought [[Kilkenny county hurling team|Kilkenny]] and Limerick together for the last great game between the two outstanding teams of the decade. Early in the second-half Kilkenny took a four-point lead; however, once Mick Mackey was deployed at midfield he proceeded to dominate the game. Limerick hung on to win the game on a score line of 3-7 to 1-7. The win gave Stokes an All-Ireland SHC medal. Limerick took a back seat to Cork and Tipperary in the Munster series of games for the next few years. In 1947, Stokes won a [[National Hurling League]] medal as Limerick defeated Kilkenny by 3-8 to 1-7 following an earlier drawn game. Stokes also lined out with the Limerick junior football team. In 1950, he won a [[Munster Junior Football Championship|Munster JFC]] medal following a 3-6 to 1-6 defeat of Cork. ==References== {{reflist}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1940}} {{Limerick Hurling Team 1973}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Stokes, Dick}} [[Category:1920 births]] [[Category:2005 deaths]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship winners]] [[Category:Gaelic games players from County Limerick]] [[Category:Hurling selectors]] [[Category:Limerick county hurling team]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:Munster inter-provincial hurlers]] [[Category:UCD Gaelic footballers]] [[Category:UCD hurlers]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

[[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Donncha Sheehan''' (born 24 August 1979) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Adare GAA|Adare]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Sheehan played hurling at all grades as a student at [[Ardscoil Rís, Limerick|Ardscoil Rís]] in [[Limerick]]. He later studied at [[University of Limerick]] and was part of the UL team that beat [[Waterford IT GAA|Waterford Institute of Technology]] by 2-14 to 2-11 to claim the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] title in 2002.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaelic-football/murray-buries-wit/26053701.html|title=Murray buries WIT|publisher=Irish Independent|date=4 March 2002|access-date=9 May 2025|first=|last=}} At club level, Sheehan first played for [[Adare GAA|Adare]] at juvenile and underage levels, and was part of the club's under-21 team that won consecutive Limerick U21AHC titles in 1999 and 2000.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Early goals give Adare the title|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=13 November 1999|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Brennan goal seals title for Adare in gripping encounter with neighbours Croom|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=11 December 2000|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to the club's senior side and was involved in five [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]]-winning teams. Sheehan [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ed Adare to three successive title wins between 2007 and 2009.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/adare-swat-na-piarsaigh-aside-to-claim-limerick-title-430709.html|title=Adare swat Na Piarsaigh aside to claim Limerick title|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=18 October 2009|accessdate=31 October 2018|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Sheehan first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as part of the under-21 team. He won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster U21HC]] medal before later captaining the team to a 1-13 to 0-13 win over [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the [[2000 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship final|2000 All-Ireland under-21 final]].{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/brilliant-limerick-rip-cork-to-shreds/26112287.html|title=Brilliant Limerick rip Cork to shreds|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=3 October 2015|date=24 August 2000}}{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/young-guns-grab-glory-for-limerick-26109433.html|title=Young guns grab glory for Limerick|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=3 October 2015|date=18 September 2000}} Sheehan made his [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] debut in 2003.{{cite '''Seán Tobin''' (born 18 December 1989) is an Irish [[hurling]] coach and former player. In a career that spanned three decades he lined out at club level with [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].

==Career==
===Murroe-Boher===

After coming to hurling prominence as a student at [[CBS Sexton Street]], Tobin later lined out in the [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] with the [[Limerick Institute of Technology]] while simultaneously joining [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe-Boher]]'s top adult club team. In 2017, he won a [[Limerick Premier Intermediate Hurling Championship|Premier Intermediate Championship]] title after top-scoring with 1–10 in a 1–21 to 1-15 replay defeat of [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportinglimerick.com/murroe-boher-crowned-premier-intermediate-hurling-champions/|title=Murroe-Boher crowned Premier Intermediate Hurling Champions|publisher=Sporting Limerick|date=19 October 2017|accessdate=24 September 2020|first=|last=}}</ref> On 9 June 2021, Tobin announced his retirement from the club game at the age of 31 because of injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Article/Index/317471|title=Limerick Munster SHC winner forced to hang up his boots because of injury|publisher=Hogan Stand|date=9 June 2021|accessdate=9 June 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

===Limerick===

Tobin first played for Limerick as a member of the minor team on 24 June 2007. He was held scoreless in a 0–12 to 3–21 [[2007 All-Ireland Minor Hurling Championship#Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]] defeat by [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/maher-sets-the-tone-as-tipperary-ease-through-1.1211945|title=Maher sets the tone as Tipperary ease through|work=The Irish Times|date=26 June 2007|accessdate=23 June 2015}}</ref> Over the following three years he was a regular with the Limerick under-21 team, however, his side enjoyed little success during that period.

Tobin made his senior debut for Limerick in a 2–09 to 0–06 [[2011 National Hurling League#Division 2|league]] defeat of [[Clare GAA|Clare]] on 13 February 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-step-up-to-the-plate-for-ogrady-26695360.html|title=Limerick step up to the plate for O'Grady|work=Irish Independent|date=14 February 2011|accessdate=26 June 2015}}</ref> He became a regular throughout the group stage games and ended the campaign with a [[National Hurling League#Division 2|Division 2]] winners' medal following a 4–12 to 2–13 defeat of Clare in the [[National Hurling League#Division 2|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/limerick-on-the-rise-26728720.html|title=Limerick on the rise|work=Irish Independent|date=2 May 2011|accessdate=26 June 2015|first=Christy|last=O'Connor}}</ref> Tobin contributed 1-01 during that game.

On 12 June 2011, Tobin made his senior championship debut in a 3–15 to 3–14 [[2011 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster semi-final]] defeat by [[Waterford GAA|Waterford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20157642.html|title=Never say die Deise reap|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=13 June 2011|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref>

In 2013, Tobin won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal following a 0–24 to 0–15 victory over Cork.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 July 2013|access-date=15 July 2013|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}}</ref>

In March 2016, Tobin left the Limerick senior team citing a lack of game time under manager [[T. J. Ryan (hurler)|T. J. Ryan]] as his primary reason.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2016/0323/776888-seanie-tobin-limerick/|title=Seanie Tobin departs Limerick panel|publisher=RTÉ Sport|date=23 March 2016|accessdate=10 June 2021|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/seanie-tobin-limerick-senior-hurling-2676812-Mar2016/|title=2013 Munster title winning forward departs the Limerick senior hurling panel|publisher=The 42|date=23 March 2016|accessdate=10 June 2021|first=|last=}}</ref>

County Limerick, Ireland }} '''William Ryan''' (11 November 1894 – 16 July 1969) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] [[Hurling|hurler]] who played for club sides [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]], [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe]] and [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] and at inter-county level with [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]]. ==Career== Ryan was just 15-years-old when he made his first appearance for [[Cappamore GAA|Cappamore]] in the [[1909 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1909 championship]]. Cappamore was not his only club, as he also won a [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|Limerick JHC]] title with [[Murroe-Boher GAA|Murroe]] in 1917. Ryan also played [[Gaelic football]] at club level and [[Captain (sport)|captain]]ed Cappamore to a defeat by Foynes in the 1925 Limerick JFC final. He won a [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] title with the [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] in 1926. Ryan's 21-year club career came to an end with a defeat for Cappamore by [[Croom GAA|Croom]] in the delayed [[1929 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1929 Limerick SHC final]].{{cite news|url=http://www.limerick.ie/media/ryanwillie.pdf|title=Great Limerick Athletes: No 77 - Willie Ryan|publisher=Limerick website|access-date=3 October 2011}} Ryan first appeared on the inter-county scene with [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] in 1914 and continued to line until his retirement in 1928. He enjoyed his first success when he was part of the Limerick team that beat [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1918 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/limerick/Profile|title=Limerick profile|date=|publisher=Hogan Stand website|access-date=13 February 2023|first=|last=}} Ryan claimed a second [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] medal following Limerick's defeat of [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] in the [[1921 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1921 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/657392/centenary-of-limerick-s-1921-all-ireland-hurling-championship-title.html|title=Centenary of Limerick's 1921 All-Ireland hurling championship title|date=18 August 2021|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=13 February 2023|first=|last=}} His other honours include three [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal and four [[Thomond Feis]] medals.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior Hurling|date=|publisher=Munster GAA website|access-date=13 February 2023|first=|last=}} Ryan's performances at inter-county level resulted in his inclusion on the [[Ireland national hurling team|Ireland]] team at the [[Tailteann Games (Irish Free State)|Tailteann Games]] in 1924. He also enjoyed a lengthy career as a referee. ==Personal life and death== Ryan, who worked as a farmer in [[Cappamore]], married Nora Power on 21 January 1931 and the couple had four children.{{cite web|url=https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/1311851351478?b=https%3A%2F%2Fcivilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie%2Fchurchrecords%2Fcivil-perform-search.jsp%3Fnamefm%3Dwilliam%26namel%3Dryan%26exact%3D%26name2fm%3D%26name2l%3D%26location%3D%26yyfrom%3D1930%26yyto%3D1936%26type%3DM%26century%3D%26decade%3D%26sort%3D%26pageSize%3D100%26ddBfrom%3D%26mmBfrom%3D%26yyBfrom%3D%26ddMfrom%3D%26mmMfrom%3D%26yyMfrom%3D%26ddDfrom%3D%26mmDfrom%3D%26yyDfrom%3D%26ddPfrom%3D%26mmPfrom%3D%26yyPfrom%3D%26ddBto%3D%26mmBto%3D%26yyBto%3D%26ddMto%3D%26mmMto%3D%26yyMto%3D%26ddDto%3D%26mmDto%3D%26yyDto%3D%26ddPto%3D%26mmPto%3D%26yyPto%3D%26locationB%3D%26locationM%3D%26locationD%3D%26locationP%3D%26keywordb%3D%26keywordm%3D%26keywordd%3D%26keywordp%3D%26event%3D%26district%3DLimerick%26submit%3DSearch|title=Marriage {{short description|Irish hurler}} {{Use dmy dates|date=October 2021}} {{Use Irish English|date=October 2021}} {{Infobox GAA player | code= Hurling | sport = Hurling | image = | name = Dan Troy | irish = Dónall Ó Troithigh | height = | nickname = | occupation = Labourer | county = Limerick | province = Munster | club = [[Newport GAA|Newport]]

[[County Tipperary]], Ireland | death_date = 18 December 1953 (aged 56) | death_place= [[Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Daniel Troy''' (1897 - 18 December 1953) was an Irish [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level he played with [[Newport GAA|Newport]] and [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]], and also lined out at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== Troy first played hurling at club level with the [[Newport GAA|Newport]] club in [[County Tipperary|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=http://www.newport.tipperary.gaa.ie/the-shamrock-hurling-team|title=The Shamrock Hurling Team|publisher=Newport GAA website|date=|access-date=23 July 2023|first=|last=}} He later joined the [[Claughaun GAA|Claughaun]] club after moving to [[Limerick]], and made his first appearances for the team during their [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]]-winning campaign in 1918.{{cite web|url=https://claughaungaa.com/history/|title=History|publisher=Claughaun GAA website|date=|access-date=23 July 2023|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nenaghguardian.ie/2022/06/04/killinan-end-finals-which-will-tell-a-lot/|title=KILLINAN END - Finals which will tell a lot|publisher=The Nenagh Guardian|date=4 June 2022|access-date=23 July 2023|first=|last=}} Troy's performances at club level resulted in his inclusion on the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He soon won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal before lining out in Limerick's defeat 9-05 to 1-03 of [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] in the [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|1918 All-Ireland final]].{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=|access-date=23 July 2023|first=|last=}} Troy sustained a serious injury during the game which resulted in a prolonged period of absence from both club and inter-county hurling. He won a second Limerick SHC medal in 1926.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/troydan153.pdf|title=Dan Troy of Claughaun|publisher=Limerick City website|date=|access-date=23 July 2023|first=|last=}} ==Death== Troy died suddenly on 18 December 1953, at the age of 56. He was the first member of Limerick's 1918 All-Ireland-winning team to die.{{cite web|url=http://www.limerickcity.ie/media/11%20olj%2053%20limk%20hurlers%20join%20centennial%20club.pdf|title=Limerick hurlers join the centennial club|publisher=Limerick City website|date=|access-date=23 July 2023|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;Claughan *[[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1918 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1918]], [[1926 Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|1926]] ;Limerick *[[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1918]] *[[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]]: [[1918 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Munster Senior Hurling Championship|1918]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{Navboxes |title=Dan Troy navigation boxes |bg= |fg= |list1= {{Limerick Hurling Team 1918}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Troy, Dan}} [[Category:1897 births]] [[Category:1953 deaths]] [[Category:Newport hurlers]] [[Category:Claughaun hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship winners]]

Born in [[Garryspillane]], [[County Limerick]], Ryan arrived on the inter-county scene at the age of eighteen when he first linked up with the Limerick minor hurling team, before later lining out with the under-21 side. He made his senior debut in the [[National Hurling League 2008|2008 National Hurling League]]. Ryan has since gone on to play a key part for Limerick, and has won one [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster]] medal and one [[National Hurling League|National League (Division 2)]] medal.{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0430/limerick_clare.html |title=Limerick 4-12 Clare 2-13 |publisher=[[RTÉ Sport]] |date=30 April 2011 |accessdate=13 June 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110603042348/http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/championship/2011/0430/limerick_clare.html |archivedate= 3 June 2011 }}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20236924.html|title=Day of joy sends tremor through Treaty|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=15 July 2013|access-date=15 July 2013|first=Diarmuid|last=O'Flynn}} He was also a regular member of the Limerick [[Gaelic football]] team for a number of seasons.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} Ryan was named as the Man of the Match in [[2013 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final]] as Limerick defeated [[Cork GAA|Cork]] by 0–24 to 0–15 with Ryan scoring three points during the game.{{cite web|url= http://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/2013/0715/462596-ryan-the-best-feeling-i-ever-had-in-my-life/|title= James Ryan credits the fans support for Limerick's long-awaited Munster Hurling title|date=16 July 2013|work=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=24 July 2013 }} At club level Ryan has won one [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|championship]] medal with [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]].{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} ==Honours== ;Inter-county * [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] (1): [[2013 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2013]] == References == {{Reflist}} {{Limerick Minor Hurling Team 2005}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Ryan, James}} [[Category:1987 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Dual players]] [[Category:Garryspillane hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:21st-century Irish sportsmen]]
