'''Patrick Ryan''' (born 1995) is an Irish [[hurling|hurler]] who plays as a Full Forward for club side [[Doon GAA|Doon]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsjoe.ie/gaa/limerick-best-supersub-country-154511|title=Limerick have the best super sub in the country|date=19 March 2018|publisher=SportsJoe|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Niall|last=McIntyre}}</ref>

==Playing career==
===University===

During his studies at the [[University of Limerick]], Ryan was selected for the college's senior hurling team. On 24 February 2018, he won a [[Fitzgibbon Cup]] medal following UL's 2–21 to 2–15 defeat of [[Dublin City University]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2018/0224/943259-ul-pull-away-to-claim-fitzgibbon-cup-glory/|title=UL pull away to claim Fitzgibbon Cup glory|date=29 February 2016|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=5 August 2018|first=Denis|last=Hurley}}</ref>

===Club===

Ryan joined the [[Doon GAA|Doon]] club at a young age and played in all grades at juvenile and underage levels, enjoying championship success in under-12, under-14 and under-15 grades. As a member of the club's minor team, he won back-to-back championship medals in 2012 and 2013 following respective defeats of [[Patrickswell GAA|Patrickswell]] and [[Na Piarsaigh GAA (Limerick)|Na Piarsaigh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/89915/Doon-retain-Limerick-minor-hurling-title.html|title=Doon retain Limerick minor hurling title|date=14 October 2013|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=30 July 2018|first=Jerome|last=O'Connell}}</ref> Ryan later made his senior championship debut for the club.{{citation needed|date=December 2021}}

===Inter-county===
====Minor and under-21====

Ryan first played for Limerick at minor level in 2012, in a season which ended with a defeat by [[Clare GAA|Clare]] in the [[Munster Minor Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] semi-final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/hurling/osullivan-sinks-cork-26849425.html|title=O'Sullivan sinks Cork|date=3 May 2012|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-football/banner-dig-deep-to-see-off-limerick-26870643.html|title=Banner dig deep to see off Limerick|date=30 June 2012|publisher=Irish Independent|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

Ryan joined the Limerick under-21 hurling team in 2014. In his second season he won a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal after a 0–22 to 0–19 win over Clare in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/clare-power-and-class-too-much-for-limerick-271062.html|title=Clare power and class too much for Limerick|date=5 June 2014|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/article/index/241856|title=Munster U21HC final: Treaty Lynch Banner|date=30 July 2015|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref> On 12 September 2015, Ryan was at midfield when Limerick defeated [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] by 0–26 to 1–07 in the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|All-Ireland final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/breakingnews/sport/limerick-ease-past-wexford-to-claim-u21-hurling-title-695616.html|title=Limerick ease past Wexford to claim U21 hurling title|date=12 September 2015|publisher=Irish Examiner|accessdate=30 July 2018|first=Eoghan|last=Cormican}}</ref> He ended the season by being named on the Bord Gáis Energy Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/197926/Eight-Limerick-hurlers-on-U-21.html|title=Eight Limerick hurlers on U-21 team of the year|date=6 October 2015|publisher=Limerick Leader|access-date=30 July 2018|first=|last=}}</ref>

====Senior====

On 12 February 2017, Ryan made his first appearance for the Limerick senior team in a 1–14 to 0-14 [[National Hurling League]] defeat by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2017/0212/852110-davys-wexford-come-good-to-ta/|title=Davy's Wexford come good to see off Limerick|date=13 February 2017|publisher=RTÉ Sport|accessdate=8 August 2018|first=Brendan|last=Furlong}}</ref>

On 19 August 2018, Ryan was a non-playing substitute when Limerick won their first [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|All-Ireland]] title in 45 years after a 3–16 to 2–18 defeat of [[Galway GAA|Galway]] in the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/limerick-are-all-ireland-hurling-champions-for-the-first-time-in-45-years-following-epic-victory-over-galway-37230532.html|title=Limerick are All Ireland hurling champions for the first time in 45 years following epic victory over Galway|publisher=Irish Independent|date=19 August 2018|accessdate=20 August 2018|first=Seán|last=McGoldrick}}</ref>

On 30 June 2019, Ryan won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster Championship]] medal as a non-playing substitute following Limerick's 2–26 to 2–14 defeat of [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the [[2019 Munster Senior Hurling Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-4703771-Jun2019/|title=More glory for Limerick as they lift Munster crown with 12-point win over Tipperary|date=30 June 2019|publisher=The 42|accessdate=1 July 2019|first=Fintan|last=O'Toole}}</ref>

Séamus Ryan (hurler).text:
{{Short description|Irish hurler and priest (1937–2023)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2021}}
{{Use Hiberno-English|date=December 2021}}
'''James L. "Séamus" Ryan'''  (1937<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.findmypast.ie/transcript?id=IRE%2FBMD%2FD%2F692879639|title=James L Ryan in 1937|work=Find My Past website| date=|access-date=13 February 2023}}</ref> – 11 February 2023) was an [[Irish people|Irish]] priest. He was a renowned lecturer and gifted [[Hurling|hurler]] who played at senior level for the [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick county team]], winning the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] title in 1955, alongside his older brother [[Liam Ryan (Limerick hurler)|Liam]] (who also became a priest and lecturer in sociology in Maynooth) who [[Captain (Gaelic games)|captain]]ed the side. Their father [[Willie Ryan (Limerick hurler)|Willie Ryan]] had also played inter-county hurling.

From Cappamore, [[County Limerick]], he went to [[St Patrick's College, Maynooth]] to study for the priesthood. At Maynooth he
earned a doctorate and was ordained a priest in 1961. Fr. Seamus with the benefit of a German Government scholarship to the University of Munster in Westphalia, Germany, studied under young Professor Ratzinger later [[Pope Benedict XVI|Pope Benedict]].<ref>[https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/local-news/123863/Limerick-priest-taught-by-Pope-is.html Limerick priest taught by Pos is not surprised by decision] by Donal O'Reagan, Limerick Leader, 2 May 2013.</ref>

Returning to Ireland in 1964, Ryan lectured in theology in [[St. Patrick's College, Thurles]] up until 1990 when he was appointed parish priest to St Matthews Parish, Ballyfermot Upper in Dublin. He retired as parish priest of St Matthew's in 2016, returning to his native Cappamore.<ref>[https://www.echo.ie/news/article/parish-priest-retires-amid-many-tributes Parish priest retires amid many tributes] by Maurice Garvey, www.echo.ie, 2 May 2016.</ref>

Ryan died on 11 February 2023.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://limerickgaa.ie/weve-lost-a-saint-parish-mourns-death-of-priest-and-limerick-hurler/|title=‘We’ve lost a saint’: Parish mourns death of priest and Limerick hurler|work=Limerick GAA website| date=11 February 2023|access-date=12 February 2023}}</ref>

[[Limerick GAA (New York)|Limerick Club, New York]] | cl_years = | cl_position = | cl_apps_points = | cl_county = 2 | cl_province = | cl_all_ireland = | colleges = | fitz = | col_years = | counties = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | ic_years = 1984-1993 | ic_position = Centre-forward | ic_apps_points = 10 (2-06) | ic_province = 0 | ic_all_ireland = 0 | nhl = 2 | all_stars = 0 | cl_update = | ic_update = 16:58, 9 December 2021 }} '''Raymond Sampson''' (born 1965) is an [[Irish people|Irish]] former [[hurling|hurler]] who played at club level with [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. He usually lined out as a forward. ==Career== Sampson first came to prominence as a [[hurling|hurler]] at juvenile and underage levels with the [[Garryspillane GAA|Garryspillane]] club before eventually progressing onto the club's top adult team.{{cite web|url=https://www.clubinfo.ie/club/garryspillane-hc/|title=Garryspillane HC|publisher=Club info website|date=|accessdate=11 January 2020|first=|last=}} During his club career he claimed championship medals in the [[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship|junior]] and [[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship|intermediate]] grades, while he also won two [[New York Senior Hurling Championship|senior]] titles with the [[Limerick GAA (New York)|Limerick Club]] in [[New York City|New York]]. Sampson also represented the [[St. Flannan's College]] team in his youth and won consecutive [[Dr. Croke Cup|All-Ireland Colleges Championship]] titles in 1982 and 1983, having earlier won consecutive [[Dr. Harty Cup|Harty Cup]] titles.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-20332230.html|title=Championship Preview: Clare and Limerick? The only differences between us are those little idiosyncrasies, those unique emblems, which distinguish us all as our own separate little tribe in the wider hurling family.|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=22 May 2015|accessdate=11 January 2020|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/regionals/newrossstandard/sport/other-sports/harty-cup-team-of-the-millennium-27457772.html|title=Harty Cup team of the millennium|publisher=Irish Independent|date=11 March 2000|accessdate=11 January 2020|first=|last=}} He first appeared on the inter-county scene as a member of the [[Limerick GAA|Limerick minor hurling team]] in 1983, before winning a [[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|Munster Under-21 Championship]] title in 1986. Sampson was a regular with the Limerick senior team for almost a decade, during which time he won two [[National Hurling League]] titles.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/584552/limerick-s-1992-nhl-final-win-ray-sampson-s-knock-out-blow-and-the-end-of-radio-days.html|title=Limerick's 1992 NHL final win - Ray Sampson's knock-out blow and the end of radio days|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=31 October 2020|accessdate=9 December 2021|first=|last=}} ==Honours== ;St. Flannan's College *[[Dr. Croke Cup]]: [[1982 Croke Cup|1982]], [[1983 Croke Cup|1983]] (c) *[[Dr. Harty Cup]]: 1982, 1983 (c) ;Garryspillane *[[Limerick Intermediate Hurling Championship]]: 1990, 1996 *[[Limerick Junior Hurling Championship]]: 1984 ;Limerick Club, New York *[[New York Senior Hurling Championship]]: 1994, 1995 ;Limerick *[[National Hurling League]]: [[1984-85 National Hurling League|1984-85]], [[1991-92 National Hurling League|1991-92]] *[[Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship]]: [[1986 All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship#Munster Under-21 Hurling Championship|1986]] ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Sampson, Ray}} [[Category:1965 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Garryspillane hurlers]] [[Category:Limerick inter-county hurlers]] [[Category:20th-century Irish sportsmen]]

He eventually progressed to the senior team and was a [[Dr Harty Cup]] runner-up in 2023.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/arid-41064920.html|title=Cashel CS crowned Harty Cup champions after historic first all-Tipperary decider|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=6 February 2023|access-date=17 February 2018|first=Therese|last=O'Callaghan}} Scully later played hurling with [[Mary Immaculate College]]. [[County Limerick]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] }} '''Pádraig Tobin''' (born 1970) is an Irish former [[hurling|hurler]]. At club level, he played with [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] and at inter-county level with the [[Limerick senior hurling team]]. ==Career== At club level, Tobin first played for [[Kilmallock GAA|Kilmallock]] at juvenile and underage levels, and was part of the club's minor team that won the Limerick MAHC title in 1987.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Kilmallock abú!|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=19 September 1987|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He progressed to adult level and won [[Limerick Senior Hurling Championship|Limerick SHC]] medals in 1992 and 1994.{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/limerick-sport/128541/1992--When-Kilmallock-conquered-Limerick.html|title=1992: When Kilmallock conquered Limerick and Munster|publisher=Limerick Leader|date=20 November 2014|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Both of these titles were subsequently followed by [[Munster Senior Club Hurling Championship|Munster Club SHC]] titles.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/shclub_teams/|title=Senior Hurling (Club)|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=7 June 2009|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} Tobin also lined out in Kilmallock's 1–17 to 2–07 defeat by [[Sarsfields GAA (Galway)|Sarsfields]] in the [[1993 All-Ireland Senior Club Hurling Championship final|1993 All-Ireland club final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/all-ireland-club-hurling/26713575.html|title=All-Ireland Club Hurling|publisher=Irish Independent|date=15 March 2011|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} At inter-county level, Tobin first played for [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] as a member of the [[All-Ireland Under-21 Hurling Championship|under-21 team]] in 1991.{{cite web|url=https://archive.irishnewsarchive.com/olive/APA/INA/Default.aspx#panel=document|title=Limerick tops in under 21 thriller|publisher=Irish Independent|date=1 August 1991|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}} He first played for the [[Limerick senior hurling team|senior team]] in 1993, but only became a regular panel member in 1996. Tobin won a [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship|Munster SHC]] medal that year, however, Limerick faced a subsequent All-Ireland final defeat by [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] respectively.{{cite web|url=https://munster.gaa.ie/history/senior-hurling/|title=Senior hurling|publisher=Munster GAA website|date=29 May 2009|access-date=20 April 2025|first=|last=}}{{cite
